### TD-411: `resume` (Every `trainer_service` Pass) Never Downloads Over FTP

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 14, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainingTool | Code fix, `resume` October 18 and `retrain` November 14, 2026 (**HIGH**, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainingTool`, by inspection (definite). `trainer_service` runs
`incremental_trainer --foreground --admin-port N resume` for every pass, and `resume` calls
`IncrementalTrainer::resume_last_session()`. That function acquires pending files and then trains on
`resp.registry_paths()` directly, under the comment "resume_last_session runs on the same machine as
the registry … ftp_server_host is always empty here". That's only true for a local registry. With
`REGISTRY_SERVER_URL` pointing at a remote `registry_server` that delivers files over FTP (TD-040's
transport), these are the registry host's paths; the `DataTransport::fetch_all()` download that `train`
performs never happens, so the trainer can't open the files. With TD-412 the pass then "succeeds" and
marks them trained.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** the FTP-or-direct download step is now `resolve_pass_files()` in `IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`, shared by
`train`, `retrain` (its pending files) and `resume`. It keeps TD-205 segment ranges. `IncrementalTrainer::resume_last_session()` takes an optional
`PassFileResolver`, which the `resume` command passes, and the downloads are cleaned up after the pass. Without a resolver, a registry that hands
out an FTP host fails the pass and releases its files instead of training on paths it can't read. The pass also now releases its batch when the
resume checkpoint is missing or fails to load; before, those returns left the files claimed.

New test `ResumeTrainsOnResolvedFilesAndReleasesOnResolverFailure`: a failed resolver releases the file, and a successful one trains on the resolved
local path and marks the registry entry trained. The old code failed it.

The rest, `retrain`, was left open then: it read its already-trained files by registry path (only pending ones were fetched), so a full
retrain against a remote FTP registry couldn't read them.

**Fix (November 14, 2026):** `retrain` first returns every trained unit to the pending queue, assigned to the model
(`DatasetRegistry::requeue_trained(all)`, TD-540's re-queue, which keeps each trained segment as that segment), then claims the whole
pool and resolves it through `resolve_pass_files()` like `train`. So against `registry_server` every file comes over FTP, the claims are
renewed, and each unit gets its own trained record for the new run (one pair count per unit, TD-334). The model is reset and its
checkpoints archived before any of this, so a pass that fails leaves the files pending, which is the honest state. A registry that
can't take the re-queue, or can't be asked for the claim, fails the pass before anything trains. Test: `retrainRemoteTests` spawns
`registry_server` with FTP on and `incremental_trainer`, trains once and retrains, and counts the FTP server's completed downloads of
the file: 2 (the old code: 1, reading the trained file by its registry path). `DatasetRegistry::trained_units()` (TD-546), which only
`retrain` used, now has no production caller.

- [x] Factor `train`'s acquire → (FTP download) → train → mark/release → cleanup sequence into one function and use it from `resume_last_session()` (with the segment ranges). (The download step is shared; acquire/mark/release stay in each caller.)
- [x] Ask the user whether ai-machine's `trainer_service` uses a remote FTP registry; if so, audit and re-queue files marked trained since it went live. Answered October 18, 2026: the trainer always takes its data from the remote services. The affected files can't be told apart (TD-334), so re-queue everything before the retraining with `dataset_manager requeue --all --model <name>` (TD-540).
- [x] Download already-trained files for `retrain` against a remote registry. (November 14, 2026: by re-queueing them and claiming the
  whole pool, see the Fix above.)

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`resume_last_session()`), `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (`train`, `retrain`, `resume`
commands), `src/TrainingPassFiles.cpp` (`resolve_pass_files()`); the `TODO: See TD-411` tags are now fix comments.

Files to Modify:

- `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
- `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`
- `tests/retrain_remote_test.cpp`, `tests/CMakeLists.txt` (`retrainRemoteTests`)

### TD-467: `MultiHeadAttention` Unchecked Loads, `num_heads == 0` SIGFPE and Hot-Loop Overhead

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 13, 2026 | Attention / MultiHeadAttention | Code fix (LOW, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MultiHeadAttention` (whose per-head backward was verified correct against finite differences):
- **Unchecked loads (verified).** `load_weights()` checks `d_model`/`num_heads` but not its matrix reads: a file truncated to half
  loaded with no error and all 256 entries of a 16-wide layer's `W_o` were still its random initialization. A damaged checkpoint
  sidecar silently yields a corrupted layer. Same class as TD-298, TD-369, TD-423, TD-426.
- **SIGFPE (verified).** `MultiHeadAttention(8, 0)` dies with SIGFPE: `d_k(d_model / num_heads)` in the initializer list runs before
  the divisibility check that would throw. Same as TD-299 (`CrossAttention`); MNS doesn't validate architectures (TD-461).
- **By inspection.** The per-head score/softmax/value loops index through the bounds-checked, out-of-line `Matrix::operator()`
  (TD-435) and walk `V` column-wise; parallelism is over heads only. A fully masked row becomes a uniform distribution over masked
  positions (no current caller produces one). `save_weights()`/`load_weights()`/`print_config()` print to `std::cout`.

Action Items:

- [x] Check every read in `load_weights()` (and writes in `save_weights()`), throwing on a short file; do it with Tier 55's shared loader fix.

**Load/save checks (October 26, 2026, with TD-423).** `save_weights()`/`load_weights()` reads and writes through `adai::binio` (`src/BinaryIO.{hpp,cpp}`): a short or over-long file throws `std::runtime_error`, the file is read into temporaries before anything changes, and a failed write or flush throws. Covered by `EncoderDecoderModelTest.EveryCheckpointFileIsCheckedOnLoad`.
- [x] Validate `num_heads > 0` before computing `d_k`.
- [x] Use raw row pointers in the per-head loops (or per-head GEMMs); replace console output with `Logger`.

**Fix (November 13, 2026, with TD-299).** `d_k` is initialized from `checked_head_dim()`, which throws `std::invalid_argument` for a
zero or negative `d_model`/`num_heads` or a `d_model` not divisible by `num_heads`; `MultiHeadAttentionConstructorTest.
DimensionNotDivisible` now also covers 0 and negative values (the old code died with SIGFPE). `forward_parallel()`'s per-head loops
read and write through row pointers, compute the scaled scores, mask and softmax row by row, and accumulate the value product over
V's rows; every sum adds the same terms in the same order, and forward (with and without a causal mask) and backward outputs hashed
bit-for-bit equal before and after across three shapes. `print_config()` logs at info and save/load at debug through `adai::Logger`
(the `PrintConfig` tests capture the log). The fully masked row case is unchanged (no caller produces one).

Location in code: `src/MultiHeadAttention.cpp` (constructor, `checked_head_dim()`, `forward_parallel()`, `print_config()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/MultiHeadAttention.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/multiheadattention_test.cpp`

### TD-426: `LayerNorm` Silent Setters, Missing Shape Checks and Unchecked Loads

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 13, 2026 | Layers / LayerNorm | Code fix (LOW, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `LayerNorm`; the first two items verified:
- `set_gamma()`/`set_beta()` print to `std::cerr` and **return without changing anything** on a shape
  mismatch: `set_gamma(1×5)` on a dim-4 norm left γ at 1 with no exception. `ModelSerializer` validates
  sizes first (`require()`), so it's latent there, but callers can't detect a failed set. Neither setter
  refreshes the GPU mirror.
- `forward()` doesn't check `input.cols == dim`, and `backward()` doesn't check its row count against the
  cached forward (or that a forward happened). Both surface as `std::out_of_range("Matrix index out of
  bounds")` from `Matrix::operator()`, not a clear dimension error.
- `load_weights()` doesn't check its reads (a truncated file keeps the old values for the rest), reads the
  saved ε and discards it, and `save_weights()` doesn't check its writes; both print to `std::cout`, as
  does `print_config()` (no production caller).
- `gpu_backward()` dereferences `gpu_` without a check.

Action Items:

- [x] Throw `invalid_argument` from the setters and on shape mismatches; check reads and writes (with the other legacy loaders, Tier 55); switch to `adai::Logger`; guard `gpu_backward()`; refresh the GPU mirror in the setters.

**Load/save checks (October 26, 2026, with TD-423).** `LayerNorm::save_weights()`/`load_weights()` reads and writes through `adai::binio` (`src/BinaryIO.{hpp,cpp}`): a short or over-long file throws `std::runtime_error`, the file is read into temporaries before anything changes, and a failed write or flush throws. Covered by `EncoderDecoderModelTest.EveryCheckpointFileIsCheckedOnLoad`.

**Fix (November 13, 2026).** The constructor rejects a dimension below 1 and an epsilon that isn't a positive finite number.
`set_gamma()`/`set_beta()` throw `std::invalid_argument` on any shape but `[1, dim]` (nothing changes) and upload the new values to the
device mirror when there is one. `forward()` throws `std::invalid_argument` unless the input has `dim` columns; `backward()` throws
`std::logic_error` without a forward and `std::invalid_argument` unless the gradient has the forward input's shape; `gpu_backward()`
does the same against its cached forward (it used to dereference a null `gpu_`). `load_weights()` adopts the file's epsilon (a
non-positive or non-finite one throws, changing nothing) and refreshes the device mirror. Save/load log at debug level and
`print_config()` at info through `adai::Logger`. Six new `LayerNormValidationTest` tests, all failing on the old code.

Location in code: `src/LayerNorm.cpp` (constructor, `forward()`, `backward()`, `set_gamma()`/`set_beta()`, `load_weights()`,
`gpu_backward()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/LayerNorm.{hpp,cpp}`

### TD-300: `CrossAttention::forward_with_cache()` Silently Reuses Stale Encoder K/V

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 13, 2026 | Attention / CrossAttention | Code fix (LOW, filed October 10, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-297 and confirmed by running the real class. Once the `KVCache` is filled,
`forward_with_cache()` ignores `kv_input` entirely. Reusing a cache with a different encoder output
silently returned attention over the **old** encoder's K/V (identical to the first call), and a mask
sized for the new encoder was rejected with a confusing `src_len` error. Enabling or changing LoRA
after the cache is filled also leaves stale K/V. Production is safe today because
`EncoderDecoderModel` builds a fresh `DecoderKVCache` per generation, but nothing documents or checks
the contract.

**Fix (November 13, 2026).** More than the row check below, since the confirmed failure includes a
same-length encoder output and a LoRA change:
- When `forward_with_cache()` fills a cache it stores a source tag in the new `KVCache::source_tag`:
  an FNV-1a hash of a per-instance id, the layer's weights version, the input's shape and 64 sampled
  values (first and last rows included), so the check costs the same for any input size. Every later
  call recomputes it and throws `std::invalid_argument` on a different row count (naming both
  shapes) or tag, before anything changes. `clear()` resets the tag.
- The weights version changes with every weight change through the layer: the setters, `load()`,
  `update_weights()`, `enable_lora()`, `merge_lora()` (through the private `weights_changed()`, which
  replaces TD-301's `refresh_gpu_mirror()` and still refreshes the device mirror) and
  `gpu_download_weights()`. A cache filled before a LoRA change, or by another `CrossAttention`, is
  refused.
- `gpu_forward_with_cache()` checks the row count and the weights the same way through
  `GPUKVCache::source_tag()`/`set_source_tag()`; it doesn't sample the content, which would copy
  from the device every step.
- Not caught, and documented in the header: an input matching at all 64 sampled positions, a change
  to the adapters' own weights (`get_lora_*()->update()`), an optimizer step taken elsewhere.

Tests: `CrossAttentionCacheSourceTest` (5; the different-length, same-length and weight/LoRA/other-layer
tests fail on the old code; the same-output and cleared-cache tests guard the reuse that must keep
working), `CrossAttentionGPUContractTest.ACachedGpuCallChecksTheEncoderLengthAndTheWeights` (oneAPI CPU
device), and `KVCache.AppendKeepsEveryRowInOrder` (`clear()` resets the tag).

Action Items:

- [x] Check `kv_input.rows` against the cached K rows (when non-empty) and throw on mismatch; document that callers must `clear()` the cache for a new encoder output. (Plus the sampled content, layer and weights.)
- [x] Test: a cache reused with a different-length encoder output throws.

Location in code: `src/CrossAttention.cpp` (`forward_with_cache()`, `gpu_forward_with_cache()`, `cache_source_tag()`, `weights_changed()`), `src/KVCache.hpp`, `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.hpp`.

Files Modified:

- `src/CrossAttention.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/KVCache.hpp` (`source_tag`), `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.hpp` (`GPUKVCache::source_tag()`)
- `tests/crossattention_test.cpp`, `tests/kvcache_test.cpp`

### TD-299: `CrossAttention` Crashes with SIGFPE When `num_heads` Is Zero

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 13, 2026 | Attention / CrossAttention | Code fix (LOW, filed October 10, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-297 and confirmed by running the real class. The constructor validates
`d_model % num_heads` in its body, but the initializer list has already computed
`d_k(d_model / num_heads)`, so `CrossAttention(8, 0)` kills the process with SIGFPE instead of
throwing. A negative `num_heads` that divides `d_model` is accepted with a negative `d_k`.
`mns_server` rejects 0 at register time and `ConfigLoader::validate()` rejects values outside 1–64,
but `chatbot_api_server` doesn't run `validate()` at startup (TD-241), so a local `NUM_HEADS=0` with
no MNS crashes the process. `MultiHeadAttention` should be checked for the same pattern.

Action Items:

- [x] Validate `d_model > 0` and `num_heads > 0` before computing `d_k` (e.g. via a static helper in the initializer list).
- [x] Test: `num_heads` of 0 and negative values throw `std::invalid_argument`.

**Fix (November 13, 2026, with TD-467).** `d_k` is initialized from `checked_head_dim(d_model, num_heads)`, a file-local helper that
throws `std::invalid_argument` when either is zero or negative or `d_model % num_heads != 0`, so the check runs before the division.
`MultiHeadAttention` has the same helper. Test `CrossAttentionConstructionTest.NonPositiveShapesThrowInsteadOfCrashing` (0, negative,
not divisible); on the old code the test process died with SIGFPE.

Location in code: `src/CrossAttention.cpp` (constructor, `checked_head_dim()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/CrossAttention.cpp`
- `src/MultiHeadAttention.cpp`
- `tests/crossattention_test.cpp`

### TD-572: `LeJEPATrainingPass` and `TrainingPassFiles`: What Stands Between Them and `stable`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 12, 2026 | `src/LeJEPATrainingPass.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/TrainingPassFiles.{hpp,cpp}`, `tests/`, `scripts/sycl_gpu_tests/` | Direct tests of both (`trainingPassFilesTests`, 5 more `lejepaTrainingPassTests` cases), and the LeJEPA pass run on ai-machine's Arc B60 through the GPU test package; both promoted to `stable` 1.0.0 |

Description:
`LeJEPATrainingPass.{hpp,cpp}` (the LeJEPA world-model pass) and `TrainingPassFiles.{hpp,cpp}` (`resolve_pass_files()`/`cleanup_downloads()`, the
download step every pass shares) were moved out of `IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` on November 12, 2026 for TD-566, and moved from `experimental`
to `beta` the same day. Neither is ready for `stable`, for these reasons:

- **`TrainingPassFiles` has no direct test.** Only its local-file branch runs in a test, indirectly, through `lejepaTrainingPassTests`. The FTP
  branch (download into `DOWNLOAD_DIR` or `<SESSION_DIR>/downloads`, one range per claimed unit, false on a failed download) and
  `cleanup_downloads()` (each download and its TD-338 checksum sidecar, a path listed twice) are untested. `DataTransport` underneath has its own
  tests (`dataTransportFtpTests`, `dataTransportFtpsTests`).
- **`LeJEPATrainingPass`'s GPU-loss handling has run only against an injected check.** A real device loss can't be produced on demand. The check
  is the chatbot pass's `GPUManager::device_usable()`, which ai-machine's soak exercised, but the LeJEPA pass itself has not run on ai-machine's
  Arc B60 since the move. Its other paths (checkpoint and pause, an unreachable registry, nothing pending, metrics) are tested only by reading
  and the earlier real-binary checks, not by `lejepaTrainingPassTests`.

Action Items:

- [x] `TrainingPassFiles` tests against a loopback `FtpDataServer` (as `dataTransportFtpsTests` set one up): a claimed batch downloads and
  each range keeps its segment; an unset `DOWNLOAD_DIR` falls back to `<SESSION_DIR>/downloads`; a failed download returns false; the
  local-registry branch passes the registry's own paths; `cleanup_downloads()` removes files and sidecars and tolerates a repeated path.
- [x] `lejepaTrainingPassTests` cases for the paths it doesn't cover: nothing pending (3), a pause through the control state (checkpoint,
  release, 1), `/admin/checkpoint`, a resumed checkpoint, a failed checkpoint load before claiming.
- [x] A LeJEPA pass on ai-machine with the redeployed binaries (`--objective=lejepa`, under `trainer_service` or by hand), ideally across a
  soak so a real engine reset reaches the new check; record the result here.
  **Package ready (November 12, 2026):** `scripts/package_sycl_gpu_tests.sh` builds it; on ai-machine,
  `./prepare_host.sh` then `./run_gpu_tests.sh --lejepa-only` runs `--objective=lejepa` on the GPU through a lifecycle (train, resume
  with nothing pending, re-queue and resume from the checkpoint, a SIGTERM drain, resume after it) and a 20-pass soak on Level Zero
  v2 that checks any device loss against TD-566, written to `lejepa_report.txt`. Tried on the oneAPI CPU device: every check passes.
  **Result on ai-machine (November 12, 2026, `adai-gpu-results-ai-machine-20261112T211115Z`):** Arc Pro B60 over Level Zero v2, GuC
  70.72.1, oneAPI runtime 2026.2.0. The lifecycle passed on the GPU: a pass trained and checkpointed in 10 s, a resume found nothing
  pending (3), a re-queued file trained from the checkpoint, a SIGTERM checkpointed and released the texts (1), and a resume continued
  from that checkpoint. All 20 soak passes (5 epochs, 640 steps each, 318 s in all) trained with no skipped batch. The kernel log
  was readable but had no GPU events in the whole run, so no real device loss reached the pass's check: the loss branch is still covered
  only by `lejepaTrainingPassTests`' injected check and by the chatbot soaks, which exercised the same `GPUManager::device_usable()`
  probe.
  **Longer soak (November 12, 2026, `adai-gpu-results-ai-machine-20261112T212322Z`):** the lifecycle passed again, and 200 fresh passes
  (3,177 s of GPU work) all trained, with no skipped batch and no kernel GPU event in the whole run. The chatbot soaks on the same host
  and firmware lost the device about once every five passes, so this workload doesn't seem to provoke the engine resets at all (it
  multiplies through `Matrix::multiply_gpu()` and runs none of the chatbot pass's device-resident kernels). Soaking longer is unlikely
  to reach the loss branch.
- [x] Then promote `LeJEPATrainingPass` to `stable` 1.0.0. (`TrainingPassFiles` was promoted November 12, 2026, below.)

**Tests added (November 12, 2026):**

- `trainingPassFilesTests` (5, new): a plain-FTP `FtpDataServer` on kernel-chosen loopback ports. It covers the local-registry branch
  (registry paths and segment ranges, nothing downloaded); an FTP batch downloaded in order with its ranges, two segments of one file
  sharing one download; the `<SESSION_DIR>/downloads` fallback; a download with credentials the server never issued returning false; and
  `cleanup_downloads()` removing downloads and sidecars, with a repeated, a missing and an empty path, and leaving other files alone.
- `lejepaTrainingPassTests` (4 → 9) gains five cases:
  - a second pass resuming the first one's checkpoint and finding nothing pending (3);
  - a re-queued file training again from the checkpoint;
  - a checkpoint that can't be loaded failing the pass before anything is claimed;
  - a pause checkpointing and releasing the files;
  - a checkpoint request written at the next batch and marked served.

  The fixture now saves where the pass resumes from (`LeJEPAEncoder::default_checkpoint_dir(SESSION_DIR)`); it used another directory, so no
  case had actually resumed.
- **Breaking the code is caught.** Removing the segment copy, the downloads fallback, the sidecar removal, the paused checkpoint, the served
  mark or the failed-load return each fails a test.

**`TrainingPassFiles` promoted to `stable` 1.0.0 (November 12, 2026).** With these tests nothing stands in its way: the ai-machine run concerns
the LeJEPA pass only, and the code is unchanged from what every pass of the deployed `incremental_trainer` has run. 

**Closed (November 12, 2026, owner decision):** `LeJEPATrainingPass.{hpp,cpp}` promoted to `stable` 1.0.0 after the two ai-machine
runs. No real device loss reached the LeJEPA pass, and soaking longer is unlikely to produce one; its loss branch is covered by the
injected-check tests and by the `GPUManager::device_usable()` probe, which the chatbot soaks proved on every one of their device losses.

Location in code: `src/LeJEPATrainingPass.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/TrainingPassFiles.{hpp,cpp}`, `tests/lejepa_training_pass_test.cpp`,
`tests/training_pass_files_test.cpp`.

### TD-552: `dataset_manager` and the Android App Can't Replace an Uploaded File

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 12, 2026 | Data / Registry clients | Code fix (LOW, filed October 24, 2026) |

Description:
Filed with TD-492 at the owner's request. Since TD-492, `POST /registry/<group>[/<kind>]/upload?filename=<name>` refuses (409) to replace
a file that is already trained (`"trained"`) or queued (`"already_queued"`) unless `&overwrite=true` is given. With it, a trained file is
replaced and queued again, and an unclaimed whole-file queue entry is replaced with its metadata refreshed. A claimed or segmented file
is always refused.

Neither client can send `overwrite`:
- **`dataset_manager`:** `add` in remote mode uploads through `RemoteTransport::upload_file()`, which has no overwrite parameter. A
  re-add now fails with the server's reason, so a deliberate replacement needs `curl … ?overwrite=true`.
- **Android ops dashboard:** the Registry tab's upload (`RegistryRepository.upload()`, `RegistryApiService.upload()`) has no overwrite
  parameter and shows the 409 as an error.

Action Items:

- [x] `dataset_manager`: an `--overwrite` flag on the commands that upload (`add` in remote mode), passed through
  `RegistryTransport::upload_file()`. Report `replaced` vs `added`, and show the 409 reason (`claimed`, `segmented`) plainly when even
  overwrite is refused.
- [x] Android: an "Overwrite existing file" option in the upload dialog, sent as `overwrite=true`. Show the server's 409 reason, and gate
  the overwrite through the same `ConfirmActionDialog` as other destructive actions, with the HTTP-call preview showing `overwrite=true`.
- [x] Tests: a `dataset_manager` overwrite test against a live registry, and a repository/unit test for the Android query parameter.
- [x] Document the flag in the `dataset_manager` operator guide and the ops dashboard docs.

**Fix (November 12, 2026).** Two more client bugs turned up: a replacement answers `{"added":false,"replaced":true}`, which both
`RemoteTransport::upload_file()` and the Android view model took for a failure, and the Android app showed a 409 as its raw JSON body.
- **C++:** `RegistryTransport::upload_file(local_path, overwrite)` returns an `UploadResult` (path, `replaced`, and `refused`, the server's
  409 reason) and sends `&overwrite=true` when asked; `DatasetRegistry::remote_upload()` passes it through and doesn't queue a replaced
  file twice. `dataset_manager add [--overwrite] <file>` prints `Uploaded as …` or `Replaced the queued file …` and says plainly why the
  server refused (already trained or queued: use `--overwrite`; claimed: wait or release; segmented: delete the segments). In local mode
  `--overwrite` is an error. `parse_add_args()` also refuses unknown options (TD-322; `add --foo` used to queue a file named `--foo`) and
  takes `--` to end them.
- **Android:** the upload dialog's "Overwrite a file of this name that is already trained or queued" checkbox; the confirm step's title,
  effect and HTTP preview (`&overwrite=true`) say so. `RegistryRepository.upload(…, overwrite)` sends the parameter only when set and
  returns a 409's reason as data, and the screen words each outcome (`uploadOutcomeMessage()`).
- **Tests:** `registryFtpConfinementTests` runs the real `dataset_manager` against a real `registry_server`: queued (refused, then replaced
  with its entry refreshed to the new pair count), trained (refused, then queued again), claimed (refused even with `--overwrite`, the claim
  untouched), and local mode. Sending no overwrite, reading `added:false` as failure, or dropping the reason each fails it. Parser tests,
  `DatasetRegistryTests` for the pass-through, and Android `RegistryRepositoryTest`/`GroupDetailViewModelTest` cases.
- **Docs:** `dataset-manager-guide.md`'s `add` section (also out of date on formats and paths), `OPERATIONS_MANUAL.md`, and the
  `RegistryTransport`, `DatasetRegistry`, `DatasetManagerTool` and `DatasetManagerArgs` references. There is no ops dashboard document
  to update; the guide mentions the dashboard's option.

Location in code: `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp`, `src/DatasetManagerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/RegistryTransport.{hpp,cpp}`
(`upload_file()`); `android/opsdashboard/src/main/java/com/adai/ops/data/registry/RegistryRepository.kt`,
`android/opsdashboard/src/main/java/com/adai/ops/network/RegistryApiService.kt` and the Registry upload dialog.

### TD-465: SafeTensors Round Trip Replaces the Decoder Embedding

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 12, 2026 | Models / ModelSerializer | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `ModelSerializer` and verified. `LLMEncoder` and `LLMDecoder` each own a separately trained `TokenEmbedding`
(the decoder's is updated in `LLMDecoder::backward()`/`update_weights()`). `export_safetensors()` writes only the encoder's as
`model.shared.weight` ("encoder and decoder share the same token embedding" — they don't), and `import_safetensors()` copies it into
both. Probe: the original model's two embeddings differed by up to 0.85; after export → import into a fresh model the decoder
embedding equalled the encoder's and the logits for the same input differed by up to **1.05**. `FullModelRoundTrip` passes because it
compares only three weight matrices. (No production caller today, so no shipped artifact is affected.)

Action Items:

- [x] Export the decoder embedding as its own tensor (e.g. `decoder.embed_tokens.weight`) and import it when present.
- [x] Extend `FullModelRoundTrip` to compare both embeddings and the model's forward output.

**Fix (November 12, 2026).** `export_safetensors()` writes the encoder's embedding as `model.shared.weight` and the decoder's as
`model.decoder.embed_tokens.weight` (the name HuggingFace uses for an untied T5 decoder). `import_safetensors()` loads each into its
own embedding; a file written before the fix has only `model.shared.weight`, which still goes to both. Two new tests, both failing on
the old code: `RoundTripKeepsBothEmbeddingsAndOutputs` (both embeddings and the logits from `next_token_logits()` match after a round
trip) and `FileWithOnlySharedEmbeddingLoadsItIntoBoth` (an older file still loads). TD-466 is unchanged.

Location in code: `src/ModelSerializer.cpp` (`export_safetensors()`, `import_safetensors()` token-embedding blocks).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ModelSerializer.cpp`
- `tests/model_serializer_test.cpp`

### TD-349: RAG Indexes Whole Files but Embeds Only Their First `max_seq_length` Tokens

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 12, 2026 | RAG / DocumentStore | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [DocumentStore.md](../reference/source/DocumentStore.md) and confirmed by running the real class.
`chatbot_api_server` adds each top-level `.txt` file under `RAG_DOCS_PATH` as **one** `DocumentStore`
document (no chunking), and `LLMEncoder::encode()` truncates input to `max_seq_length` tokens before
embedding. A long document is therefore represented by its opening only. With `max_seq_length = 16`,
two documents sharing their first 16 tokens got **bit-identical embeddings** and tied on every query,
including one matching the tail of one of them exactly. At the default `MAX_SEQ_LENGTH = 512`,
content past roughly the first page of each file is unretrievable, yet the whole file text is what
`RAGInference` puts in the prompt.

Action Items:

- [x] Chunk documents at index time (e.g. overlapping windows within `max_seq_length` tokens), each chunk its own entry with a parent-document reference, and return chunks rather than whole files.
- [x] Test: content past the first window is retrievable.

**Fix (November 12, 2026).** Since TD-365, `encode()` keeps an over-long input's *last* `max_seq_length` tokens, so a long
document was represented by its ending rather than its opening; either way only one window of each file was embedded.
`DocumentStore::addDocument()` now compares `LLMEncoder::count_tokens()` (new: the untruncated token count) with the encoder's
`max_seq_length` and splits a longer document at whitespace into chunks that each fit: pieces of a whitespace run plus a word (the
tokenizer's pre-tokens don't cross them), filled to the window by their token counts and checked against the real count, the next chunk
starting about a quarter window back and sharing at least one piece. Each chunk is an entry `<id>#<n>` with `parent_id`, `chunk_index`,
`chunk_count` and the document's metadata; `removeDocument(id)` removes every chunk, and an id or chunk id can't be added twice. A document
that fits stays one entry under its own id. Retrieval returns chunks, and `RAGInference` puts their text in the prompt unchanged.
`chatbot_api_server` logs `Indexed N documents (M entries)`. Tests (`DocumentStoreChunkTest`, 6): chunks fit, overlap, start and end the
document; an opening outside the encoder's window is retrievable (two documents with the same long ending used to embed identically);
chunks still overlap when every word is longer than a quarter window; removal, duplicate ids, and a short document keeping its id; plus
`LLMEncoderTest.CountTokensIsTheUntruncatedEncodeLength`. Removing the chunking, either overlap rule, removal by parent or the parent
duplicate check each fails a test; the exact-fit check never changes a chunk with this tokenizer, so no test reaches it.

Location in code: `src/DocumentStore.cpp` (`addDocument()`, `chunkRanges()`), `src/LLMEncoder.cpp` (`count_tokens()`), `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp` (RAG indexing loop); tagged `TD-349`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DocumentStore.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`
- `src/RAGInference.cpp`
- `tests/documentstore_test.cpp`

### TD-571: Findings From the November 11, 2026 Trace of the Files TD-569 Touched

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 11, 2026 | Training / `trainer_service` / Config | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed November 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found while re-tracing the reference documents of every file TD-569 touched, for possible promotion to `stable`:

- **`reset` ignores a mistyped flag** (MEDIUM, verified). `parse_reset_command_args()` dropped every token but `--yes`/`--keep-data`, so
  `incremental_trainer reset --yes --keep-dat` reset everything and deleted the data registry without asking, exiting 0.
- **The LeJEPA pass records its files as trained before its final save** (MEDIUM, verified). With `WORLD_MODEL_ARTIFACT_PATH` under a
  read-only directory, the pass logged "Pass complete", recorded the file as trained, then failed on the save and exited 1 with no
  checkpoint: the training was lost while the queue said the data was done.
- **`trainer_service` hides its own status while a pass's admin API is down** (LOW, verified). The proxy added its fields
  (`seconds_since_pass_progress`, the pass counters) only to a 200, and a pass started its admin API only after GPU initialization and the
  model's construction. A pass stuck there showed a bare 503 until TD-569's stall limit stopped it.
- **The epoch that triggers early stopping skips the epoch callback** (LOW, by inspection). `ChatbotTrainer::train()` broke out before
  `record_epoch()` and the callback, so that epoch was missing from `IncrementalTrainer`'s session history, MNS progress and the admin API.
- Smaller (by inspection): the proxy escaped only five characters in its idle `PUT` error bodies (TD-453's class); a failed MNS model lookup at trainer
  start-up was swallowed by a `catch (...)`, so an unreachable MNS fell back to the local paths silently; the trainer's start-up `[MNS]`
  lines went to stdout, so a `trainer_service` pass's log file missed them; the reload diff showed `METRICS_DB_URL` (which can hold a
  database password), while `to_string()` hid it.

Action Items:

- [x] `reset` refuses any other argument.
- [x] Save the world model first; mark the files trained only after it is written, and release them when it fails.
- [x] Add the service's fields to every `/admin/status` answer; start the pass's admin API before GPU initialization.
- [x] Run early stopping's break after the epoch is recorded and reported.
- [x] The small items.

**Fix (November 11, 2026):**

- `ResetCommandArgs::error`: an unknown `reset` argument exits 1 before anything is reset (`UnrecognizedTokensAreAnError`).
- `run_lejepa_training_pass()` saves, then marks; a failed save is logged and the files are released (checked with the real binary: no
  trained record, the claim cleared).
- `with_supervisor_fields()` runs on every `/admin/status` answer that is a JSON object, 503/504 included
  (`StatusOfAnUnreachablePassStillCarriesTheServiceFields`). `run_training_pipeline()` no longer initializes the GPU; each pass builds its
  `PassAdminApi` first and then calls `init_gpu()`, before the model is built, so the per-pass admin API answers, and a SIGTERM drains,
  during GPU initialization.
- `ChatbotTrainer::train()` checks early stopping after the tracker and the epoch callback
  (`TheEpochThatTriggersEarlyStoppingReachesTheEpochCallback`).
- The proxy's idle `PUT` error bodies, the ones with variable text, are built with nlohmann/json; the MNS model lookup's failure is logged with its reason; the `[MNS]` lines go
  through `Logger::deferred()`, so they reach the pass's log file; `is_secret_key()` covers `METRICS_DB_URL`
  (`ReloadHidesTheMetricsDatabaseUrl`).

Each new test fails with its fix reverted. Versions: `IncrementalTrainerArgs` 0.17.0/0.18.0, `IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` 0.36.0,
`TrainerServiceProxy` 0.4.1/0.8.0, `ChatbotTrainer.cpp` 0.22.2, `Config.cpp` 1.31.1.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`, `src/TrainerServiceProxy.{hpp,cpp}`,
`src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp`, `src/Config.cpp`, `src/CMakeLists.txt`.

### TD-570: `BPETokenizer::load_vocab()` Takes Header Syntax Inside the Token and Merge Sections

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 11, 2026 | NLP / BPETokenizer | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed November 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found while re-tracing `BPETokenizer` (verified with a scratch program linked against the debug `adai_nlp`).
`read_vocab_file()` applied its header rules to every line of the file, whatever section it was in:

- a line starting with `#` was skipped as a comment;
- a line starting with `NORMALIZATION`, `WHITESPACE`, `TOKENIZER_MODE`, `VOCAB_SIZE` or `RESERVED_SPECIAL_IDS`, or equal to
  `SPECIAL_TOKENS`/`VOCAB`, or starting with `BPE_MERGES`, was read as that header line or section marker.

`save_vocab()` escapes neither `#` nor letters, so a vocabulary that contains such a token doesn't load back as it was saved:

- **`#` tokens vanish.** Built from `## Heading`, `#include` and `#tag`, a 60-token vocabulary loaded back as 58: the `#` and `##` tokens and
  the `#`+`#` merge were skipped. `"## Heading #include #tag"` encoded to 7 ids instead of 6 and decoded as `" Heading #include #tag"`.
- **A keyword token breaks the load.** A cased vocabulary built from `WHITESPACE` lines has the token `WHITESPACE` at id 40, and
  `load_vocab()` threw `Unknown WHITESPACE '40'`, so a checkpoint carrying it can't be loaded. A token starting `TOKENIZER_MODE` would have
  switched the mode mid-file; one starting `BPE_MERGES` would have ended the vocabulary early.

The first training pass loads the vocabulary it has just built back from the file (`IncrementalTrainer::build_model()`), as every later
pass and every server do. So markdown, code and hashtags in training data never reached the model as their real tokens, and a vocabulary
with a keyword token would have failed every pass. Vocabulary files are written correctly; only reading was wrong.

Action Items:

- [x] Apply the header rules only before the first section; read every line inside `VOCAB` and `BPE_MERGES` literally.
- [x] Round-trip tests with `#` tokens and every header keyword as a token.

**Fix (November 11, 2026):** section markers carry no tab and every `VOCAB`/`BPE_MERGES` entry does (a tab inside a token is written as
`\t`), so a line with a tab is always an entry; a tabless `SPECIAL_TOKENS`, `VOCAB` or `BPE_MERGES…` line changes the section; and the
format comment, `#` comments, header keywords and the unknown-header-line error (TD-563) apply only before the first section. The constructor's
doc comment, which still called ASCII the default, now says Unicode (TD-564). Tests: `TokensStartingWithAHashSurviveSaveAndLoad`,
`TokensStartingWithAHeaderKeywordSurviveSaveAndLoad` (all eight keywords), `HeaderCommentsAndUnknownHeaderLinesAreStillHandled`; the first two
fail with the old reader. `BPETokenizer.cpp` 2.0.2, `.hpp` 2.0.1.

**Effect on existing models:** a vocabulary file with `#` tokens now loads them, so text with `#` encodes to ids the model never trained on
(they used to be `<unk>` or other splits). Those checkpoints should be retrained, which TD-358 and TD-563 already plan. No vocabulary with a
keyword token can have been in use, since it couldn't load.

Location in code: `src/BPETokenizer.cpp` (`read_vocab_file()`).

### TD-569: `trainer_service` Has No Time Limit for a Pass That Stops Making Progress

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 11, 2026 | Training / `trainer_service` | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed November 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found in the second ai-machine soak (November 11, 2026; see TD-566's on-device results). In pass `soak_l0v1_10` (the v1 Level
Zero adapter, `SYCL_UR_USE_LEVEL_ZERO_V2=0`) the kernel logged `GT0: Engine reset: engine_class=ccs` 0.7 s after a checkpoint
save. The pass then wrote nothing more and didn't exit, and the test script killed it at its 15-minute limit. The November 10
soak had two such hangs on v1, one after an engine reset.

TD-566 stops a pass when a sample fails and the device check finds the GPU unusable. A pass whose GPU call never returns has no
failed sample, so that check never runs. `trainer_service` waits for each child with no limit: its loop calls
`ChildProcess::poll_exit()` every 200 ms and ends a pass early only on a stop request (`stop_and_wait()`). A hung pass therefore
stalls the always-on service. Nothing more trains, its claimed files stay claimed until their lease runs out, and `/admin/status`
shows `training` with a stale epoch. The only way out is `systemctl restart`. `Restart=always` doesn't help, because the
service hasn't exited. No pass on the default v2 adapter has hung in 40 passes across both soaks. But the driver is the cause,
and a later driver or runtime update could change that.

A fixed wall-clock limit doesn't fit, because a legitimate pass over a large queue runs for hours. What's missing is a check
for progress.

Action Items:

- [x] The child reports progress from the thread that does the work: each optimizer step, each validation sample, each file
  downloaded or tokenized, and each checkpoint written. A heartbeat file in a directory `trainer_service` passes to the child
  works whether or not the admin API is on (the child's admin port exists only when it is). A separate timer thread would keep
  beating while the training thread is stuck, so it must not be used.
- [x] `trainer_service` stops a child whose heartbeat is older than a new `TRAINER_PASS_STALL_MINUTES` setting (default
  around 15, 0 = off). It uses the existing `stop_and_wait()`, which sends SIGTERM and kills the child after 25 s, and logs
  the pass as stalled.
- [x] Count stalled passes as failures for TD-523's backoff, and report `total_passes_stalled` in `/admin/status` beside
  `total_passes_crashed`/`total_passes_failed`.
- [x] The killed pass can't release its claims. Check that the next pass reclaims them by `run_id` (TD-406/TD-415), or that
  they expire under the claim lease (TD-494).
- [x] Tests: a stub child that stops beating is stopped and counted, and one that keeps beating through a long pass isn't.
  Never signal anything but the recorded child pid.
- [x] Update `TrainerServiceMain.md`, `ChildProcess.md` if it changes, the admin-API table in CLAUDE.md, and
  `scripts/adai-trainer.service`'s comments.

**Fix (November 11, 2026):**

- **Progress from the working code.** A process-wide counter, `adai::note_pass_progress()` (`src/PassHeartbeat.{hpp,cpp}`, in
  `adai_core`), is bumped by the working code:
  - each training and validation sample, each tokenized pair and each quality-backfill pair (`ChatbotTrainer`);
  - each line of a dataset file (`DatasetRegistry::load_conversation_pairs()`) and each FTP download chunk (`DataTransport.hpp`);
  - each BPE merge, each LeJEPA batch, and each checkpoint attempt (`IncrementalTrainer::perform_auto_save()`).

  The per-epoch quality thread doesn't bump it, so it can't hide a stuck training thread.
- **The heartbeat file.** `incremental_trainer --heartbeat-file <path>` (needs `--foreground`) starts a `PassHeartbeatWriter`
  right after parsing its arguments, so a hang in GPU initialization counts too. It writes `"<pid> <count>"` through a rename
  every 2 s while the count changes, and removes the file at exit.
- **The supervisor.** The wait for a pass moved to `wait_for_pass()` (`src/PassSupervision.{hpp,cpp}`). It reads the file
  every 2 s, and `PassStallWatch` times the unchanged count on `trainer_service`'s own steady clock, ignoring a file with
  another pid.
  - At `TRAINER_PASS_STALL_MINUTES` (new, default 30 rather than 15 so a slow stretch is never mistaken for a stall; 0–10080,
    0 = off) it logs an error and calls `stop_and_wait()`.
  - The pass is counted in the new `total_passes_stalled` and in `consecutive_failures`, and backs off like a failure. It isn't
    also counted as crashed or failed.
  - `/admin/status` also reports `seconds_since_pass_progress`. The file is `<SESSION_DIR>/trainer_service_pass_<pool>.heartbeat`, `<pool>`
    the pass's dataset pool. (Amended the same day: it first had one fixed name, so a chatbot and a LeJEPA service sharing `SESSION_DIR` would
    have overwritten each other's file and each stopped the other's healthy pass as stalled. The `trainer_service` smoke test checks the name.)
- **Claims.** A killed pass's claims are taken back by the next pass, which uses the same run id (MNS's current run, or the
  persistent `chatbot_run_id`/`lejepa_run_id`), or they expire under the claim lease.
- **Tests:** `passHeartbeatTests` (16) drives `wait_for_pass()` with real `/bin/sh` children:
  - a pass that stops beating is stopped with SIGTERM (exit 143);
  - one that keeps beating past the limit exits 0;
  - one that ignores SIGTERM is killed;
  - an earlier pass's file doesn't keep a silent one alive;
  - a stop request ends the wait;
  - without a file there is no check.

  Removing the stall check, or the pid check, makes them fail. Also new: the flag and pass-command cases in
  `incrementalTrainerArgsTests`, the setting in `configTests`, and the status fields in `trainerServiceProxyTests`.

Location in code: `src/PassHeartbeat.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/PassSupervision.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/TrainerServiceMain.cpp`,
`src/TrainerServiceControlState.hpp`, `src/TrainerServiceProxy.cpp`, `src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`,
`src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`, `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}`, and the progress calls in `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp`,
`src/DatasetRegistry.cpp`, `src/DataTransport.hpp`, `src/BPETokenizer.cpp`, `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`.

### TD-568: MNS Manager GUI Argument Handling, Keyboard Selection and a Stale Highlight

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 11, 2026 | Client / GUI | Code fix (LOW, filed November 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found while reviewing `mns_manager_gui` for promotion to `stable`, after TD-452/TD-455 (all verified):

- **Arguments.** `MnsManagerGUI_main.cpp` (tagged `stable`) built `QApplication` before reading its arguments, so
  `mns_manager_gui --help` aborted with a core dump on a host with no display instead of printing the usage
  (`chatbot_gui` had the same bug, fixed under TD-266). `--url` or `--config` with no value was ignored, and an unknown
  argument (`--urll http://h:8083`) too: the window opened on the configured or default server.
- **Keyboard selection.** The models and roles tables loaded a record only on `cellClicked`, so moving the selection with
  the arrow keys highlighted a model without loading it, while the actions kept acting on the previously clicked one.
- **Stale highlight.** Refilling the models table (Refresh, or after any action) left the current row where it was, so it
  highlighted whichever model now sat in that row while the actions and the detail view belonged to the selected one.
- **Stylesheet.** It still styled `QSpinBox`, which the Register tab no longer uses since TD-455.

The same review found two bugs in the then-uncommitted TD-452/TD-455 change, fixed in that change rather than here: the
Server field started empty (the toolbar was built before the URL was stored), and a typed role filter was reset to `(all)`
whenever the role list was refilled (`GET /roles` lists only roles with a production model), leaving the table filtered.

Action Items:

- [x] Read the arguments before `QApplication`; a value flag with no value and an unknown argument print the usage and
  exit 1.
- [x] Load the record when the current row changes, by mouse or keyboard; refilling a table doesn't select a row, and the
  models table keeps the selected model highlighted (or none).
- [x] Refresh also reloads the selected record, since selecting its row again no longer does.
- [x] Remove the `QSpinBox` rule.

**Fix (November 11, 2026):** `main()` checks for `--help`/`-h` anywhere and parses `--url`/`--config` before creating
`QApplication`, with `Missing value for <flag>` and `Unknown argument: <arg>` errors (exit 1). Both tables load on
`currentCellChanged` when the row changes; `populateModelsTable()`/`populateRolesTable()` refill under a `QSignalBlocker`, the
models table re-highlights the selected model's row (or clears the highlight), the roles table clears it. Refresh fetches the
selected record with the lists. Four new smoke checks (the old binary failed all nine of their assertions: `--help` with no
display, missing values, an unknown argument) and three new `mnsManagerGuiWidgetTests` cases (keyboard selection, the
highlight and record after a refresh, no load on refill); breaking each change was caught. `MnsManagerGUI_main.cpp` 1.1.0,
`MnsManagerGUI.cpp` 0.11.0, `.hpp` 0.9.1.

Location in code: `src/MnsManagerGUI_main.cpp`, `src/MnsManagerGUI.cpp` (`createModelsTab()`, `createRolesTab()`,
`createToolbar()`, `populateModelsTable()`, `populateRolesTable()`, `applyStylesheet()`).

Files Modified:

- `src/MnsManagerGUI.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/mns_manager_gui_widget_test.cpp`
- `tests/smoke/mns_manager_gui_main_test.sh`

### TD-037: No Qt Test Infrastructure for GUI Classes

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 10, 2026 | `src/ChatbotGUI.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/MnsManagerGUI.{hpp,cpp}`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `tests/` | Qt Test adopted: widget suites for both GUIs (`chatbotGuiWidgetTests`, `mnsManagerGuiWidgetTests`), run offscreen by `ctest` |

Description:
`ChatbotGUI.{cpp,hpp}` and `MnsManagerGUI.{cpp,hpp}` have no automated coverage, and this repo
has no QTest (or any Qt-aware test) infrastructure at all — every other test in `tests/` is a
plain GTest with no Qt event loop. Real widget behavior is hard to test without one; the more
tractable near-term step is separating non-widget logic (state transitions, signal/slot wiring
decisions, data formatting) out of the widget classes into plain C++ that GTest can already
exercise, deferring full widget testing until QTest is actually adopted.

**Update (September 13, 2026):** picked the logic-extraction path over adopting QTest — this
entry's own Description already called that out as the more tractable near-term step, so this
wasn't treated as an open question needing a separate decision. Also found and closed a real gap
along the way: `MnsJsonHelpers.hpp` (used by `MnsManagerGUI` for JSON parsing/formatting and URL
parsing) was *already* plain, Qt-free, GTest-exercisable code — including two real bug fixes in
its own history (TD-068, TD-102) — yet had zero tests of its own despite being tagged `stable`.

- Added `tests/mnsjsonhelpers_test.cpp` (37 tests, `MnsJsonHelpersTests` in `ctest`): full coverage
  of `find_string_end`, `json_value`, `json_array_objects` (including the TD-068 brace-desync
  regression), `json_escape`, `json_pretty` (including the TD-102 escaped-backslash regression),
  and `ParsedUrl::from`.
- Extracted two more pieces of real logic that were previously inline in `MnsManagerGUI`'s slots,
  into new functions in `MnsJsonHelpers.hpp`, each with its own tests: `parse_tags()` (the
  "Register" tab's comma-separated `key=value` tags field, extracted verbatim from
  `onRegisterModel()`) and `build_register_model_body()`/`build_set_candidate_body()` (the
  `POST /models` and `PUT /models/{name}/state` request bodies `onRegisterModel()`/
  `onSetCandidate()` used to build inline). Verified via revert-confirm-fail: temporarily broke
  the tags-joining comma logic and confirmed the new test caught it before restoring.
- Extracted `ChatbotGUI::onStrategyChanged()`'s combo-box-index-to-strategy-name switch statement
  into a new `src/ChatbotGuiLogic.hpp` (`generation_strategy_for_index()`), with its own
  `tests/chatbotguilogic_test.cpp` (2 tests, `ChatbotGuiLogicTests` in `ctest`) covering every
  combo box index plus the out-of-range fallback.
- Confirmed both `chatbot_gui`/`mns_manager_gui` binaries still build and link cleanly against the
  refactored call sites.
- `MnsJsonHelpers.hpp` bumped 1.0.1 → 1.1.0 (stays `stable`); `ChatbotGuiLogic.hpp` is a new file,
  tagged `beta` from the start (100% branch coverage). `ChatbotGUI.cpp`/`MnsManagerGUI.cpp` stay
  `beta` (still capped — the widgets themselves remain untested) but their status comments now
  note what's covered.

Action Items:

- [x] Decide whether to adopt QTest (`Qt::Test` component, `QTEST_MAIN`) as a second test
  framework alongside GTest, or to keep pushing logic out of the widget classes instead — the
  latter, per this entry's own Description.
- [x] Extract testable non-widget logic from `ChatbotGUI`/`MnsManagerGUI` into plain classes — done
  for the highest-value pieces (see the Update above): URL/JSON parsing, the tags mini-parser, two
  request-body builders, and the strategy-index mapping. `onSetTraining`/`onPromote`/`onRetire`/
  `onDelete`'s own request bodies are one-or-zero-field string literals with no real logic worth
  extracting on their own.
- [x] Add tests for the extracted logic — done (39 new tests total across two new test files).
- [x] Full widget-level testing (button clicks, layout, signal/slot wiring under a real Qt event
  loop) — done November 10, 2026 with Qt Test (see the Resolution below).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChatbotGUI.cpp` / `src/ChatbotGUI.hpp` — done (see Update above); the widgets themselves
  (button clicks, layout) remain untested.
- `src/MnsManagerGUI.cpp` / `src/MnsManagerGUI.hpp` — done (see Update above); same widget-level
  caveat.
- `src/MnsJsonHelpers.hpp` — done (tested, gained `parse_tags`/`build_register_model_body`/
  `build_set_candidate_body`).
- `src/ChatbotGuiLogic.hpp` — new file, done.
- `tests/CMakeLists.txt` — done (`mnsjsonhelpersTests`, `chatbotguilogicTests` registered); no
  QTest integration needed, per the Decision above.

**Resolution (November 10, 2026): Qt Test adopted for the widgets.** Owner request: adopt QTest and test the widgets
themselves, closing this item.

- **Build.** The top-level `CMakeLists.txt` finds Qt's `Test` component beside `Widgets` (`ADAI_QT_TEST_FOUND`); it
  ships in the same `qtbase5-dev`/`qt6-base-dev` package, and the GUIs don't depend on it. `tests/CMakeLists.txt` builds
  `chatbotGuiWidgetTests` and `mnsManagerGuiWidgetTests` (`QTEST_MAIN`, AUTOMOC, the real `ChatbotGUI.cpp`/
  `MnsManagerGUI.cpp`) whenever their GUI binary is built, and `ctest` runs them with `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`, so no
  display is needed. CI's Linux job now installs `qtbase5-dev`, so the GUIs and both suites build and run there too.
- **Harness** (`tests/qt_widget_test_support.hpp`). Each test builds the real window against an in-process

- **`chatbotGuiWidgetTests` (18 tests):** connection notices (connected, unreachable, untrained model, invalid URL
