### TD-566: Training Keeps Going After the GPU Is Lost, and Reports an Epoch That Trained Nothing as Loss 0

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 10, 2026 | Training / ChatbotTrainer | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed November 10, 2026) |

Description:
Found in the SYCL GPU test run on ai-machine (package `adai-sycl-gpu-tests-bf3501cb-20261109`, November 10, 2026). In the
`SEED=8` training pass the kernel logged `xe 0000:2d:00.0: [drm] GT0: Engine reset: engine_class=ccs` with a device coredump at
11:03:44, and at 11:03:45 sample 6 of epoch 2 failed with `UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`. It's the same Arc B60 `xe` driver
instability as the host's earlier incidents, not a fault in this code: the same 18 samples had run in epoch 1, and the two `SEED=7`
passes and every test binary passed. What the trainer did next was the problem:

- **It kept going.** Every later GPU call failed with `UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY`, and the trainer tried each remaining
  sample of epoch 2, validation, every sample of epoch 3 and validation again, about 20 seconds of failures (longer for a real
  dataset) before `train()` failed. `ChatbotTrainer` treats a failed sample as that sample's problem (TD-267, TD-272), which is
  right for a bad sample and wrong for a lost device.
- **It reported an epoch that trained nothing as loss 0.** Epoch 3 had 0 updates and logged `Loss: 0.000000 - Perplexity:
  1.000000`. `train_epoch()` divides by the update count only when it's above zero, else records 0; the epoch callback and the
  metrics reporter pass that on, so the dashboards and MNS progress would show a perfect epoch.
- **It tried to copy the device weights back** after the failure, which can only fail on a lost device.

The pass did end as a failure and released its file, so nothing was marked trained; under `trainer_service` a new process would
have started (TD-172). The fix makes that happen at once.

Action Items:

- [x] `GPUManager::device_usable()` (SYCL and CUDA; the no-GPU stub returns false): one small allocation outside the pool, a fill,
      a copy back and a wait. A lost or reset device fails it.
- [x] `ChatbotTrainer` runs it after any training or validation sample fails; if the device is unusable, the pass stops with
      `GPUDeviceLostError` and `train()` returns false without copying the device weights back. A sample that fails on a working
      device is handled as before.
- [x] An epoch in which no training sample produced an update throws `EpochTrainedNothingError` (unless the epoch was aborted), so
      nothing records or reports a loss for it and the pass fails.
- [x] Tests.

Fix (November 10, 2026): as above. The check is a `std::function` member, `device_usable_`, set in GPU builds and replaced by
tests. Tests: `ChatbotTrainerCacheTest.LostDeviceStopsTheEpochAtTheFirstFailedSample` (two failing samples, one device check),
`LostDeviceStopsValidation`, `EpochThatTrainsNothingFailsInsteadOfReportingZero`, and
`GPUManagerTest.DeviceUsableOnlyOnAnInitializedWorkingDevice`. With the fix's checks removed, the three trainer tests fail. All
four pass in the debug build and on the oneAPI CPU device (`build/sycl-cpudev`), where the probe reports the working device as
usable. A real device loss can't be produced on demand; the next ai-machine run will show it.

On-device result (November 10, 2026): verified on ai-machine's Arc Pro B60 (package `adai-sycl-gpu-tests-4cae6a4f-dirty-20261110`,
oneAPI runtime 2026.2.0, run 21:58 UTC). In a soak of 40 back-to-back 10-epoch passes, 5 of the 20 passes on the default Level
Zero v2 adapter lost the device after a `GT0: Engine reset: engine_class=ccs`, at random points (epochs 1 to 9). Each pass stopped
at its first failed sample, within 0.5 s, logged "Not copying the device weights back", and reported no loss-0 epoch; one of the
five surfaced as `UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES` instead of `DEVICE_LOST` and was caught by the same device check. After every
loss the device ran work again in the next process. With `SYCL_UR_USE_LEVEL_ZERO_V2=0` (the v1 adapter) no pass lost the device,
but 2 of 20 hung until killed at the 15-minute limit, one of them after an engine reset; a hang is worse for the always-on service
than a fast failure, so the default v2 adapter stays.

Second on-device result (November 11, 2026): the same package and soak, run after `scripts/sycl_gpu_tests/guc_firmware.sh install`
put GuC 70.72.1 in place of Ubuntu's 70.44.1 (the driver asks for 70.49.4; `guc_info` confirmed 70.72.1 loaded). Engine resets
didn't become rarer: 8 in 40 passes, against about 7 before. On v2, 5 of 20 passes lost the device again (epochs 1 to 9). On v1,
2 of 20 lost it and 1 hung until killed at the 15-minute limit, 0.7 s after an engine reset. TD-566's check stopped all 7
losses: 0.5 s after the failed sample for `DEVICE_LOST`, under 1 ms for `OUT_OF_RESOURCES` (4 of the 7). None copied weights
back or recorded a loss-0 epoch, and the device ran work in the next process every time. The firmware isn't the cause and v2
stays the default. Across both runs, no pass on v2 hung; a pass that hangs isn't caught by this check, since no sample fails
(TD-569).

**The LeJEPA pass (November 12, 2026).** It has its own training loop and didn't use this check: it caught each failed batch, logged
"Skipping batch" and went on, so after a device loss every later batch failed the same way and the pass then "completed" on the batches
before it, saving and recording its files as trained. Each of those quick failures also counted as progress for TD-569's stall check.
The pass moved to `src/LeJEPATrainingPass.{hpp,cpp}` (with the shared download step, `src/TrainingPassFiles.{hpp,cpp}`) so it can be
tested, and now does what the chatbot pass does: after a failed batch it checks the device (`GPUManager::device_usable()` when a GPU is in
use), and a lost one stops the pass at once with no checkpoint and its files released (exit 1); a batch that fails on a working device is
still skipped; an epoch in which no batch trained fails the pass. `LeJEPAPassHooks` lets tests answer the device check and fail a batch.
Tests: `lejepaTrainingPassTests` (a whole pass against a local registry and a tiny world model, a failed batch on a working GPU, a lost
GPU, an epoch that trains nothing); the last two fail with their check removed. Compiled in the SYCL build too (`build/sycl-cpudev`).

Location in code (the LeJEPA part): `src/LeJEPATrainingPass.cpp` (`run_lejepa_training_pass()`).

Location in code: `src/ChatbotTrainer.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/gpu/GPUUtils.hpp`, `src/gpu/sycl/GPUUtils_SYCL.hpp`.

### TD-533: `sample_to_jsonl()` Writes Raw Control Characters; Unused Sample Metadata

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 10, 2026 | Data / JSONL Format | Code fix (LOW, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainingSampleMeta.hpp`:
- **Verified:** `sample_to_jsonl()` escapes only `"`, `\`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`; `\x01`/`\x08` are written raw, and Python's `json.loads` rejected the line
  ("Invalid control character"), so registry-produced JSONL (Gutenberg/HuggingFace via DataFetcher) can be unreadable by other tools.
- **By inspection:** `weight` and `split` look like sampling/split controls but nothing reads them (`quality` only goes to private copies, TD-273);
  numbers use locale-dependent `stof`/`stoi` (trailing garbage accepted) and default 6-digit output; a NaN `quality` is written as `nan`.

Action Items:

- [x] Escape every control character (`\u00XX`) and non-finite numbers; drop or implement `weight`/`split`.

**Fix (November 10, 2026):** owner's choice to drop `weight`/`split`.
- `json_esc()` escapes every character below 0x20: `\b`, `\f`, `\n`, `\r` and `\t` in short form, the rest as `\u00XX`.
- `quality` is written with `std::to_chars` (the shortest text that reads back as the same float, whatever the locale), and only when finite, so
  `inf` is never written (NaN already failed the `>= 0` check).
- The reader parses numbers with `std::from_chars`: the whole token must be a number (`0.5x`, `42abc`, `4.5` as a count, or an overflowing `1e400`
  keep the default), independent of the locale. Raw control characters inside strings are still read, so files written before the fix load.
- `SampleMeta::split` and `SampleMeta::weight` are removed; nothing set or read them. A line that still has them loads and they are ignored.

Verified: a line with `\x07`, `\x08`, `\x01`, `\x0c` and `quality` 0.123456789 is now accepted by Python's `json` with the exact text and
`0.12345679`, and an infinite quality is left out; the old header's output was rejected on both lines ("Invalid control character", and `inf`).
Four new tests (control characters checked with nlohmann/json, exact and finite quality, malformed numbers, the removed fields ignored) all
failed on the old header.

Location in code: `src/TrainingSampleMeta.hpp` (`tsm_detail::json_esc()`, `format_float()`, `member_flt()`/`member_inum()`,
`sample_to_jsonl()`, `SampleMeta`).

Files Modified:

- `src/TrainingSampleMeta.hpp`
- `tests/training_sample_meta_test.cpp`, `tests/DatasetRegistryTests.cpp`, `tests/chatbottrainer_test.cpp`

### TD-455: MNS Manager GUI Error Detection, UI-Thread HTTP and Register Defaults

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 10, 2026 | MNS / Manager GUI | Code fix (LOW, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MnsManagerGUI`, by inspection:
- **Error detection.** Every action treats an empty body as "Connection failed" and a body containing the text `"error"` as
  failure; the `http*()` helpers return only the body, so the HTTP status is never consulted. A non-2xx reply without that
  key reads as success; a successful reply containing that text (a tag or label) reads as failure.
- **UI-thread HTTP.** Every request is a synchronous `httplib` call (connect 5 s, read 10 s) on the UI thread, so a slow or
  unreachable server freezes the window on every selection or filter change (same class as TD-263).
- **Register defaults.** The spin boxes start at d_model 128, 4 heads, d_ff 512, 6/6 layers, max sequence 1024, matching
  neither `config.mns.conf` (512/8) nor `config.trainer.conf` (768/12), for an immutable architecture; the layer minimum of 1
  prevents standalone encoder/decoder records (plus TD-452's missing fields).
- **Minor.** The role filter is never populated from `/roles`; typed filter values aren't URL-encoded; `#ifndef` guard;
  four duplicated `http*()` helpers.

Action Items:

- [x] Return status and body from the HTTP helpers and judge success by status.
- [x] Run requests off the UI thread (`QtConcurrent`/`QNetworkAccessManager`).
- [x] Load Register defaults from a chosen config (or leave them blank and required); allow 0 layers per kind.
- [x] Populate the role filter from `/roles`; URL-encode filter values.

**Fix (November 10, 2026, with TD-452):** one `http()` helper returns `{reached, status, body, error}`, and success is a
2xx status; a failure shows the server's `error` and the status in a dialog (`… (HTTP 409)`, or `HTTP 500: <body>`
without an `error` field), or "Connection failed (<reason>)". Requests run on a worker thread, one at a time, with the
`ChatbotGUI` pattern (`runRequest()`/`setBusy()`, the result posted back to the GUI thread); the tabs, panels, URL field,
Connect and Refresh are disabled meanwhile and the status line shows what runs. The destructor stops the request in
flight (`httplib::Client::stop()`) and joins the worker. The Register tab's architecture starts blank and required, with
**Load from config...** (`ConfigLoader::load()`, as `mns_cli register --from-config`); standalone kinds take one layer
count. The role filter is filled from `/roles` (keeping the current choice, a typed one too, since `/roles` lists only roles with a production model), and model names, filters and the promote role
are URL-encoded (`adai::url_encode()`). `#pragma once`, one HTTP helper. `MnsManagerGUI.cpp` 0.10.0, `.hpp` 0.9.0.
Widget tests for each behaviour; breaking it was caught: success judged by the text `"error"` (two tests), unencoded names,
an empty role filter, and requests run on the GUI thread (the click then took the 10 s read timeout). Verified the same day: the helper tests' nine new cases (unescaping, spacing, object values, nearest-first keys, no
array fallback, a top-level array by empty key, control-character escaping, one-line empty containers, field order,
text that isn't JSON) each fail on the old header; `mnsManagerGuiWidgetTests` (31) passes, and the register, training and
candidate requests the real window builds were accepted by a real `mns_server` (encoder, decoder, world model with its
SIGReg settings, linked chatbot, `run-01`, candidate; a duplicate name showed `model_name already registered (HTTP 409)`).

Location in code: `src/MnsManagerGUI.{hpp,cpp}`.

Files Modified:

- `src/MnsManagerGUI.{hpp,cpp}`, `tests/mns_manager_gui_widget_test.cpp`

### TD-454: MNS Manager GUI's Training → Candidate Workflow Fails Against Server-Allocated Run IDs

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 10, 2026 | MNS / Manager GUI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MnsManagerGUI` and verified by sending the GUI's exact request bodies to a real `mns_server`.
`onSetTraining()` requires a typed run ID and sends `{"state":"training","run_id":"…"}`. Since run IDs became
server-allocated (CLAUDE.md, "MNS/registry-authoritative run and session numbering"), the server ignores a client
`run_id` for this transition, allocates `run-NN`, and reads `new_run` to decide whether to start a fresh run:

```text
Set Training,  run ID "my-run"   → state training, run_id "run-01"
Set Candidate, run ID "my-run"   → 409 "run_id does not match the active run; this trainer's run has been superseded"
Set Training,  run ID "my-run-2" → run_id still "run-01" (the GUI never sends new_run)
```

So the typed run ID is silently discarded, Set Candidate fails with a misleading "superseded" error unless the user copies
the allocated `run-NN` out of the detail panel, and the GUI can't start a new run. `docs/operations/guides/mns-manager-gui-guide.md`'s
walkthrough (enter `run-42`, Set Training, Set Candidate) follows exactly this path, and its `mns_cli` table shows
`set-training <name> <run-id>`, a form `mns_cli` no longer has.

Action Items:

- [x] Set Training: drop the run-ID requirement, add a "start a new run" checkbox (`new_run`), and show the allocated `run_id` from the reply.
- [x] Set Candidate: default the run ID to the selected record's `run_id`.
- [x] Correct the GUI guide's field table, walkthrough and `mns_cli` equivalence table.

**Fix (November 10, 2026):** Set Training sends `mns_gui::build_set_training_body(new_run)` (`MnsJsonHelpers.hpp`):
no run ID, plus `"new_run":true` when the new **Start a new run** checkbox is ticked. The status line shows the
allocated `run-NN`, which also fills Set Candidate's **Run ID** field (moved to the Set Candidate row). Selecting a
model fills that field from the record's `run_id`. Verified against a real `mns_server` with the GUI's own bodies
in its order (`MnsManagerGUILiveTest.GuiTrainingWorkflow_UsesTheAllocatedRunId`): training → `run-01`, candidate
with the record's run ID → 200, training with a new run → `run-02`, and without → still `run-02`. With the old body
the new-run step stayed at `run-01`, and the two new `BuildSetTrainingBodyTest` tests failed. The widget wiring itself
is covered by `mnsManagerGuiWidgetTests` since TD-037 closed (November 10, 2026).

Location in code: `src/MnsManagerGUI.cpp` (`setupDetailPanel()`'s action rows, `onSetTraining()`, `onModelSelected()`),
`src/MnsJsonHelpers.hpp` (`build_set_training_body()`).

Files Modified:

- `src/MnsManagerGUI.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/MnsJsonHelpers.hpp`
- `tests/mnsjsonhelpers_test.cpp`, `tests/mns_manager_gui_test.cpp`
- `docs/operations/guides/mns-manager-gui-guide.md`

### TD-452: `MnsJsonHelpers` Parsing Gaps and a GUI Register Body Without TD-196 Fields

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 10, 2026 | MNS / Manager GUI | Code fix (LOW, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MnsJsonHelpers` (used only by the optional Qt `mns_manager_gui`):
- **Verified.** `json_value()` doesn't unescape string values (`C:\\models\\v3.bin`, `caf\u00e9 \"x\"` displayed as-is);
  it matches only `"key":` with no space (`"state" : "training"` → empty) and returns a fragment for object values;
  `json_array_objects()` falls back to the first other array when the key is absent (e.g. an error body);
  `json_escape()` escapes only `"`, `\` and `\n`, so tabs, carriage returns and other control characters produce
  invalid JSON; `json_pretty()` renders `{}`/`[]` as three-line blocks.
- **By inspection.** `build_register_model_body()` has no `kind`, `run_group` or `connection`, so the GUI can register
  only legacy bundled `chatbot` records, not encoders, decoders, world models or linked pairs (TD-196), and can't set a
  run group. `ParsedUrl` accepts `https://` with port 8083 (as TD-451).

Action Items:

- [x] Unescape string values; return `nullopt` for a missing array key; complete `json_escape()` (or adopt TD-453's shared library).
- [x] Add kind, run group and encoder/decoder/world-model fields to the GUI's Register tab and body.

**Fix (November 10, 2026, with TD-455):** `MnsJsonHelpers.hpp` (2.0.0) parses with the vendored nlohmann/json, as an
`ordered_json` so the detail view keeps the server's field order: `json_value()` unescapes and returns the key nearest the
top (a record's own `run_id` over its history's), any spacing works, object values come back whole; `json_array_objects()`
is empty for a missing key (an empty key reads a top-level array); `json_escape()` escapes every control character;
`json_pretty()` keeps `{}`/`[]` on one line; text that isn't JSON gives empty results. `find_string_end()`,
`build_register_model_body()`/`RegisterModelArch` and `ParsedUrl` are removed. The Register tab has Kind, Run group,
linked Encoder/Decoder and SIGReg fields, showing those of the chosen kind, and builds its request with `mns_cli`'s own
`adai::build_register_request()` (`MnsCliCommands.cpp`, now linked into the GUI), so both share one set of rules and one
body. The server URL is parsed with `adai::parse_url()`, and an `https://` URL is refused with a message instead of being
sent as plain HTTP (this GUI's httplib has no TLS). Verified the same day: the helper tests' nine new cases (unescaping, spacing, object values, nearest-first keys, no
array fallback, a top-level array by empty key, control-character escaping, one-line empty containers, field order,
text that isn't JSON) each fail on the old header; `mnsManagerGuiWidgetTests` (31) passes, and the register, training and
candidate requests the real window builds were accepted by a real `mns_server` (encoder, decoder, world model with its
SIGReg settings, linked chatbot, `run-01`, candidate; a duplicate name showed `model_name already registered (HTTP 409)`).

Location in code: `src/MnsJsonHelpers.hpp`, `src/MnsManagerGUI.cpp` (`createRegisterTab()`, `onRegisterModel()`, `setServer()`).

Files Modified:

- `src/MnsJsonHelpers.hpp`, `src/MnsManagerGUI.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/CMakeLists.txt`
- `tests/mnsjsonhelpers_test.cpp`, `tests/mns_manager_gui_test.cpp`, `tests/mns_manager_gui_widget_test.cpp`, `tests/qt_widget_test_support.hpp`, `tests/CMakeLists.txt`

### TD-381: `chatbot_api_server` Ignores `GPU_STRATEGY`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 10, 2026 | GPU / GPUManager | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 12, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `GPUUtils.hpp`, by inspection (definite). `incremental_trainer` maps
`GPU_STRATEGY` (`background` → low-priority stream, `full` → high) into
`Matrix::gpu_try_initialize()`'s third argument. `chatbot_api_server` calls
`gpu_try_initialize(config.gpu_device_id, config.gpu_memory_fraction)` with only two arguments, so it
always gets the default low-priority stream. `config.chatbot.conf` ships `GPU_STRATEGY=full`, and
CLAUDE.md documents the key for both binaries, but on the server it has no effect: serving GPU work
always yields to other GPU tenants (including a trainer on the same card).

Action Items:

- [x] Pass `config.gpu_strategy == GPUStrategy::BACKGROUND` as the third argument, and log the mode as `incremental_trainer` does.

**Fix (November 10, 2026):** `chatbot_api_server` passes the strategy the same way as
`incremental_trainer` and logs it (`[GPU] GPU ready — strategy: full (high-priority stream)`).
Verified with the real binary from the `sycl-cpudev` build on the oneAPI CPU device
(`ADAI_SYCL_ALLOW_CPU_DEVICE=1`), reading the queue flags from `SYCL_UR_TRACE=2`. The old binary
created its queue with `UR_QUEUE_FLAG_PRIORITY_LOW` under both `GPU_STRATEGY=full` and `background`.
The fixed one uses `PRIORITY_HIGH` for `full` and `PRIORITY_LOW` for `background`. The code is
shared by both backends; CUDA wasn't run (no device). There's no unit test, because the call sits in
the server's `main` under `ADAI_ENABLE_GPU`, which the CPU test builds don't compile.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp` (GPU initialization).

Files Modified:

- `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`

### TD-225: BPETokenizer Logging and API Hygiene

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 10, 2026 | NLP / Tokenizer | Code fix (LOW, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-220. Smaller issues in the `stable`-tagged tokenizer:

- **`std::cout`/`std::cerr` in library code** throughout (`build_vocab()`, `build_bpe_merges()`,
  `pre_tokenize()`, `decode()`, `save_vocab()`, `load_vocab()`, `print_vocab_stats()`), against
  the project's logging rule. `pre_tokenize()` prints progress for any input producing ≥ 1,000
  matches, including long chat inputs on the server and interleaved lines from parallel
  preprocessing threads.
- **`decode()` skips unknown IDs** with only a `cerr` warning, so out-of-range model output is
  silently truncated.
- **`encode()`/`decode()` aren't `const`** though they mutate nothing. That forces
  `measure_fertility()` to copy the whole tokenizer on every call, and blocks encoding through a
  `const BPETokenizer&`.
- **`get_top_tokens()` is misnamed:** it returns the lowest IDs, not the most frequent tokens (the
  tokenizer stores no frequencies). `vocab_builder` prints its output as if it were frequency.
- **Unportable rebuilds:** base-unit IDs and pair-count ties follow `unordered_map` iteration
  order, so the same corpus can produce different vocabs on different standard libraries.
- **Unchecked special IDs:** `load_vocab()` accepts any special-token IDs a file declares, while
  `BatchProcessor`, `TextGenerator` and `Dataset` use the `adai::SpecialTokenIDs` constants
  directly. Nothing checks that they agree.
- **Lenient UTF-8:** `is_valid_utf8()` accepts overlong encodings, surrogates and lead bytes up to
  `0xF7`.
- **Stale pointer:** `DataFetcher.cpp`'s TD-006 TODO says FIM special tokens are "defined in
  BPETokenizer.cpp"; they aren't (the tokenizer has only four specials).

Action Items:

- [x] Replace console output with `adai::Logger` (progress at `debug`, or a callback).
- [x] Count unknown IDs in `decode()` and log once per call at `warn`, or offer a strict mode that
  throws.
- [x] Mark `encode()`, `tokenize()`, `pre_tokenize()`, `apply_bpe()`, `decode()` `const` (the
  cache is `thread_local`, so no `mutable` is needed), and drop `measure_fertility()`'s copy.
- [x] Rename `get_top_tokens()` (e.g. `get_tokens_by_id()`) or record merge frequencies during
  training to make it true; update `vocab_builder`.
- [x] Make base-ID assignment and tie-breaking deterministic (sort by frequency, then by token).
- [x] Warn (or throw) in `load_vocab()` when the special IDs differ from `SpecialTokenIDs`. (Done with TD-505, November 9, 2026: it throws.)
- [x] Tighten `is_valid_utf8()` to RFC 3629.
- [x] Fix `DataFetcher.cpp`'s pointer to say the FIM tokens still need adding (TD-006).

Fix (November 10, 2026):
- **Logging:** `BPETokenizer.cpp` writes nothing to `std::cout`/`std::cerr`. `build_vocab()` logs its three stages and result at
  `info`, merge progress at `debug` every tenth of the target; `save_vocab()`/`load_vocab()` log one `info` line each; an unknown
  special-token key is a `warn`. `pre_tokenize()` has no progress output at all, since it runs once per text.
  `print_vocab_stats()` is replaced by `vocab_stats()`, which returns the text, and `vocab_builder` prints it.
- **`decode()`:** ids with no token are still left out, but each call logs one warning with their count, the first one and the
  vocabulary size (`left out 2 of 4 ids with no token (first: 99999; …)`), instead of one `cerr` line per id.
- **`const`:** `encode()`, `decode()`, `tokenize()`, `pre_tokenize()`, `apply_bpe()`, `encode_conversation()` and `encode_prompt()`
  are `const`. `measure_fertility()` calls `encode()` directly; its probe copy is gone. The copy also left out
  `first_ordinary_id_`, so it could encode text to a reserved id that the real tokenizer maps to `<unk>`.
- **`get_tokens_by_id()`** replaces `get_top_tokens()`; `vocab_builder --stats` now says "First 20 tokens by id".
- **Determinism:** base units take ids by corpus frequency, most frequent first, ties by their bytes (pair ties were already
  deterministic since TD-220), and `save_vocab()` writes the `VOCAB` section in id order. Two `vocab_builder` runs on one corpus
  write byte-identical files.
- **UTF-8:** `is_valid_utf8()` follows RFC 3629: overlong forms (`C0`, `C1`, `E0 80-9F`, `F0 80-8F`), surrogates (`ED A0-BF`),
  code points past U+10FFFF (`F4 90-BF`) and lead bytes `F5`-`FF` are invalid, so `encode()` throws `TokenizerEncodingError` for
  them and `ChatbotTrainer` skips such pairs as it does other invalid UTF-8.
- **`DataFetcher.cpp`:** the TD-006 comment now says the FIM tokens don't exist yet and would take reserved ids (TD-565).

Tests: `BPETokenizerHygieneTest` in `tokenizer_test.cpp` (base-unit order, id-ordered file, `const` use, no stdout from a long
encode or from build/save/load, 13 invalid and 9 valid UTF-8 cases); `DecodeUnknownTokenIDWarning` checks the single warning;
`VocabStatsDescribesTheVocabulary` replaces the two `print_vocab_stats()` tests. Built against the old tokenizer, all six runtime
tests fail and the `const` test doesn't compile.

Files Modified: `src/BPETokenizer.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/VocabBuilder.cpp`, `src/DataFetcher.cpp`, `examples/BPETokenizerexample.cpp`,
`tests/tokenizer_test.cpp`, `tests/tokenizer_error_handling_test.cpp`, `tests/vocabbuilder_test.cpp`.

Location in code: `src/BPETokenizer.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/DataFetcher.cpp`; tagged `TODO: See TD-225` before the fix.

Files to Modify:

- `src/BPETokenizer.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/VocabBuilder.cpp`, `src/DataFetcher.cpp`
- `tests/tokenizer_test.cpp`, `tests/vocabbuilder_test.cpp`

### TD-212: BatchedInferenceEngine Can Fail or Abandon Requests It Already Accepted

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 10, 2026 | Inference / Serving | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-211. Three paths let an accepted request end badly through no fault of its own:

1. **One throwing request fails its whole group.** `process_batch()` runs every request's
   generation inside one `try`. If request *k*'s `model_fn` or tokenizer throws, the outer `catch`
   sets that exception on **every** promise in the group, including requests before *k* whose text
   was already generated (and is discarded) and requests after *k* that never ran. This is the same
   blast-radius shape as the empty-response bug fixed in the same function (see its comment block),
   but for real generation errors instead of the stats update.
2. **Shutdown drains only one final group.** `batch_processing_loop()` calls
   `collect_batch_no_wait()` once, which takes at most `max_batch_size` requests. Anything else
   still queued is destroyed with the engine, and its future throws `std::future_error`
   (`broken_promise`). `shutdown()`'s doc comment says it "waits for pending requests to complete".
3. **`submit()` races `shutdown()`.** `submit()` checks `running_` *before* taking
   `queue_mutex_`. A request that passes the check and is enqueued after the worker's final drain is
   never processed and also ends in `broken_promise`.

Not hit by `chatbot_api_server` today (its engine lives for the whole process, and its
`model_fn` rarely throws), but (1) can turn one bad request into N failed HTTP responses under
concurrent load.

Action Items:

- [x] Wrap each request's `generate_text()` call in its own `try/catch` and fail only that
  request's promise.
- [x] Make shutdown drain the queue completely (loop `collect_batch_no_wait()` until empty), or
  explicitly fail leftovers with a clear "engine shut down" exception instead of `broken_promise`.
- [x] Re-check `running_` under `queue_mutex_` in `submit()` so no request can be enqueued after
  the final drain.
- [x] Add regression tests for all three (none exist today).

**Fix (November 10, 2026):**
- `process_batch()` gives each request its own `try`. A throw from one request's `model_fn` or tokenizer fails only that request with its own
  exception; the requests before and after it are answered. The token-count update keeps its own guard, before `set_value()` (TD-162).
- `shutdown()` clears `running_` while holding `queue_mutex_`, and the worker then calls `collect_batch_no_wait()` until the queue is empty, so
  every accepted request is answered before `shutdown()` returns.
- `submit()` checks `running_` under `queue_mutex_`, so a request is either refused (`Cannot submit request: engine is shutdown`) or queued before
  the final drain.

Verified: three new tests, all failing on the old header. A throwing request queued between two others behind a held worker failed both
neighbours before; now only itself. Five requests queued behind a held worker at shutdown (`max_batch_size` 2) left three with
`std::future_error` before; now all five are answered. Four threads submitting while the engine shuts down, 50 rounds, left unanswered futures
in the first round before; now every future returned is answered. The engine's 57 tests pass repeatedly.

Location in code: `src/BatchedInferenceEngine.hpp` (`submit()`, `shutdown()`,
`batch_processing_loop()`, `process_batch()`).

Files Modified:

- `src/BatchedInferenceEngine.hpp`
- `tests/batchedinferenceengine_test.cpp`

### TD-565: Vocabularies Have No Room for Future Special Tokens

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 9, 2026 | NLP / Tokenizer | Code fix (owner request) (LOW, filed November 9, 2026) |

Description:
Filed and fixed at the owner's request: reserve 20 ids for special tokens in every new vocabulary. Since TD-295, new vocabularies
put `<pad>`/`<unk>`/`<bos>`/`<eos>` at 0-3 and the turn tokens at 4-6, then ordinary tokens from 7. Any later special token (the
reasoning plan's `<think>`/`</think>`, which it numbered 4 and 5, already taken) would have had to move every ordinary token, which
means another vocabulary format, a new embedding and output layout, and retraining. Found while reviewing the stream-of-consciousness
analysis (`docs/proposals/stream_of_consciousness_analysis.md`, SC-0).

Action Items:

- [x] `SpecialTokenIDs::RESERVED_SLOTS` (20) and `FIRST_UNASSIGNED` (7); `adai::reserved_slot_token(id)` names the placeholder for
      an unassigned id, `<reserved_7>` to `<reserved_19>`.
- [x] `build_vocab()` adds the turn tokens at 4-6 and a placeholder entry at each of 7-19, all special, and starts ordinary tokens
      at 20. The placeholders are real vocabulary entries, so the model's embedding and output layers already have their rows and a
      later special token takes one without resizing a trained model. A vocabulary of 20 or fewer ids has no room past them and
      keeps the old layout (no turn tokens, ordinary from 4); real vocabularies are 2,000 or more.
- [x] Unassigned ids behave as unknowns: `encode()` never returns an id below `first_ordinary_id()` (a vocabulary hit there becomes
      `<unk>`), `decode()` drops them, and every generation path masks ids 4 to `first_ordinary_id() - 1` (`mask_unknown_ids()`).
- [x] Vocabulary format v4: `save_vocab()` writes `RESERVED_SPECIAL_IDS <n>`. `load_vocab()` marks every id below it special
      whatever its name, so a later build can rename a slot (e.g. `<think>`) without changing other ids, and refuses a missing slot,
      a count other than 4, 7 or 20, or turn tokens missing under a larger count. A v1-v3 file keeps its layout: ordinary tokens
      from 7 with TD-295's turn tokens, from 4 without. An older binary refuses a v4 file (TD-563).
- [x] `BPETokenizer::first_ordinary_id()`: 20, 7 or 4.
- [x] Tests.

Fix (November 9, 2026): as the items above. Tests: `BPETokenizerReservedSlotTest` (`NewVocabulariesReserveTwentyIds`,
`ReservedIdsActAsUnknown`, `SurvivesSaveAndLoadAsFormatV4` (incl. a renamed slot, a missing slot and an unsupported count),
`OlderLayoutsKeepTheirIds`, `SmallVocabulariesHaveNoSpecialBlock`), `TurnTokenGenerationTest.TurnTokensAreMaskedAndIdPromptsUsed`
(ids 4-19 masked, 20 not); the format tests now expect v4 and drop the new line when simulating older files, and the TD-295 tests
expect ordinary tokens from 20. Retraining needs are TD-563's: build the retraining vocabulary with this layout, and deploy
v4-aware binaries before it.

Location in code: `src/SpecialTokens.hpp`, `src/BPETokenizer.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`.

### TD-536: `vocab_builder` JSON Loader and Operator Documentation Drift

| November 9, 2026 | Tooling / vocab_builder | Code fix (LOW, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `VocabBuilder.cpp`/`VocabBuilderHelpers.hpp` (by inspection): the `json` loader collects every quoted string in the file,
object keys included, without unescaping (`\"` ends a string early, `\n` stays two characters); OPERATIONS_MANUAL.md §4 says `--output` defaults to
`vocab.txt` (it's required), `--vocab-size` to 10,000 (5,000), and lists `--min-frequency`, `--num-merges` and `--special-tokens`, which don't exist (the
frequency flag is `--threshold`, default 1); the JSONL loader inherits TD-531/TD-532.

Action Items:

- [x] Parse `json` input with `nlohmann/json` (string array only). The other half, fixing OPERATIONS_MANUAL.md §4 from `--help`, was done with TD-534 (October 17, 2026); the JSONL loader's TD-531/TD-532 gaps are fixed too.

- `docs/operations/OPERATIONS_MANUAL.md`

Fix (November 9, 2026): `load_json_format()` parses the file with the vendored nlohmann/json. A top-level array of strings is read with
every escape decoded (`\"`, `\n`, `\u00e9`, `\\`), empty strings skipped as before; invalid JSON, an object, or any non-string element

### TD-505: Special-Token IDs Aren't Enforced and Most `SpecialTokens` Helpers Are Unused

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 9, 2026 | NLP / SpecialTokens | Code fix (LOW, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `SpecialTokens.hpp` (see [SpecialTokens.md](../reference/source/SpecialTokens.md)). The header declares PAD/UNK/BOS/EOS = 0/1/2/3
standardized and "must not be changed", but:
- **Verified:** `BPETokenizer::load_vocab()` takes the IDs from the file's `SPECIAL_TOKENS` section without checks. A vocabulary with PAD=5, UNK=4, BOS=1,
  EOS=0 loaded and encoded `ab` as `1 2 3 0`; one with BOS = EOS = 3 loaded and every target became `3 … 3` (starting with the stop token).
  `SpecialTokenConfig::validate()` (which rejects duplicates) is never called.
- **By inspection:** the tokenizer and `EncoderDecoderModel::sync_special_tokens()` follow the file, but `PipelineInferenceEngine` (BOS/EOS/PAD),
  `ChatbotAPI`'s `/chat/batch` padding and `BatchProcessor`'s defaults use the constants, so a non-standard vocabulary would pad with the wrong token and
  start/stop pipeline generation on the wrong IDs. `vocab_builder` always writes 0–3, so shipped vocabularies are unaffected.
- **Unused API:** of the helpers, only `is_stop_token()` is used outside tests; `BPETokenizer.cpp` repeats the strings as literals; the vocabulary-format
  example omits `TOKENIZER_MODE` and `BPE_MERGES`.

Action Items:

- [x] In `load_vocab()`, reject special-token IDs other than 0–3 (the header's rule) or at least call `validate()`.
- [x] ~~Or make the constant-using components take IDs from the tokenizer.~~ Not needed: with the ids enforced, the constants are the tokenizer's ids.
- [x] Remove the unused helpers or use them (strings in `BPETokenizer.cpp`); fix the format example.

Location in code: `src/SpecialTokens.hpp` (`validate()`, format example), `src/BPETokenizer.cpp` (`load_vocab()` SPECIAL_TOKENS section), `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp`, `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (batch padding); tagged `TODO: See TD-505`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/SpecialTokens.hpp`
- `src/BPETokenizer.cpp`
- `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp`
- `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp`

Fix (November 9, 2026): `load_vocab()` refuses a file whose `pad_token_id`/`unk_token_id`/`bos_token_id`/`eos_token_id` aren't 0-3, or
whose `<pad>`/`<unk>`/`<bos>`/`<eos>` entries aren't at those ids, with a `VocabularyFileError` naming the field (with TD-223 the
tokenizer is left as it was). Every shipped vocabulary already uses 0-3 (`vocab_builder` always wrote them), so none is affected. The
components that use the constants (`/chat/batch` padding, `BatchProcessor`, `TextGenerator`'s defaults) are therefore correct for
any vocabulary that loads; `PipelineInferenceEngine` was retired (TD-474). `SpecialTokens.hpp` (2.0.0) drops `validate()`,
`is_special_token()`, `is_special_token_string()`, `get_special_token_string()`, `get_special_token_id()` and the three
`create_*` set/map helpers: none had a caller outside their tests, and they knew only ids 0-3, so they would have called `<user>` or a
reserved id an ordinary token (TD-295, TD-565). `SpecialTokenConfig` and `is_stop_token()` (used by `TextGenerator`) stay.
`BPETokenizer.cpp` uses `SpecialTokenStrings` instead of literals, the header's file-format example shows format v4, and the
orphaned, never-built `tests/test_migration.cpp`, which called the removed helpers, is deleted. Tests:
`NonStandardSpecialTokenIdsAreRefused` (BOS = EOS, PAD = 5, `<bos>` at 9 and a BOS/EOS swap inside 0-3 each used to load; it failed on
the old code), `ReservedSlotsFollowTheTurnTokens`; the removed helpers' tests went with them. Also closes TD-225's "unchecked special
IDs" item.

### TD-476: `PortableSocket` Short Writes Truncate FTP Transfers; Unchecked Socket Setup

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 9, 2026 | Platform / PortableSocket | Code fix (LOW, filed October 16, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `PortableSocket`:
- **Short writes (verified).** A blocking `send()` returns a partial count when a signal interrupts it after queuing some data, even with
  `SA_RESTART`: sending 8 MiB over a socket pair with a slow reader and one signal mid-send returned **219,264 bytes**. `send_bytes()` passes that
  through, and `FtpDataServer`'s `RETR` loop checks only `sent < 0` before adding the full chunk to `bytes_sent`, so the transfer is silently
  truncated while the server reports success (the client then fails on size, or reuses a same-size stale file, TD-338). Control replies ignore the
  result. Needs a signal during a transfer, rare in `registry_server` today.
- **By inspection.** `WinsockGuard` ignores a failed `WSAStartup()` (and still calls `WSACleanup()`); `set_reuse_addr()`/`set_recv_timeout()` ignore
  `setsockopt()` failures; Winsock doesn't apply `SO_RCVTIMEO` to `accept()`, so the PASV wait is unbounded on Windows (Linux returns `EAGAIN` after the
  timeout, verified); `last_socket_error()` reads `errno` late; `recv_bytes()` doesn't retry `EINTR`; no tests, and the MinGW build has never been run.

Action Items:

- [x] Add `send_all()` (loop until written, retry `EINTR`) and use it for every `FtpDataServer` send; retry `EINTR` in `recv_bytes()`.
- [x] Check and report `WSAStartup()`/`setsockopt()` results; bound PASV `accept()` with `select()`/`poll()` so it works on both platforms.
- [x] Unit tests (socket pairs) for short writes and timeouts.

Fix (November 9, 2026): `send_all()` sends every byte, repeating after a signal, and every plain `FtpDataServer` send uses it, so a short write can
no longer count as a whole `RETR` chunk. `recv_bytes()` repeats on `EINTR`; a receive timeout still returns -1. `WinsockGuard::ok()` reports a failed
`WSAStartup()` (no `WSACleanup()` then) and `FtpDataServer::start()` refuses to run; the `setsockopt()` helpers return a result the server logs on
failure. `wait_readable()` (`poll()`/`select()`) bounds the PASV `accept()` on both platforms. `SSL_write()` isn't partial in OpenSSL's default mode;
a signal there aborts the transfer with 426 rather than truncating it.

Tests: `portable_socket_test.cpp` (8 tests over socket pairs, signals sent only to a thread of the test process). `SendAllSurvivesASignalMidSend` and
`RecvRetriesWhenInterrupted` fail with the old single `send()`/`recv()`. The Windows branches were built with MinGW-w64 and run under Wine (Winsock
start, bounded wait 301 ms for 300, `send_all()` of 4 MiB over loopback, a failed `setsockopt()` reported).

Location in code: `src/PortableSocket.hpp` (`send_bytes()`, `recv_bytes()`, `WinsockGuard`, `set_recv_timeout()`); `src/FtpDataServer.hpp` (`RETR` send loop).

Files to Modify:

- `src/PortableSocket.hpp`
- `src/FtpDataServer.hpp`

Found while tracing `ModelNameServiceServer` and verified with the real `mns_server`. `ModelNameService::init_db()` logs

false, so `mns_server` exits 1 before binding its port.

Tests: `model_name_service_start_test.cpp` (the two refusals fail on the old code, a good database still serves). Real binary: a garbage `models.db` and a read-only one both exit 1; a good one keeps serving.

### TD-461: MNS Accepts Unbuildable Architectures at Registration

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 9, 2026 | MNS / Server | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `ModelNameService` and verified against a real `mns_server`. Architecture is immutable after
registration, but `handle_register()` validates it only for standalone `encoder`/`decoder`/`world_model` kinds (positive
fields, correct layer field). A legacy (inline) `chatbot` gets **no validation**: `POST /models {"model_name":"noarch","role":"chatbot"}`
returned 201 and stored every architecture field as 0 (which `ModelNameClient::get_architecture()` then hands to the trainer and chat
server, TD-459). No kind checks divisibility: `d_model 100, num_heads 8` returned 201 although `MultiHeadAttention`'s constructor
rejects `d_model % num_heads != 0`, so the model can never be built. The only remedy is delete and re-register.

Action Items:

- [x] Require all six fields positive for a legacy chatbot, and `d_model % num_heads == 0` for every kind; return 400 with the offending field.
- [x] Live tests for missing arch and non-divisible heads.

Fix (November 9, 2026): `handle_register()` answers 400 naming the field for any legacy `chatbot` missing one of the six fields, any field outside 1 to 2^30 (a negative value used to wrap to a
huge size), and `d_model` not divisible by `num_heads`, in every kind that carries an architecture. A linked chatbot takes its architecture from its already checked encoder and decoder, so its zero inline fields
are still accepted. Records registered earlier aren't touched.

Tests: `MNSLiveTest.UnbuildableArchitecturesAreRefused` (fails on the old code); the live tests that registered with no architecture now send one.

Location in code: `src/ModelNameService.cpp` (`handle_register()`).

- `tests/model_name_service_live_test.cpp`

### TD-460: MNS Retirement Leaves Role Mappings and Is Undone by Running Trainers

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 9, 2026 | MNS / Server | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `ModelNameService` and verified against a real `mns_server`:
- **Stale role.** `retired` is reachable from any state via `PUT /models/{n}/state`, but only `handle_promote()`/`handle_delete()`
  update `roles_`, and `handle_resolve_role()` doesn't check state. After promoting `prod-a` to `chatbot` and retiring it,
  `GET /roles/chatbot/production` still returned `prod-a` (`"state":"retired"`, with its artifact), so a `chatbot_api_server`
  with `MODEL_ROLE=chatbot` keeps loading the retired model.
- **Revival by a running trainer.** `candidate` may be entered from `retired` ("revival"), and the `run_id` ownership check
  applies only when leaving `training`. Retiring a model during `run-01`, then sending the trainer's normal
  `{"state":"candidate","run_id":"run-01",…}` returned 200 and state `candidate`: the operator's retirement is silently undone
  at the end of the pass.

Action Items:

- [x] On `→ retired`, remove any role mapping to the model (or refuse to retire a `production` model without a replacement); make `resolve_role` return 404/409 for a non-`production` record.
- [x] Require an explicit flag (or no `run_id`) for `retired → candidate` revival, and reject a trainer's `run_id`-bearing candidate call when the model isn't `training`.
- [x] Live tests for both.

Fix (November 9, 2026): retiring a model removes every role mapped to it, `resolve_role` answers 404 unless the mapped model is `production`, and a mapping left by
an earlier retirement is dropped when `mns_server` loads. `retired → candidate` needs `"revive":true` (`mns_cli set-candidate --revive`), which a trainer never sends, so
its `set_candidate()` gets 409 and the model stays retired. `initializing → candidate` with a `run_id` stays allowed: `mns_cli set-candidate` always sends one for an import.
A `chatbot_api_server` with `MODEL_ROLE` gets the 404 at startup and treats it like any failed MNS lookup.

Tests: `MNSLiveTest.RetiringProductionModelClearsItsRole`, `MNSLiveTest.RetiredModelIsRevivedOnlyWithTheFlag`, `BuildSetCandidateRequest.ReviveIsSentOnlyWhenAskedFor` (all
fail on the old code). A database with a stale mapping written by the old server stops resolving after a restart on the new one.

Location in code: `src/ModelNameService.cpp` (`handle_state_transition()`, `handle_resolve_role()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ModelNameService.cpp`

### TD-458: A NaN Training Loss Makes MNS's JSON Unparseable

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 9, 2026 | MNS / Client | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `ModelNameClient` and verified end to end with a real `mns_server`. `push_progress()` writes the loss with
`operator<<`, so a diverged epoch's NaN is sent as `nan`. `ModelNameService::handle_progress_update()` accepts it
(`json_double()` → `stod`) and the record serializer writes it back verbatim: `GET /models/{name}` returned
`"progress":{…,"loss":nan,…}`, and both that record and the entire `GET /models` list were rejected by Python's `json` module.
It persists (SQLite) until the next progress push for that model, and when the run is superseded the snapshot is archived into
`training_history` with `final_loss` NaN permanently. Any strict JSON client of the MNS API breaks for every model when one run
diverges, the moment monitoring matters most. Same class as TD-443 (metrics).

Action Items:

- [x] Client: send non-finite values as `null` (or omit them).
- [x] Server: reject or normalize non-finite numbers on input, and never emit `nan`/`inf` (write `null`).
- [x] Repair any stored NaN `progress_loss`/`training_history.final_loss` rows on startup.

Fix (November 9, 2026): `push_progress()` sends a non-finite loss as `null`. `mns_server` reads `null`, `nan` and `inf` as a loss with no finite value
(NaN in memory, NULL in SQLite) and always writes it as `null`. Stored rows need no rewrite: NaN was saved as NULL, which used to read back as 0 and now
reads back as `null`, and a stored infinity is normalized when loaded. `json_double()` no longer accepts non-finite values anywhere, so a `link-world-model`
setting can't put one into the record either. The Android dashboard's `final_loss` is nullable and shows `diverged`.

Tests: `ModelNameClientTest.PushProgressSendsNonFiniteLossAsNull`, `MNSLiveTest.NonFiniteProgressIsNullAndKeepsJsonValid` (both fail on the old code; the
live test runs against a real `mns_server`). A real server restart keeps `null`.

Location in code: `src/ModelNameClient.cpp` (`push_progress()`); `src/ModelNameService.cpp` (`handle_progress_update()`, the record serializer's `progress` and history output).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ModelNameClient.cpp`
- `src/ModelNameService.cpp`
- `tests/modelnameclient_test.cpp`

### TD-457: `ModelNameClient` Retries Non-Idempotent Requests After a Timeout

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 9, 2026 | MNS / Client | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `ModelNameClient` and verified with a mock server. `http_post()`/`http_put()` retry up to 3 times on a
network error, **timeout** or 5xx, even when the server already processed the request. With a mock that answered the first
`PUT` after 1.5 s and a 1 s client timeout, one `set_training("m", true)` call reached the server **twice** and returned
the second reply. Against `mns_server`:
- `set_training(new_run = true)` (`incremental_trainer retrain`) increments `current_run_number` on each delivery, so a slow
  MNS skips a run number (nothing is ever recorded under the first allocation).
- `register_model()`'s retry gets `409` (the name now exists) and throws although registration succeeded (no production
  caller today).
- `set_training(new_run = false)`, `set_candidate()` and `push_progress()` are idempotent enough to repeat.

Action Items:

- [x] Retry only idempotent requests (GETs, and PUTs explicitly marked safe), or add an idempotency key the server deduplicates for `new_run` allocation and registration.
- [x] Add a test with a slow mock server asserting a single delivery for non-idempotent calls.

Fix (November 9, 2026, owner's choice of the idempotency key): `set_training(new_run = true)` and `register_model()` send one random `request_id` per call,
and `http_put()`/`http_post()`'s retries repeat it. `mns_server` keeps each model's last id (`ModelRecord::last_request_id`, table `request_ids`, so it survives a
restart). A repeated id returns the original result: the same run with nothing allocated or archived, or a registration's `201`. A different id or none behaves as
before, and an id over 128 bytes is `400`. An old server ignores the field, so upgrading the server first or the client first are both safe.

Tests: `modelnameclient_test.cpp` (`NewRunRetryRepeatsItsRequestId`, `RegisterRetryRepeatsItsRequestId`, `EachNewRunCallHasItsOwnRequestId`) and
`model_name_service_live_test.cpp` (`RepeatedRequestIdDoesNotAllocateAnotherRun`, `RepeatedRequestIdGetsTheRegistrationReply`, `OverLongRequestIdIsRejected`), all
failing on the old code. With a real `mns_server` restarted between delivery and retry, the retry still returned `run-01` and the next new run `run-02`.

Location in code: `src/ModelNameClient.cpp` (`set_training()`, `register_model()`); `src/ModelNameService.cpp` (`handle_register()`, `handle_state_transition()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ModelNameClient.cpp`, `src/ModelNameService.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/modelnameclient_test.cpp`

### TD-410: `IncrementalTrainer` Session Bookkeeping and Hard-Coded Training Policy

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 9, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | Code fix (LOW, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainer`, by inspection:
- `run_training()` calls `finalize_session(…, num_epochs, …)` with the **requested** epoch count, not the
  completed one, although early stopping is always on.
- `make_incremental_config()` hard-codes `enable_early_stopping = true`, `patience = 5` and
  `restore_best_weights = true`, and the config-file constructor forces `LRSchedule::WARMUP_COSINE`;
  none is configurable.
- `IncrementalConfig::save_incremental_checkpoints` and `checkpoint_dir` are never read.
- `update_best_checkpoint()` returns early when symlinks are disabled, so in-process best tracking
  isn't updated in that mode.
- `retrain` (`reset_model_for_config()`) clears and saves an empty history, orphaning every earlier
  checkpoint (which TD-407 then never removes).

Action Items:

- [x] Pass `epochs_fully_completed`; expose early-stopping and schedule settings through `ServiceConfig`; remove the unused fields; separate best tracking from symlink updates; archive or delete old checkpoints on `retrain`.

Fix (November 9, 2026): a session and its MNS summary record the epochs actually run (`ChatbotTrainer::get_epochs_run()`; `epochs_fully_completed`, which the entry suggested, is the callback's 0-based index and misses the epoch that triggers early stopping). `EARLY_STOPPING_ENABLED` (true), `EARLY_STOPPING_PATIENCE` (5, at least 1),
`RESTORE_BEST_WEIGHTS` (true) and `LR_SCHEDULE` are settings with the old fixed values as defaults. `LR_SCHEDULE` takes `linear_warmup` (default) or `constant` only: the decaying
schedules would re-decay every pass, which TD-269 removed. The unused `save_incremental_checkpoints`/`checkpoint_dir` are gone, and best tracking no longer depends on symlinks.

`retrain` (owner's choice: archive): the entry above was out of date, because an emptied history made the next start's cleanup delete every old checkpoint as having no
history line, including one MNS might serve. `reset_model_for_config()` now moves them and a copy of the history to `<SESSION_DIR>/archive/<UTC time>/`, and a move that fails stops
the retrain. Nothing deletes archives. An MNS artifact path pointing at a moved checkpoint is stale until that model's next candidate.

Tests: `incrementaltrainer_test.cpp` (`EarlyStoppedPassRecordsCompletedEpochs`, `BestCheckpointIsTrackedWithoutSymlinks`, `RetrainArchivesPreviousCheckpoints`, all failing on the old code;
`RetrainWithNothingToArchiveMakesNoArchive`, `TrainingPolicyComesFromTheServiceConfig`), `config_test.cpp` (`TrainingPolicyKeys`, `ValidateRejectsPatienceBelowOne`).

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`run_training()`, `make_incremental_config()`), `src/IncrementalTrainer.hpp` (`IncrementalConfig`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/IncrementalTrainer.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}`

### TD-391: SYCL Lists the Same GPU Once per Platform and Doesn't Log the Backend

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 9, 2026 | GPU / GPUManager | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 12, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `GPUUtils_SYCL.hpp`, by inspection. `enumerate_gpu_devices()` collects
`device_type::gpu` devices from **every** SYCL platform. With both the Level Zero and OpenCL runtimes
installed (the usual oneAPI setup, and what ai-machine's driver packages provide), one Intel Arc card
appears once per platform, so `device_count()` is 2 and `GPU_DEVICE_ID=0` means "whichever platform
enumerates first". The startup log prints the device name via `get_device_info()`, but not the
platform or backend, so nobody can tell whether training runs on Level Zero (the expected, faster path
for oneMKL) or OpenCL. Given ai-machine's driver-instability history (SIGSEGV in `libigc`, see
[ONEAPI_SYCL_DRIVER_SEGFAULT.md](../../operations/guides/troubleshooting/ONEAPI_SYCL_DRIVER_SEGFAULT.md)), knowing the backend matters for diagnosis too.

Action Items:

- [x] Prefer one backend (Level Zero first, OpenCL as fallback) and de-duplicate physical devices.
- [x] Log the platform and backend in `get_device_info()`/the startup line.
- [x] Ask the user to check ai-machine's current selection (`sycl-ls`, or the new log line). Done November 10, 2026: every pass of the GPU test package on ai-machine's Arc logs `Backend: level_zero (Intel(R) oneAPI Unified Runtime over Level-Zero V2)`, again on November 12.

Fix (November 9, 2026): `enumerate_gpu_devices()` passes every listed device through `adai::gpu::select_devices()`
(`src/gpu/DeviceSelection.hpp`, no SYCL types). Level Zero is numbered first and OpenCL last, whatever order the platforms come in, and a device is dropped
when a better backend lists one of the same vendor and name that no other listing has matched, so two identical cards stay two. SYCL has no device identity
that works across backends. If a runtime reports a different name for the card, it stays listed twice, but `GPU_DEVICE_ID=0` is still Level Zero.
`ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR` still narrows the list first. `get_device_info()` has a `Backend:` line, and `Matrix::gpu_initialize()`/`gpu_try_initialize()` log the device info at INFO.

Tests: `device_selection_test.cpp` (6 tests, in every build; 5 fail with the selection disabled). The whole enumeration ran on the oneAPI CPU device (`Backend: opencl (Intel(R) OpenCL)`, `gpuutilsTests` 23 passed);
no machine here has two runtimes for one GPU, so the rule itself is covered only by the unit tests.

Location in code: `src/gpu/DeviceSelection.hpp`, `src/gpu/sycl/GPUUtils_SYCL.hpp` (`enumerate_gpu_devices()`, `get_device_info()`), `src/Matrix.cpp`.

Files Modified:

- `src/gpu/DeviceSelection.hpp` (new)
- `src/gpu/sycl/GPUUtils_SYCL.hpp`
- `src/Matrix.cpp`
- `tests/device_selection_test.cpp` (new)
- `tests/CMakeLists.txt`


On-device result (November 10, 2026): on ai-machine's Arc Pro B60 (Level Zero), package `adai-sycl-gpu-tests-bf3501cb-20261109`, run November 10, 2026, `deviceSelectionTests` passed and the trainer logged
`Device 0: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics / Backend: level_zero (Intel(R) oneAPI Unified Runtime over Level-Zero V2)`, so the
card is chosen through Level Zero, not OpenCL.

### TD-223: Tokenizer Mutators Can Leave It Gutted or With Duplicate IDs

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 9, 2026 | NLP / Tokenizer | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-220 and confirmed by running the real code:

- **`load_vocab()` isn't exception-safe.** It clears every table before parsing, so a malformed
  file leaves the tokenizer gutted (a trained 12-token tokenizer had 1 token after a failed load).
  `chatbot_api_server --pipeline-inference` catches a failed `enable_pipeline_inference()` (which
  reloads the encoder's private tokenizer), logs a warning and keeps serving, potentially with that
  tokenizer broken.
- **A second `build_vocab()` corrupts IDs.** It restarts base IDs at 4 and appends to the existing
  merges. Two calls produced 3 IDs shared by two different tokens. `tokenizer_test`'s
  `RepeatedBuildVocab` says "Second build should replace vocabulary" but only checks that the size
  changed, so it passes.

No production caller reuses an instance for a second build today; every one constructs a fresh
tokenizer.

Action Items:

- [x] `load_vocab()`: parse into local tables, validate, then swap them in, so a failure leaves the
  previous state untouched (strong exception guarantee).
- [x] `build_vocab()`: reset to the four specials first (true replacement, as the test intends), or
  throw if the tokenizer is already trained.
- [x] Fix `RepeatedBuildVocab` to check ID uniqueness and that the first build's tokens are gone;
  add a failed-load-preserves-state test.

Location in code: `src/BPETokenizer.cpp` (`load_vocab()`, `build_vocab()`),
`src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp` (pipeline-inference catch), `tests/tokenizer_test.cpp`
(`RepeatedBuildVocab`); tagged `TODO: See TD-223`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/BPETokenizer.cpp`
- `tests/tokenizer_test.cpp`, `tests/tokenizer_error_handling_test.cpp`

Fix (November 9, 2026): `load_vocab()` reads the file into a new tokenizer (`read_vocab_file()`) and moves it into place only
when the whole file loaded, so a failed load leaves the tokenizer, its settings and its layout as they were. `build_vocab()` on a
tokenizer that already has a vocabulary starts from a new one with the same mode, normalization and whitespace settings, so
ids run from 0 with none repeated and the standard special layout (TD-565) applies. The `--pipeline-inference` catch the
description mentions went with `PipelineInferenceEngine` (TD-474). Tests: `RepeatedBuildVocab` now checks that every id is used
once, ids run 0 to size-1, and the first build's tokens are gone (it failed on the old code with 13 ids used twice);
`FailedLoadKeepsThePreviousVocabulary` and `RebuildAfterLoadStartsFromTheStandardLayout` are new; all three failed before the fix.

### TD-546: `retrain` Trains a Partly Trained Segmented File Twice

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 8, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainingTool | Code fix (LOW, filed October 19, 2026) |

Description:
Found while rechecking `IncrementalTrainingTool` after TD-333. `retrain` trains on every path in `trained_files()` (each listed once, whole) plus
whatever it acquires from pending. A TD-205 segmented file with some segments trained and others still pending is therefore loaded whole from the
trained list, and its pending segments are acquired and trained again, so those pairs are trained twice in that retrain pass. It only arises with
segmented files that are part-way through training.

Action Items:

- [x] Build retrain's trained-file list from the trained records' units (whole files and segments), not `trained_files()`, or drop a trained path's
  pending segments from the acquired batch.

Fix (November 8, 2026): new `DatasetRegistry::trained_units()` lists what was trained, whole files and segments (a whole-file record covers its
segments, and a re-trained unit is listed once). `retrain` reads those ranges, so a trained segment no longer brings in the rest of its file. Files
still pending are acquired as before.

Tests (`DatasetRegistryTests.cpp`): `TrainedUnitsListSegmentsNotTheirWholeFile`, `TrainedUnitsWholeFileRecordCoversItsSegments`. Real binaries, a
30-pair file in three segments with the first trained: `retrain` loaded 50 pairs before (10 + 30 + 10) and 30 now (10 + 10 + 10).

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (`retrain`), `src/DatasetRegistry.{hpp,cpp}` (`trained_units()`).

### TD-537: `vocab_builder` Legacy Loader Reads Different Text From the Trainer

Found while tracing `VocabBuilderHelpers.hpp` (see [VocabBuilderHelpers.md](../reference/source/VocabBuilderHelpers.md)); verified.
`ChatbotTrainer::load_conversation_data()` trims legacy `INPUT:`/`RESPONSE:` lines (spaces and `\r`), accepts indented prefixes and keeps only complete

while its response was kept; `load_plain_text()` also keeps CRLF's `\r`. The vocabulary is learned from slightly different text than training
tokenizes (merges spent on edge whitespace).

the parser training reads with, so CRLF, indented prefixes, multi-line responses and a UTF-8 BOM are handled once, and unpaired texts add nothing.

### TD-469: `Optimizer` Global Weight Decay, Unused `amsgrad` and Duplicate Registration

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 8, 2026 | Core / Optimizer | Code fix (LOW, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `Optimizer`, by inspection:
- **Global weight decay.** One `weight_decay` applies to every group, including LayerNorm `gamma`/`beta`, biases and token embeddings,
  which are conventionally excluded. Production uses AdamW with `WEIGHT_DECAY=0.01`, `lr = 1e-4`: a `1 − 1e-6` shrink per step on
  everything, so norm gains drift toward 0 unless gradients counter it. No per-group control exists.
- **Unused `amsgrad`** member.
- **No duplicate check.** `add_parameter_group()` accepts a matrix already registered, which then updates twice per `step()` (TD-297's
  layer paths can register twice).
- **Minor.** Groups hold raw pointers into layer members (stable today via `unique_ptr`); norms accumulate in `float` over very large
  counts; `get_weight_norm()`'s debug counter is an unsynchronized static.

Action Items:

- [x] Per-group weight decay (e.g. a flag at registration), with norms, biases and embeddings excluded by default.
- [x] Remove `amsgrad` or implement it; reject (or ignore) duplicate registration; accumulate norms in `double`.

Fix (November 8, 2026):
- **Per-group decay.** `add_parameter_group(weights, gradients, apply_weight_decay = true)`; `ParameterGroup::decay` and `decay_rate()`.
  Every rule (`step_sgd/sgd_momentum/adam/adamw()`) and the device optimizer (`GPUOptimizer::update_params()`) use the group's own rate, and
  a group with no decay and an all-zero gradient is skipped on both. Registered without decay: LayerNorm gains and biases, the
  feed-forward and LM-head biases, both token embeddings and the decoder's 1×1 world-model/hippocampal gates. So `WEIGHT_DECAY` now applies
  to the attention and feed-forward weight matrices and the LM head's output weights only. Before, AdamW at `WEIGHT_DECAY=0.01`, `lr=1e-4`
  shrank every LayerNorm gain by `1e-6` per step.
- **Duplicate registration** was already ignored (TD-297); the stale TODO is gone. A re-registration keeps the first registration's flag.
- **`amsgrad`** removed (unused). **Norms** (`get_gradient_norm()`, `get_weight_norm()`) accumulate in `double`; the TD-013 debug log with
  an unsynchronized static counter is removed. `Optimizer::groups()` gives read-only access to the groups.

Tests: `PerGroupDecayTest` (all four rules): an excluded group matches an optimizer with no decay, and with no gradient isn't touched;
`OptimizerNormTest.LargeNormsAccumulateInDouble` (2048×2048 of 0.01: 20.48; the old code gave 20.4245, 0.27% low);
`EncoderDecoderModelTest.WeightDecayOnlyForWeightMatrices` (every vector-shaped group and the embeddings undecayed, every weight matrix
decayed); `GPUOptimizerRuleTest.DeviceHonoursPerGroupDecay` on the oneAPI CPU device (all four rules). The per-group tests use the new
registration flag, so they can't run on the old code.

Location in code: `src/Optimizer.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/GPUOptimizer.cpp`, and the registrations in `src/LayerNorm.cpp`, `src/TokenEmbedding.cpp`,
`src/LanguageModelHead.cpp`, `src/FeedForward.cpp`, `src/DecoderBlock.cpp`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/Optimizer.{hpp,cpp}`
- the layers' `register_parameters()`

### TD-428: LeJEPA Two-Update Workaround Is Obsolete After TD-195

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 8, 2026 | World Model / LeJEPAEncoder | Code fix (LOW, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `LeJEPAEncoder`, by inspection. `train_step()` applies the target-view gradient
and the context-view gradient as two separate `backward()` + `update_weights()` pairs, re-running the
context forward pass in between. The in-code TD-189 comment justifies this by saying
`LayerNorm`/`FeedForward`/`MultiHeadAttention::backward()` overwrite their gradient members, but TD-195
made all three accumulate. The workaround now only costs: Adam's step counter advances twice per sample,
every registered parameter (including the predictor, whose gradient is zero during step 1) is moved by
momentum twice, and the objective is optimized as two sequential half-steps.

Action Items:

- [x] Accumulate both views' gradients (target backward, then a context re-forward and backward) and call `update_weights()` once; update the stale comment; compare a short pretraining run before and after (see Fix).

Fix (November 8, 2026): `train_tokens()` (`train_step()` and `train_batch()`) runs the target view's backward, re-runs the context view's
forward on unchanged weights, runs its backward, and calls `update_weights()` once. `get_last_gradient_norm()` is now the norm of the combined
gradient. Each text now gets one optimizer step where it got two, so a pretraining run with the same `LEARNING_RATE` moves the weights less per
sample.
A 480-step CPU pass on the same data (Adam, default rate): average predictor loss 0.45 → 0.73 and SIGReg loss 0.56 → 0.46, old → new, so the
predictor learns more slowly per text while the embeddings stay closer to the Gaussian target.

Tests (`lejepaencoder_test.cpp`): `TrainStepTakesOneOptimizerStep` (fails on the old code: Adam moved weights by more than the learning rate),
`TrainStepUpdateMatchesFiniteDifferences` (relative error 0.001; about 0.8 when the context forward is removed). A new `seed_span_rng()` replays
the masked span.

Location in code: `src/LeJEPAEncoder.cpp` (`train_tokens()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/LeJEPAEncoder.cpp`, `src/LeJEPAEncoder.hpp`
- `tests/lejepaencoder_test.cpp`

### TD-371: Residual-Branch Output Isn't Scaled for Depth

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 8, 2026 | Transformer / FeedForward | Code fix (LOW, filed October 12, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `FeedForward` and measured. With unit-variance input (what `LayerNorm` produces),
a freshly initialized FFN's output has a standard deviation of about 1.35 (1.38 at d=64, 1.32 at
d=256, 1.37 at d=512, `d_ff = 4·d_model`). Every Pre-LN block adds this, plus its attention output,
to the residual stream unscaled, so the stream's variance grows with depth from the first step.
GPT-2-style models initialize the residual branch's output projections (`W2` here, the attention
`W_o`) with an extra `1/√(2·num_layers)` factor to keep it bounded. This isn't a bug; it's an
initialization choice that bears on the open hypothesis that Pre-LN residual growth caused the
epoch-5 divergence on ai-machine.

Action Items:

- [x] Decide whether to scale `W2` (and the attention output projections) at initialization, which needs the layer count passed down. Owner decision November 8, 2026: scale them, on by default.
- [x] If adopted, compare a short training run against the current initialization before switching, since it changes training dynamics (existing checkpoints are unaffected). Done on a toy set only, see the Fix paragraph; the first real retraining's per-layer gradient norms are the real check.

Fix (November 8, 2026, owner's choice): `EncoderBlock::scale_residual_init()` and `DecoderBlock::scale_residual_init()` shrink each
residual branch's output projection once, right after `LLMEncoder`, `LeJEPAEncoder` or `LLMDecoder` builds its stack. The factor is one over the
square root of the stack's total branch count: `1/√(2·num_layers)` for an encoder and `1/√(3·num_layers)` for a decoder, which has cross-attention as
a third branch. At the shipped 8 encoder and 24 decoder layers that is 0.25 and 0.118. The gated world-model and hippocampal paths start at
`tanh(0) = 0`, so they add nothing at initialization and aren't scaled. Only new weights change; a loaded checkpoint replaces them. This sets the
starting point only, so it doesn't by itself answer the Pre-LN growth question from the epoch-5 divergence.

Compared with three unseeded runs each (CPU, 12 pairs, `d_model` 64, 4 encoder and 6 decoder layers, 6 epochs): final validation loss 2.16, 2.41 and
2.59 unscaled against 1.80, 1.42 and 1.56 scaled. The scaled runs also logged the overfitting warning, which is expected on 12 pairs.

Tests: `ResidualInitScalingTest` in `tests/encoderdecoder_test.cpp` (branch outputs shrink by the expected factor in every block; the input
projections don't) and `EncoderBlockResidualInitTest` in `tests/encoderblock_test.cpp` (an 8-block stack stays near its input's scale).

Location in code: `src/EncoderBlock.cpp`, `src/DecoderBlock.cpp` (`scale_residual_init()`), called from `src/LLMEncoder.cpp`, `src/LeJEPAEncoder.cpp` and `src/Decoder.cpp`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/EncoderBlock.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/DecoderBlock.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/LLMEncoder.cpp`
- `src/LeJEPAEncoder.cpp`
- `src/Decoder.cpp`
- `src/FeedForward.cpp` (comment only)

### TD-344: `DecoderBlock` Dropout Is Stored but Never Applied

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 8, 2026 | Transformer / DecoderBlock | Code fix (LOW, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-341, by inspection. The constructor takes `dropout` (default 0.1, which
`LLMDecoder` passes), stores it in `dropout_rate`, and `save()`/`load()` persist it, but no forward
path applies dropout. Training gets no dropout regularization despite the parameter.

**Update (October 11, 2026, from [EncoderBlock.md](../reference/source/EncoderBlock.md)):** `EncoderBlock`
has the same gap: `dropout` (default 0.1) is stored, saved, loaded and printed but never applied, so
none of the encoders (chatbot, RAG, LeJEPA world model) get dropout either. Fix both blocks together.

Action Items:

- [x] Either implement dropout (training-mode only, on sub-layer outputs) or remove the parameter and its persistence (keeping load() compatible). **Owner decision (November 8, 2026): implement, default 0.1.**

Fix (November 8, 2026):
- **Where.** Inverted dropout on each block's branch outputs before they are added to the residual stream: the encoder's attention and
  feed-forward outputs, and the decoder's self-attention, cross-attention and feed-forward outputs. Kept elements are scaled by
  `1 / (1 - rate)`, so nothing changes at inference. The gated world-model and hippocampal paths, which have their own learned tanh gate,
  get none. The new `Dropout` component (`src/Dropout.{hpp,cpp}`) holds one branch's mask for its backward pass.
- **When.** Only while training. A block's dropout is off unless switched on; `EncoderDecoderModel::set_dropout(rate)` enables it and it
  then follows `set_training()`, so `validate()` and the in-training quality generations (which call `set_training(false)`) never drop.
  Only `ChatbotTrainer::train()` calls `set_dropout()`, with the configured rate, and sets it back to 0 when it returns, so a saved, cloned
  or reused model, the serving model and the frozen world model never drop. The LeJEPA world-model pass doesn't use it.
- **Config.** New `DROPOUT` key (`config.trainer.conf`, environment, default 0.1, `[0, 1)`, 0 = off), mapped through
  `make_incremental_config()` into `TrainingConfig::dropout`; `ConfigLoader::validate()` and the trainer refuse a value outside `[0, 1)`.
- **GPU.** The mask is a pure function of a seed and the element index (`adai::dropout_mask_value()`, `src/DropoutMask.hpp`, a splitmix64
  hash usable in host, CUDA and SYCL code). A new kernel (`dropout_forward_gpu()`, CUDA and SYCL) writes the mask and scales the branch on
  the device; the backward multiplies the branch gradient by the kept device mask. Only the 64-bit seed crosses to the device, as a kernel
  argument, per the owner's GPU rule. The same seed gives the same mask on the CPU and on either backend.

Tests: `dropoutTests` (new, `tests/dropout_test.cpp`): off changes nothing, about the rate is dropped and the rest scaled, the backward
uses the forward's mask, seeds replay masks and calls differ, rates outside `[0, 1)` are refused, the mask function's statistics; the
encoder and decoder blocks' input gradients with dropout on against finite differences (masks replayed from a seed); a model drops nothing
without `set_dropout()`, drops after it only in training mode, and refuses a bad rate. `ChatbotTrainerTest`
`TrainAppliesDropoutOnlyWhileTraining`: training with `dropout = 0.5` works and leaves the model at 0; `dropout = 1` fails. GPU, on the
oneAPI CPU device (`build/sycl-cpudev`, `ADAI_SYCL_ALLOW_CPU_DEVICE=1`): `GPUDropoutTest` checks the device mask equals the CPU mask for a
seed, and the encoder and decoder blocks' GPU forward and backward match the CPU with dropout on. The new tests use the new interface, so
they can't run on the old code, which never read `dropout_rate` in any forward path.

Location in code: `src/Dropout.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/DropoutMask.hpp`, `src/EncoderBlock.cpp` and `src/DecoderBlock.cpp` (forwards, backwards,
`set_dropout()`), `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp` (`set_dropout()`, `set_training()`), `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp` (`train()`),
`src/gpu/MatrixGPU.cu`, `src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.cpp` (`dropout_forward_gpu()`), `src/Config.cpp` (`DROPOUT`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/Dropout.{hpp,cpp}` (new), `src/DropoutMask.hpp` (new), `src/EncoderBlock.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/DecoderBlock.{hpp,cpp}`,
  `src/encoder.hpp`, `src/LLMEncoder.cpp`, `src/Decoder.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/ChatbotTrainer.{hpp,cpp}`,
  `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`, `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.{hpp,cu}`, `src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.{hpp,cpp}`,
  `src/CMakeLists.txt`, `config.trainer.conf`
- `tests/dropout_test.cpp` (new), `tests/chatbottrainer_test.cpp`, `tests/gpu_optimizer_test.cpp`, `tests/CMakeLists.txt`

### TD-336: Legacy Training-File Parser Truncates Responses; BOM Breaks JSONL Detection

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 8, 2026 | Data / DatasetRegistry | Code fix (LOW, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-333, by inspection. `load_conversation_pairs()`:
- In the legacy `INPUT:`/`RESPONSE:` format, keeps only the **first line** of a response; continuation
  lines are dropped.
- Detects JSONL by the first non-empty line starting with `{`. A UTF-8 byte-order mark before it
  makes a JSONL file parse as legacy and load 0 pairs.

Action Items:

- [x] Append continuation lines to the current response; strip a leading BOM before detection; test both.

Fix (November 8, 2026): `scan_conversation_pairs()` (behind `load_conversation_pairs()` and `count_pairs()`) starts after a UTF-8 BOM in both
formats, so a JSONL file's first line and a legacy file's first `INPUT:` are read. Lines after `RESPONSE:` are appended to the response with `\n`,
keeping their indentation, until a blank line (which still ends a pair) or the next `INPUT:`/`RESPONSE:`. Text between a blank line and the next
`INPUT:` stays ignored, and so does text between `INPUT:` and `RESPONSE:`. `ChatbotTrainer::load_conversation_data()` (no production caller) and
`vocab_builder` keep their own parsers until TD-537 shares one.

Tests (`DatasetRegistryTests.cpp`): `LegacyResponseKeepsContinuationLines`, `ByteOrderMarkBeforeJsonlIsSkipped`, `ByteOrderMarkBeforeLegacyIsSkipped`
(all three fail on the old code).

Location in code: `src/DatasetRegistry.cpp` (`scan_conversation_pairs()`).
