- `tests/DatasetRegistryTests.cpp`

### TD-295: Conversation Role Labels Are Spoofable and Roles Aren't Escaped

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 8, 2026 | NLP / ConversationContext | Code fix (owner's choices: the proposal as recommended, plus multi-turn training data now); vocabulary rebuild and retrain remain (LOW, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-291. `format_for_model()` writes plain-text `Role: content` lines, so message
content containing `\nAssistant: …` can impersonate a turn in the prompt (and `BPETokenizer`
collapses newlines anyway, TD-224, blurring turn boundaries). `serialize()` writes roles raw, so a
custom role containing `|` or a newline would corrupt the file; a regular message with role
`SYSTEM` would be restored as the system message.

Action Items:

- [x] Escape (or reject) role strings in `serialize()`; restrict roles to a known set or a safe charset.
- [x] Consider neutralizing role-label prefixes inside content when formatting prompts. Owner decision (November 4, 2026): rather than neutralizing text labels, use real turn tokens (`<system>`/`<user>`/
      `<assistant>`) that only the prompt formatter can write. Text labels can't be made safe: the tokenizer lowercases and
      collapses whitespace (TD-224), so typed labels and real ones look the same to the model. Design for review first:
      [Conversation Turn Tokens](../../proposals/conversation_turn_tokens_plan.md) (vocabulary ids 4–6, id-based prompts, the
      same format in training, generation masking, old vocabularies unchanged; needs a vocabulary rebuild and retrain, so best
      done with TD-224 and the TD-358 retraining).

Fix (November 8, 2026), following the proposal:

- **Vocabulary:** `build_vocab()` puts `<system>`, `<user>`, `<assistant>` at ids 4-6 and ordinary tokens from 7. `has_turn_tokens()` is true
  only when all three are spelled and numbered so, which an older vocabulary never is; those keep today's text prompts exactly.
- **Prompts:** a `ModelPrompt` carries text alone or finished ids, and every string still converts to one. `ConversationContext::encode_for_model()`
  writes each turn's token and its content's ids, then `<assistant>` as the reply cue; turn ids enter only there, so nothing typed can
  create one. A plain string (`/chat`, the trainer's quality checks, `train_step()`) is `<user> text <assistant>` through
  `BPETokenizer::encode_prompt()`. Sessions count a message as one token plus its content, with one token of the budget kept for the cue.
- **RAG:** `RAGInference::buildTurnPrompt()`: a `<system>` turn with the retrieved context, the latest earlier turns that fit whole, and the question last.
- **Training:** `preprocess_data()` encodes inputs the same way (`kPreprocessFormatVersion` 5). A JSONL sample may carry
  `"history":[{"role":"system|user|assistant","content":"..."},...]`, oldest first (`SampleMeta::history`); a malformed one rejects that
  line. Later turns are kept first when it is too long. The vocabulary builders read history text too. Without turn tokens history is ignored.
- **Generation:** `mask_unknown_ids()` also masks ids 4-6, and `next_token_logits()` (speculative and batched paths) now masks too.
- **Roles:** `add_message()` refuses a role that isn't 1-32 of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` or that is the reserved `SYSTEM`, so a bad import fails and leaves the session alone.

Checked end to end on a scratch setup: a real `incremental_trainer` pass (CPU, 20 pairs including 4 multi-turn) built a vocabulary with the tokens, and
`chatbot_api_server` answered from that checkpoint: `/chat` gave the trained replies, and "say it again" after "where do you live" gave
"in the machine" only through the conversation's earlier turn. GPU generation tests pass on the oneAPI CPU device; not run on real GPU hardware.

The RLHF update path still re-encodes prompts its own way (deferred with TD-500). `RAGInference::generate()`, the standalone path no server
uses, sends its text prompt as one user turn.

Tests: `tests/tokenizer_test.cpp` (`BPETokenizerTurnTokenTest`), `tests/conversationcontext_test.cpp` (`ConversationContextRoleTest`),
`tests/training_sample_meta_test.cpp` (history), `tests/chatbottrainer_test.cpp` (`InputsUseTurnTokensAndHistory`),
`tests/encoderdecoder_test.cpp` (`TurnTokenGenerationTest`), `tests/raginference_test.cpp` (`TurnPromptHasContextHistoryAndQuestionWithinTheLimit`),
`tests/chatbotapi_test.cpp` (`TypedRoleLabelsAndTurnTokensStayOrdinaryText`, `ASessionAnswersFromTurnTokenPrompts`).

Location in code: `src/BPETokenizer.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/ConversationContext.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/ChatbotAPI.{hpp,cpp}`,
`src/RAGInference.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/ChatbotTrainer.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/TrainingSampleMeta.hpp`, `src/SpecialTokens.hpp`.

### TD-224: Tokenizer Normalization Is Lossy: No Capitals, Newlines, or Tabs

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 8, 2026 | NLP / Tokenizer | Code fix for whitespace (owner's choice: preserve all); case done by TD-560–TD-563; rebuild and retrain remain (TD-563) (LOW, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-220 and confirmed by running the real code. `pre_tokenize()` lowercases every
input (all bytes in ASCII mode, ASCII bytes in Unicode mode) and replaces every whitespace run with
a single space. `"Hello World\nSecond\tline"` round-trips as `"hello world second line"`.
Consequences:

- No model trained here can read case, line structure or indentation, or produce them: no
  capitalized sentences, paragraphs, lists or code layout in chatbot output.
- The vocab file's `\n`/`\t`/`\r` escaping can never fire for real tokens.

This is a design property, not an accident in one line, and changing it invalidates every existing
vocab and checkpoint.

Action Items:

- [x] Owner decision: keep it (and document it as a product limitation), or move to
  case-preserving, whitespace-preserving tokenization (GPT-2-style, typically with byte-level
  fallback).
  Decided November 4, 2026 for letter case: keep it, in new vocabularies only (option chosen over lowercase-plus-case-marker tokens
  after measuring about 11–16% more tokens on local prose). Work filed as
  [TD-560](#td-560-tokenizer-should-keep-letter-case-in-new-vocabularies) (tokenizer and v2 vocabulary format),
  [TD-561](#td-561-bleu-compares-lowercase-output-with-cased-references) (BLEU case mismatch, independent),
  [TD-562](../guides/TECHNICAL_DEBT.md#td-562-vocabulary-sizing-and-tools-assume-lowercase-text) (sizing and tools) and
  [TD-563](../guides/TECHNICAL_DEBT.md#td-563-rebuild-vocabularies-and-retrain-with-case-and-deploy-in-order) (rebuild, retrain, deployment order). Whitespace
  decided November 8, 2026: preserve all of it, in new vocabularies only.
- [x] If changed: bump the vocab file format (v3: a `WHITESPACE PRESERVE|COLLAPSE` line), keep
  loading v1 and v2 files with the old normalization so existing checkpoints stay usable. The retrain
  is TD-563's.

Fix (November 8, 2026): `WhitespaceHandling` (`PRESERVE`, the default for a new tokenizer, or `COLLAPSE`) is stored in the vocabulary
file. `pre_tokenize()` no longer rewrites whitespace under `PRESERVE`, so any text round-trips exactly. `build_vocab()` always gives
space, newline and tab a base token, because `vocab_builder`'s line-based formats never show it a newline, which would otherwise encode
as `<unk>`. `vocab_builder --collapse-whitespace` builds the old kind. The format is v3 so that a v2-era binary refuses the file
instead of silently collapsing. Deploy v3-aware binaries before the first v3 file, and note that a trainer re-saves a v1/v2 vocabulary
as v3 with each checkpoint (still `COLLAPSE`), so a v3 trainer needs a v3 `chatbot_api_server` too.

Measured on 500 KB of this repository's Markdown and C++ (218 chunks with their newlines, vocabulary 3,000): 163,151 tokens collapsed,
163,422 preserved (+0.17%), no `<unk>`, and 218 of 218 chunks round-trip exactly (0 of 218 collapsed). Not measured on the real training data.

Tests: `tests/tokenizer_test.cpp` (`NewVocabulariesKeepWhitespace`, `WhitespaceHasATokenEvenIfTheCorpusLacksIt`,
`CollapseWhitespaceIsTheOldBehaviour`, `SaveAndLoadRestoreWhitespaceAndWhitespaceTokensSurvive`, `V2VocabularyLoadsAsCollapse`,
`UnknownWhitespaceSettingIsRefused`).

Location in code: `src/BPETokenizer.cpp` (`pre_tokenize()`, `build_vocab()`, `save_vocab()`, `load_vocab()`).

Files Modified: `src/BPETokenizer.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/VocabBuilder.cpp`, `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`, `tests/tokenizer_test.cpp`,
`docs/development/reference/source/{BPETokenizer,VocabBuilder}.md`.

### TD-543: `dataset_manager segment` Queues a Client-Local Path on a Remote Registry

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 7, 2026 | Data / dataset_manager CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 19, 2026) |

Description:
Found while checking TD-542's fix against a real `registry_server`. With `REGISTRY_SERVER_URL` set, `dataset_manager add d.jsonl` uploads the file,
which the server queues as `<data_dir>/<group>/uploads/d.jsonl`. `segment` instead needs the file locally (it counts the pairs with
`count_pairs()`) and queues the path exactly as given. Run anywhere but the registry host, the segments name a client path the server can't read or
serve over FTP, so a pass that claims them fails to load them. They also don't match the uploaded whole entry, so TD-542's replacement doesn't
apply to it. Segmenting on the registry host, with the server's own path, works.

Action Items:

- [x] Decide the remote flow: upload the file first and segment the uploaded path, or count pairs on the server (for example a pair count in the
  queue entry, which `num_entries` already records for uploads) so a client can segment a server path it can't read. **Owner decision
  (November 7, 2026): both.**
- [x] Refuse a client-only path in remote mode instead of queuing it.

Found while fixing it: the server's `num_entries` counted non-blank lines, not training pairs, while segments are indexed by parsed pair. A JSON
line that isn't a pair, or a legacy `INPUT:`/`RESPONSE:` file, made the count too high, so the last segments would load nothing and their pass
fail (TD-412). The Android `createSegments()` already split by this count.

Fix (November 7, 2026): with `REGISTRY_SERVER_URL` set, `segment <path>` does one of three things:
- **`<path>` is queued on the server as a whole file** (the path `list-pending` shows): it is split by the server's pair count for it
  (`num_entries`), so the client needn't be able to read it. An entry with no count (the server can't read it) is refused.
- **Otherwise, `<path>` is a local file:** its pairs are counted, it is uploaded as `add` does, and the uploaded server path is segmented; the new
  segments replace the uploaded whole entry (TD-542). A failed upload (for example a file of that name already queued there) is refused,
  pointing at its server path.
- **Anything else** is refused and nothing is queued.

Local mode is unchanged. `registry_server` now records `num_entries` as `DatasetRegistry::count_pairs()`, the pair count the trainer reads, and
`count_pairs()` counts without keeping the pairs (`scan_conversation_pairs()`, shared with `load_conversation_pairs()`), which also closes
TD-335's counting item. A fetch already recorded its pairs written; uploads, manual adds and `overwrite` uploads now record pairs too.

Tests (`registry_ftp_confinement_test.cpp`, the real `dataset_manager` against a spawned `registry_server`):
`DatasetManagerSegmentUploadsALocalFileFirst` segments a client-side file into two segments of the uploaded `…/uploads/` path;
`DatasetManagerSegmentsAServerPathByItsServerPairCount` uploads a file of 5 pairs, 1 non-pair JSON line and 1 blank line, checks `num_entries`
is 5 and splits the server path into 5 one-pair segments that replace the whole entry; `DatasetManagerSegmentRefusesAnUnknownRemotePath`. On
the old code the first two fail (the client path was queued; `num_entries` was 6).

Location in code: `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp` (`segment`), `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`count_jsonl_entries()`), `src/DatasetRegistry.cpp`
(`count_pairs()`, `scan_conversation_pairs()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp`, `src/RegistryServer.cpp`, `src/DatasetRegistry.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/registry_ftp_confinement_test.cpp`

### TD-375: `FtpDataServer` Has No Connection Limits or Timeouts

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 7, 2026 | Data / FtpDataServer | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 12, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `FtpDataServer`; the read behaviour was verified, the rest is by inspection.
`listener_loop()` spawns one **detached** thread per connection with no cap. `read_line()` reads a byte
at a time with **no idle timeout and no length limit**: a 2 MB line with no newline was accepted and
the connection stayed open. So any client that can reach the control port can exhaust
`registry_server`'s threads and memory before logging in. The detached threads aren't tracked, so
`stop()` (and the destructor) can't end them; a connection open at shutdown keeps running against a
destroyed `FtpDataServer` (use-after-free).

Action Items:

- [x] Cap concurrent connections (reply `421` beyond the cap); set a control-socket receive timeout (for example 60 s pre-auth, a few minutes after login); limit command lines to 512 bytes as RFC 959 implementations commonly do.
- [x] Track connection threads (or their sockets) so `stop()` can shut them down and join before destruction.

Fix (November 7, 2026):
- **Limits.** At most 64 control connections at once; more are answered `421 Too many connections` and closed. A control socket gives up
  after 60 s without a line before login and 300 s after (`SO_RCVTIMEO`), and a line over 1,024 bytes gets `500 Command line too long`
  and the connection is closed. The line cap is 1,024 rather than 512 because registry paths in `RETR` can pass 500 bytes.
  `set_connection_limits(max_connections, pre_login_timeout_s, idle_timeout_s)` changes them before `start()`; `registry_server` uses the
  defaults.
- **Tracked connections.** Each connection is a `Connection` record (thread, socket, the current data socket) in a list instead of a
  detached thread. A finished thread shuts its socket down, so the peer sees the close at once; the socket is closed only after the thread
  is joined, by the listener when the next connection arrives, by the sweep thread every minute, or by `stop()`. So a closed descriptor
  number is never shut down by mistake after reuse.
- **`stop()` ends everything.** It shuts down every control socket and any open data socket, which wakes threads blocked reading or
  writing, then joins them. The PASV wait checks for shutdown every second, a transfer checks between 64 KiB chunks, and a data socket has
  a 60 s send timeout (new `adai::set_send_timeout()`), so a client that stops reading can't hold a transfer, or `stop()`, forever.

Tests (`FtpDataServerLiveTest`, a real server on loopback): `AnOverlongCommandLineIsRefusedAndClosed`, `AnIdleConnectionIsClosedBeforeLogin`
(1 s limit), `ConnectionsBeyondTheCapGet421` (cap 2), `StopEndsOpenConnections` (destroying the server closes an open client within 3 s).
On the old code all four fail (no reply and no close to the 4 KB line, the idle connection stayed open, the third connection got 220, and
the client stayed connected after the server was destroyed). The 75 FTP server tests pass, including the FTPS session-reuse ones. Checked by
hand against a real `registry_server --ftp-enabled`: a 4 KB line got 500 and a close, and a normal `USER`/`QUIT` session still works.

Location in code: `src/FtpDataServer.hpp` (`listener_loop()`, `reap_finished_connections()`, `read_line()`, `handle_connection()`,
`stop()`, `accept_from_client()`, `cmd_retr()`), `src/PortableSocket.hpp` (`set_send_timeout()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/FtpDataServer.hpp`, `src/PortableSocket.hpp`
- `tests/FtpDataServerTests.cpp`

### TD-374: FTP Re-Login Leaks Rate-Limit Slots

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 7, 2026 | Data / FtpDataServer | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 12, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `FtpDataServer` and verified. `PASS` claims a per-`run_id` rate-limit slot,
but `USER` resets the connection's login without releasing it, and the end-of-session cleanup releases
only the latest `run_id`. After one connection logged in twice and quit, a run with
`max_sessions_per_run = 2` and **one** open session was refused a second (`421 Too many concurrent
sessions`). Each such connection leaks a slot until `registry_server` restarts; after
`max_sessions_per_run` leaks, that `run_id` can't download anything. libcurl doesn't re-login on one
connection, so this takes a misbehaving or hostile client.

Action Items:

- [x] In `cmd_user()` (and before a second successful `PASS`), release the held slot and clear the login.
- [x] Test: repeated `USER`/`PASS` on one connection, then quit, leaves no slots held.

Fix (November 7, 2026): `cmd_user()` releases the slot a logged-in connection holds, with a "Session ended by a new USER" audit line,
before clearing the login. A second `PASS` without a new `USER` already gets 503, so it can't claim a second slot.

Tests: `FtpDataServerLiveTest.ReLoginReleasesTheRateLimitSlot` (`max_sessions_per_run = 2`): one connection logs in three times and
quits, then two sessions of the run both log in. On the old code the second got 421.

Location in code: `src/FtpDataServer.hpp` (`cmd_user()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/FtpDataServer.hpp`
- `tests/FtpDataServerTests.cpp`

### TD-330: `dataset_manager` Output, Exit Code and Flag Hygiene

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 7, 2026 | Data / dataset_manager CLI | Code fix (LOW, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-326, by inspection:
- Success lines report the **requested** pair count ("Book added (500 pairs)"), not what was
  written.
- `models` silently falls back to `http://localhost:8083` when `NAME_SERVICE_URL` is unset, while
  `assign` skips verification in that case.
- There's no `--help` (it prints "Unknown command").
- `--config`/`--kind` are stripped from anywhere in argv, and a trailing one with no value becomes
  an ordinary argument.

- [x] Report actual pair counts; make `models` require `NAME_SERVICE_URL`; add `--help`; only parse global flags before the command and require their values.

Fix (November 7, 2026):
- **Pair counts.** `gutenberg`, `gutenberg-batch` and `huggingface` report the pairs actually queued, read back from the queue entry's
  `num_entries` (where `registry_server` records a fetch's `pairs_written`) or counted in the local file (`queued_pairs()`), e.g.
  `(40 pairs of 50 requested)` when a dataset is smaller than the request; the requested number is shown only when it wasn't reached.
- **`models`** exits 1 with `NAME_SERVICE_URL is not set` instead of trying `http://localhost:8083`. (`assign` still skips the MNS check
  without it; that is the documented standalone behaviour.)
- **Help.** `--help`, `-h` and `help` print the usage and exit 0.
- **Global options** are read only before the command, each needing its value (`Missing value for --config`); an unknown option before
  the command is an error. A command's own arguments are no longer searched for `--config`/`--kind`, and `status`, `list-pending`,
  `list-trained`, `clear-pending` and `models` refuse arguments, so a `--kind` placed after one of them is reported instead of ignored.

Tests (`registry_ftp_confinement_test.cpp`, the real binary): `DatasetManagerGlobalOptionsAndHelp` (help, a `--kind` after `status`, a
value-less `--config`, an unknown global option, `models` without `NAME_SERVICE_URL`) and `DatasetManagerReportsThePairsActuallyQueued`
(a seeded 20-row HuggingFace cache asked for 50 pairs: the line names the count in the queue entry). Both fail on the old binary.

### TD-329: `dataset_manager` Uses the MNS `run_group` Only in `assign`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 7, 2026 | Data / dataset_manager CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-326, by inspection. Only `assign` resolves the model in MNS and adopts its
`run_group` (the MNS-authoritative standard in CLAUDE.md). `status`, `list-*`, `unassign`, `delete`,
`migrate`, `segment` and the fetch commands all use the config file's `RUN_GROUP`. When MNS has
given a model a different group, `assign` writes into that group while every other command reads
or changes another, so operators see and edit the wrong pool.

Action Items:

- [x] Resolve the effective `run_group` once at startup (from MNS when `NAME_SERVICE_URL` + a model are known, else config) and use it for every command; print which group is in use.

Found while fixing it: `assign` looked the model up with `resolve_model()`, whose `/resolve` endpoint MNS answers with 409 while the
model is still `initializing`, so `assign` failed with "not found in name service" for every model registered but not yet trained,
which is when its data is usually queued.

Fix (November 7, 2026): `dataset_manager` resolves the group once, before running any command but `models`
(`resolve_run_group()`). The model is the one the command names (`assign`, `unassign`, `requeue --model`), otherwise `MODEL_NAME`; a
fetch command's `[model]` is only the registry's slice-cursor key, so it doesn't count. The lookup is the new
`ModelNameClient::lookup_model()`, which reads the full record (`GET /models/{name}`) in any state and returns nothing for an
unregistered model. The model's MNS `run_group` wins when it has one; a model MNS doesn't know, or one with no group on record, keeps the
config's `RUN_GROUP` (as `incremental_trainer` does). When the name service doesn't answer the command changes nothing and exits 1, since
it can't know its pool; it says to start MNS or unset `NAME_SERVICE_URL`. `assign` still requires its model to be registered. Against a
`registry_server` the group in use and where it came from are printed to stderr (so `list-*` output stays parseable). A local pool is
`SESSION_DIR[/<kind>]` and has no group, so local commands other than `assign` don't contact MNS. `migrate`'s source and destination
share the one group, as before.

Tests: `ModelNameClientTest.LookupModelReadsTheRecordInAnyState` (an initializing record, 404 → nothing, 500 → throws, a nested
`run_group` ignored). `RegistryFtpConfinementTest.DatasetManagerUsesTheModelsMnsRunGroupForEveryCommand` runs the real `dataset_manager`
against the spawned `registry_server` and a stand-in MNS (an initializing model whose `/resolve` answers 409): `assign`, `unassign` and
`delete` act on the model's MNS group, the config group is untouched, and an unregistered `MODEL_NAME` uses the config group.
`DatasetManagerRefusesWhenTheNameServiceDoesNotAnswer`: `delete` exits 1 and the file stays queued. On the old code both fail (`assign`
exited 1 for the initializing model; with MNS down `delete` removed the file from the config group). Checked by hand: `status` with MNS
down exits 1 with the message, and a local `list-pending` doesn't contact MNS.

Location in code: `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp` (`run_group_model()`, `resolve_run_group()`), `src/ModelNameClient.cpp`
(`lookup_model()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp`, `src/ModelNameClient.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/CMakeLists.txt`
- `tests/modelnameclient_test.cpp`, `tests/registry_ftp_confinement_test.cpp`

### TD-328: `dataset_manager` Stores Relative Paths in the Local Pool

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |

Description:
Found alongside TD-326 and confirmed by running the binary. In local mode, `add data.jsonl` stored
`data.jsonl` verbatim (`DatasetRegistry::add_file()` doesn't canonicalize), and `DataFetcher`'s local
output dirs are relative (`gutenberg_data/`, `huggingface_data/`). A trainer whose working
directory differs (e.g. a systemd unit with its own `WorkingDirectory`) resolves these against the
wrong directory and can't find the files.

Action Items:

- [x] Store `fs::absolute()`/`weakly_canonical()` paths in local mode (in `add_file()` or the CLI).

`add_files()` all queue absolute paths. `segment` normalizes its path the same way in local mode. So that `add data.jsonl` followed by
`remove data.jsonl` still matches, `dataset_manager` turns a relative file target of `remove`, `assign`, `unassign`, `delete`, `requeue`,
`migrate` and `segment` into the same absolute form in local mode (`local_target()`), unless that exact string is already queued or trained
(an entry from before this fix). Against `registry_server` paths are the server's and are used as given.

Tests: `DatasetRegistryTest.AddFileStoresAnAbsolutePath` (a relative, unnormalized path from another working directory);

by hand: a local `gutenberg 11 3` queued `<cwd>/gutenberg_data/gutenberg_11_training.jsonl`.

### TD-327: `dataset_manager remove` Reports Success in Remote Mode Without Removing Anything

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 7, 2026 | Data / dataset_manager CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-326 and confirmed against a live local `registry_server`.
`DatasetRegistry::remove_pending()` erases the entry from its in-memory list, calls
`save_pending_list()` and **ignores its result**. `RemoteTransport::save_pending()` is a no-op that
returns `false`. `dataset_manager remove <path>` printed "✅ Removed from pending queue… Pending
files: 0" and **exited 0**, yet `list-pending` still showed the file, which will still be trained.
The usage text says `remove` is "local mode only", but nothing enforces it. `clear-pending` does
fail in remote mode, but with the misleading "Failed to save pending list".

Action Items:

- [x] Refuse `remove`/`clear-pending` in remote mode with a message pointing at `delete` (or implement them via `delete_entries()`).
- [x] Make `remove_pending()` return the save result.

Fix (November 7, 2026): `remove` and `clear-pending` check `REGISTRY_SERVER_URL` first. When it is set they change nothing, print
that the command works only on a local pool and suggest `dataset_manager delete <file>` (noting that `delete` also removes trained
records and needs `--force` for a claimed file), and exit 1. They were refused rather than reimplemented through `delete_entries()`
because `delete` is a different operation: it drops trained records too. `DatasetRegistry::remove_pending()` now returns
`save_pending_list()`'s result, and the CLI checks whether the file is queued first so "not found" and "could not save" get their own
messages. Local-mode behaviour is unchanged.

Tests: `DatasetRegistryRemovePendingTest.ReturnsFalseWhenTheQueueCanNotBeSaved` (a transport whose `save_pending()` returns false, as
`RemoteTransport`'s does); `RegistryFtpConfinementTest.DatasetManagerRemoveRefusesInRemoteMode` runs the real `dataset_manager` against
the spawned `registry_server`: `remove` and `clear-pending` exit 1 and the file stays queued. This is the first test to run a
`dataset_manager` command (TD-331). On the old code both fail (`remove` exited 0; `remove_pending()` returned true). Checked by hand:
local `remove` still removes and exits 0.

Location in code: `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp` (`refuse_local_only_command()`, `remove`, `clear-pending`), `src/DatasetRegistry.cpp`
(`remove_pending()`).

### TD-324: `dataset_manager segment` Range Validation Gaps

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 7, 2026 | Data / dataset_manager CLI | Code fix (LOW, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-321. Confirmed by running the parser:
- `--ranges 0-2147483647` overflows `b - a + 1` (UBSan: signed integer overflow), producing a
  segment of -2147483648 pairs.
- Overlapping ranges (`0-9,5-14`) and a repeated `--ranges` are accepted, so the same pairs are
  queued (and trained) twice.
- `--count -5 --ranges 0-1` is accepted, `--count` silently ignored (the exclusivity check uses
  `split_count > 0`).

By inspection: `DatasetManagerTool.cpp` checks the file's pair count but never checks explicit
ranges against it, so a range past the end is queued.

Action Items:

- [x] Compute the count in 64-bit (or reject `B` near `INT_MAX`); reject overlapping/duplicate ranges and repeated `--ranges`; reject `--count` < 1.
- [x] In `DatasetManagerTool.cpp`, reject ranges that extend past `count_pairs()`.

Fix (November 7, 2026): `parse_segment_args()` computes each range's size in 64 bits and refuses one over `INT_MAX` pairs (`0-2147483647`;
`1-2147483647` still fits), refuses overlapping or repeated ranges in any order (adjacent ones are fine), and refuses a second `--ranges`
or `--count`. `--count` below 1 is already an error since TD-323, so `--count -5 --ranges 0-1` now hits the exclusivity check. `segment`
refuses, before queuing anything, a range that ends past the file's last pair (counted locally, or the server's count since TD-543).

Tests: `ParseSegmentArgs.RangeValidationGaps` (fails on the old parser). Checked by hand on a 5-pair file: the old binary queued
`--ranges 0-1,3-9` (a `[3, 10)` segment) and exited 0; the new one exits 1 with "Range 3-9 goes past the file's last pair (4)" and queues
nothing.

Location in code: `src/DatasetManagerArgs.cpp` (`parse_segment_args()`), `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp` (`segment`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/DatasetManagerArgs.cpp`
- `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp`
- `tests/dataset_manager_args_test.cpp`

### TD-322: `dataset_manager` Treats Unknown Flags as File Targets

Description:
Found alongside TD-321 and confirmed by running the parsers. `assign`, `unassign`, `delete` and
`migrate` push every argument they don't recognize into `targets`:
- `delete f.jsonl --delete-file` (typo) deletes the entry but **keeps the file**, with no warning.
- `unassign m --froce` silently does nothing useful.

the other parsers. `--` ends the options, so a file whose name starts with `-` can still be given (`delete -- --odd.jsonl`).

### TD-313: HuggingFace Cache Accepts Partial Downloads and Races Concurrent Fetches

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 7, 2026 | Data / DataFetcher | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-309, by inspection. `download_hf_full_dataset()` logs and skips any Parquet part
that fails to download or convert, and succeeds if one part converted. `ensure_huggingface_cached()`
then treats any non-empty `full_dataset.jsonl` as complete, so the missing parts are never retried.
An interrupted download (a crash mid-append) likewise leaves a truncated cache that's served
indefinitely. Two concurrent `fetch/huggingface` requests for the same dataset (different models, or a
retry) download into the same `parquet/part_<i>.parquet` and `full_dataset.jsonl` at once, and the
second request may see the first's half-written cache as complete.

Action Items:

- [x] Download into a temp directory and rename into place only when every part succeeds; write a completion marker and check it instead of file size.
- [x] Serialize fetches per dataset in `registry_server` (a per-dataset mutex or lock file).

Fix (November 7, 2026):
- **All parts or nothing.** `download_hf_full_dataset()` downloads the listing and every Parquet part into a private
  `.download-<random>` folder and converts them into that folder's JSONL, deleting each part once converted. Any failed download or
  conversion abandons the whole attempt. Only after every part converted is the JSONL renamed over `full_dataset.jsonl`, and then
  `full_dataset.complete` (dataset, split, parts, rows) written atomically. The folder is always removed; one left by a crash is removed once
  older than a day. The old layout's `parquet/` folder and `parquet_info.json` are deleted after a successful download.
- **The marker decides.** `ensure_huggingface_cached()` serves a cache only when `full_dataset.complete` exists, so a cut-short download,
  a cache from before this fix, or one whose marker write failed is downloaded again.
- **One download at a time.** `ensure_huggingface_cached()` holds a per-dataset mutex (keyed by the dataset folder) from the cache check
  through the download, so a second request for the same dataset in `registry_server` waits and then finds the finished cache. The mutex
  is in `DataFetcher`, so `RegistryServer.cpp` needed no change. Separate processes can still download at once, but each in its own folder,
  and the final rename is atomic.
- **Testable offline.** `FetcherConfig` gained `huggingface_api_url` (default `https://datasets-server.huggingface.co`) and, for tests
  only, `extra_download_hosts` and `allow_plain_http`; `download_hf_full_dataset()` is now a const member function.

Tests (`tests/DataFetcherTests.cpp`, `HuggingFaceCacheTest`, a local httplib server listing two parts that serve the repo's Parquet
fixtures): `AFailedPartCachesNothingAndTheNextCallDownloadsAgain`, `AnUnmarkedCacheIsDownloadedAgain`, `ConcurrentRequestsDownloadOnce`. On
the old cache logic (the HEAD sources given only the test address settings) all three fail: the half-downloaded dataset was cached, the
unmarked file was served, and two concurrent requests downloaded twice. The pre-seeded caches in `SplitIsFlattenedIntoTheOutputDirectory`
and `dataset_registry_live_test.cpp` now write the marker too. Checked by hand against a real `registry_server` and HuggingFace: two
simultaneous `fetch/huggingface` requests for `tatsu-lab/alpaca` made one download and got rows 0–5 and 5–10; the old binary made two
downloads and answered one request `fetch_failed`.

Location in code: `src/DataFetcher.cpp` (`download_hf_full_dataset()`, `ensure_huggingface_cached()`, `hf_dataset_mutex()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/DataFetcher.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/DataFetcherTests.cpp`, `tests/dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`, `tests/CMakeLists.txt`

### TD-312: `DataFetcher` Downloads Through Shell `curl` Commands

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 7, 2026 | Data / DataFetcher | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-309, by inspection. Every download is `std::system("curl -L -f -s … \"<path>\"
\"<url>\"")`. Inside double quotes, `$(…)` and backticks still expand.
- `registry_server` allow-lists `dataset_id`/`split`, so its endpoint isn't injectable (but see
  TD-310 for `..`).
- `dataset_manager`'s local mode passes them unvalidated (the operator's own shell, but a pasted ID
  containing `$(…)` runs it).
- Parquet URLs from HuggingFace's API response are interpolated unvalidated.
- `HF_TOKEN` is put on the curl command line, visible to other local users via `ps`.
- `curl` runs with no `--connect-timeout`/`--max-time`, synchronously inside `registry_server`'s
  request handler, so a stalled server holds a worker thread indefinitely.

Action Items:

- [x] Download with libcurl (already an optional dependency for the FTP transport) or `posix_spawn` with an argv array, never a shell.
- [x] Pass the token via a header option, not argv; set connect and total timeouts; validate URLs are `https://` on expected hosts.

Fix (November 7, 2026): new `adai::http_download()` (`src/HttpDownload.{hpp,cpp}`, in `adai_core`) downloads one file with libcurl in
process, with no shell and no `curl` process. It:
- refuses, before connecting, a URL that isn't `https://` or whose host isn't allowed (an exact name or a `.suffix`). `DataFetcher` allows
  `gutenberg.org`, `huggingface.co`, `hf.co` and their subdomains, which also covers the Parquet URLs from HuggingFace's API reply.
- follows redirects (to download CDNs) over HTTPS only.
- sends `HF_TOKEN` as an in-process `Authorization` header, never on a command line, and never to a host a redirect leads to.
- has a 30 s connect timeout, gives up when the transfer stays below 1 KB/s for 60 s, and stops after an hour.
- writes to `<output>.part` and renames it into place only after a complete 2xx download with a body, so a failure leaves any earlier
  file untouched.

`download_file()` and `download_hf_full_dataset()` use it, and `dataset_id`/`split` are percent-encoded into the API query
(`adai::url_encode_component()`), so `dataset_manager`'s local mode, which doesn't allow-list them, can no longer run a pasted `$(…)`. A
build without libcurl can't download and says so; libcurl was already used by `adai_core` when found (`ADAI_HAVE_LIBCURL`, beside
TD-444's `ADAI_METRICS_PUSH_CURL`).

Tests: `httpDownloadTests` (new) runs `http_download()` against a local httplib server (plain `http://` allowed only by a test flag): the
body and bearer header arrive; a 404 leaves an existing output and no `.part`; `http://` and an unlisted host are refused with no request
made; exact and suffix host entries; the token isn't sent to the host a redirect leads to; a server that stalls for 4 s fails within 3 s
with a 1 s limit; an empty body fails; percent-encoding. `DataFetcherDownloadTest.CommandSubstitutionInAUrlIsNotRun` and
`PlainHttpIsRefused`: on the old code the first created its marker file through the shell and the second downloaded over `http://`.
Checked by hand: `dataset_manager gutenberg 11 5` and `huggingface tatsu-lab/alpaca 5` in local mode download for real (the Parquet part
through its CDN redirect, 52,002 rows).

Location in code: `src/HttpDownload.cpp` (`http_download()`), `src/DataFetcher.cpp` (`fetch_to()`, `download_file()`,
`download_hf_full_dataset()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/HttpDownload.{hpp,cpp}` (new), `src/DataFetcher.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/CMakeLists.txt`
- `tests/http_download_test.cpp` (new), `tests/DataFetcherTests.cpp`, `tests/CMakeLists.txt`

### TD-311: Gutenberg Training Pairs Are Next-Sentence Non-Sequiturs

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 7, 2026 | Data / DataFetcher | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-309 and confirmed by running the real code. `create_qa_pairs_from_text()` pairs
`"<template>" + s[i]` with `s[i+1]` and `"Summarize: " + s[i] + s[i+1]` with `s[i+2]`. The
"answer" is just whatever the author wrote next, and the "summary" is the following sentence, so the
model is trained to answer "Can you explain: X" with an unrelated continuation. `extract_sentences()`
also splits on abbreviations: `Mr.`, `Mrs.` and `Dr.` end a "sentence", so `"Mr."` is dropped and
the rest is split mid-clause (verified on Pride-and-Prejudice-style text). The template comes from
unseeded `rand()` (same sequence every run), and every pair is tagged `language="en"` regardless of
the book. Every Gutenberg fetch produces this data.

Action Items:

- [x] Decide the intended task (the user's call). Options: plain continuation/completion pairs labelled as such (`task_type="completion"`), real QA from a better source, or dropping the QA/summary templates. **Owner decision (November 7, 2026): continuation pairs.**
- [x] Handle common abbreviations in sentence splitting (fold into TD-309's scanner).
- [x] Use a seeded RNG (or no templates), and set `language` from the book's metadata or leave it empty.

Fix (November 7, 2026):
- **Pairs.** `create_continuation_pairs()` replaces `create_qa_pairs_from_text()` and `generate_question_from_sentence()`. A pair is two
  consecutive sentences in and up to the next two out, with no template wording; pairs don't overlap, so the registry's per-model book cursor
  still advances through the book. Every pair is tagged `task_type="completion"`, `domain="literature"`. With the templates gone, so is
  `rand()`.
- **Sentence splitting.** `extract_sentences()` doesn't end a sentence at the `.` of a title (`Mr`, `Mrs`, `Ms`, `Dr`, `St`, `Prof`, `Rev`,
  `Capt`, … 24 in all), a capital initial (`J.`, but not `I.` or `A.`, which end sentences), a dotted form (`e.g.`, `i.e.`, `U.S.`), or a
  dot between two letters or digits. The TD-309 equivalence test with the old regex on ordinary prose still passes.
- **Language.** `gutenberg_language()` reads the `Language:` line before the `*** START` marker (24 language names mapped to BCP-47 codes);
  mixed or unknown languages, and books with no header, are left empty instead of `"en"`. The `files/<id>/<id>-0.txt` editions
  `DataFetcher` downloads often start at `*** START` with no header, so most books get no language until TD-314 adds other sources.
- **Registry cache.** `registry_server` caches a book's sentences as `sentences_v2.txt`; a book cached by an older build is re-split from
  its saved `book.txt` without downloading it again. A model's book cursor counts sentences, so it may land somewhere else in the
  re-split book; the slice code already clamps or wraps a cursor past the end.

Tests (`tests/DataFetcherTests.cpp`): the `GutenbergSliceTest` cursor and wraparound tests now expect continuation pairs, plus
`PairsAreTaggedCompletionWithoutTemplates` and `LanguageComesFromTheCachedBooksHeader`; `AbbreviationsDoNotEndASentence` and
`LanguageIsReadFromTheHeaderOnly`. On the old code every new or rewritten test fails (the language parser test can't compile there). Checked
by hand: `dataset_manager gutenberg 1342 400` (Pride and Prejudice) in local mode gave 400 completion pairs with no text ending at a bare
`Mr.`, `Mrs.` or `Dr.`; the old binary's 400 pairs had 96 such texts.

### TD-497: `RemoteTransport` Hides Paths With `}` and Multiplies Backslashes

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 5, 2026 | Data / RegistryTransport | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryTransport.cpp`; verified against a local `registry_server`. `RemoteTransport` parses responses by slicing each object at
the next `}` and reading strings up to the next `"`, with no unescaping (the server doesn't unescape requests either, TD-494):
- After `add_pending("/data/a}b.jsonl")`, `load_pending()` (what `dataset_manager status` shows) returned 2 of 3 entries. The legacy acquire response still
  listed it, but the FTP acquire response is parsed as objects, so with FTP on the server would claim the file and the client drop it, stranding the claim
  (by inspection).
- `add_pending("C:\data\w.jsonl")` was stored with doubled backslashes and came back from `load_pending()`/`acquire()` with each backslash quadrupled, a
  path that doesn't exist; Windows trainers (TD-160) can't use a remote registry with native paths. A `"` in a path truncates it.

Action Items:

- [x] Parse responses (and build requests) with the vendored `nlohmann/json`, together with TD-494's server-side parsing and TD-453.
- [x] Live tests with `}`, `{`, `\`, `"` and non-ASCII paths.

Fix (November 5, 2026): every `RemoteTransport` request body is built as an `nlohmann::json` object and dumped with invalid UTF-8
replaced by U+FFFD, and every reply is parsed with `nlohmann::json::parse()` (no exceptions) and read by key with type checks
(`json_str()`/`json_num()` shared with TD-496's file reader, plus `json_flag()`, `json_list()`, `json_strings()`). A reply that isn't a
JSON object is logged and treated as a failure (`acquire()` sets `failed`; claims it may have made expire with the TD-494 lease). The
substring helpers (`json_string()`, `json_int()`, `json_bool()`, `json_string_array()`, `json_int_array()`, the hand-built arrays) are
gone. `load_registry()` now also reads `model_id`. On the server, `json_escape()` (used for every string in a reply) is now
`nlohmann::json(s).dump()` without its quotes: every control character is escaped and invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD, so a path stored before
TD-496 can no longer make a whole reply invalid JSON (only `"`, `\`, `\n`, `\r` and `\t` were escaped before).

Tests: `RegistryFtpConfinementTest.RemoteTransportRoundTripsPathsWithJsonSyntax` runs the real `registry_server` (FTP on) and sends
`a}b`, `c{d`, `back\slash`, `quo"te`, `café 日` and `C:\data\w.jsonl` through `add_pending()`, `load_pending()`, the FTP `acquire()`,
`commit_trained()`, `load_registry()`, `requeue_trained()` and `delete_paths()`; every path comes back exactly. On the old code `a}b`
was missing from every listing, `quo"te` came back as `quo\`, and backslashes doubled. `ReplyStaysValidJsonForOldUnusualPaths` seeds
a queue holding a BEL character and invalid UTF-8 and reads it back (the U+FFFD substitute, where the old server sent the raw byte).
Both run under `ctest`, so they need no manually started server. `datasetRegistryLiveTests` (106) pass against the new server, and
`dataset_manager` against it lists an uploaded `x}y "q".jsonl` exactly.

Location in code: `src/RegistryTransport.cpp` (the `RemoteTransport` JSON helpers and every `RemoteTransport` method),
`src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`json_escape()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/RegistryTransport.cpp`, `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `tests/registry_ftp_confinement_test.cpp`

### TD-496: Registry Flat-File Formats Break on Spaces, Tabs and Newlines in Paths

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 5, 2026 | Data / RegistryTransport | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryTransport.cpp`; verified. The trained registry is space-separated and read with `>>`: a record for
`/data/my file.jsonl` loaded back as `data_file='/data/my'`, `checksum='file.jsonl'`, `num_samples=0`, `trained=false`. `registry_server`'s upload accepts
filenames with spaces, so such files are recorded as untrained records that `delete` and `trained`'s dedupe can't match. The pending file is
tab-separated, so a path containing a tab or newline (also accepted by upload) breaks it the same way (by inspection).

Action Items:

- [x] Switch both files to an escaped or structured format (JSON Lines), reading the old formats for migration.
- [x] Reject paths containing control characters at `add_pending`/upload. Spaces stay allowed, since the new format stores them.

Fix (November 5, 2026): `data_registry.txt` and `pending_files.txt` keep their names but are now JSON Lines: a header line
(`# adai data registry, JSON Lines v2` / `# adai pending queue, JSON Lines v2`), then one JSON object per entry with every field named.
A file without the header is read in the old space- or tab-separated format, so existing queues and registries load unchanged and are
written in the new format by the next save. A line that isn't a JSON object is skipped with an error log; a mistyped field takes its
default. Paths with invalid UTF-8 stored before the fix are written with U+FFFD instead of making the save throw.
A new `registry_path_problem()` (`RegistryTransport.hpp`) refuses empty paths, control characters (C0, DEL and C1, so tab, newline
and carriage return) and invalid UTF-8. `LocalTransport::add_pending()` returns false for such a path (`dataset_manager add` exits 1),
and `registry_server` answers 400 to `pending/add` and to an upload `filename` that fails it. Spaces and non-ASCII names are accepted.
Older binaries can't read the new files (they would take each JSON line as a path), so roll back `registry_server`, `dataset_manager`
and `incremental_trainer` together, or restore the files from before the upgrade.
`RemoteTransport` still has TD-497's own parsing gaps (`}`, `"`, `\\`); spaces and tabs go through it unchanged.

Tests: `LocalTransportPhase9Test` `TrainedRecordWithSpaceInPathRoundTrips`, `PendingEntriesWithSpacesTabsAndNewlinesRoundTrip`,
`OldFormatFilesLoadAndAreRewrittenAsJsonLines`, `UnreadableJsonLineIsSkippedOthersKept`,
`AddPendingRefusesControlCharactersButTakesSpaces`; `RegistryPathProblemTest` (2). On the old code the first five fail (the spaced path came
back as `/data/my`, untrained; a newline split one entry into two; tab, newline and invalid UTF-8 paths were queued). Checked with the real
`registry_server`: an old-format group loads and is rewritten as JSON Lines, `my file.jsonl` uploads, trains and reloads after a restart as
one trained record, a tab in an upload name and a newline in `pending/add` get 400; `datasetRegistryLiveTests` (106) pass against it.
`dataset_manager add` queues a spaced path and refuses a tab. Tests that read or edited the files by hand (the live test's claim helper, `SighupTest.LejepaPassTrainsEachSegmentOnceAndReclaimsAfterACrash`) now go through `LocalTransport`.

Location in code: `src/RegistryTransport.cpp` (`LocalTransport::load_registry()`/`save_registry()`, `load_pending()`/`save_pending()`,
`add_pending()`, `registry_path_problem()`), `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`handle_pending_add()`, `handle_upload()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/RegistryTransport.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `tests/RegistryTransportTests.cpp`, `tests/dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`, `tests/sighup_test.cpp`

### TD-321: `dataset_manager` Treats `--count` ≤ 0 as "All"

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 5, 2026 | Data / dataset_manager CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [DatasetManagerArgs.md](../reference/source/DatasetManagerArgs.md) and confirmed by running the real
parsers. `parse_assign_args()` and `parse_migrate_args()` accept any integer for `--count`, and a
value ≤ 0 with no file targets selects **everything**:
- `LocalTransport::assign()` and `registry_server`'s assign handler both treat "no paths and
  `count <= 0`" as `assign_all`.
- `dataset_manager migrate` copies `count` entries only if `count > 0`, otherwise all of them.

So `dataset_manager assign my-model --count -2` (or `--count 0`) assigns **every pending file** to
`my-model`, and `migrate chatbot --count 0` migrates every legacy entry. Assigning everything is
only documented as "omit `--count`", so a typo silently turns "first N" into "the whole pool".

Action Items:

- [x] Reject `--count` values < 1 in both parsers (keep "omit `--count`" as the only way to say all).
- [x] Optionally have the transports/server treat `count <= 0` with an explicit count parameter as an error rather than `assign_all`.
- [x] Tests: `--count 0` and `--count -2` are usage errors.

Fix (November 5, 2026): `parse_assign_args()` and `parse_migrate_args()` read `--count` with `parse_strict_int()` and require at
least 1. `0`, `-2`, a partial number like `3x` or an empty value is a usage error (exit 1) whose message says to omit `--count` to
assign or migrate everything. Omitting `--count` is now the only way to say "all". For the transports and server (the second item), 0
must keep meaning "all", because the Android dashboard's `AssignRequestDto` sends `count: 0` by default. So only a negative count is
refused: `LocalTransport::assign()` logs an error and assigns nothing, and `registry_server`'s `assign` answers 400
(`count must be 0 (all) or a positive number`) without changing the queue. `DatasetManagerTool.cpp` needed no change, since `migrate`
only sees a count of at least 1 now. TD-323's other partial-number cases (`gutenberg`, `huggingface`, `segment --count`) are unchanged.

Tests: `ParseAssignArgs.CountBelowOneOrPartialIsAnError`, `ParseMigrateArgs.CountBelowOneOrPartialIsAnError`,
`LocalTransportPhase9Test.AssignRefusesNegativeCount`, `RegistryFtpConfinementTest.AssignRefusesNegativeCount` (the real
`registry_server`; count 0 still assigns every entry). On the old code all four fail: the parsers accepted every value, `LocalTransport`
assigned all 3 entries for `-2`, and the server answered 200. `datasetManagerArgsTests` now compiles `Config.cpp` for the strict parser,
as `registryServerArgsTests` does. Checked with the real `dataset_manager` on a local pool: `assign m --count -2`, `--count 0`,
`--count 3x` and `migrate chatbot --count 0` exit 1 with nothing changed, and `assign m --count 2` assigns the first two files.

Location in code: `src/DatasetManagerArgs.cpp` (`parse_count()`, `parse_assign_args()`, `parse_migrate_args()`),
`src/RegistryTransport.cpp` (`LocalTransport::assign()`), `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`handle_assign()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/DatasetManagerArgs.cpp`, `src/RegistryTransport.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/RegistryServer.cpp`, `src/DatasetRegistry.hpp`
- `tests/dataset_manager_args_test.cpp`, `tests/RegistryTransportTests.cpp`, `tests/registry_ftp_confinement_test.cpp`,
  `tests/CMakeLists.txt`

### TD-564: Byte-Level ASCII Was the Default Tokenizer Mode

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 4, 2026 | NLP / Tokenizer | Code fix (owner request) (LOW, filed November 4, 2026) |

Description:
Filed and fixed at the owner's request with TD-560: make Unicode mode (ISO/IEC 10646, one BPE unit per UTF-8 code point) the
default. `BPETokenizer`, `TrainingConfig::tokenizer_mode`, `ServiceConfig::unicode_tokenizer` (`TOKENIZER_MODE`), `recommend_vocab_size()`
and `vocab_builder` all defaulted to ASCII mode, which splits every multi-byte character into byte tokens, so accented and non-Latin
text needs more tokens and merges learned across byte fragments. The shipped `config.trainer.conf`/`config.chatbot.conf` also set
`TOKENIZER_MODE=ascii`. On plain ASCII text the two modes split identically.

Action Items:

- [x] Unicode by default in the tokenizer, `TrainingConfig`, `ServiceConfig` and `recommend_vocab_size()`; `vocab_builder` builds Unicode
      vocabularies unless given the new `--ascii` (`--unicode` still accepted); the shipped configs say `unicode`.
- [x] Existing vocabularies unchanged: `load_vocab()` takes the mode from the file, and a file without a `TOKENIZER_MODE` line (the
      oldest format) now loads as ASCII instead of keeping the constructor's (now Unicode) mode. That replaces TD-416's rule that
      such a file follows the configured mode: the line was added in the same commit as Unicode mode (`32dd127`, June 21, 2026), so
      a file without it was always built in ASCII mode; following a configured (now default) `unicode` would misread it.
- [x] Tests.

Fix (November 4, 2026): as the items above. Tests: `UnicodeModeIsDefault` (replaces `AsciiModeIsDefault`, which pinned the old default
and failed after the change, as did `VocabBuilderWorkflowTest.DefaultModeIsAscii`, `TokenizerModeConfigTest.DefaultModeIsASCII` and
`ChatbotTrainerTest.Config_DefaultValues`, all updated), `UnicodeIsTheDefaultModeAndFilesKeepTheirOwn` ("é" is one token, an ASCII vocabulary file loads as
ASCII), `VocabularyWithoutAModeLineLoadsAsAscii`, `ConfigTest.TokenizerModeDefaultsToUnicode` (and the tests that pinned the old
default updated), `MakeIncrementalConfigDefaultsToUnicodeMode`. Checked with real binaries: `vocab_builder` writes `TOKENIZER_MODE UNICODE`
by default (with "é" as one token) and `ASCII` with `--ascii`; a fresh `incremental_trainer` pass with no mode configured built a
Unicode, cased vocabulary; a session started by the old binary continued in ASCII mode. Retraining needs are TD-563's: the change
applies only to vocabularies built from now on.

Location in code: `src/BPETokenizer.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/Config.hpp`, `src/ChatbotTrainer.hpp`, `src/VocabBuilder.cpp`, `config.trainer.conf`,
`config.chatbot.conf`.

### TD-561: BLEU Compares Lowercase Output With Cased References

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 4, 2026 | Training / Metrics | Code fix (LOW, filed November 4, 2026) |

Description:
Found November 4, 2026 while weighing TD-560 (by inspection). The per-epoch generation-quality metrics compare the model's generated
reply (always lowercase, since the tokenizer lowercases everything, TD-224) with the validation target text as written in the dataset,
capitals included (`ChatbotTrainer::compute_generation_quality_metrics()` and its async variant pass `target_text`; the generation
backfill's `sentence_bleu()` likewise). `GenerationQualityEvaluator::tokenize_13a()` follows sacreBLEU's default, which is
case-sensitive, so every capitalized reference word is a miss and BLEU-1/2/4 are biased low by however much of the references is
capitalized. ROUGE is unaffected (`tokenize_rouge()` lowercases both sides, as rouge-score does). This exists today, independent of
TD-560.

Action Items:

- [x] Compare with the normalization the model's tokenizer applies: with a `lowercase` vocabulary, lowercase the references (as sacreBLEU's
      `lowercase=True`) for BLEU and for the generation backfill's sentence BLEU; with a `cased` vocabulary (TD-560), keep BLEU
      case-sensitive. Until TD-560 exists, lowercase always.
- [x] Note in the metrics docs that BLEU scores before the fix are biased low and not comparable with later ones.
- [x] Tests: a lowercase hypothesis against a capitalized identical reference scores 100 under a lowercase tokenizer.

Fix (November 4, 2026): `GenerationQualityEvaluator::evaluate()` and `sentence_bleu()` take a flag that lowercases ASCII letters on
both sides before the 13a tokenizer (sacreBLEU's `lowercase=True`; ASCII only, as the tokenizer lowercases). `ChatbotTrainer::bleu_lowercases()`
sets it when the model's tokenizer is `LOWERCASE`, for the per-epoch scores (sync and async) and the generation backfill; with a cased
vocabulary (TD-560) BLEU stays case-sensitive. Tests: `GenerationQualityCase.LowercaseBleuMatchesALowercaseAnswer` (an identical answer
that differs only in case scores 100 with the flag and less without it; ROUGE is the same either way; non-ASCII letters aren't folded)
and `ChatbotTrainerCacheTest.BleuLowercasesOnlyForALowercaseVocabulary`.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp` (`compute_generation_quality_metrics()`, `backfill_generation_quality()`),
`src/GenerationQualityMetrics.{hpp,cpp}`.

- `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp`, `src/GenerationQualityMetrics.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/generation_quality_test.cpp`, `tests/chatbottrainer_test.cpp`

### TD-560: Tokenizer Should Keep Letter Case in New Vocabularies

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 4, 2026 | NLP / Tokenizer | Code fix (owner decision: keep case) (MEDIUM, filed November 4, 2026) |

Description:
Filed at the owner's request to apply the TD-224 decision: keep letter case, as GPT-2-style tokenizers do. `BPETokenizer::pre_tokenize()`
lowercases every input before the regex split (all bytes in ASCII mode, ASCII bytes in Unicode mode), so no model trained here can read
or write a capital letter: replies are all lowercase, and names, acronyms, sentence starts and code identifiers are lost.

Measured on local English prose (about 94,000 words from `docs/lessons/` and the license texts, with a Python copy of the tokenizer's
regex and merge rule; 23% of words had a capital, more than typical prose because of all-caps legal text): keeping case raises distinct
words by 23% and held-out token counts by 15.1% / 16.0% / 10.9% at vocabularies of 1,000 / 2,000 / 4,000 tokens. The cost falls as the
vocabulary grows, since merges for both cases are learned. Expect roughly 10–15% fewer words per `max_seq_length` (and per TD-294
session budget) and about that much more compute per sample. Lowercase-plus-marker tokens were the alternative considered (+12–16%,
shared embeddings for "The"/"the"); the owner chose keeping case.

This changes only new vocabularies. Existing vocabularies and checkpoints must keep working exactly as now.

Action Items:

- [x] A normalization setting in the tokenizer: `cased` (no lowercasing in `pre_tokenize()`) or `lowercase` (today's behaviour), held by
      `BPETokenizer` and applied in every path that pre-tokenizes (encode, `build_vocab()`, `recommend_vocab_size()`'s probe, Unicode
      and ASCII modes). The regex patterns already match both cases.
- [x] Vocabulary file format v2: `save_vocab()` writes `# BPE Tokenizer Vocabulary v2.0` and a `NORMALIZATION CASED|LOWERCASE` header
      line; `load_vocab()` reads it, and a file without it (every v1 file) loads as `lowercase`, so existing checkpoints are unaffected.
      An unknown value is an error, not a silent default.
- [x] New vocabularies are `cased` by default (`build_vocab()`, `IncrementalTrainer::bootstrap_vocab()`, `vocab_builder`), with a way to
      build a `lowercase` one deliberately (a `vocab_builder` flag and, if wanted, a `config.trainer.conf` key).
- [x] Every other `BPETokenizer` owner follows its vocabulary's setting: `LeJEPAEncoder`'s world-model tokenizer, `LLMEncoder`,
      `DocumentStore`/RAG (which embeds with the model's tokenizer since TD-247).
- [x] Tests: v1 files load as lowercase and tokenize byte-for-byte as before; v2 cased round-trips "Hello World" with its capitals;
      the header is written and read; an unknown normalization value is refused; `tokenizer_test.cpp`'s lowercase assertions are kept for
      the lowercase mode and paired with cased ones.

Whitespace (newlines, tabs collapsed to one space) is the other half of TD-224 and is not part of this decision; if it changes too, it
should share this format version so vocabularies are rebuilt once.

Fix (November 4, 2026): `TextNormalization` (`CASED` | `LOWERCASE`) on `BPETokenizer`, default `CASED`, with
`get_normalization()`/`set_normalization()`. `pre_tokenize()` lowercases only for `LOWERCASE`; `build_vocab()` counts base characters
the same way (a lowercase vocabulary used to give capital letters ids that encoding never produces); `measure_fertility()`'s probe copies
it. `save_vocab()` writes format v2 (`# BPE Tokenizer Vocabulary v2.0`, `NORMALIZATION CASED|LOWERCASE`); `load_vocab()` starts from
`LOWERCASE`, so a v1 file tokenizes exactly as before, and refuses an unknown value. `vocab_builder` builds cased vocabularies, or
lowercase ones with `--lowercase`; `IncrementalTrainer::bootstrap_vocab()` builds cased ones and logs it. The other owners
(`LeJEPAEncoder`, `LLMEncoder`, RAG through the model's tokenizer) take the setting from the vocabulary they build or load, so no change
was needed there. No `config.trainer.conf` key for lowercase bootstrapping was added; `vocab_builder --lowercase` covers it.

Tests: `NewVocabulariesKeepCase`, `LowercaseNormalizationIsTheOldBehaviour`, `SaveWritesV2HeaderAndLoadRestoresNormalization`,
`V1VocabularyLoadsAsLowercase`, `UnknownVocabularyFormatsAreRefused` (TD-563), `LowercaseVocabularyHasNoCapitalTokens`; the two tests that
asserted lowercasing (`PreTokenizeBasic`, `UnicodeModePreTokenizeLowercasesOnlyASCII`) now set `LOWERCASE` (both failed with the new
default, as expected). The full suite passes with cased as the default. Checked with real binaries: `vocab_builder` writes v2 headers
(`CASED` by default, `LOWERCASE` with `--lowercase`); a fresh `incremental_trainer` pass on capitalized data built a cased vocabulary with
capital-letter tokens; the new trainer continuing a session started by the old binary kept its v1 vocabulary and lowercase tokenization,
and wrote the checkpoint's copy as v2 `LOWERCASE`.

Location in code: `src/BPETokenizer.{hpp,cpp}` (`pre_tokenize()`, `save_vocab()`, `load_vocab()`, `build_vocab()`), `src/VocabBuilder.cpp`,
`src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`bootstrap_vocab()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/BPETokenizer.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/VocabBuilder.cpp`, `src/VocabBuilderHelpers.hpp`, `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
- `tests/tokenizer_test.cpp` (and the vocab-file tests)
- `docs/development/reference/source/BPETokenizer.md`, `docs/operations/OPERATIONS_MANUAL.md` (`vocab_builder`)

### TD-495: `LocalTransport` Saves Truncate the Queue When a Write Fails

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 4, 2026 | Data / RegistryTransport | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryTransport.cpp` (see [RegistryTransport.md](../reference/source/RegistryTransport.md)); verified with a scratch program.
`LocalTransport::save_pending()`/`save_registry()` open the file with a truncating `std::ofstream` and rewrite it in place. A write that fails part-way
(disk full, quota) or a process killed mid-write leaves the file truncated. With `RLIMIT_FSIZE` = 4 KiB, rewriting a 2,001-entry pending file (74,890
bytes) returned false and left **114 of 2,001 entries**. `registry_server` stores every group's queue and trained registry through `LocalTransport`
and ignores the return value, so a full disk silently cuts queues short; trained files dropped from the registry can be re-queued and trained again.

Action Items:

- [x] Write to `<file>.tmp`, flush/fsync, then `rename()` over the original (and fsync the directory).
- [x] Have `registry_server` handlers check the save result and return 500 instead of reporting success.
- [x] Test with a size-limited write.

Fix (November 4, 2026): a new `adai::write_file_atomically()` (`src/AtomicFile.{hpp,cpp}`, in `adai_core`) writes a temporary file
beside the target, flushes and fsyncs it, renames it over the target and fsyncs the directory. `LocalTransport::save_pending()`/
`save_registry()` use it and return `false` (with the reason logged) when it fails, leaving the old file whole. `add_pending()`
rewrites the queue atomically instead of appending, which could leave a cut-off line. `LocalTransport`'s own callers report a failed save
(`acquire()` claims nothing and sets `failed`; `assign()`/`unassign()` report nothing changed; `requeue_trained()` sets `ok = false`;
the rest log an error). In `registry_server`, every save goes through `must_save()`, which throws on failure, and a server-wide
exception handler answers 500 with the reason. Where a handler saves pending then registry, a failed second save leaves the first
changed: the file is then both pending and trained, so it trains again rather than being lost. Writing needs a writable data directory
now (the temporary file is created there), which `registry_server` needs anyway.

Tests: `AtomicFileTests` (3, including a write under a 4 KiB file-size limit in a child); `LocalTransportPhase9Test`
`FailedSaveKeepsEveryPendingEntry` (the verified case: 2,001 entries under a 4 KiB limit), `FailedRegistrySaveKeepsTheOldRegistry`,
`FailedAddPendingLeavesNoPartialLine`, `AcquireThatCannotSaveClaimsNothing`; on the old code they kept 92 of 2,001 and 98 of 300 entries
and `add_pending()` left a cut-off line, reporting success. `RegistryDiskFullTest.FailedQueueSaveIsAnErrorAndKeepsTheWholeQueue` runs the
real `registry_server` under a 4 KiB file-size limit over a 300-entry queue: the old binary answered 200 to an add and kept 60 entries,
the new one answers 500 and keeps all 300.

Location in code: `src/AtomicFile.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/RegistryTransport.cpp` (`LocalTransport::save_pending()`, `save_registry()`,
`add_pending()` and their callers), `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`must_save()`, the exception handler).

Files to Modify:

- `src/AtomicFile.{hpp,cpp}` (new), `src/RegistryTransport.cpp`, `src/RegistryServer.cpp`, `src/CMakeLists.txt`
- `tests/atomicfile_test.cpp` (new), `tests/RegistryTransportTests.cpp`, `tests/registry_ftp_confinement_test.cpp`, `tests/CMakeLists.txt`

### TD-294: Conversation Token Budget Is Unrelated to the Model's Sequence Length

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 4, 2026 | NLP / ConversationContext | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-291. `ConversationContext` budgets with `estimate_tokens()` (bytes ÷ 4 +
spaces ÷ 2), which counts bytes, so it overestimates non-ASCII text, and bears no relation to
`BPETokenizer`'s real counts. `ChatbotAPI`'s `Session` hardcodes a 2048-token budget, unrelated to the
model's `MAX_SEQ_LENGTH` (e.g. 512 or 1024). The GUI hardcodes 480 for an assumed 512 (TD-266).
Over-long prompts don't crash: `PositionalEncoding` warns and leaves positions beyond its length
unencoded, so response quality silently degrades as conversations grow.

Action Items:

- [x] Size the session budget from the model's `max_seq_length` (minus a response/format margin), via a `ChatbotAPI` setting. `set_session_token_budget()`, default 0 = the model's `max_seq_length`; no margin is needed, since the reply is decoded separately and the role prefixes and separators are counted.
- [x] Pass real token counts from the tokenizer when adding messages (the API already supports it), or inject a token-count function into `ConversationContext`. Injected: `set_token_counter()`.

Fix (November 4, 2026): `ConversationContext::set_token_counter()` takes a token-count function; with one, each message counts as
the prompt line `format_for_model()` writes for it (`"Role: content\n"`), so the budget measures what the model gets. Setting it
recounts and truncates; imports, the TD-292 tail cut, summaries and copies use it; without one, `estimate_tokens()` as before.
`count_message_tokens()` gives the count for a message not yet added. `ChatbotAPI` creates each session with
`session_token_budget()` tokens, `set_session_token_budget()`'s value or, by default, the model's `max_seq_length` (the formatted
conversation is the encoder's input, which keeps only its last `max_seq_length` tokens since TD-365, so a longer history used to
be cut mid-message from the front), and the model's tokenizer as the counter. The TD-292 check counts the same way, so a message
longer than the model's input is refused with 400. The GUI item is moot: `chatbot_gui` is a server client since TD-260.

Tests: `ConversationContextTokenCounter` (5: a message counts as its prompt line and the total equals the prompt's length;
setting a counter recounts and evicts; eviction by real counts; imports and copies keep the counter; an over-long newest message
keeps a tail that fits) and `ChatbotAPITest.SessionBudgetIsTheModelsInputLengthInRealTokens` (the budget is the model's
`max_seq_length` and settable; after 9 turns the exported conversation's real token count fits it; a message the old 2048-token
estimate would accept but longer than the model's input is refused). `ConcurrentTurnsOnOneSessionAreSerialized` now sets a large
budget, since it counts every turn. The new tests use new functions, so they don't build on the old code. Checked with the real
`chatbot_api_server` and a model with `max_seq_length` 64: after 7 turns the old server held all 10 messages (past the encoder's
input) and accepted a 360-character message; the new one held the 2 newest and refused it (400, "about 126 tokens; a session holds
at most 64").

Location in code: `src/ConversationContext.{hpp,cpp}` (`set_token_counter()`, `count_message_tokens()`), `src/ChatbotAPI.{hpp,cpp}`
(`Session`, `get_or_create_session()`, `session_token_budget()`, `handle_chat_session()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChatbotAPI.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/ConversationContext.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/conversationcontext_test.cpp`, `tests/chatbotapi_test.cpp`
- (`src/ChatbotGUI.cpp`: moot since TD-260)

### TD-276: ChatbotTrainer Hygiene: Dead Fields, Logging, Stale Test File

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 4, 2026 | Training / ChatbotTrainer | Code fix (owner decision on accuracy) (LOW, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-267:

- `calculate_accuracy()` is tested but unused by training; `training_accuracies`/`validation_accuracies` are never filled; validation always reports accuracy −1.
- `TrainingConfig::verbose` is deprecated and unused; `log()` sends every level to `Logger::info` (DEBUG not mapped) and ignores its colour argument; `COLOR_*` macros are redefined locally.
- `validate_and_correct_config()` (standalone `initialize_model()` path only) silently changes `d_model`/`d_ff`, which would break compatibility with an MNS-registered architecture.
- `tests/chatbottrainer_test.cpp.old` is an unbuilt January-2026 leftover.

Action Items:

- [x] Compute token accuracy in `validate()` (or remove the dead vectors and getters). Owner's choice: compute it, on the GPU path with a device-side count.
- [x] Remove `verbose`; map `log()` levels to `Logger` levels.
- [x] Make `validate_and_correct_config()` fail instead of silently changing architecture.
- [x] Delete `tests/chatbottrainer_test.cpp.old`.

Fix (November 4, 2026):

- **Validation token accuracy.** `EncoderDecoderModel::token_accuracy()` counts the target positions whose first maximum logit
  is the target (`total` only counts target ids inside the vocabulary). `evaluate_tokenized()`/`gpu_evaluate_tokenized()` take an
  optional `TokenAccuracy*`. On the GPU path a new kernel, `matrix_token_correct_gpu()` (CUDA and SYCL: one work-group per row,
  argmax with the lowest index on ties, flags summed on the device), counts from the logits `gpu_forward()` left there, so one
  number per sample is downloaded. `validate()` sums the counts, keeps the share in `validation_accuracies`
  (`get_validation_accuracies()`), logs it and sends it with `update_validation_metrics()` (always -1 before), so both
  dashboards, which hid -1, now show it. Training accuracy isn't computed: `training_accuracies` and `calculate_accuracy()`
  (only tests used it) are removed.
- **`log()`** maps SILENT (errors) to `Logger::error`, DEBUG to `debug`, NORMAL/VERBOSE to `info`; the unused colour argument and
  the local `COLOR_*` macros are removed. `TrainingConfig::verbose` is removed.
- **`validate_and_correct_config()`** throws `std::invalid_argument` when `d_model` isn't a positive multiple of `num_heads` (it was
  rounded up) and only warns about an unusual `d_ff` ratio (it was reset to 4x).
- `tests/chatbottrainer_test.cpp.old` is deleted.

Tests: `TokenAccuracyTest` (ties, out-of-vocabulary targets, rows past the targets), `MatrixGPUTD003Test.TokenCorrectCountMatchesHostArgmax`
(the kernel against a host argmax, 40 rows of 1000, a tie, out-of-range targets; run on the oneAPI CPU device, CUDA compile-checked
only), `MetricsTrackerWiringTest.ValidationReportsTokenAccuracy` (a memorised pair reaches accuracy 1.0, and every value reaches
the reporter; also run on the CPU device's GPU path), `ChatbotTrainerLogTest.LevelsMapToLoggerLevelsAndFilter` and
`ChatbotTrainerCacheTest.ArchitectureIsNeverSilentlyChanged`; the five `calculate_accuracy()` tests are replaced. The new tests use new
APIs, so they don't build on the old code. Checked with real binaries: a 3-epoch `incremental_trainer` pass over 20 pairs against a
real `metrics_api_server` recorded `epoch_validation_accuracies` `[-1, -1, -1]` with the old trainer and `[0, 0.333, 0.417]` with the new.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotTrainer.{hpp,cpp}` (`validate()`, `log()`, `validate_and_correct_config()`),
`src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}` (`token_accuracy()`, `evaluate_tokenized()`, `gpu_evaluate_tokenized()`),
`src/gpu/MatrixGPU.{hpp,cu}`, `src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.{hpp,cpp}` (`matrix_token_correct_gpu()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChatbotTrainer.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.{hpp,cu}`, `src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/chatbottrainer_test.cpp`, `tests/matrixgpu_td003_test.cpp`
- `tests/chatbottrainer_test.cpp.old` (deleted)

### TD-274: ChatbotTrainer Saves the Best Model to a Fixed File in the Working Directory

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 4, 2026 | Training / ChatbotTrainer | Code fix (LOW, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-267. With early stopping and `restore_best_weights` on, `validate()` saves each
new best to the relative path `"best_model_temp.bin"` (five sidecar files) in the process's working
directory. It's never cleaned up, it's shared by every trainer running in that directory, and
`train()` restores from whatever is there at the end.

Action Items:

- [x] Save under the session directory (or a unique temp directory) and remove it after restoring. Both: a unique directory under the session directory (the system temp directory for a bare `ChatbotTrainer`).

Fix (November 4, 2026): `validate()` saves the best weights to `<best_model_dir>/best_model_<random>/best.bin`, a directory of this
trainer's own created on the first save of each `train()` call. `TrainingConfig::best_model_dir` is new: empty means the system temp
directory, and `IncrementalTrainer::make_incremental_config()` sets it to the session directory, since the copy is as large as a
checkpoint. `remove_best_model_copy()` deletes the directory with every sidecar at the start of `train()`, after the restore, on
`train()`'s failure path and in the destructor, so a later `train()` can't restore an earlier call's best either. A process killed
mid-pass still leaves its directory in the session directory; nothing sweeps those.

Tests: `MetricsTrackerWiringTest.BestWeightsCopyIsPrivateAndRemovedAfterTraining`: during training the copy and its sidecars sit
in one `best_model_*` directory under `best_model_dir`; it is gone after `train()` and after a second `train()`; nothing appears in
the working directory; two trainers get different directories. Checked with real `incremental_trainer` passes (20 pairs, 2 epochs)
run from an empty working directory: the old binary left the 16 `best_model_temp.bin*` files there, the new one nothing there or in
the session directory; both restored the best epoch. Seen in the same check, not changed: the `latest_checkpoint.bin*`/
`best_checkpoint.bin*` links (TD-005/TD-408) are created in the working directory by design.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotTrainer.{hpp,cpp}` (`validate()`, `train()`, `remove_best_model_copy()`, destructor),
`src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`make_incremental_config()`).

write `meta.quality` into `ChatbotTrainer`'s private `training_data`/`validation_data`, which have
no accessor. `IncrementalTrainer` passes pairs via `add_training_pair()` (no metadata) and never
