### TD-271: ChatbotTrainer's Tokenized Cache Can Pair With a Different Random Split

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 4, 2026 | Training / ChatbotTrainer | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-267. `train()` runs `split_data()` (a fresh `std::random_device` shuffle)
**before** `preprocess_data()` loads the tokenized cache. The cache holds the tokenized split from
the run that wrote it. Counts match, so the load succeeds, but `tokenized_training_data[i]` no longer
corresponds to `training_data[i]`, and per-index metadata writes (`meta.token_count`, quality
backfill) land on the wrong pairs. Training still uses a valid split (the cached one). Separately,
the split is different on every pass, so validation loss isn't measured on the same samples from
one pass to the next. Only the misalignment depends on `cache_tokenized_data` (default off).

Action Items:

- [x] Make the split deterministic (seed from the cache key or dataset checksum), or cache the split itself (indices) alongside the tokenized data. Deterministic from each pair's own text, so also independent of load order.
- [x] Include the split seed or validation membership in the cache key. The key includes `validation_split`; membership follows from the data already in it, and a load checks it.
- [x] Test: two `train()` calls with caching produce aligned raw/tokenized pairs.

Fix (November 4, 2026): `split_data()` ranks each pair by a hash of its own input and response (FNV-1a 64, the same on
every platform) and takes the `size / validation_split` lowest-ranked pairs as validation, ties by load order; both sets
keep the load order. The same data splits the same way on every pass, in any load order, so a cache written by an earlier
pass matches, and validation losses over the same data are measured on the same pairs. `load_tokenized_cache()` also checks
that each cached pair's stored texts are the raw pair at its index (an empty placeholder for a skipped pair matches) and
otherwise reports a miss. `kPreprocessFormatVersion` is 4, so caches holding old random splits aren't reused, and
`compute_tokenized_cache_key()` includes `validation_split`.

Tests: `ChatbotTrainerCacheTest.SplitIsTheSameEveryTimeAndIndependentOfLoadOrder`, `CacheFromADifferentSplitIsNotLoaded`
and `SecondPassWithCacheKeepsRawAndTokenizedPairsAligned` (two real `train()` passes with the cache on: aligned pairs, the
same validation set). All three fail on the old code (3 of 3 runs). Checked with real `incremental_trainer` passes over 20
pairs with `CACHE_TOKENIZED_DATA=true`: two passes with the cache cleared between them wrote different cache files with the
old binary and byte-identical ones with the new; a third pass hit the cache with both, which for the old binary meant pairs
tokenized under another split.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp` (`split_data()`, `load_tokenized_cache()`), `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
(`compute_tokenized_cache_key()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChatbotTrainer.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (cache key)
- `tests/chatbottrainer_test.cpp`

### TD-268: ChatbotTrainer Only Ends Metrics Epochs When There Is Validation Data

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 4, 2026 | Training / ChatbotTrainer | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-267. `train()` calls `metrics_reporter_->end_epoch()` only inside
`if (!tokenized_validation_data.empty())`. A run with `validation_split = 0`, or too little data to
split, starts epochs on the reporter (`train_epoch()` calls `start_epoch()`) but never ends them, so
the dashboard never records epoch completion, loss or perplexity for those runs. The gradient norm
passed to `end_epoch()` is also the last window's (`optimizer->get_gradient_norm()`), not the
epoch average already computed in `gradient_norms.back()`.

Action Items:

- [x] Call `end_epoch()` every epoch, passing a "no validation" value (as the epoch callback does with 0.0) when there's no validation data.
- [x] Pass `gradient_norms.back()` as the epoch gradient norm.
- [x] Test with a reporter mock and `validation_split = 0`.

Fix (November 4, 2026): `train()` ends every completed epoch on the reporter, after validation when there is any. The
validation loss is 0 without validation data (`IMetricsReporter::end_epoch()`'s "not computed", which `metrics_api_server`
already treats as such); the gradient norm is the epoch average, `gradient_norms.back()`; and the epoch's wall-clock seconds
are passed as well (always 0 before). Early stopping is still checked only with validation data, now after the epoch has
been ended. An aborted epoch is still not ended. `last_grad_norm_`, read only by the old call, is removed.

Tests: `MetricsTrackerWiringTest.EndsEveryEpochOnTheReporterWithoutValidationData` (3 epochs, `validation_split = 0`: every
started epoch ended, with its loss, validation loss 0, epoch-average gradient norm, learning rate and a positive duration)
and `EndsEachEpochOnceWithItsValidationLoss`, with a recording `IMetricsReporter`. On the old code the first saw 0 of 3 epochs
ended and the second the last window's gradient norm. Checked with a real `incremental_trainer` pass of 6 pairs (no
validation set) against a real `metrics_api_server`: the old binary left the session at `total_epochs_completed: 0` with
empty `epoch_losses`; the new one recorded all 3 epochs with the logged losses and the epoch-average gradient norm.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp` (`train()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChatbotTrainer.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/chatbottrainer_test.cpp`

### TD-264: `chatbot_gui` Launcher Hardcodes Qt5 and x86_64 Paths

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 4, 2026 | Client / GUI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-260. `ChatbotGUI_wrapper.cpp` always sets
`QT_QPA_PLATFORM_PLUGIN_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/qt5/plugins`, but CMake builds
`chatbot_gui_binary` against **Qt6 when available** (Qt5 is only the fallback), so a Qt6 build is
pointed at Qt5 platform plugins. Library paths are hardcoded for x86_64 Debian/Ubuntu. It also
puts system paths **before** the user's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and drops it entirely if it contains
`/snap/`.

Action Items:

Both: CMake passes the build's Qt platform plugin directory (`ADAI_QT_PLATFORM_PLUGIN_DIR`), and the wrapper sets it only under snap.
- [x] Derive library paths from the build (or don't override them unless snap is detected). No library directory is set at all; only snap entries are removed.
- [x] Preserve the user's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` order, removing only `/snap/` entries. Also for `QT_PLUGIN_PATH`.

Fix (November 4, 2026): the wrapper applies the changes `adai::gui_launch::launch_environment()` returns
(`src/ChatbotGuiLaunchEnv.{hpp,cpp}`, Qt-free so it is unit-tested). It still unsets `GTK_PATH`/`SNAP`/`SNAP_COMMON`/

had an effect, because Qt loads platform plugins from that directory itself rather than its `platforms/`
subdirectory (seen with `QT_DEBUG_PLUGINS=1`); Qt now loads `libqoffscreen.so` from the configured directory. The two
launcher scripts, `run_chatbot_gui.sh` and `chatbot_gui_fixed.sh`, set the same x86_64 Qt5 paths and replaced
`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` before running the wrapper; they now leave the environment to it. The operator docs' manual
`QT_QPA_PLATFORM_PLUGIN_PATH` examples (GUI troubleshooting, MNS Manager GUI guide) now name the `platforms`
directory via `qmake -query`/`qtpaths6`.

### TD-260: `chatbot_gui` Never Loads a Trained Checkpoint

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 4, 2026 | Client / GUI | Code fix (owner decision: the GUI is a client of `chatbot_api_server`) (**HIGH**, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [ChatbotGUI.md](../reference/source/ChatbotGUI.md). `ChatbotGUI::initializeChatbot()`
calls `model->load_model(model_path)` only if `std::ifstream(model_path).good()`. But
`EncoderDecoderModel::save_model(path)` writes only sidecar files (`path.config`, `.vocab`,
`.encoder`, `.decoder`, `.lm_head`) and **never a file at `path` itself**, so for any real
checkpoint the check fails, `load_model()` is never called, and the GUI **silently** chats with a
randomly initialized model. No message is shown. `IncrementalTrainer.cpp` documents this exact
trap ("checking for that bare path here would reject every legitimately-saved checkpoint
unconditionally") and checks the five sidecars instead. Passing an existing sidecar such as
`model.config` doesn't help: `load_model()` appends the suffixes again and throws.

Action Items:

- [x] Check for the sidecars (or just call `load_model()` and handle its exception), the same way `IncrementalTrainer` does; consider a shared `EncoderDecoderModel::checkpoint_exists(path)` helper. Superseded: the GUI loads no checkpoint at all now; the server does.
- [x] When no checkpoint is found, show a clear warning in the chat pane that the model is untrained (matching TD-246's server-side stance). The pane warns when the server reports an untrained model.
- [x] Update the default/usage text (`chatbot_model.bin`) to describe a checkpoint base path. The usage is now `chatbot_gui [server_url]`.

**Fix (November 4, 2026), owner decision:** a first fix made the GUI find and load the checkpoint's files. The owner
rejected it: the GUI shouldn't run its own copy of the model at all, but be a client of the served model, like the
`chatbot` CLI. So:

- `ChatbotClient` (`src/ChatbotClient.{hpp,cpp}`, new) is the HTTP session with `chatbot_api_server`, taken out of
  `ChatbotCLI`: `POST /chat/session` with only the changed settings (TD-254), a new session when the server answers
  404 (TD-232), `/clear-session`, `/chat/session/export` and `/import`, and `cancel()` for a request in flight. It
  prints nothing; each call returns what happened. `ChatbotCLI` keeps its public API, its messages and its save-file
  policy (TD-258) and delegates to it; its 66 tests pass unchanged.
- `chatbot_gui [server_url]` (default `http://localhost:8080`) builds no model, tokenizer or `ConversationContext`
  and links none of the model libraries. Its settings start at "server default" and are sent once changed, with the
  server's ranges (`GenerationLimits`). Save writes the server's export (temp file + rename), Load imports into the
  server, Clear clears the server's session. On connecting, the chat pane says whether the server was reached and
  warns when it reports an untrained model (`/health` 503, TD-246). The old `[vocab_file] [model_file]` form exits 1
  saying why.
- Requests run on a worker thread (TD-263). The launcher scripts, the GUI build checks and the operator guides
  describe the server client.
- Checked by driving the real `ChatbotGUI` class headless (offscreen Qt) against a real `chatbot_api_server`: two
  turns went to one server session and got the server's replies, and the event loop ran about 21,000 times during
  one reply. An unreachable server and an `ALLOW_UNTRAINED_MODEL` server each gave their notice.

Tests: `chatbotclientTests` (11, new, against a stub server: health including an untrained server, session adoption,
only changed settings sent, a lost session retried in a new one, clear/export/import outcomes, `cancel()` ending a
request in flight, the atomic write); `chatbotguilogicTests` (9: the server's strategy names with "Server default"
first, which settings are sent, the connection notices); the GUI smoke tests (usage, and the old two-argument form
exits 1, which the old binary instead ran with); the launcher script test (it names the server, not `vocab.txt`).
`chatbotcliImprovedTests` (66) pass unchanged on the refactored CLI.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotGUI.cpp` (`initializeChatbot()`, removed).

- `src/ChatbotClient.{hpp,cpp}` (new), `src/ChatbotCLI.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/ChatbotGUI.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/ChatbotGUI_main.cpp`,
  `src/ChatbotGuiLogic.hpp`, `src/CMakeLists.txt`

### TD-522: `TrainerControlState` Stale Design Text, Unused `Pausing` Phase and Dead Wake Logic

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 3, 2026 | Training / Admin API | Code fix (LOW, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainerControlState.hpp` (see [TrainerControlState.md](../reference/source/TrainerControlState.md)); by inspection:
- **Stale design text:** the class and enum comments describe the always-on `incremental_trainer serve` loop; since TD-172 the state lives for one child
  pass and `trainer_service` keeps its own `TrainerServiceControlState`.
- **`TrainerPhase::Pausing` is never set** anywhere, though the enum comment and CLAUDE.md's admin-API table list `pausing` as a reported phase; a draining
  pass reports `training`/`checkpointing` then `idle`.
- **`wake()`/`interruptible_sleep()` are dead in the child** (nothing sleeps; `/admin/resume`'s `wake()` reaches no waiter); the supervisor's
  `TrainerServiceControlState` duplicates the mechanism.
- **Log ring vs log file:** `log()` stores Debug entries the logger filters out (contradicting "the same messages"), the API ignores `recent_logs()`'s
  `limit`, and messages are unbounded.
- **Phase isn't reset on an exception** in `IncrementalTrainer` (only normal and pause paths set `Idle`).

Action Items:

- [x] Update the comments for the TD-172 design; set `Pausing` while draining (or remove it from the enum and CLAUDE.md).
- [x] Remove or share the wake/sleep code; skip ring entries below the logger level; cap message length; reset the phase on exceptions.

Location in code: `src/TrainerControlState.hpp` (class/enum comments, `wake()`, `log()`); the `TODO: See TD-522` tags are removed.

**Fix (November 3, 2026):** The comments now describe the per-pass design: one `TrainerControlState` per `resume --admin-port`
pass, with `trainer_service` keeping its own state. The pass now reports `pausing`:
- The pass writes its phase through `set_phase()`.
- `/admin/pause` calls `request_pause()`, which shows a loading, tokenizing or training pass as `Pausing` straight away.
- Later phase updates stay `Pausing` until the pass drains, except `Checkpointing` and `Idle`, so a draining pass reports
  `pausing`, `checkpointing`, then `idle`.
- `/admin/resume` calls `clear_pause()`, which restores the phase the pass had.
- SIGTERM/SIGINT can only store `paused` (no locking in a signal handler), so their drain shows from the pass's next phase update.

The other changes:
- **Wake code.** The per-pass `wake()`/`interruptible_sleep()` copy is removed. Nothing sleeps in a pass, and
  `TrainerServiceControlState` keeps the supervisor's copy, the one in use.
- **Log ring.** `log()` skips messages below the logger's level, so the ring holds what the pass's log file holds. The ring's
  copy of a message is cut to 4 KiB at a UTF-8 boundary, marked " [truncated]".
- **`?limit=`.** `GET /admin/logs` takes `?limit=N` (0–200, else 400) in the pass and in the proxy, which checks it and passes
  it on. `kMaxAdminLogEntries` lives in `TrainerAdminConfig.hpp`.
- **Phase after an exception.** A new `TrainerPhaseResetOnThrow` guard in `train_on_files()`/`retrain_on_files()` resets the
  phase to `Idle` when an exception leaves the pass. The LeJEPA pass already did this.

Tests:
- `trainerControlStateTests` cover the pause transitions, the signal path, the exception guard, level filtering and the
  character-safe cut. They replace the three removed sleep tests.
- `trainerAdminApiTests` cover `pausing` and its restore in `/admin/status`, and the logs limit.
- `trainerServiceProxyTests` cover the limit, both checked and forwarded. That test fails on the old code: a bad limit was
  accepted and every entry returned.
- The other new tests call API the old code doesn't have.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainerControlState.hpp`
- `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
- `CLAUDE.md`
- `src/TrainerAdminAPI.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/TrainerAdminConfig.hpp`, `src/TrainerServiceProxy.cpp`, `src/TrainerServiceControlState.hpp`, `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`
- `tests/trainer_control_state_test.cpp`, `tests/trainer_admin_api_test.cpp`, `tests/trainer_service_proxy_test.cpp`

### TD-439: `metrics_api_server` Backend Name and Admin-Store Location Gaps

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 3, 2026 | Metrics / Server CLI | Code fix (LOW, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MetricsApiServerArgs`:
- **Unknown backend accepted (verified in the parser).** `--storage-backend postgress` (or `postgres` in a
  build without `ADAI_ENABLE_POSTGRES`) is accepted; `MetricsDatabaseFactory::create()` logs a warning and
  returns no database, so the server runs file-only while startup prints `Storage backend: postgress`.
- **Admin store location (by inspection).** `main()` puts `daemon_config.db` in the directory of the
  **file-configured** `db_path`, computed before CLI flags. With `scripts/install_metrics_service.sh`'s
  defaults that's the same directory as `--db-path`, but with a custom `--metrics-dir` it's
  `<install>/training_sessions`, which the unit's `ProtectSystem=strict` + `ReadWritePaths=<metrics dir>`
  makes read-only, so the store fails to open and admin settings can't persist.
- **Precedence (by inspection).** CLI flags beat saved admin settings, so an admin-mutable flag added to
  `ExecStart` would silently undo every `PUT /admin/config` on restart. Latent with the installer's flags.
- **Hygiene.** The header names the test `MetricsApiServerArgs_test.cpp` (it's
  `metrics_api_server_args_test.cpp`).

Action Items:

- [x] Validate `--storage-backend` against the compiled-in backends and fail at startup on an unknown one.
- [x] Locate the admin store from the final `db_path` (or a dedicated `--admin-dir`), and warn when a CLI flag overrides a saved admin value.
- [x] Fix the header comment.

Location in code: `src/MetricsApiServerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`; `src/TrainingMetricsAPIServer.cpp` (`admin_config_db_dir`); the `TODO: See TD-439` tags are removed.

**Fix (November 3, 2026):**
- **Backend name.** `--storage-backend` must be one of the five names, in any case, stored lower-case; anything else is a
  usage error. `metrics_storage_backend_names()` in `Config.hpp` is now the one list, also used by the config-file and
  environment parsers.
- **Backend support.** Before anything is written to disk, `main()` checks the final backend, whichever layer set it, with
  `check_metrics_storage_backend()`. A postgres backend in a build without `ENABLE_POSTGRES_METRICS` exits 1 with a message
  naming the backends this build has (`supported_metrics_storage_backends()`, also listed in `--help`).
- **Admin store.** `main()` first parses the flags onto a copy to find the final `db_path` (`db_path` isn't admin-mutable, so
  saved settings can't move it), then opens `daemon_config.db` in that directory (`metrics_admin_store_dir()`). Under the
  installer's unit, that is the writable `--metrics-dir`.
- **Override warnings.** The parser records which admin-mutable settings a flag set (`admin_keys_from_flags`).
  `flag_overridden_admin_settings()` then warns once for each saved value that a flag replaced with a different one.
- **Header.** The header names the right test file.

Tests:
- `metricsApiServerArgsTests` gained four tests: the backend name in any case and a typo, postgres with and without support,
  the admin store following `--db-path`, and the override warnings.
- With the real binary:
  - `--storage-backend postgres`, or `METRICS_STORAGE_BACKEND=postgres` in the file, exits 1 without creating anything.
  - `--storage-backend postgress` exits 1; the old binary ran with it.
  - `--db-path <dir>/metrics.db` puts `daemon_config.db` in `<dir>`; the old binary put it in `./training_sessions`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/MetricsApiServerArgs.hpp`
- `src/MetricsApiServerArgs.cpp`
- `src/TrainingMetricsAPIServer.cpp`
- `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}`, `tests/metrics_api_server_args_test.cpp`

### TD-308: Session Counters Reuse the Config Store's Table and Scan It per Allocation

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 3, 2026 | Core / DaemonConfigStore | Code fix (per-allocation scan with TD-304) (LOW, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-304, by inspection. `registry_server` and `LocalTransport` keep session counters
in `session_counters.db` through `DaemonConfigStore`, so the file contains a table named
`daemon_config` holding counters. Each allocation reads **every** counter ever stored via
`load_all()` to look up one key, and the table gains a row per run forever. It's cheap at today's
scale but confusing and O(runs) per allocation.

Action Items:

- [x] Add `get(key)` (or fold this into TD-304's `increment(key)`). Done November 3, 2026: `increment(key)` reads and writes
  the one key in a transaction.
- [x] Consider a dedicated counter class or table name. Done November 3, 2026: `SessionCounterStore`, table
  `session_counters`.

Location in code: `src/RegistryTransport.cpp` (`LocalTransport::next_session()`), `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`handle_session_next`); the `TODO: See TD-308` tags went with TD-304's fix.

**Fix (November 3, 2026):**
- **A dedicated store.** New `src/SessionCounterStore.{hpp,cpp}` keeps the counters in their own `session_counters` table
  with an integer `value` column. `next(key)` adds 1 and returns the new value in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction (the
  TD-304 behaviour, including the 5 s busy timeout and the restart at 1 past `INT_MAX`); `current(key)` reads one counter.
  `LocalTransport::next_session()` and `registry_server`'s `session/next` use it.
- **`DaemonConfigStore` holds admin settings only.** `increment()` is removed (version 2.0.0).
- **Existing files keep counting.** Opening a `session_counters.db` written before the change moves its `daemon_config`
  rows into `session_counters` and drops the old table, in one write transaction, so a restarted registry or trainer
  continues at the next number instead of handing out `session-01` again for a run it already numbered. A key in both
  tables keeps the larger value. The move is logged with its count. Upgrade every binary that shares one
  `session_counters.db` (a `registry_server`, or standalone trainers sharing a `SESSION_DIR`) together: an older binary
  that opens the file after the move would recreate an empty `daemon_config` table and start again at 1 (the next newer
  open merges it back, keeping the larger value).

Tests:
- New `sessionCounterStoreTests` (9): counting per key, persistence across reopen, the table name (no `daemon_config`
  table in the file), moving pre-TD-308 counters and continuing from them (7 → 8; a non-numeric value counts as 0), the
  larger value winning when both tables count a key, four concurrent opens of an old file moving it exactly once,
  restarting at 1 past `INT_MAX` or below 0, waiting for and then giving up on another writer, and 400 concurrent `next()`
  calls over four connections with no number lost or repeated. The `increment()` tests moved here from
  `daemonConfigStoreTests`.
- The real `registry_server` on a `session_counters.db` written by the old code (`m1|run-01` at 7): `session/next` answered
  `session-08` then `session-09`, logged the move, and the file was left with only the `session_counters` table.
- Test fix (November 3, 2026): a full parallel `ctest` run failed `sessionCounterStoreTests` once. Under heavy disk-sync
  load a commit can take seconds, so a thread in the concurrent-`next()` test waited past the 5 s default busy timeout,
  and its store's constructor threw outside the test's `try`, aborting the binary (reproduced: every run aborted with
  four `dd conv=fsync` loops and six CPU loops running). The two concurrency tests now open their stores with a
  120 s busy timeout (they check that nothing is lost or repeated; the timeout has its own test) and count a constructor
  failure as a test failure. Under the same load the binary then ran 198 times without a failure. No product change.

Files to Modify:

- `src/SessionCounterStore.{hpp,cpp}` (new), `src/DaemonConfigStore.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/RegistryTransport.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/RegistryServer.cpp`, `src/CMakeLists.txt`
- `tests/sessioncounterstore_test.cpp` (new), `tests/daemonconfigstore_test.cpp`, `tests/CMakeLists.txt`

### TD-307: `DaemonConfigStore::load_all()` Hides Read Errors

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 3, 2026 | Core / DaemonConfigStore | Code fix (LOW, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-304, by inspection. `load_all()` stops at the first non-`SQLITE_ROW` step result
without checking whether it was an error, so a mid-scan failure returns a partial map with no
warning. The `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` result is ignored: on filesystems without shared memory,
SQLite falls back to rollback journalling where readers can be blocked, so a daemon's startup
overlay can silently drop persisted overrides.

Action Items:

- [x] Check the final step result and warn (or throw) on errors; log when WAL couldn't be enabled.

Location in code: `src/DaemonConfigStore.cpp` (constructor, `load_all()`); the `TODO: See TD-307` tags are removed.

**Fix (November 3, 2026):**
- **Read errors throw.** `load_all()` throws `std::runtime_error` when a step fails partway through
  (`read failed after N row(s): …`) or when the table can't be prepared at all. These used to end silently with the rows
  before the error, or an empty map with a warning. Every caller already catches the throw and starts from its file/CLI
  settings with a warning, so a daemon now loads all of its saved settings or none of them, and says which.
- **Accurate warnings.** `registry_server` and the trainer's per-pass admin API said "admin config changes won't persist"
  for any failure. A store that opened but couldn't be read still saves later PUTs, so they now say that only when the store
  didn't open.
- **WAL checked.** The constructor reads back the mode `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` actually set, keeps it as
  `journal_mode()`, and logs a warning when it isn't `wal`.

Tests:
- `daemonConfigStoreTests` gained three:
  - a view in place of the table whose second row fails to evaluate makes `load_all()` throw `read failed after 1 row(s)`;
    the old code returned the first row;
  - a dropped table makes it throw; the old code returned an empty map;
  - `journal_mode()` is `wal` for a file and `memory` for `:memory:`, which logs the warning.
- With the real `registry_server`, a `daemon_config.db` whose second saved row can't be read:
  - the old binary silently applied the first saved setting (`ftp_max_sessions_per_run` 9) and dropped the other;
  - the new one warns and starts from the file values (4 and 30).

Files to Modify:

- `src/DaemonConfigStore.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/RegistryServer.cpp`, `src/TrainerAdminAPI.cpp` (warning text)
- `tests/daemonconfigstore_test.cpp`

### TD-306: `registry_server` and `metrics_api_server` Admin PUTs Don't Range-Check Values

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 3, 2026 | Admin config API | Code fix (LOW, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-304, by inspection. `registry_server`'s `PUT /admin/config` accepts any integer
for `ftp_token_ttl_minutes`/`ftp_max_sessions_per_run`, and `metrics_api_server`'s accepts any
integer for its nine tunables. Negative values are applied and persisted; a negative
`max_live_sessions` is cast to `size_t` and becomes enormous. The trainer PUTs already validate their
ranges.

Action Items:

- [x] Add range checks matching each setting's meaning and return 400 for out-of-range values (validating all keys first, per TD-305).

Location in code: `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (admin PUT handler), `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp` (admin PUT handler); the `TODO: See TD-306` tags are removed.

**Fix (November 3, 2026):**
- **One range table per daemon.** `Config.hpp` has `metrics_admin_int_settings()` (11 settings) and
  `registry_admin_int_settings()` (2), with minimums matching `ConfigLoader::validate()`: TTL, live sessions, memory records
  and the staleness threshold at least 1, the rest at least 0 (0 meaning off or no limit), all at most `INT_MAX`. The PUT
  handlers, the saved-override loaders and `metrics_api_server`'s flags all read them, so the three can't drift.
- **Whole body first.** Both handlers parse the body with nlohmann/json and check every key before applying any. A value
  that isn't a whole number in range, a non-boolean `enable_prometheus`, an immutable key, a body that isn't a JSON object,
  or no recognized key gets 400 naming the key and its range (`'max_live_sessions' must be a whole number >= 1`), and nothing
  changes. `registry_server`'s check is `parse_registry_admin_config()` in `RegistryServerArgs`, so it is unit-tested.
- **Spacing.** `metrics_api_server` used to find keys by substring, so `"key" : 5` (a space before the colon) was skipped
  silently. Any JSON spacing now works.

Tests:
- `registryServerArgsTests` gained four tests: valid values, out-of-range and non-integer values rejected with nothing
  applied (including a valid key next to a bad one), immutable, unknown and malformed bodies, and a saved override held to the
  same range.
- `trainingMetricsApiRoutesTests` gained two: ten bad bodies each get 400 and change nothing (these got 200 on the old code),
  and boundary values (`max_live_sessions` 1, sweep 0, retention 0) are accepted with any spacing.
- With the real binaries: `{"ftp_token_ttl_minutes": -5}` gets 400 and `daemon_config.db` keeps its value; the old
  `registry_server` answered 200 and saved `-5`, which issues FTP tokens that are already expired.
  `{"max_live_sessions": -1}` gets 400 from `metrics_api_server`.

TD-305's atomic multi-key persistence is still open.

- `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp`, `src/MetricsApiServerArgs.cpp`, `src/Config.hpp`
- `tests/registry_server_args_test.cpp`, `tests/training_metrics_api_routes_test.cpp`, `tests/CMakeLists.txt`

### TD-305: A Rejected or Failed `PUT /admin/config` Still Partly Applies

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 3, 2026 | Admin config API | Code fix (validate-first part October 19, 2026, with TD-519) (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-304, by inspection. Two problems:

- **Trainer PUTs apply keys before validating later ones.** Both `TrainerAdminAPI::handle_put_config()`
  and `TrainerServiceProxy::handle_put_config_idle()` apply the body key by key and return 400 at the
  first invalid value. `{"auto_save_enabled":false,"auto_save_every_samples":-5}` is rejected with 400,
  but auto-save is already off:
  - in a live child, in memory only, so live state and `daemon_config.db` disagree;
  - in the idle proxy, already written to the DB, so the next pass starts with auto-save off.
- **Multi-key persistence isn't atomic in any daemon.** `TrainerAdminAPI`, `ModelNameService`,
  `TrainingMetricsAPI` and `registry_server` call `DaemonConfigStore::set()` once per key with no
  transaction, after the in-memory state is already updated. If one `set()` throws (e.g. locked,
  TD-304), earlier keys are persisted and later ones aren't, and the exception escapes the handler,
  so the client sees an error for a change that partly applied and will partly revert on restart.

Action Items:

- [x] Validate every key in the body before applying or persisting any of them. Done October 19, 2026 for both trainer handlers with TD-519's
  shared `parse_trainer_admin_config()`; the tests now include a body whose third key is invalid, which changes nothing.
- [x] Add `DaemonConfigStore::set_many()` (one transaction) and persist before (or atomically with) updating in-memory state; return a clear 500 when persistence fails.
- [x] Tests: a body with one invalid key changes nothing; a persistence failure leaves memory and DB consistent.

Location in code: `src/TrainerAdminAPI.cpp` (`handle_put_config()`), `src/TrainerServiceProxy.cpp` (`handle_put_config_idle()`), `src/DaemonConfigStore.hpp`; the `TODO: See TD-305` tags are removed.

**Fix (November 3, 2026):**
- **One transaction.** `DaemonConfigStore::set_many()` writes every pair inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE … COMMIT`. If anything
  fails, it rolls back and throws, so either all the pairs are stored or none are.
- **Save, then apply.** All five `PUT /admin/config` handlers (the trainer's per-pass API, `trainer_service`'s idle proxy,
  `mns_server`, `metrics_api_server` and `registry_server`) work out the resulting values and save them with `set_many()`.
  They change the in-memory settings only after the save worked. A failed save answers 500 with valid JSON
  (`could not save the admin config (<reason>); nothing was changed`), logs the reason, and leaves memory and
  `daemon_config.db` as they were. Before, the exception escaped the handler: the trainer API answered with httplib's
  non-JSON error page after already changing its settings in memory.
- **One PUT at a time.** Each handler holds its own mutex while it saves and applies, so two concurrent PUTs can't save in
  one order and apply in the other. `DaemonConfigStore`'s comment used to claim callers already serialized access, but the
  httplib handlers run on a thread pool.

Tests:
- `daemonConfigStoreTests` gained three: `set_many()` stores every pair; a failure partway through, forced by a trigger that
  rejects one key, stores none of them, and the store still works afterwards; and a write lock held by another connection
  makes it throw and store nothing.
- `trainerAdminApiTests`, `trainerServiceProxyTests` and `trainingMetricsApiRoutesTests` each gained one: while another
  connection holds `daemon_config.db`'s write lock, a PUT answers 500 and changes nothing in memory or on disk. On the old
  handlers, the trainer API answered with a non-JSON page after turning auto-save off and changing retention in memory; the
  metrics API changed `retention_days` and `max_live_sessions` in memory; the idle proxy failed only the message check,
  because its first `set()` already failed there.
- With the real `mns_server` and `registry_server`, a PUT made while a Python script holds the lock answers 500, and
  `GET /admin/config` and `daemon_config.db` keep their previous values.

Since TD-304, a save that overlaps another writer waits up to 5 s for it, and the handler tests use a trigger to
make the save fail.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DaemonConfigStore.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/TrainerAdminAPI.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/TrainerServiceProxy.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/ModelNameService.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.{hpp,cpp}`

- `tests/daemonconfigstore_test.cpp`, `tests/trainer_admin_api_test.cpp`, `tests/trainer_service_proxy_test.cpp`,

### TD-304: Session Counters Can Be Duplicated and `DaemonConfigStore` Has No Busy Timeout

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 3, 2026 | Core / DaemonConfigStore | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [DaemonConfigStore.md](../reference/source/DaemonConfigStore.md) and confirmed by running the real
class. `DaemonConfigStore` never sets `sqlite3_busy_timeout()`, so any write while another
connection holds the write lock fails immediately: with a second connection in a write
transaction, `set()` threw `database is locked` after 0.1 ms.

`LocalTransport::next_session()` (standalone trainers, no `REGISTRY_SERVER_URL`) allocates session
numbers as `load_all()` → `+1` → `set()` with no transaction and no lock. Two processes each doing
200 such increments against one `session_counters.db`:
- 284 of 400 calls **threw** (`database is locked`);
- the counter ended at **113** although 116 calls reported success, so 3 increments were lost (two
  callers handed the same session number).

`IncrementalTrainer::begin_run()` catches the throw and continues with an **empty** session ID.
`registry_server`'s `handle_session_next` is safe within one process (it holds
`g_session_store_mtx`) but would race the same way across processes. `trainer_service` and its child
also share `TRAINER_ADMIN_DIR/daemon_config.db`, so a write overlapping a child's start or exit
fails instead of waiting.

Action Items:

- [x] Set `sqlite3_busy_timeout()` (e.g. 5 s) in the constructor.
- [x] Add an atomic `increment(key)` (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` read-modify-write, or `UPDATE … RETURNING`) and use it in both `next_session()` implementations.
- [x] Tests: two connections writing concurrently both succeed; concurrent increments are never lost or duplicated.

Location in code: `src/DaemonConfigStore.cpp` (constructor, `set()`), `src/RegistryTransport.cpp` (`LocalTransport::next_session()`), `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`handle_session_next`); the `TODO: See TD-304` tags are removed.

**Fix (November 3, 2026):**
- **Busy timeout.** The constructor sets `sqlite3_busy_timeout()` before anything else touches the file. The default is
  `DaemonConfigStore::kDefaultBusyTimeoutMs` (5 s), and a constructor parameter lets tests shorten it. A write that meets
  another writer now waits for it rather than failing at once, which also covers `trainer_service` and its pass sharing
  `daemon_config.db`.
- **Atomic counter.** `increment(key)` reads the key's value and writes it back plus one inside a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`
  transaction, and returns the new number. A missing or non-numeric value counts as 0, as before. Both
  `LocalTransport::next_session()` and `registry_server`'s `handle_session_next` use it, so processes sharing
  `session_counters.db` can no longer be handed the same number. It reads one key instead of `load_all()` (TD-308's scan).
- **Errors.** `handle_session_next` answers 500 with JSON when `increment()` throws. It used to let the exception escape.
  `LocalTransport`'s throw still reaches `IncrementalTrainer::begin_run()`, which logs it and continues without a session id.

Tests:
- `daemonConfigStoreTests` gained three:
  - `set()`, `set_many()` and `increment()` all wait for a writer that releases the lock after 300 ms;
  - `increment()` counts per key and treats a non-numeric value as 0;
  - four threads, each with its own connection, run 400 increments with no failures, no repeated number, and a final count
    of 400.
- With `sqlite3_busy_timeout()` taken out, all three writes in the first test throw `database is locked`.
- The TD-305 handler tests used a held write lock to make a save fail; with the timeout that would now wait. They use a
  trigger that rejects writes instead.
- With the real binaries: two `registry_server` processes on one data directory, each sent 100 concurrent
  `session/next` requests for the same run. All 200 answers were different numbers and the counter ended at 200. On the old
  code, the second process couldn't open `session_counters.db` at startup (no busy timeout while the first held the lock), so
  its 100 requests got `session_counters.db unavailable`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DaemonConfigStore.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/RegistryTransport.cpp`
- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `tests/daemonconfigstore_test.cpp`; the TD-305 tests in `tests/trainer_admin_api_test.cpp`,
  `tests/trainer_service_proxy_test.cpp` and `tests/training_metrics_api_routes_test.cpp`

### TD-259: `chatbot` Code Hygiene: Unchecked `/set` Values, Global Helpers, Heavy Header

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 3, 2026 | Client / CLI | Code fix (`/set` value checks with TD-254) (LOW, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-253:

- `/set` numbers use `std::stoi`/`std::stof`, which accept partial input (`10abc` → 10), and
  nothing range-checks them (negative length, `top_p` 5). Moot while TD-254 stands.
- `escape_json_string()`, `unescape_json_string()` and `parse_json_value()` in `ChatbotCLI.cpp`
  have external linkage at global scope, so another translation unit defining the same global names
  would collide (`MetricsPushClient.cpp` is safe only because its copy is in an anonymous namespace).
- `ChatbotCLI.hpp` includes all of `httplib.h` (via an unusual `<../external/...>` path) and
  `#define`s the `COLOR_*` macros for every includer.

Action Items:

- [x] Use full-consumption parsing and range checks for `/set` values. Done November 3, 2026 with TD-254 (`GenerationLimits`).
- [x] Move the JSON helpers into an anonymous namespace (or replace them with nlohmann/json). Replaced with nlohmann/json.
- [x] Forward-declare `httplib::Client` in the header (pimpl or `unique_ptr` to an incomplete type) and move the colour macros to `constexpr` values in the `.cpp`.

**Fix (November 3, 2026):**

- The three global helpers are gone. Request bodies are `nlohmann::ordered_json` dumped with invalid UTF-8 replaced
  by U+FFFD (a Latin-1 `café` used to make the chat request invalid JSON). Replies are parsed once and only their
  top-level fields read, so `\uXXXX` escapes are decoded (`caf\u00e9` used to be shown as written), a nested field of the same name is no longer read in place of the real one, and pretty-printed
  replies read cleanly. A reply that isn't JSON is an error with its status. `/set` floats are sent in their shortest
  form.
- `ChatbotCLI.hpp` forward-declares `httplib::Client` and no longer includes `httplib.h`; the move operations are
  defaulted in the `.cpp`, and `post_chat_turn()` became a lambda in `generate_response()`. The `COLOR_*` macros are
  `constexpr` constants in `ChatbotCLI.cpp`. The `chatbot` target adds `external/` for nlohmann/json.
- Checked with the real binaries against a stub server: given `café` from a Latin-1 terminal and a reply holding a
  nested `response`, the old `chatbot` sent invalid JSON and printed the nested value; the new one sent valid JSON and
  printed `café ok`.

Tests: in `chatbotcliImprovedTests`, `ChatbotCLIHeaderTest` (3, using the new `tests/chatbotcli_header_test.cpp`,
which includes only `ChatbotCLI.hpp` and defines the old global helper names), four `ChatbotCLIErrorReplyTest`
reply-parsing tests and two request-body tests. On the old code the binary fails to link (multiple definition of
the helpers); with those names renamed, six tests fail. `ColorCodeTest` was removed.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChatbotCLI.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/CMakeLists.txt`
- `tests/chatbotcli_improved_test.cpp`, `tests/chatbotcli_header_test.cpp` (new), `tests/CMakeLists.txt`
- `docs/development/reference/source/ChatbotCLI.md`

### TD-258: `chatbot` Can Lose or Overwrite Saved Conversations

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 3, 2026 | Client / CLI | Code fix (LOW, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-253:

- No `SIGINT` handling: Ctrl+C kills the process without the auto-save that `/exit` performs.
- The `/exit` auto-save always writes the same file, so starting a new conversation and exiting
  **silently overwrites** a previously saved one.
- Saves truncate and then write (not atomic), so a crash mid-write leaves a partial file.
- After a server restart, the CLI keeps sending its old `session_id` and the server silently
  creates a fresh, empty session under it (TD-232), so the history disappears with no message.

Action Items:

- [x] Handle `SIGINT` by setting a flag the REPL checks, then auto-save and exit.
- [x] Warn (or prompt) before an auto-save would overwrite a file the current session didn't load; consider timestamped files.
- [x] Write saves to a temporary file and rename.
- [x] Detect a reset session (e.g. `message_count` from the server) and tell the user.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotCLI.cpp` (`run()`, `save_conversation()`); the `TODO: See TD-258` tags are removed.

**Fix (November 3, 2026):**

- **Ctrl+C:** `run()` installs a `SIGINT` handler for its duration (a file-local `InterruptHandler`, restoring the
  previous handler on return) that only sets a `sig_atomic_t` flag. It is installed without `SA_RESTART`, so a read
  waiting at the prompt returns, and with `SA_RESETHAND`, so a second Ctrl+C ends the process at once. The loop checks
  the flag before each prompt and after each read: Ctrl+C at the prompt prints `Interrupted` and ends the session like
  `/exit` (with its save); during a reply, the reply arrives first (cpp-httplib retries reads interrupted by a signal),
  then the session ends without reading more input. Windows uses `std::signal()`.
- **No silent overwrite:** the client tracks the file its conversation is saved to (`get_active_save_path()`) and
  whether that file holds this session's conversation (it loaded or saved it there). A save that would replace an
  existing file that doesn't goes instead to a new file named after it with the local date and time
  (`conversation_history-20261103-142501.txt`, then `-2`, `-3` … if taken), which later saves keep using, and says why.
  `/load` makes the loaded file the save target again. This applies to `/save` as well as the auto-save, since both
  would have lost the earlier conversation.
- **Atomic saves:** each save writes `<target>.tmp-<n>` beside the target and renames it over the target; on any
  failure the temporary is removed and the previous file is untouched.
- **Lost session:** since TD-232 the server answers 404 for a session it no longer holds, so the client never reuses
  a dead id silently. On that 404 (chat, `/clear` or the save's export) the client now says the server has forgotten
  the earlier messages and, when they were saved, where (`/load restores them` for the configured file), starts a new
  session, and stops treating the save file as the new session's, so the next save doesn't replace the earlier
  conversation with only what followed. An export that gets 404 writes nothing.

Tests:
- `chatbotcliImprovedTests` gained eight tests (58 in all, all passing):
  - `ChatbotCLISaveTest` against a stub server that also answers export and import: an existing file this session
    didn't load is kept and the conversation saved, twice, to one dated file; a loaded file is saved back in place; a
    new file is created with no temporary left behind; a save into a directory that takes no new files keeps the
    previous file (the old code truncated and rewrote it in place); a lost session after `/load` is reported with
    `/load restores them` and leaves the file alone; an export answered 404 writes nothing.
  - `ChatbotCLIInterruptTest`: `SIGINT` raised in the test process where the next read would wait (as a terminal read
    returns on Ctrl+C) saves and exits and restores the default handler; `SIGINT` raised while the stub answers a chat
    request lets that reply print, then saves and exits without sending the next line.
  - On the old code the four save tests that check keeping files or the lost-session message fail, and both interrupt
    tests end the test process by `SIGINT` (they signal only themselves). `LostSessionStartsANewOneAndTheTurnSucceeds`
    now checks the new messages.
- The old and new `chatbot` binaries were run against a Python stub server. With an earlier conversation on disk,
  `hello` then `/exit`: the old binary replaced it; the new one kept it and saved to
  `conversation_history-20261103-213822.txt`. After `hello`, `SIGINT` sent to the `chatbot` process the script started:
  the old binary died by the signal with nothing saved; the new one printed `Interrupted`, saved and exited 0.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChatbotCLI.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/chatbotcli_improved_test.cpp`
- `docs/operations/guides/chatbot-guide.md`

### TD-255: `chatbot` Shows Server Error Replies as Empty Responses

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 3, 2026 | Client / CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-253 and confirmed against a stub server. `generate_response()` treats any
HTTP 200 reply as success and prints its `response` field. `ChatbotAPI` returns HTTP 200 with
`{"success":false,"error":...}` for errors it returns rather than throws (TD-236). The CLI doesn't
check `success`, so the user sees an empty `Bot:` line and the error message is lost. Thrown server
errors (HTTP 500) are printed as the raw JSON body.

Action Items:

- [x] Check `success`; on `false`, print the `error` field in `COLOR_ERROR`.
- [x] Print only the `error` field (not the raw JSON) for non-200 replies.
- [x] Test with a stub returning `success:false`.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotCLI.cpp` (`generate_response()`, `run()`); the `TODO: See TD-255` tag is removed.

**Fix (November 3, 2026):** since TD-236 the server sends its errors with HTTP 400 or 500, so the raw-JSON case is the
one users meet today; HTTP 200 with `"success":false` is still handled for older servers.
- `generate_response()` treats a reply as a success only when it is HTTP 200 and `success` isn't `false`. Otherwise it
  returns `Error: <status> - <error>` (no status for a 200), adds `(request id …)` when the server sent one (TD-238's
  500s), says the server gave no reason when a `success:false` reply has no `error`, and shows only the status for a body
  with no `error` field (for example a proxy's HTML page).
- `did_last_turn_fail()` reports whether the last turn failed, and `run()` prints a failed turn in `COLOR_ERROR`.

Tests:
- `chatbotcliImprovedTests` gained eight. Against a stub server: HTTP 200 with `success:false` (with and without an
  `error`), a 400 whose message contains quotes, a 500 with a request id, a 502 with an HTML body, a successful reply,
  and `run()` printing the error in `COLOR_ERROR`. Against the real test `ChatbotAPI`: a temperature of 9 set through the
  setter, which skips `/set`'s checks, comes back as `Error: 400 - …temperature…` with no JSON.
- The new tests call `did_last_turn_fail()`, which the old code doesn't have, so the old and new `chatbot` binaries were
  compared against a stub server instead (`printf 'hello\n' | chatbot <url>`):
  - 200 `{"success":false,"error":"model is busy"}`: the old binary printed an empty `Bot:` line, the new one
    `Error: model is busy` in red;
  - 400: old `Error: 400 - {"success":false,"error":"\"temperature\" must be between 0 and 2"}`, new
    `Error: 400 - "temperature" must be between 0 and 2`;
  - 500: old `Error: 500 - {"success":false,"error":"Internal server error","request_id":"r-42"}`, new
    `Error: 500 - Internal server error (request id r-42)`.

### TD-254: `chatbot`'s `/set` Generation Settings Have No Effect

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 3, 2026 | Client / CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-253 and confirmed by running the real binary: after `/set temp 0.2` the next
request body carried `"temperature":0.2`. `ChatbotCLI::generate_response()` sends `max_length`,
`temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `beam_width` and `strategy` with every message, but
`ChatbotAPI`'s handlers ignore them and always use the server's defaults (see
[ChatbotAPI.md](../reference/source/ChatbotAPI.md) §3). The CLI confirms each `/set` and
`/settings` shows the new values, yet generation never changes. The strategy names also don't
match: the CLI accepts `sampling` and `top-k`, the server uses `temperature` and `top_k`, so even a
server that honoured them would fall back to `nucleus`. The user guide
([chatbot-guide.md](../../operations/guides/chatbot-guide.md)) documents `/set` as working (its
Generation Strategies section is already flagged under TD-164).

Action Items:

- [x] Owner decision: support per-request generation settings in `ChatbotAPI` (validated and bounded; easiest after TD-226's nlohmann/json switch), or remove the per-request settings from the CLI. Decided November 3, 2026: the server honours them.
- [x] If supported: align strategy names on the server's (`temperature`, `top_k`) and accept the CLI's old names as aliases.
- [x] Update `chatbot-guide.md` either way.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotCLI.cpp` (`handle_setting()`, `chat_turn_body()`), `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (`generation_config_for()`); the `TODO: See TD-254` tags are removed.

**Fix (November 3, 2026), owner's choice: the server honours per-request settings.**
- **One set of limits.** New `src/GenerationSettings.{hpp,cpp}`: `adai::GenerationLimits` (length 1-4096, temperature
  0-2, top_p 0-1, top_k 1-1000, beam width 1-16) and `canonical_generation_strategy()`, which maps any case of the
  server's names, plus the CLI's old `sampling`/`top-k` and `top_p`/`top-p`, to the server's names. `ConfigLoader::validate()`
  checks the server's defaults against the same limits, `ChatbotAPI` checks requests, and `chatbot` checks `/set` values
  (the file is compiled into `chatbot`, which doesn't link `adai_core`).
- **The server.** `ChatbotAPI::generation_config_for(request_body)` copies the defaults and applies any of `max_length`,
  `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `beam_width` and `strategy` the request sets, for that request only; `/chat`,
  `/chat/session`, `/chat/batch` and `/chat/batch-session` all use it. A wrong type or out-of-range value is HTTP 400
  naming the field and its range, and nothing is generated; `/chat/session` checks before it touches the session.
  `null` counts as absent.
- **The CLI sends only what was changed.** It used to send all six settings with its own built-in values on every
  message; honouring those would have silently overridden every server's configured defaults. Now it sends only settings
  changed with `/set`, `/set <parameter> default` stops sending one, and `/settings` shows `server default` for the rest.
  `/set` values must be whole numbers in range (TD-259's first item: `10abc` was read as 10, and a negative length or
  `top_p 5` was accepted).
- `chatbot-guide.md` describes `/set`, `/settings` and the real ranges; `rest-api.md` documents the request fields.

Tests:
- `chatbotapiTests` gained five: request settings replace the defaults and only those sent (`null` ignored, defaults
  untouched); every strategy name and alias; 16 out-of-range or mistyped bodies refused and the limits accepted; a
  refused request creates no session and leaves an existing conversation as it was, on all four handlers; and
  `max_length: 1` caps the `/chat` and `/chat/session` replies at one token where the default allows 40 (100 repeats, no
  failures).
- `chatbotcliImprovedTests` gained six: unchanged settings aren't sent, changed ones are (strategy aliases sent as the
  server's names), `/set … default`, partial and out-of-range values refused, `/settings`, and a `/set length 1` turn
  against the real test `ChatbotAPI` returning at most one token.
- The new tests use methods the old code doesn't have, so they were not run against it. The real `chatbot_api_server`
  (untrained model, `MAX_GEN_LENGTH=40`, greedy) was compared instead:
  - `"temperature":9` and `"strategy":"fast"`: HTTP 200 on the old binary, 400 on the new one;
  - reply length with `"max_length":1`: 110 characters on the old binary (the same as without it), 2 on the new one
    (146 without it).
