### TD-253: `chatbot` Spins Forever at End of Input

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 3, 2026 | Client / CLI | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [ChatbotCLI.md](../reference/source/ChatbotCLI.md), and confirmed by running the real
`chatbot` binary against a stub server. `ChatbotCLI::run()` never checks `std::getline()`'s result.
At EOF (Ctrl+D in a terminal, or stdin from a file or pipe running out) `getline` fails and leaves
the line empty, the empty-line check `continue`s, and the loop prints `You: ` forever. With stdin
at EOF it printed **18.6 million prompts (284 MB) in 3 seconds** before being killed: in a
terminal it pins a CPU core, and with output redirected it fills the disk at about 95 MB/s. It
also never reaches the `/exit` auto-save. The old internals doc listed Ctrl+D as an exit path.

Action Items:

- [x] Break out of the loop when `std::getline()` fails (`if (!std::getline(std::cin, user_input)) break;`), running the same auto-save as `/exit`.
- [x] Test: `chatbot < /dev/null` against a stub server exits promptly with status 0.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotCLI.cpp` (`run()`); the `TODO: See TD-253` tag is removed.

**Fix (November 3, 2026):**
- **End of input is `/exit`.** `run()` checks `std::getline()`'s result; when it fails it finishes the `You: ` line and
  handles the input as `/exit`, so the conversation is saved (when a message was sent) and `Goodbye!` printed, and the
  process exits 0.
- **A second symptom, found while testing.** When the input's last line has no newline (`printf 'hello' | chatbot`),
  the old loop didn't spin on an empty line: a failed `getline()` leaves the string unchanged, so it sent `hello` to the
  server again on every pass. Against a stub server the old binary sent **4,322 requests in 3 seconds**, never saved, and
  had to be killed. The fix covers it too: that line is sent once.
- The user guide says Ctrl+D and the end of piped input end (and save) the session, and its batch example no longer
  needs a trailing `/exit`.

Tests:
- `chatbotcliImprovedTests` gained three, each running the real `run()` against the test `ChatbotAPI` with `std::cin`
  fed from a string. A guard on `std::cout` feeds `/exit` after 50 prompts, so the old code fails instead of hanging:
  - empty input ends the session after one prompt without saving; the old code hit the guard;
  - a message, a blank line and then end of input saves the conversation (2 messages); the old code hit the guard;
  - a last line without a newline is sent once and saved; the old code re-sent it until the guard.
- The real `chatbot` against a stub server: `< /dev/null` exits 0 at once (817 bytes of output); `printf 'hello' |`
  sends one `/chat/session` and one `/chat/session/export` request, then exits 0.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChatbotCLI.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/chatbotcli_improved_test.cpp`
- `docs/operations/guides/chatbot-guide.md`

### TD-525: `TrainerServiceProxy` Misreports Long Checkpoint Waits and Idle Config

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Training / Service Supervisor | Code fix (LOW, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainerServiceProxy.cpp` (see [TrainerServiceProxy.md](../reference/source/TrainerServiceProxy.md)); verified with the real proxy and
a real child `TrainerAdminAPI`:
- **Checkpoint waits:** proxied requests use a 5 s read timeout while the child honours any `wait_ms`. `POST /admin/checkpoint?wait_ms=8000` returned
  **503 "training pass is starting or exiting; try again shortly"** (after 10 s, with httplib retrying once) although the child had set
  `checkpoint_requested`; a retry requests another checkpoint. The same 503 text is returned for every request when the child's admin API failed to bind.
- **Idle config:** with no child, `GET /admin/config` overlays `daemon_config.db` onto hardcoded defaults and never reads `config.trainer.conf`, which the
  child seeds from; a child seeded with 250 samples reported 250, the idle proxy 1000. The shipped config matches the hardcoded defaults, which hides it.
- **By inspection:** `wait_ms` is re-inserted into the proxied path unencoded; `paused` in `/admin/status` is the child's flag during a pass and the
  supervisor's when idle; a new client per request; pause/resume proxy failures ignored.

Action Items:

- [x] Set the checkpoint proxy's read timeout from `wait_ms` (capped, with TD-521); return a distinct error for a timeout vs a refused connection.
- [x] Pass the loaded `ServiceConfig` tunables to the proxy as the idle defaults.
- [x] Encode `wait_ms` (or parse it as an integer); log failed pause/resume proxies.

**Fix (November 2, 2026):** the proxy parses `wait_ms` as a whole number from 0 to 300,000 (5 minutes, lowered to the
pass's own 60,000 by TD-521 the same day, `TrainerServiceProxy::kMaxCheckpointWaitMs`; anything else is a 400), rebuilds the proxied path from the number, and waits
`wait_ms` + 5 s for the child's answer. One `proxy()` replaces the three per-method helpers and tells failures apart: a
refused connection is still 503 "starting or exiting", while a child that took the request and didn't answer in time is
504 "did not answer within N s; the request may still have been applied". `trainer_service` passes the loaded
`config.trainer.conf` tunables to the proxy (`TrainerAdminDefaults`), and the idle `GET /admin/config` overlays
`daemon_config.db` on them, as the next pass does. A pause or resume the running pass doesn't accept is logged. `paused`
meaning the child's flag during a pass is left as is: `supervisor_paused` already reports the service's flag. New tests
(`trainer_service_proxy_test.cpp`): a checkpoint that completes 6 s into a 10 s wait is relayed as the child's 202
(503 on the old code), malformed and oversized `wait_ms` are 400s, a child that never answers is a 504, and the idle
config reports the given defaults with an override on top.

Location in code: `src/TrainerServiceProxy.{hpp,cpp}` (checkpoint route, `proxy()`, `handle_get_config_idle()`), `src/TrainerServiceMain.cpp`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainerServiceProxy.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/TrainerServiceMain.cpp`
- `tests/trainer_service_proxy_test.cpp`

### TD-524: `trainer_service` Child Port, Binary Resolution, Backoff and Unit Write Paths

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Training / Service Supervisor | Code fix (LOW, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainerServiceMain.cpp` and `scripts/adai-trainer.service` (by inspection):
- **Child admin port with admin disabled:** `--admin-port` is always passed, so each child binds `127.0.0.1:TRAINER_CHILD_ADMIN_PORT` (8085) even with
  `TRAINER_ADMIN_ENABLED=false`, contrary to the opt-in "no new ports" intent in CLAUDE.md.
- **`PATH` fallback:** started by a bare name, `trainer_service` launches whichever `incremental_trainer` is first on `PATH`, possibly a different version
  from the one installed beside it.
- **No backoff:** a fixed 45 s after crashes or launch failures. (Since October 19, 2026, TD-523 backs off failed and crashed passes; a failed
  `ChildProcess::start()` still retries after a fixed 45 s.)
- **Unit write paths:** `adai-trainer.service` sets `ProtectSystem=strict` with `ReadWritePaths` that omit `/opt/adai/downloads` (the default
  `DOWNLOAD_DIR=downloads` under `WorkingDirectory=/opt/adai`), so FTP downloads would fail read-only under the shipped unit; the empty-`LOG_FILE_PATH`
  fallback log in the working directory likewise (TD-431).

Action Items:

- [x] Pass `--admin-port` only when the admin API is enabled; resolve the child next to the real executable path (`/proc/self/exe`), not `PATH`.
- [x] Exponential backoff on consecutive crashes/failures (done for failed and crashed passes with TD-523; launch failures remain); add the download directory to `ReadWritePaths` (and set `LOG_FILE_PATH` in the shipped config).

**Fix (November 2, 2026):**
- **Child admin port.** `trainer_service_child_argv()` takes the port as optional; `trainer_service` passes it only with
  `TRAINER_ADMIN_ENABLED`, so with the admin API off no pass opens a port.
- **Binary resolution.** The new `sibling_executable_path()` (`IncrementalTrainerArgs`) finds `incremental_trainer` in
  the running executable's own directory (`/proc/self/exe`, or the module path on Windows), then argv[0]'s, and uses a
  `PATH` search only when neither is known (with a warning).
- **Launch failures** back off like failed passes (45 s doubling to 15 min, counted in `consecutive_failures`).
- **Unit.** `adai-trainer.service`'s `ReadWritePaths` gains `/opt/adai/downloads`, with a leading `-` on the optional
  directories so a missing one doesn't stop the unit starting; the generated `--with-systemd` unit in
  `install_incremental_trainer.sh` gains `downloads` too, and the script now creates `downloads` and `tokenized_cache`.
  `LOG_FILE_PATH` is documented in the unit and `config.trainer.conf` as needed under `ProtectSystem=strict`; it's not
  set in the shipped config because TD-431 decides what an empty value should mean.

Tests: `TrainerServiceChildArgv.NoAdminPortWithoutTheAdminApi`, `SiblingExecutablePath.UsesTheRunningExecutablesDirectory`
and `SighupTest.TrainerServiceLaunchesItsSiblingAndPassesTheAdminPortOnlyWhenEnabled` (a copy of `trainer_service`
started by bare name with a decoy `incremental_trainer` first on `PATH`: the stub beside it runs, without
`--admin-port` while the API is off and with it when on). The old binary ran the decoy and passed `--admin-port`
with the API off. `systemd-analyze verify` accepts the unit. The launch-failure backoff is tested since TD-278 made a failed
`exec` a launch failure (`SighupTest.TrainerServiceReportsAChildItCannotExecute`).

Location in code: `src/TrainerServiceMain.cpp` (child argv, loop), `src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`,
`scripts/adai-trainer.service`, `scripts/install_incremental_trainer.sh`, `config.trainer.conf`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainerServiceMain.cpp`
- `scripts/adai-trainer.service`
- `config.trainer.conf`

### TD-521: `TrainerAdminAPI` Stale Header, Unbounded `wait_ms` and Checkpoint Accounting

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Training / Admin API | Code fix (LOW, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainerAdminAPI.{hpp,cpp}` (by inspection): the header still calls the class the "always-on HTTP admin daemon for
`incremental_trainer serve`" (removed by TD-172; it now lives for one child pass behind `trainer_service`'s proxy); `POST /admin/checkpoint?wait_ms=N`
holds an httplib worker for any N, so a few long waits can exhaust the pool; completion is judged by `checkpoints_written` increasing, so an auto-save
landing during the wait is reported as the requested checkpoint; persisted overrides loaded in `start()` aren't range-checked (only `PUT` validates).

Action Items:

- [x] Rewrite the header for the TD-172 design; cap `wait_ms` (e.g. 60 s); track forced checkpoints separately; validate overrides on load.

**Fix (November 2, 2026):** the class comment describes the per-pass API behind `trainer_service`'s proxy. `wait_ms`
must be a whole number from 0 to `kMaxCheckpointWaitMs` (60,000, `TrainerAdminConfig.hpp`), else 400, and the proxy
uses the same limit (it was 300,000 under TD-525). Requested checkpoints are numbered: `POST /admin/checkpoint` takes a
ticket (`TrainerControlState::request_checkpoint()`), the pass takes the request with `take_checkpoint_request()` and,
once the checkpoint is written, records it with `mark_checkpoint_served()` (chatbot and LeJEPA passes;
`IncrementalTrainer::perform_auto_save()` now reports whether it saved). `completed` is true only when this request's ticket
is served, so an auto-save in the window no longer counts, and a failed save isn't reported as complete.
Saved overrides go through the new `parse_trainer_admin_overrides()`, the `PUT` checks per key, in `start()` and in
`trainer_service`'s idle config; an invalid one is logged and the config file's value kept. Tests: an auto-save during the
wait leaves `completed:false`; malformed and oversized `wait_ms` are 400s with no request made; invalid saved overrides are
ignored and logged on load (these three fail on the old code, the oversized wait holding the old server for 60 s);
ticket accounting and the override parser have unit tests, and the real-binary LeJEPA test still sees its requested
checkpoint complete.

Location in code: `src/TrainerAdminAPI.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/TrainerControlState.hpp`, `src/TrainerAdminConfig.{hpp,cpp}`,
`src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`run_training()`, `perform_auto_save()`), `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (LeJEPA pass).

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainerAdminAPI.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/TrainerControlState.hpp`
- `src/TrainerAdminConfig.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/TrainerServiceProxy.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/IncrementalTrainer.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`

### TD-520: Trainer Admin Status Emits NaN Losses as Invalid JSON

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Training / Admin API | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainerAdminAPI.cpp`; verified. `handle_status()` streams `last_loss`/`best_loss` as raw doubles; with `last_loss = NaN` (a
diverged pass) the body contained `"last_loss":nan` and `json.load` failed at that character, so the dashboard loses the entire status during exactly
the event an operator needs to see (the TD-443/TD-458/TD-510 class). `best_loss` starts at `0.0`, which reads as a perfect loss until validation runs.
`TrainerServiceProxy` forwards the child's body unchanged.

Action Items:

- [x] Emit non-finite losses as `null` (or a string), and `best_loss` as `null` until a validation loss exists.
- [x] Test with NaN and infinity.

Location in code: `src/TrainerAdminAPI.cpp` (`handle_status()`); the `TODO: See TD-520` tag is removed.

**Fix (November 2, 2026):** `handle_status()` sends a non-finite `last_loss`/`best_loss` as `null` and adds `loss_diverged`, true when the
pass has trained samples and its last loss isn't finite, so a diverged pass is told apart from one that hasn't reported a loss yet.
`TrainerControlState::last_loss`/`best_loss` start as NaN (no loss yet), so `best_loss` is `null` until a validation loss exists
instead of a perfect-looking 0. The LeJEPA pass only takes a finite epoch average as its best loss. `TrainerServiceProxy`'s idle
status sends `null` losses and `loss_diverged: false`. Finite losses are written with 17 significant digits. The Android ops
dashboard's `TrainerStatusDto` takes nullable losses and `loss_diverged` (the old non-null `Double` would have rejected `null`), and
the Trainer screen shows "(none yet)" or "diverged (NaN/inf)". Tests: `trainerAdminApiTests` parses the status strictly with
NaN, +inf and -inf losses and before any loss, `trainerServiceProxyTests` does the same for the idle body and a diverged child
proxied through, `trainerControlStateTests` checks the NaN defaults, and the dashboard's `TrainerStatusDtoTest` decodes `null`,
diverged and older numeric bodies. The first three fail on the old code.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainerAdminAPI.cpp`
- `src/TrainerControlState.hpp`
- `tests/trainer_admin_api_test.cpp`
- `src/TrainerServiceProxy.cpp`, `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`, `tests/trainer_service_proxy_test.cpp`, `tests/trainer_control_state_test.cpp`
- `android/opsdashboard/.../TrainerDtos.kt`, `TrainerScreen.kt`, `TrainerStatusDtoTest.kt`

### TD-431: Trainer Processes Share One Rotating Log File and Ignore `LOG_LEVEL`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Core / Logger | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `Logger` and verified. When `LOG_FILE_PATH` is empty, `trainer_service`
(`TrainerServiceMain.cpp`) and `incremental_trainer`'s `train`/`retrain`/`resume` fall back to
`chatbot_server.log` in the working directory, so `trainer_service` and every child pass it launches write
the **same file through separate `rotating_file_sink_mt`s**. spdlog's rotating sink isn't multi-process
safe: each process rotates on its own size count and renames files out from under the other. Two processes
writing 30,000 lines each to a 1 MB × 3 log retained 34,162 lines (2.80 MB), against 47,031 lines (3.85 MB)
for one process writing the same 60,000 lines, about 27% less history than configured (no corrupted
lines). This contradicts LOG_FILE_STANDARDS.md (empty path should mean console-only), and the name
suggests the chatbot server's log. Separately, both trainer binaries always initialize at `INFO`; only
`chatbot_api_server` applies `LOG_LEVEL`.

Action Items:

- [x] Give each process its own file (for example `<LOG_FILE_PATH>.child` or `incremental_trainer.log`), or log the children to stderr and let `trainer_service` capture it; use console-only when `LOG_FILE_PATH` is empty.
- [x] Apply `LOG_LEVEL` in both trainer binaries.

**Fix (November 2, 2026), owner's choice of a file per pass:**
- **`trainer_service`** logs to `LOG_FILE_PATH`, or the console when it's empty (the journal under systemd), and gives
  each pass `--log-file <pass_log_path()>`: the same name with `.pass` before the extension (`trainer.log` →
  `trainer.pass.log`). Each file is now rotated by one process. With `LOG_FILE_PATH` empty the passes inherit the
  console.
- **`incremental_trainer`** has a new global `--log-file <path>` (also usable by hand; `trainer_service` itself refuses
  it). It logs to `--log-file`, else `LOG_FILE_PATH`; empty means the console for a foreground run, and, for a detached
  run whose stdout/stderr go to `/dev/null`, `default_background_log_path()`: `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (else
  `~/.local/state`)`/adai/log/incremental_trainer.log`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\adai\Logs` on Windows, as
  LOG_FILE_STANDARDS.md says. `chatbot_server.log` is no longer used by either.
- **`LOG_LEVEL`** reaches both through `Logger::init(Logger::parse_level(...))` (new), and the replay of start-up messages
  logged before `init()` (TD-290) now skips those below the level, so `LOG_LEVEL=WARN` writes no INFO line.
- The guides (`training-guide.md`, `COMMANDS.md`, `OPERATIONS_MANUAL.md`, `TRAINING_FIX_STRATEGY.md`), the unit and
  `config.trainer.conf` no longer point at `chatbot_server.log`.

Tests: `PassLogPath`, `TrainerServiceChildArgv.PassesThePassLogFile`, `ParseIncrementalTrainerGlobalArgs.LogFileFlag`,
`DefaultBackgroundLogPath.UsesTheXdgStateDirectory`, and against the real binaries
`SighupTest.TrainerServicePassesLogToTheirOwnFileAndLogLevelApplies` (with `LOG_FILE_PATH` set, the pass gets
`--log-file <dir>/trainer.pass.log` and `LOG_LEVEL=WARN` leaves no INFO line in `trainer_service`'s file; with it empty,
no `--log-file` and no `chatbot_server.log`) and `SighupTest.IncrementalTrainerLogsToTheConsoleOrItsLogFile`. Both fail
on the old binaries.

Location in code: `src/TrainerServiceMain.cpp`, `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (`run_training_pipeline()`),
`src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.{hpp,cpp}` (`--log-file`, `pass_log_path()`, `default_background_log_path()`),
`src/Logger.{hpp,cpp}` (`parse_level()`, replay level).

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainerServiceMain.cpp`
- `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`
- `src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/Logger.{hpp,cpp}`

### TD-430: `Logger` Lazy Initialization Races and Can Throw From a Log Call

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Core / Logger | Code fix (LOW, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `Logger` and verified. `Logger::get()` lazily calls `init(INFO)` when `logger_` is
null, without synchronization, and `logger_` is a plain static `shared_ptr`. When several threads log
before `init()`, more than one calls `init()`, and `spdlog::stderr_color_mt()` throws
`spdlog_ex("logger with name 'adai' already exists")` from inside the logging call: 3 of 8 threads threw
in a fresh process (every one of 200 forked trials saw a throw). The concurrent `shared_ptr` reads and
writes are a data race, and calling `init()` again while other threads log is unsafe the same way. The
binaries call `init()` early in `main()`, so tests and code that logs from threads during startup are
what's exposed. Also: `init(level, name)` drops only the **new** name (a logger registered under a
previous name lingers), `FileConfig::compress` only changes startup log lines, and `Level::ERROR`
collides with the Windows `<wingdi.h>` `ERROR` macro.

Action Items:

- [x] Guard initialization with `std::call_once` (or a mutex) and make `logger_` an atomic `shared_ptr`/`spdlog::default_logger()`; never throw from a log call; drop the previous logger's own name on re-init; rename `Level::ERROR` (or `#undef` guard).

**Fix (November 2, 2026):** `init()` and `get()`'s lazy init share one mutex, and `logger_` is only read and
written with `std::atomic_load`/`std::atomic_store`, so concurrent first use creates one logger and a thread logging
during a re-init gets the old or the new logger. The console logger is built directly instead of with
`spdlog::stderr_color_mt()`, which threw when the name was taken, and registering it can't throw. Re-init drops the
previous logger's own name. `Level::ERROR` is now `Level::ERR`, so `Logger.hpp` compiles after `<wingdi.h>`.
`FileConfig::compress` is documented as only logging a start-up note. `tests/logger_init_race_test.cpp` (its own
binary; each race runs in a forked child that only it waits for): 8 threads' first log calls in 50 fresh processes,
200 re-inits while 4 threads log, the previous name dropped, `ERR` with the Windows `ERROR` macro defined. On the old
code the file doesn't compile, and with the names adapted three of four fail (a throw on trial 0, a segfault during
re-init, the old name still registered). TSan-clean, children included.

Location in code: `src/Logger.{hpp,cpp}` (`get()`, `init()`, `install()`, `Level`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/Logger.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/logger_test.cpp`, `tests/logger_init_race_test.cpp`

### TD-416: `incremental_trainer` Command Hygiene

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainingTool | Code fix (LOW, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainingTool`; the first item verified:
- `train abc`/`retrain abc`: the epoch argument goes through an uncaught `std::stoi`, so the process
  aborts (exit 134).
- The SIGTERM/SIGINT handler logs through spdlog and calls `std::exit(0)` (not async-signal-safe; runs
  static destructors under the training thread), doesn't checkpoint or release claimed files, and exits
  0.
- `init` and `retrain` override `AUTO_SAVE_*` with hard-coded 30 min / 1,000 samples.
- The LeJEPA path's tokenizer is always ASCII (`TOKENIZER_MODE` ignored).
- `status`/`history` build a full `IncrementalTrainer`, which loads the best checkpoint and runs the
  deleting `cleanup_dead_sessions()` (TD-406/TD-407), just to print.
- The interactive MNS model pick reads stdin (EOF under systemd, which is the intended failure but
  undocumented).

Action Items:

- [x] Parse epochs with validation; have the signal handler only set a flag that the training loop polls (then checkpoint, release, exit non-zero); use the configured auto-save values; thread `TOKENIZER_MODE` to LeJEPA; give `status`/`history` a read-only path.

**Fix (November 2, 2026):** every item.
- **Epochs.** `parse_epochs_arg()` (`IncrementalTrainerArgs`): a whole number of at least 1, else `Invalid epoch count
  '<v>'` and exit 1; a third argument is an error too.
- **Signals.** The handler only stores atomics. Every `train`/`retrain`/`resume` pass now builds a `PassAdminApi` (its
  HTTP listener still only with `--admin-port`), whose `TrainerControlState` it registers for the handler. The first
  SIGTERM/SIGINT sets that state's `paused` and new `stop_signal`, so the pass drains as for `/admin/pause` (chatbot
  and LeJEPA alike): it stops at the next sample or batch, checkpoints, releases its claimed files and exits 1, and
  the log says "stopped by SIGTERM". With no pass running, or on a second signal, the process `_exit(1)`s at once.
  `trainer_service`'s graceful-stop wait went from 10 s to 25 s (still inside the unit's `TimeoutStopSec=30`) to give
  that checkpoint time.
- **Auto-save.** `init` and `retrain` no longer override `AUTO_SAVE_*`.
- **Tokenizer mode.** New `LeJEPAEncoder::set_tokenizer_mode()`; the LeJEPA pass and the trainer's world-model attach
  use `TOKENIZER_MODE` as the chatbot does. A vocabulary that records its own mode still wins on load, as for the
  chatbot, so only headerless vocabularies are affected.
- **`status`/`history`** read `session_history.txt` through the new static `IncrementalTrainer::read_session_history()`
  and print without building a trainer: no model, no checkpoint load, no `cleanup_dead_sessions()`, and no vocabulary
  needed (TD-414's `status`/`history` crash).
- **Model pick.** Without a terminal on stdin it now fails at once with "set MODEL_NAME or pass --model"; the choice
  is parsed strictly.

Tests: `ParseEpochsArg`, `LeJEPAEncoderTokenizerMode`, `train abc`/`retrain 0` in `SighupTest.IncrementalTrainerExitsOneOnABadFlag`,
`SighupTest.SigtermDrainsALejepaPass` (exit 1, a checkpoint, the file unclaimed) and
`SighupTest.StatusAndHistoryAreReadOnlyAndNeedNoVocabulary` (exit 0 with no vocabulary; an unreferenced checkpoint file
survives). On the old binary `train abc` was killed by SIGABRT, SIGTERM exited 0 with no checkpoint and the file still
claimed, and `status`/`history` failed. A chatbot `train 1000` pass stopped by SIGTERM was checked by hand: "stopped by
SIGTERM (epoch 0, 68 sample(s))", its file released, exit 1.

### TD-414: First-Run Vocabulary Bootstrap Is Unreachable From the CLI

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainingTool | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainingTool` and verified with the built binary. Every command
constructs `IncrementalTrainer(vocab, model, cfg)`, whose three-argument constructor calls
`build_model()` → `load_vocab()` unconditionally. The first-run vocabulary bootstrap
(`pending_vocab_build_` → `bootstrap_vocab()`) exists only in the config-file constructor, which
`main()` never uses. On a fresh `SESSION_DIR` with data queued and no `vocab.txt`, `train 1` aborted
with `terminate called … VocabularyFileError: Could not open vocabulary file: vocab.txt` (exit 134), and
so did `status` and `history`. A vocabulary has to be built separately first (`vocab_builder`), which
the usage text doesn't mention; this matches the "missing `VOCAB_PATH`" crash from ai-machine's first
deployment.

Action Items:

- [x] Move the missing-vocab handling into the three-argument constructor (defer `build_model()` until `bootstrap_vocab()`), and make `status`/`history` work without a model.
- [x] Catch exceptions in `main()`'s command dispatch with a clear message.

**Update (November 2, 2026):** `status` and `history` no longer build a trainer (TD-416), so they work without a
vocabulary; `train`/`retrain`/`resume` still need one.

**Fix (November 2, 2026):** a new `IncrementalTrainer::defer_until_vocab_exists()` is used by all three constructors:
with no vocabulary file it sets `pending_vocab_build_` and skips building the model, and the first training pass
(`train_on_files()`/`retrain_on_files()`, so `train`, `retrain` and `resume`) builds the vocabulary from its data with
`bootstrap_vocab()` and then the model. Only the config-file constructor did this before. `VOCAB_BUILD_SIZE` reaches
the explicit-paths constructors through a new `IncrementalConfig::vocab_build_size`, and `reset_model_for_config()`
(`retrain`) skips building a model while the vocabulary is pending. `main()` now wraps the command dispatch: an
exception logs and prints `❌ <message>` and exits 1 instead of reaching `std::terminate` (exit 134).

Tests: `IncrementalTrainerTest.FirstPassBuildsTheVocabularyWhenThereIsNone`, `IncrementalConfigMapping.VocabBuildSizeIsMapped`,
and `SighupTest.AFirstTrainBuildsTheVocabularyAndExceptionsExitOne` against the real binary (a fresh `SESSION_DIR`
with queued data: `train 1` exits 0 and writes the vocabulary; `init` with an unreadable vocabulary path exits 1).
The old binary exited 134 for both. By hand, `train`, `retrain` and `resume` all build the vocabulary on a fresh
directory, and `init` leaves it for the first pass.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (`train` construction, `status`), `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (constructors).

Files to Modify:

- `src/IncrementalTrainer.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`

### TD-404: `derive_run_id()` Can Collide Across Hosts

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Training / CLI | Code fix (LOW, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainerArgs`, by inspection. `derive_run_id()` returns
`RUN_ID` if set, else the first 8 characters of the hostname plus `_` plus `pid % 10000`. The LeJEPA
pretraining path always uses it (it never calls `begin_run()`), and `train`/`retrain` use it when MNS
doesn't allocate a run id. With a shared remote registry, run ids decide who owns claimed files, so
two hosts with the same 8-character prefix (for example `ai-machi…`) and a coinciding PID tail would
share ownership.

Action Items:

- [x] Use the full hostname plus PID plus a random suffix (or a UUID), or allocate LeJEPA run ids from MNS like the chatbot path.

**Fix (November 2, 2026):** `derive_run_id()` is now the full hostname (sanitized), the full PID and 8 random hex
digits, so two hosts or two processes never derive the same id. Ids that must survive a restart come from
`persistent_run_id()`, generalized with a name: the LeJEPA pass already kept `lejepa_run_id` in its world-model directory
(TD-415), and without MNS the chatbot `train`/`retrain`/`resume` passes now keep `SESSION_DIR/chatbot_run_id`
(`incremental_trainer` sets `RUN_ID` from it; an explicit `RUN_ID` and an MNS-allocated run id still come first). A
restarted chatbot pass therefore reclaims the files a crashed one claimed, as an MNS run does. `IncrementalTrainer`'s
own last-resort fallback, for other callers, gained a random part too.

Tests: `DeriveRunId.IsTheFullHostnamePidAndARandomPart`, `PersistentRunId.TheChatbotIdHasItsOwnFile`, and
`SighupTest.AChatbotPassReclaimsACrashedPassesFilesWithoutMns` against the real binary (a file claimed under the stored id
by a "crashed" pass: `resume` reclaims and trains it, exit 0). The old binary found nothing to claim (exit 3).

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.{hpp,cpp}` (`derive_run_id()`, `persistent_run_id()`),
`src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (`run_main()`), `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`resume_last_session()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.cpp`
- `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`

### TD-282: `ChildProcess` Windows Path Has Known Gaps

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Training / Service Supervisor | Code fix (LOW, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-277; affects only Windows builds (none shipped today):

- command-line quoting escapes `"` but not backslashes preceding a quote, so arguments ending in `\` break;
- a child that genuinely exits with code 259 (`STILL_ACTIVE`) is treated as still running forever;
- `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` only reaches a child sharing the supervisor's console, otherwise the fallback is an immediate `TerminateProcess()`.

Action Items:

- [x] Use the standard `CommandLineToArgvW`-compatible quoting algorithm.
- [x] Detect exit via `WaitForSingleObject(handle, 0)` instead of comparing to `STILL_ACTIVE`.
- [x] Document (or replace) the console-event stop mechanism.

**Fix (November 2, 2026):**
- **Quoting.** A new `ChildProcess::windows_command_line()` (compiled on every platform, so it has ordinary unit tests)
  quotes an argument only when it's empty or has whitespace or a quote, and inside quotes doubles backslashes before a
  quote or the closing quote, as `CommandLineToArgvW` and the Microsoft C runtime expect.
- **Exit detection.** `poll_exit()` waits on the process handle with `WaitForSingleObject(handle, 0)` and only then reads
  the exit code, so a child that exits with 259 is seen as exited.
- **Console-event stop.** Documented in `request_stop()`: `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` reaches a pass only when it shares the
  supervisor's console; with no console (a Windows service) the fallback `TerminateProcess()` ends it at once, without
  a checkpoint. Run `trainer_service` from a console for graceful stops on Windows.

Tests: `ChildProcessTest.WindowsCommandLineQuotesLikeCommandLineToArgvW` on Linux, and a scratch harness cross-compiled
with MinGW against the real `src/ChildProcess.cpp` and run under Wine: it launches itself with nine awkward arguments
(empty, spaces, `C:\dir with space\`, embedded quotes, backslashes before quotes, a tab) and gets every one back
exactly, and a child exiting with 259 is reported as exited with 259. The same harness against the old code got the
arguments back mangled and never saw the 259 child exit.

Location in code: `src/ChildProcess.{hpp,cpp}` (`windows_command_line()`, Windows `start()`/`poll_exit()`,
`request_stop()` documentation).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChildProcess.cpp`

### TD-281: `ChildProcess` Forks a Multithreaded Process and Leaks File Descriptors

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Training / Service Supervisor | Code fix (LOW, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-277. `trainer_service` runs its httplib admin proxy on other threads, so
`start()`'s `fork()` happens in a multithreaded process. The child calls only `execvp()`, but that
isn't on POSIX's async-signal-safe list (its PATH search may allocate), a theoretical post-fork
deadlock. The child also inherits every descriptor not marked close-on-exec: httplib marks its
listening socket, but accepted connections use plain `accept()`, so an admin connection in flight at
launch time stays open in the pass until it exits.

Action Items:

- [x] ~~Use `posix_spawn()`~~ Resolve the path before forking and `execve()` it: `posix_spawn()` can't set TD-280's parent-death signal between fork and exec, so `fork()` stays, with only async-signal-safe calls in the child.
- [x] Close inherited descriptors in the child (`close_range(3, ~0U, CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC)` where available, or spawn file actions).

**Fix (November 2, 2026):** `start()` resolves the program before `fork()` (a new `resolve_program()`: a name with a
`/` as given, else the first executable regular file on `PATH`, `/usr/bin:/bin` if unset), and the child calls
`execve()` with the current environment, so it makes only async-signal-safe calls. In the child, every descriptor from 3
up is marked close-on-exec (`close_range(3, ~0U, CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC)`, or `fcntl()` per descriptor up to the
`RLIMIT_NOFILE` read before forking), so an accepted admin connection or any other descriptor opened without
`O_CLOEXEC` no longer reaches the pass. The TD-278 error pipe is close-on-exec already, so a failed `exec` still reports
through it. A name not found on `PATH` is now reported as `No such file or directory` by `start()` itself.

Tests: `ChildProcessTest.TheChildInheritsNoDescriptorsBeyondStdio` (a descriptor opened without `O_CLOEXEC` as fd 200
is not open in the child; the old code leaked it) and `ChildProcessTest.ABareNameIsFoundOnPath`.

Location in code: `src/ChildProcess.cpp` (`start()`, `resolve_program()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChildProcess.cpp`

### TD-280: `trainer_service` Passes Can Be Orphaned if the Supervisor Is Hard-Killed

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Training / Service Supervisor | Code fix (LOW, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-277. `ChildProcess` signals only the direct child, sets no process group, and
uses no `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`. Under systemd the default `KillMode=control-group` kills the whole cgroup,
but if `trainer_service` is hard-killed outside systemd (manual `kill -9`, a crash, another
supervisor), a running pass keeps going, still holding dataset claims and the GPU, while a
restarted `trainer_service` launches a second pass.

Action Items:

- [x] In the child before `exec`: `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM)` (Linux), re-checking `getppid()` for the fork race; optionally a process group so stop requests reach grandchildren.
- [x] Document the systemd `KillMode` requirement in the service file.

**Fix (November 2, 2026):** on Linux the child calls `prctl(PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, SIGTERM)` before `exec` (the setting
survives `exec`), then exits if `getppid()` no longer matches the parent (it died first); a failed `prctl()` is
reported like a failed `exec` (TD-278). A pass whose `trainer_service` is hard-killed now gets SIGTERM and drains
(TD-416: checkpoint, release its claims, exit). It follows the forking *thread*; `trainer_service` calls `start()` from
its main thread, which lives as long as the process. Process groups were left out on purpose: signalling a group means
`kill()` with a negative pid, the hazard TD-279 just removed. `adai-trainer.service` documents that `KillMode` must stay
`mixed` or `control-group`.

Tests: `ChildProcessTest.TheChildDiesWithAHardKilledSupervisor` (a disposable supervisor process forked by the test
starts the child and is SIGKILLed) and `SighupTest.APassDoesNotOutliveAHardKilledTrainerService` (the real
`trainer_service` with a stub pass, SIGKILLed). Each signals only processes the test spawned, with checked pids above
0. Neither was run against the old code (see TD-279); the old `start()` has no parent-death handling at all.

Location in code: `src/ChildProcess.cpp` (`start()`), `scripts/adai-trainer.service`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChildProcess.cpp`
- `scripts/adai-trainer.service`

### TD-279: `ChildProcess::request_stop()` Can Signal Every Process if Called Concurrently

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Training / Service Supervisor | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-277. The header says `request_stop()` is safe to call from a signal handler's
thread. On POSIX it checks the plain `bool running_` and then calls `kill(pid_, SIGTERM)`, but nothing
is atomic, and `stop_and_wait()`'s give-up path sets `pid_ = -1` **before** clearing `running_`
(compilers may also reorder the other paths' stores). A concurrent call could therefore read
`running_ == true` and `pid_ == -1`, and `kill(-1, SIGTERM)` sends SIGTERM to **every process the user
can signal**. It isn't reachable today (`trainer_service`'s handler only sets a flag), but the
documented contract invites it.

Action Items:

- [x] Guard `kill()` with `pid_ > 0` (and the Windows path with a non-null handle).
- [x] Make `running_`/`pid_` atomic, or drop the signal-handler safety claim from the header.

**Fix (November 2, 2026):** `running_`, `pid_` and the Windows handle are atomics. `request_stop()` and
`stop_and_wait()`'s force kill read the pid once and signal only a pid above 0 (a non-null handle on Windows);
`poll_exit()` calls `waitpid()` only with a pid above 0 (`waitpid(-1, ...)` would reap any child); and every path that
ends a child clears `running_` before `pid_`/the handle, so a concurrent `request_stop()` returns early. A narrow window
remains in which a stop request racing the reap can signal a PID the kernel has just recycled; that is the usual limit of
signalling by PID and only a pidfd would close it.

**Verified for real, by accident (November 2, 2026):** a stress test that called `request_stop()` from a second thread
while children started and exited passed on the fixed code, under TSan as well. Run against the old code, it hit the race:
`kill(-1, SIGTERM)` reached every process the user owned and ended the desktop session, twice. That test was removed so a
regression can never do this during `ctest`. `ChildProcessTest.RequestStopIsANoOpWithoutALiveChild` checks only the
stopped states.

Location in code: `src/ChildProcess.{hpp,cpp}` (`request_stop()`, `stop_and_wait()`, `poll_exit()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChildProcess.{hpp,cpp}`

### TD-278: `ChildProcess` Reports a Failed `exec` as a Successful Launch

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Training / Service Supervisor | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-277 and confirmed by running the real class: with a missing binary,
`start()` returns **true** (after `fork()`), and the failure only appears later as exit code **127**
from `poll_exit()`. `trainer_service` counts that as a crashed pass and retries after every poll
interval, indefinitely, without ever reporting that `incremental_trainer` couldn't be executed
(e.g. after a bad install or a wrong path).

Action Items:

- [x] Detect exec failure in `start()`: a close-on-exec pipe the child writes `errno` to before `_exit()`, or `posix_spawn()` (which reports exec errors directly on glibc).
- [x] Log the exec error with the path; have `trainer_service` back off (or stop) on repeated launch failures rather than retrying silently.
- [x] Test: `start({"/nonexistent"})` returns false.

**Fix (November 2, 2026):** `start()` creates a close-on-exec pipe before `fork()`. A successful `exec` closes the
child's end, so the parent reads end-of-file; a failed one writes `errno` first, and `start()` reaps the child, logs
`could not execute '<path>': <reason>` and returns false. `trainer_service` then backs off as for any failed launch
(added with TD-524: 45 s doubling to 15 min, counted in `consecutive_failures`) and counts no pass.

Tests: `ChildProcessTest.AFailedExecIsReportedByStart` (a missing path and a non-executable file both return false; a
real launch still works after) and `SighupTest.TrainerServiceReportsAChildItCannotExecute` (a non-executable
`incremental_trainer` beside `trainer_service`: `/admin/status` shows a launch failure with 0 passes launched and 0
crashed, and the log names the path and "Permission denied"). The old `ChildProcess` fails the second test.

Location in code: `src/ChildProcess.{hpp,cpp}` (`start()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChildProcess.cpp`
- `src/TrainerServiceMain.cpp`
- `tests/child_process_test.cpp`

### TD-277: `ChildProcess` Reports Every Signal Death as Exit Code 128

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 2, 2026 | Training / Service Supervisor | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [ChildProcess.md](../reference/source/ChildProcess.md), and confirmed by running the real
class: a child killed by SIGSEGV and one killed by SIGKILL both come back from `poll_exit()` as
**128**. The header calls 128 "POSIX convention", but the shell convention is **128 + signal number**
(139 for SIGSEGV, 137 for SIGKILL). On ai-machine the known pass-killing failure is a SIGSEGV inside
the Intel graphics compiler ([ONEAPI_SYCL_DRIVER_SEGFAULT.md](../../operations/guides/troubleshooting/ONEAPI_SYCL_DRIVER_SEGFAULT.md)),
and an OOM kill would be SIGKILL. `trainer_service`'s `/admin/status` `last_exit_code` can't tell them
apart, which removes exactly the diagnosis TD-172's process isolation was meant to make possible.

Action Items:

- [x] Report `128 + WTERMSIG(status)` for signal deaths (and note core dumps via `WCOREDUMP` in a log line).
- [x] Update the header and `TrainerServiceControlState::last_exit_code`'s comment; keep `total_passes_crashed` counting unchanged.
- [x] Test: SIGSEGV → 139, SIGKILL → 137.

**Fix (November 2, 2026):** `poll_exit()` reports `128 + WTERMSIG(status)` for a signal death and logs the signal's
name and whether it dumped core (`pid N was killed by signal 11 (Segmentation fault), core dumped`); SIGTERM, the
graceful stop `ChildProcess` itself sends, logs at info level, every other signal as a warning. `total_passes_crashed`
still counts every code of 128 and up. The header and `TrainerServiceControlState`'s comments are updated.

Test: `ChildProcessTest.ASignalDeathIs128PlusTheSignalNumber` (a child that sends itself SIGSEGV reports 139, SIGKILL
137); the old code reported 128 for both.

Location in code: `src/ChildProcess.{hpp,cpp}` (`poll_exit()`), `src/TrainerServiceControlState.hpp`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChildProcess.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/TrainerServiceControlState.hpp`
- `tests/child_process_test.cpp`

### TD-557: `trainer_service` Ignores `--help` and Bad Arguments

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | Training / Service Supervisor | Code fix (LOW, filed November 1, 2026) |

Description:
Found November 1, 2026 while checking `trainer_service`'s flags for TD-401 (verified with the real binary). `trainer_service`
parses its command line with `incremental_trainer`'s global-flag parser but never looked at the result beyond the three flags it
forwards:
- `trainer_service --help` started the always-on service (it has no help text), so an operator asking what it accepts got a
  running supervisor that launched training passes.
- The parser's own errors (TD-401: `--admin-port abc`, a flag missing its value) were ignored, and so were `--foreground`,

`--objective`/`--dataset-kind` being parsed and dropped is TD-403.

`--help`/`-h` anywhere sets `help`, and `--foreground`, `--admin-port` and leftover positionals become errors next to the
parser's own. `trainer_service`'s `main()` prints a new `print_usage()` and exits 0 for help, 1 for an error, before loading
any config or starting anything. Tests: `ParseTrainerServiceArgs` (3) and, against the real binary,

### TD-488: `registry_server` Accepts Malformed Numbers, Valueless Flags and Unknown Arguments

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | Data / Registry Server CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryServerArgs.cpp` (see [RegistryServerArgs.md](../reference/source/RegistryServerArgs.md)); verified with the real
`registry_server` binary:
- **Numbers:** every numeric flag uses bare `std::stoi`. `--port abc` threw an uncaught `std::invalid_argument` (abort, core dump, exit 134); `--port 8090x`
  was accepted as 8090; `--port 99999` logged "listening on port 99999" but bound 34463. By inspection, nothing is range-checked: `--ftp-ttl 0` or negative
  issues already-expired FTP tokens, `--ftp-max-sessions 0` makes every FTP login fail with 421, `--ftp-pasv-min > --ftp-pasv-max` empties the PASV pool (425).
- **Valueless flags:** a value flag is matched only when a value follows, so a trailing one is dropped silently. A bare `--admin-enabled` left
  `PUT /admin/config` open (HTTP 200); a trailing `--ftp-secret` leaves the key random, a trailing `--port` falls back to 8082. (Unknown values such as
  `flase` fail closed, 403, unlike TD-456.)
- **Unknown arguments:** ignored without a message (`--portt 8091` started on 8082), so typos such as `--ftp-enable` leave features off. The header documents
  this as preserved legacy behaviour and a test asserts it.

Action Items:

- [x] Parse numbers with full-string checks and ranges (ports 1–65535, TTL and sessions > 0, PASV min ≤ max); report errors and exit non-zero instead of aborting.
- [x] Treat a value flag with no value, and any unknown argument, as an error with usage; update `UnrecognizedArgumentIsSilentlyIgnored`.
- [x] Share the helper with TD-240/TD-438/TD-456.

**Fix (November 1, 2026).** `parse_registry_server_args()` checks its 10 numeric flags against a range table through TD-240's
`parse_strict_int()`: ports (`--port`/`-p`, `--ftp-port`, `--ftp-pasv-min`/`-max`) 1–65535, `--ftp-ttl`, `--max-upload-mb` and
`--max-concurrent-fetches` at least 1, `--ftp-max-sessions` and `--claim-lease-minutes` at least 0. (0 sessions means unlimited in
`FtpDataServer`, not "every login fails" as filed; 0 lease means claims never expire.) `--ftp-pasv-min` above `--ftp-pasv-max` is an
error, and so is a range emptied by the file and a flag together (`RegistryServerEffectiveConfig::errors`, exit 1). A value flag given
no value says `Missing value for --ftp-secret`, an unknown argument is `Unknown argument: --portt`, and `--admin-enabled` takes the
shared boolean words (`parse_strict_bool()`) with anything else an error, as `mns_server` since TD-456. `main()` prints the error with
usage and exits 1; `--port abc` used to abort with a core dump. Saved `ftp_token_ttl_minutes`/`ftp_max_sessions_per_run` overrides that
aren't whole numbers in range are skipped with a warning (`override_warnings`). The TD-494 flags used to be clamped (`-5` → 0) and are
now errors. Tests: `EveryNumericFlagIsAWholeNumberInRange`, `AFlagMissingItsValueSaysSo`, `AnUnknownArgumentIsAnError` (replaces
`UnrecognizedArgumentIsSilentlyIgnored`), `AdminEnabledTakesTheSharedBooleanWords` (replaces the lenient one), `PasvMinAbovePasvMaxIsAnError`,
`AnEmptyPasvRangeFromFileAndFlagIsAnError`, `BadSavedOverridesAreSkippedWithAWarning`, and `SighupTest.RegistryServerExitsOneOnABadFlag`
(the real binary exits 1 for `--port abc`, `--port 99999`, `--portt 8091` and a bare `--admin-enabled`; the old one aborted with signal
6 on the first and started on the second).

Location in code: `src/RegistryServerArgs.cpp` (`parse_registry_server_args()`); tagged `TD-488`.

### TD-456: `mns_server` Treats a Mistyped `--admin-enabled` as `true` and Doesn't Range-Check `--port`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | MNS / Server CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MnsServerArgs` and verified with the real `mns_server`:
- **Admin flag typo.** `parse_bool_flag()` returns the default for unrecognized text, and `--admin-enabled`'s default is `true`.
  Started with `--admin-enabled flase`, the server kept `PUT /admin/config` enabled; an unauthenticated
  `PUT {"registry_group":"hijacked"}` returned 200 and the server logged `admin config updated`. The admin settings
  (`registry_url`/`registry_group`) control where MNS proxies dataset-registry requests. (MNS has no authentication on any
  endpoint; this is about honouring an explicit operator choice.)
- **Port.** `std::stoi` with no range check: `--port 99999` logged `listening on port 99999` and listened on **34463**
  (mod 65536); `8083x` → 8083; `0` → a random port; negatives accepted. Clients using `NAME_SERVICE_URL` then can't find MNS
  and fall back to local architecture.
- **Minor (by inspection).** A value-taking flag with no value is reported as "Unknown argument"; `--admin-enabled` has no
  config key (unlike `metrics_api_server`'s `METRICS_API_ALLOW_CONTROL`); the header names the test
  `MnsServerArgs_test.cpp` (it's `mns_server_args_test.cpp`).

Action Items:

- [x] Make an explicit but unrecognized `--admin-enabled` value an error (keep the lenient default only when the flag is absent).
- [x] Parse `--port` with the shared checked helper (whole string, 1–65535) from TD-438/TD-240.
- [x] Report "missing value for --flag"; consider an `MNS_ADMIN_ENABLED` config key; fix the header comment.

**Fix (November 1, 2026).** `parse_mns_server_args()` refuses an `--admin-enabled` value that isn't a boolean
(`Invalid value for --admin-enabled: 'flase' (expected true/false, yes/no, on/off, enabled/disabled or 1/0)`), through a new public
`parse_strict_bool()` in `Config.hpp`, the TD-286 parser; `parse_bool_flag()`, which fell back to the default, is gone. `--port`/`-p`
must be a whole number 1–65535 (`parse_strict_int()`), and a value flag given no value says `Missing value for --port`. `main()`
already exited 1 on a parse error. A new `MNS_ADMIN_ENABLED` key (`ServiceConfig::name_service_admin_enabled`, default true, shipped
in `config.mns.conf` with a note that MNS has no authentication) sets the default that `--admin-enabled` overrides. The header names
the real test file. Tests: `AnUnrecognisedAdminEnabledValueIsAnError`, `AdminEnabledAcceptsTheSharedBooleanWords`,
`PortMustBeAWholeNumberInRange`, `AFlagMissingItsValueSaysSo`, `AdminEnabledComesFromTheConfigUnlessTheFlagIsGiven`, the key added to
`EveryBooleanKeyAcceptsAnyCaseOfTheSameWords`, and `SighupTest.MnsServerRefusesAMistypedAdminEnabledAndHonoursTheConfigKey` (the real
binary exits 1 on `--admin-enabled flase`, which the old binary started with, and with `MNS_ADMIN_ENABLED=false` answers
`PUT /admin/config` with 403).

Location in code: `src/MnsServerArgs.cpp` (`parse_bool_flag()`, `parse_mns_server_args()`); tagged `TD-456`.

- `src/MnsServerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}`, `config.mns.conf`
- `tests/mns_server_args_test.cpp`, `tests/config_test.cpp`, `tests/sighup_test.cpp`, `tests/CMakeLists.txt`

### TD-451: `mns_cli` Has No HTTPS and Minor Option Handling Gaps

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | MNS / CLI | Code fix (LOW, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MnsCliTool`:
- **No HTTPS (verified).** `parse_url()` strips `https://` but keeps the default port 8083, and `make_http()` always
  builds a plain `httplib::Client`: `mns_cli --url https://127.0.0.1 health` reported `connection to 127.0.0.1:8083
  failed`. `mns_cli` can't reach MNS through a TLS endpoint (the Cloudflare tunnel) and can't send Access headers.
  Same gap as TD-444 (`MetricsPushClient`).
- **`--help` (verified).** Only recognized as the first word; `mns_cli list --help` sent a `list` request.
- **By inspection.** `--url`/`--config` are taken from anywhere on the line, so they can't be command argument values;
  `ModelNameClient.hpp` is included but unused; the file comment still mentions `config.conf`; the four `http_*()`
  helpers are duplicates.

Action Items:

- [x] Support `https://` (`httplib::SSLClient`, port 443 by default) and optional extra headers (shared helper with TD-444), or reject `https://` clearly.
- [x] Recognize `--help` per command; stop global-option parsing at the command word.
- [x] Remove the unused include, fix the comment, fold the `http_*()` helpers into one.

**Fix (November 1, 2026):** `mns_cli` sends every request through one function that uses libcurl whenever `adai_core`
has it (the same `ADAI_METRICS_PUSH_CURL` build switch as `MetricsPushClient`, TD-444; the repository's builds all have
it), so `https://` is real TLS with certificate checks rather than httplib's `SSLClient`, which would have needed OpenSSL
support compiled into httplib. A build without libcurl refuses `https://` with a clear message. `parse_url()` now gives
`https://` port 443 (`http://` keeps 8083), keeps a URL path as a prefix for every request, accepts `[IPv6]:port`, and
reports a bad port (`abc`, `0`, `99999`, empty), a missing host or another scheme as an error (it used to keep 8083 for a
bad port and read `ftp://x` as a host). Extra headers come from the new `NAME_SERVICE_HEADERS` key (file or environment,
`METRICS_SERVER_HEADERS`'s format, hidden in config dumps) plus repeatable `--header 'Name: value'`; the CA bundle from
the new `NAME_SERVICE_CA_FILE` or `--ca-file`. The header-list parser moved to `Config` as `parse_http_header_list()`,
which `parse_metrics_server_headers()` now calls. Global options (`--url`, `--config`, `--header`, `--ca-file`,
`--help`) are read only before the command word; an unknown one is an error. `<command> --help` prints that command's
entry and sends nothing (the usage text is now a per-command table). Because a global option written after the command
now reaches the command, the commands that took bare positionals (`get`, `resolve`, `delete`, `roles`, `resolve-role`,
`promote`, `health`, `update`) now reject extra arguments and unknown options instead of ignoring them, so `delete m --url
X` is an error rather than a delete on the default server; `update` takes `--run-group` in any position (TD-449's
ordering item). The unused include is gone, the file comment is fixed, and the four `http_*()` copies are one function.
Tests (`mnsCliCommandsTests`): 8 new (`Td451ParseUrl`, `Td451ExactArguments`, `Td451Headers`, and three
`Td451MnsCliBinary` tests that run the real binary: `list --help` sent a request, a global option after the command and
an unknown global option were accepted, a bad URL port was ignored, and `https://127.0.0.1:1` connected to port 8083 with
plain HTTP; all three fail on the old binary). Verified by hand against a local TLS server with a self-signed
certificate: refused without a CA, accepted with `--ca-file` or `NAME_SERVICE_CA_FILE`, both header sources arrive, and
the URL path is prefixed.

Location in code: `src/MnsCliTool.cpp` (`make_http()`, `main()`); `src/MnsCliCommands.cpp` (`parse_url()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-451`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/MnsCliTool.cpp`
- `src/MnsCliCommands.cpp`

### TD-450: `mns_cli register` Takes Architecture Defaults from `config.mns.conf`, Not the Trainer's Config

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | MNS / CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MnsCliTool`, by inspection of the code, config files and guide. `main()` loads
`discover_config_path(--config, "config.mns.conf")`, the `mns_server` daemon's file, and `register` fills every
architecture field not given as a flag from it. The repository's `config.mns.conf` has `D_MODEL=512`, `NUM_HEADS=8`,
`D_FF=2048`, `MAX_SEQ_LENGTH=1024`; `config.trainer.conf`'s fallback block has `D_MODEL=768`, `NUM_HEADS=12`. So
`mns_cli register my-model chatbot` without architecture flags permanently registers 512/8, and since MNS is
authoritative (and architecture immutable), the trainer silently adopts it instead of the 768/12 its own config shows.
The usage text doesn't say where the defaults come from; `docs/operations/guides/mns-cli-guide.md` says they come
from `config.conf` (the pre-split file, now a fallback after `config.mns.conf`) "so registration stays consistent with
what the trainer will use", which the split configuration no longer guarantees.

Action Items:

- [x] Require explicit architecture flags for `register` (or a `--from-config <file>` that names the trainer's config), and print the architecture being registered before sending.
- [x] Decide whether `config.mns.conf` should keep an architecture block at all.
- [x] Update `mns_cli`'s usage text and mns-cli-guide.md.

**Fix (November 1, 2026):** `register` no longer takes any architecture field from `mns_cli`'s own config. Every field
comes from a flag, or the ones not given from `--from-config <file>`, the trainer's config read the way the trainer reads
it (`ConfigLoader::load()`, so the environment applies too). A field that is still missing is an error naming each missing
flag and pointing at `--from-config` (exit 1, nothing sent). A linked chatbot (`--encoder`/`--decoder`) needs no
architecture and can't take `--from-config`. Before sending, `mns_cli` prints the architecture and where it came from on
stderr (`Registering m (chatbot) with d_model=768 ... (from /etc/adai/config.trainer.conf)`), so stdout stays the server's
JSON. For a standalone kind the own layer count comes from `--num-layers`, else the file's matching key
(`NUM_DECODER_LAYERS` for a decoder, `NUM_ENCODER_LAYERS` otherwise), and the other count is 0; this also fixes TD-449's
layer-count item. `--num-layers` on a chatbot is now an error (it was ignored). `config.mns.conf`'s architecture block is
gone: `mns_server` never read it, and `mns_cli` no longer does. The usage text, mns-cli-guide.md and the MNS Manager GUI
guide are updated. Tests (`mnsCliCommandsTests`): 6 new (`Td450Register`, `Td450FromConfig`, and `Td450MnsCliBinary`,
which runs the real binary against a config with the old 512/8 block; the old binary sent it and failed only on the
connection), all failing on the old code; the existing register tests now pass a full architecture.

Location in code: `src/MnsCliTool.cpp` (`main()`'s config loading, `cmd_register()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-450`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/MnsCliTool.cpp`
- `src/MnsCliCommands.cpp`
- `config.mns.conf`
- `docs/operations/guides/mns-cli-guide.md`

### TD-449: `mns_cli` Request-Building Gaps: Layer Counts, Relink Resets, Encoding

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | MNS / CLI | Code fix (LOW, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MnsCliCommands`:
- **Layer counts (verified).** For `--kind encoder`/`decoder`/`world_model`, the own-kind layer field is set and the other
  zeroed only when `--num-layers` is given; without it the request carries the config's `num_encoder_layers` **and**
  `num_decoder_layers` (6/6), which `mns_server` rejects with a layer-count error instead of a usage message.
- **Relink resets (by inspection).** `link-world-model` always sends all eight connection fields with defaults for
  omitted flags, and `handle_link_world_model()` replaces the whole connection, so re-running it to change
  `--inject-every-n-layers` turns hippocampal memory off and resets its tuning.
- **Encoding (verified).** Names and query values aren't URL-encoded: `get a/state` requested `/models/a/state`;
  `list --role "a b&c"` built `/models?role=a b&c`. `json_escape()` escapes only `"`, `\`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, so other
  control characters (e.g. `\x01` in a tag) produce invalid JSON.
- **Minor.** `--sigreg-*` silently ignored for kinds other than `world_model`; `update` requires the exact order
  `<name> --run-group <value>`; `parse_url()` accepts `https://` though `mns_cli` connects with plain HTTP.

Action Items:

- [x] Require `--num-layers` for standalone kinds (or derive it from the config's matching field and zero the other). (Done with TD-450, November 1, 2026: `--num-layers`, else `--from-config`'s matching key, else a usage error; the other count is 0.)
- [x] Make `link-world-model` send only the fields given (server-side merge), or document full replacement in its usage.
- [x] URL-encode path segments and query values; escape all control characters as `\u00XX`; reject `--sigreg-*` for other kinds.
- [x] `update` option order and `parse_url()`'s `https://` handling (done with TD-451, November 1, 2026: `--run-group` in any position, extra arguments rejected; `https://` is real TLS on port 443).

**Fix (November 1, 2026):** the remaining items.
- **Relink.** `link-world-model` sends only the settings given, plus `"merge":true`; `handle_link_world_model()` then
  keeps the current value of every field the body leaves out. Without `merge` the body still replaces the whole link,
  omitted fields taking their defaults, because the Android dashboard sends only non-default values (kotlinx
  serialization omits defaults) and relies on that. A new `--hippocampal-disabled` turns the memory off now that
  omitting `--hippocampal-enabled` keeps it as it is; the two flags are exclusive.
- **Encoding.** A new `url_encode()` percent-encodes every model and role name in a path and every `list` filter value
  (everything but RFC 3986 unreserved characters). `json_escape()` writes every other control character below 0x20
  as `\u00XX`.
- **`--sigreg-*`** are a usage error for any kind but `world_model`.

Tests: `mnsCliCommandsTests` (link body, `--hippocampal-disabled`, control characters, `UrlEncoding`,
`SigregFlagsAreOnlyForWorldModels`) and `MNSLiveTest.LinkWorldModel_MergeKeepsOmittedFieldsAndPlainBodyReplaces`
(63/63 live tests pass against a local `mns_server`). With the real binaries, relinking with only
`--inject-every-n-layers 2` kept `hippocampal_memory_enabled:true` and capacity 64; the old binaries reset them to
`false` and 512, and the old server fails the live test.

Location in code: `src/MnsCliCommands.cpp` (`build_link_world_model_request()`, `json_escape()`, `url_encode()`, path
builders, `build_register_request()`), `src/ModelNameService.cpp` (`handle_link_world_model()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/MnsCliCommands.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/ModelNameService.cpp`
- `tests/mns_cli_commands_test.cpp`, `tests/model_name_service_live_test.cpp`

### TD-448: `mns_cli` Ignores Unknown Flags, Misreads `set-training` Arguments and Aborts on Bad Numbers

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | MNS / CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MnsCliCommands` and verified (scratch program against the builders, and the real `mns_cli`):
- **Unknown flags ignored.** Every `build_*_request()` skips arguments it doesn't recognize, and a value-taking flag
  at the end of the line is dropped. `register m chat --dmodel 256` built a request with the config file's
  `d_model` (512) and no error. Architecture is immutable after `register` (CLAUDE.md), so the only fix is delete
  and re-register. `list`, `link-world-model` and `set-candidate` behave the same way.
- **`set-training`'s stray arguments.** Anything other than `--new-run` becomes the metrics session key:
  `set-training m --new_run` built `{"state":"training","new_run":false,"metrics_session_key":"--new_run"}`,
  continuing the current run and linking a bogus metrics session.
- **Unchecked numbers.** `std::stoul`/`std::stoi`/`std::stof` exceptions are caught nowhere (not in the builders,
  not in `MnsCliTool.cpp`'s `main()`): `mns_cli register foo chatbot --d-model abc` printed `terminate called after
  throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'` and aborted with a core dump (exit 134). `--d-model -1` was sent as
  18,446,744,073,709,551,615 (`stoul` wraps); `512x` → 512.

Action Items:

- [x] Reject unknown flags and flags missing their value with a usage error in every builder.
- [x] `set-training`: accept at most one positional session key and reject `-`-prefixed unknowns.
- [x] Parse numbers with a checked helper (whole string, positive, in range), returning `make_error()`; catch any remaining exception in `main()` with exit 2.
- [x] Tests for misspelled flags, stray `set-training` arguments, malformed/negative numbers.

**Fix (November 1, 2026):** the builders with options (`list`, `register`, `link-world-model`,
`set-training`, `set-candidate`) read them through one `parse_options()` helper in `MnsCliCommands.cpp`: an
unknown option, a value flag with no value (last, or followed by another `--` flag), a stray positional and a
`--tag`/`--summary` without `key=value` are usage errors. Counts use the shared `parse_strict_size()`
(architecture sizes, `--num-layers`, `--sigreg-num-sketches` and `--hippocampal-capacity` at least 1, layer
counts, `--inject-every-n-layers` and `--limit` at least 0, at most `INT_MAX`), floats `parse_strict_float()`
(finite; `--sigreg-lambda` and the alphas at least 0, the decays 0–1). `set-training` takes `--new-run` and at
most one session key. `main()` reports a trailing `--url`/`--config` and catches anything still thrown (exit 2).
Eight new tests, one running the real binary, all fail on the old code (it exited 134 on
`register foo chatbot --d-model abc`). Every `mns_cli` invocation in the docs and scripts still parses.

Location in code: `src/MnsCliCommands.cpp` (`parse_options()` and the builders); `src/MnsCliTool.cpp` (`main()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/MnsCliCommands.cpp`
- `src/MnsCliTool.cpp`
- `tests/mns_cli_commands_test.cpp`

### TD-438: `metrics_api_server` Accepts Invalid Numbers and Exits 0 on Bad Arguments

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | Metrics / Server CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MetricsApiServerArgs` and verified (scratch program against the real parser, and the
real `metrics_api_server`):
- **Unchecked numbers.** `parse_metrics_api_server_args()` uses `std::atoi`/`std::strtoul` with no range
  checks. `--port abc` → 0, and **the real server listened on a random ephemeral port** (39915) while
  printing `Server starting on http://0.0.0.0:0`; `--port 99999` printed `:99999` and **listened on 34463**
  (mod 65536). `--max-live-sessions -1` wraps to 18,446,744,073,709,551,615 (no cap);
  `--sweep-interval-seconds 0` disables `MetricsSessionRegistry`'s eviction sweep; `--persist-seconds 1e3`
  → 1 and `8081x` → 8081 (truncated); negative ports, pool sizes and intervals are accepted.
- **Saved admin overrides.** `apply_metrics_admin_overrides()` re-applies `daemon_config.db` values at
  startup with the same gaps (`stoull("-1")` wraps; `"50abc"` → 50; negative TTLs applied), so a bad
  `PUT /admin/config` (TD-306) persists across restarts.
- **Exit code.** `main()` prints usage and **exits 0** on any parse error (verified with `--bogus`), so a
  mistyped flag in a unit's `ExecStart` looks like a clean stop and `Restart=on-failure` doesn't retry. A
  value-taking flag with no value is reported as "Unknown option".

Action Items:

- [x] Parse numbers with a checked helper (whole string, in range: port 1–65535, counts and intervals ≥ 1 or a documented 0 meaning) shared with TD-240; reject with a clear message.
- [x] Validate the saved admin overrides the same way (skip and warn on out-of-range values).
- [x] Exit non-zero on parse errors; report "missing value for --flag".
- [x] Add tests for non-numeric, partial, negative and out-of-range values.

**Fix (November 1, 2026).** `MetricsApiServerArgs.cpp` has one table of its 13 numeric settings (flag, admin-store key, range), used
by both `parse_metrics_api_server_args()` and `apply_metrics_admin_overrides()`. Each value goes through TD-240's
`parse_strict_int()` plus the range, which matches `ConfigLoader::validate()` (TD-288): `--port` 1–65535, `--max-live-sessions`,
`--max-memory-records`, `--staleness-threshold-seconds` and `--db-pool-size` at least 1, the rest at least 0, where 0 is the
documented "off"/"no limit" (`--sweep-interval-seconds 0` stays the TD-446 way to turn the sweep off; negatives no longer do). A bad
flag returns `Invalid value for --port: '99999' (expected 1-65535)`, a value flag with no value `Missing value for --db-path`, and
`main()` now exits 1 on any parse error. A saved admin override that fails the same check is skipped with a warning
(`Ignoring saved admin setting max_live_sessions='-1' (expected a whole number >= 1)`); range-checking the `PUT` itself is TD-306.
Tests: `EveryNumericFlagRefusesNonNumbersPartialsAndNegatives` (13 flags × `abc`/`8081x`/`1e3`/`-1`/empty),
`OutOfRangeValuesAreRefused`, `AFlagMissingItsValueSaysSo`, `OutOfRangeOrPartialSavedValuesAreSkipped`, `DocumentedZeroesAreAccepted`,
and `SighupTest.MetricsApiServerExitsOneOnABadFlag` (the real binary exits 1 for `--port abc`, `--port 99999`, `--bogus` and a
valueless `--max-live-sessions`; the old binary started on `--port abc`); all but the zeroes guard fail on the old code.

Location in code: `src/MetricsApiServerArgs.cpp` (`parse_metrics_api_server_args()`, `apply_metrics_admin_overrides()`); `src/TrainingMetricsAPIServer.cpp` (`main()`'s error exit); tagged `TD-438`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainingMetricsAPIServer.cpp`
- `src/MetricsApiServerArgs.hpp`
- `tests/metrics_api_server_args_test.cpp`, `tests/sighup_test.cpp`, `tests/CMakeLists.txt`

### TD-415: LeJEPA Pass Ignores Segment Ranges and Strands Claims After a Crash

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainingTool | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainingTool`, by inspection. `run_lejepa_training_pass()` loads each
acquired file with `load_conversation_pairs(path, pairs)`, without the TD-205 segment range the chatbot
path passes, so a file queued as N segments is loaded in full N times when its segments are claimed.
Its run id is always `derive_run_id()` (hostname prefix + PID tail, TD-404), never MNS-allocated, and
claimed files are only reclaimable by the same run id. After a crash, kill, or SIGTERM (whose handler
exits without releasing, TD-416), the claimed files stay claimed by a run id no later process will have,
until released by hand.

Action Items:

- [x] Pass `file_ranges()` through the LeJEPA loader; allocate a stable run id for the world model (MNS, or a persisted one per world-model directory) so a restarted pass can reclaim its own files.

**Fix (November 1, 2026):** done after TD-403 let `trainer_service` run LeJEPA passes, where both problems repeat
every pass.
- **Segments.** `run_lejepa_training_pass()` loads each claimed unit with its own segment range, as the chatbot pass
  does, so a file queued as N segments is read once in total and each segment's trained record has its own count.
- **Run id.** The new `persistent_run_id()` (`src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`) keeps the pass's run id in
  `<world-model checkpoint dir>/lejepa_run_id`: `RUN_ID` when set, else an id created once as `lejepa-` +
  `derive_run_id()` + 8 random hex digits (temporary file + rename). Registries hand a claim back to the run id that
  made it, so the next pass reclaims a crashed, killed or SIGTERMed pass's files. The random part also keeps two hosts
  from sharing an id (TD-404's collision, for this pass). If the file can't be written the pass still runs with the new
  id and logs a warning.

Tests: `PersistentRunId.ConfiguredWinsElseTheIdIsCreatedOnceAndReused` and, against the real binary,
`SighupTest.LejepaPassTrainsEachSegmentOnceAndReclaimsAfterACrash` (a file queued as two 2-row segments, both claimed by
a "crashed" pass under the persisted id: the next pass exits 0 and records 2 rows per segment). The old binary couldn't
claim them and trained nothing; on unclaimed segments it recorded 4 rows for each (the whole file twice).

A world-model directory is meant for one trainer at a time; two concurrent LeJEPA passes on one directory would share
the id, as they already share the checkpoint.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (`run_lejepa_training_pass()`), `src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`
(`persistent_run_id()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`
- `src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`

### TD-403: `trainer_service` Drops `--objective` and `--dataset-kind`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | Training / CLI | Code fix (LOW, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainerArgs`, by inspection. `trainer_service` parses its command
line with the same parser but forwards only `--config`, `--model` and `--gpu-strategy` to each child
(plus `--foreground --admin-port N resume`). `--objective` and `--dataset-kind` given to
`trainer_service` are silently ignored, so the always-on service can only run chatbot training, never
LeJEPA world-model pretraining.

Action Items:

- [x] Decide whether `trainer_service` should support `--objective=lejepa` (forward both flags) or reject them with a clear message. Owner decision (November 1, 2026): always forward both, since the service must be able to train every kind of model.
- [x] Give the LeJEPA pass the per-pass admin API (status, checkpoint, pause draining) the chatbot pass has (done November 1, 2026, below).

**Fix (November 1, 2026):** the new `trainer_service_child_argv()` (`src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`) builds each
pass's command line and always includes `--objective=<objective>` and `--dataset-kind <kind>`, the kind from
`resolve_dataset_kind()` (an explicit `--dataset-kind`, else `world_model` for `lejepa` and `chatbot` otherwise).
`trainer_service` logs both at startup and lists them in `--help`. Forwarding alone wasn't enough: `resume`, the command
every pass runs, ignored `--objective` and always ran chatbot training. It now runs the LeJEPA pass for
`--objective=lejepa` (needs `WORLD_MODEL_ENABLED=true`, `NUM_EPOCHS` epochs over whatever is pending), and that pass now
uses resume's exit codes (TD-523): 3 when nothing is pending, 1 when the registry can't be asked. It used to return 1
for both, which `trainer_service` would count as a failure and back off.

Tests: `TrainerServiceChildArgv.AlwaysPassesTheObjectiveAndTheDatasetKind`, and against the real binaries
`SighupTest.TrainerServicePassesObjectiveAndDatasetKindToEveryPass` (a copy of `trainer_service` with a stub
`incremental_trainer` beside it records each pass's arguments) and
`SighupTest.LejepaResumeTrainsTheWorldModelAndThenReportsNothingPending` (a queued `world_model` file is trained into
`world_model_checkpoint/`, exit 0, then exit 3). On the old binaries the stub saw neither flag, and `--objective=lejepa
resume` ran chatbot training, exited 1 and wrote no world-model checkpoint.

**Admin API for the LeJEPA pass (November 1, 2026):** the per-pass admin API hosting moved out of the chatbot `resume`
into a `PassAdminApi` helper (`IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`) that both resume passes use, and
`run_lejepa_training_pass()` takes its `TrainerControlState`. The pass reports its phase (`loading_data`, `training`,
`checkpointing`, then `idle`), run id, epoch, samples and losses; writes a checkpoint on `POST /admin/checkpoint`; takes
`AUTO_SAVE_*` live from `PUT /admin/config`; and on `POST /admin/pause` stops at the next batch, checkpoints, releases
its files to the pool and exits 1, as a paused chatbot pass does. Test:
`SighupTest.LejepaPassAnswersTheAdminApiAndDrainsOnPause` (status shows training with the `lejepa-` run id, a requested
checkpoint completes, pause exits 1 with the file unclaimed); the old binary never answered `/admin/status`. TD-415 (the
segment ranges) was fixed the same day.

Location in code: `src/TrainerServiceMain.cpp`, `src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.{hpp,cpp}` (`trainer_service_child_argv()`),
`src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (`resume`, `run_lejepa_training_pass()`).

- `src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`
