Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainerArgs`, by inspection. `--dataset-kind <k>` is stored as given
and `resolve_dataset_kind()` returns it unchanged. With `RemoteTransport` it becomes a URL segment,
which `registry_server` rejects (404) unless it's `encoder`/`decoder`/`world_model`/`chatbot`. With
`LocalTransport`, `DatasetRegistry` joins it as `session_dir + "/" + kind`, so a typo silently selects
a new, empty sub-pool ("no pending data") and a value containing `..` or `/` puts the local registry
files outside `session_dir`.

Action Items:

- [x] Validate the value against the four kinds (shared with `dataset_manager --kind` and `DATASET_KIND`) and reject anything else.

**Fix (November 1, 2026):** one list, `adai::is_dataset_kind()` (inline in `src/Config.hpp`), which
`dataset_manager`'s `is_valid_dataset_kind()` now calls. `parse_incremental_trainer_global_args()` rejects any other
`--dataset-kind` value with `Invalid value for --dataset-kind: '<v>' (expected encoder, decoder, world_model or chatbot)`,
so `incremental_trainer` exits 1 (TD-401's error path). As a backstop for programmatic callers, `DatasetRegistry`'s
transport factory and `DatasetRegistry::local_pool_dir()` throw `std::invalid_argument` for an unknown non-empty kind,
remote or local. Tests: `ParseIncrementalTrainerGlobalArgs.DatasetKindMustBeOneOfTheFourKinds`,
`DatasetConfigTest.AnUnknownDatasetKindIsRefused`, and `--dataset-kind ../x status` added to
`SighupTest.IncrementalTrainerExitsOneOnABadFlag` (the old binary took `../x` and went on to abort). All three fail on
the old code.

### TD-401: `incremental_trainer` Flag Parsing Crashes or Silently Misreads Bad Values

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | Training / CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainerArgs` and verified against `build/debug/bin/incremental_trainer`:
- `--admin-port abc` **aborts the process**: `std::stoi` throws and `main()` calls
  `parse_incremental_trainer_global_args()` outside any `try` (`terminate called … what(): stoi`, exit
  134). An out-of-range value throws `out_of_range` the same way.
- `--admin-port 8084x` is accepted as 8084, and no port range is checked.
- `--objective=` isn't validated: `main()` only tests `== "lejepa"` and `resolve_dataset_kind()` maps
  anything else to `chatbot`, so `--objective=lejpa` was accepted silently. With `train`, that runs
  chatbot training (on the chatbot pool) instead of world-model pretraining. The test
  `UnrecognizedObjectiveFallsBackToChatbot` asserts this fallback.
- A flag missing its value (for example a trailing `--config`) is appended to the positional
  arguments instead of rejected (`status --config` carried on); the tests specify this too.

Action Items:

- [x] Parse `--admin-port` with full-string, range-checked parsing (1–65535) and report a usage error; wrap the parse in `main()`'s error handling.
- [x] Reject unknown `--objective` values (`chatbot`/`lejepa` only) and flags missing their value, with a clear message; update the tests that assert the permissive behaviour.

**Fix (November 1, 2026):** `parse_incremental_trainer_global_args()` sets `error`/`error_message`, and
`main()` prints it with the usage and exits 1 before loading any config. A global value flag (`--config`,
`--gpu-strategy`, `--model`, `--admin-port`, `--dataset-kind`) with no value (last, or followed by another
`--` flag) says `Missing value for <flag>`. `--admin-port` goes through the shared `parse_strict_int()` and
must be 1–65535. `--objective=` must be `chatbot` or `lejepa`, and a bare `--objective` says to use `=`.
Command flags such as `reset --yes` still pass through. Four tests that asserted the permissive behaviour
were replaced; `SighupTest.IncrementalTrainerExitsOneOnABadFlag` runs the real binary, which on the old
code aborted with SIGABRT for `--admin-port abc` and `99999` and ran on for `--objective=lejpa` and a
trailing `--config`. `resolve_dataset_kind()` keeps its chatbot fallback, now unreachable from argv.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.cpp` (`parse_incremental_trainer_global_args()`).

- `src/IncrementalTrainerArgs.cpp`

Description:
Found alongside TD-246. On `SIGHUP`, `main()` applies only the log level and four generation
fields (`max_gen_length`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `strategy`), and warns only for a port change.
Changes to session timeout, RAG settings, model/architecture, GPU settings and the rest are
dropped without any message, while the log reports a successful configuration reload. Reload also
doesn't redo MNS resolution, so the in-memory `config` reverts to local file values for model path
and architecture (unused after startup, but wrong). Found by reading the code.

running, `RAG_NUM_DOCS`/`RAG_THRESHOLD`/`RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH` (a new `RAGInference` over the same documents, swapped
in with `enableRAG()`, so a request in flight keeps the engine it started with). The new
`keep_loaded_model_settings()` (`src/ChatbotApiServerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`) copies the loaded model's settings (model and
vocabulary paths, architecture, draft model, world-model and hippocampal setup) from the running config into the

### TD-250: Hippocampal Memory in `chatbot_api_server` Is Lost on Crash and Can Land in the Working Directory

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | Inference / Serving / Server | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-246. When the world model and hippocampal memory are attached
(experimental, TD-193/194), the memory changes with every generated response, but `main()` saves it
**only on graceful shutdown**. A crash, `SIGKILL`, OOM kill or the hang in TD-248 loses everything
since the last clean stop. Its paths are `MODEL_PATH + ".hippocampal"`, `".hippocampal.assoc"`
and `".hippocampal.swap"`, so with an empty `MODEL_PATH` (random-init mode) they become hidden
files in the process's working directory.

Action Items:

- [x] Save periodically (time- or write-count-based) using write-to-temp-then-rename, in addition to shutdown.
- [x] Add an explicit `HIPPOCAMPAL_STATE_PATH` (defaulting to the current derivation), and refuse to attach with neither it nor `MODEL_PATH` set.
- [x] Test: state survives a simulated crash after the periodic save.

**Fix (November 1, 2026):** `chatbot_api_server` saves a changed memory every `HIPPOCAMPAL_SAVE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (new,
default 300; 0 = only at shutdown) from its main loop, and once more at shutdown, through a new
`EncoderDecoderModel::save_hippocampal_memory()`. That takes `model_mutex_`, which every memory change happens under
(generation), so it can save while requests are being served and both files come from the same moment. It saves only
when the memory changed: `HippocampalMemory` has a `revision()` counter, bumped by writes, evictions,
`commit_attention()`, decays, recalls, `clear()` and loads. `HippocampalMemory::save()`/`save_associations()` now write
`<path>.tmp` with checked writes (`adai::binio::Writer`) and rename it over the file, so a crash or failed write mid-save
keeps the previous file (TD-398's unchecked-write item). The state path is the new `HIPPOCAMPAL_STATE_PATH`, else
`MODEL_PATH + ".hippocampal"` as before; the association matrix and swap file are that path plus `.assoc` and `.swap`
(the old names when it's derived). With neither key set the memory isn't attached and a warning says why. Tests:
`Td250HippocampalSave` (atomic save, a failed save keeps the previous file, the revision changes only with the memory),
`EncoderDecoderModelTest.SaveHippocampalMemorySkipsUnchangedState`, config parsing/validation, and two real-binary tests:
with a 1 s interval, a SIGKILL after one `/chat` leaves a loadable state holding the request's episode (the old binary
wrote nothing within 10 s), and with no path the memory isn't attached (the old binary attached it and left
`.hippocampal.assoc` in the working directory).

Location in code: `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp` (hippocampal attach, shutdown save); tagged `TODO: See TD-250`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`
- `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/HippocampalMemory.{hpp,cpp}` (if atomic save lives there)

### TD-249: `chatbot_api_server`'s `SIGHUP` Handler Isn't Async-Signal-Safe

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | Inference / Serving / Server | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-246. `signal_handler()`'s doc comment says it "is async-signal-safe and only
sets atomic flags", but the `SIGHUP` branch also calls `adai::Logger::info()`. spdlog takes locks
and allocates, so a `SIGHUP` delivered to a thread that's mid-log can deadlock or corrupt logger
state. The main loop's reload branch already logs the reload, so the call isn't needed.

Action Items:

- [x] Remove the logger call from the handler; log "SIGHUP received" in the main loop when it sees the flag.
- [x] Check the other daemons' signal handlers for the same pattern.

**Fix (November 1, 2026):** the `SIGHUP` branch only sets `reload_config_requested`; the main loop logs "SIGHUP received
- configuration reload requested" when it picks the flag up, so the handler now really only sets atomic flags. The other
handlers: `trainer_service` and `metrics_api_server` only set flags; `mns_server` and `registry_server` call httplib's
`Server::stop()` from the handler (it is `shutdown()`/`close()` plus an atomic exchange, but has the pre-listen gap
tracked as TD-464 and TD-494); `incremental_trainer`'s handler logs and calls `std::exit(0)`, already tracked as TD-416
(no checkpoint, no release of claimed files, exit code 0).

Location in code: `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp` (`signal_handler()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-249`.

- `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`

### TD-248: `chatbot_api_server` Can Hang If Shutdown Arrives During Server Startup

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | Inference / Serving / Server | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-246 and confirmed against the vendored cpp-httplib source.
`ChatbotAPI::start()` sets its `running_` flag, then calls `httplib::Server::listen()`. httplib's
`Server::stop()` only acts once the server is inside `listen_internal()` (`if (is_running_) {...}`).
A `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` that arrives after the server thread starts but before httplib is listening
(e.g. a quick `systemctl restart`) has its `stop()` silently ignored. `listen()` then blocks
forever, `server_thread.join()` hangs, and further signals do nothing because the shutdown flag is
already set. Only systemd's stop timeout or `SIGKILL` ends the process, which also skips the
hippocampal memory save (TD-250).

Action Items:

- [x] After launching the server thread, wait for `httplib::Server::wait_until_ready()` before entering the main loop; or, on shutdown, call `stop()` repeatedly until the server thread exits.
- [x] Test: requesting shutdown immediately after start terminates promptly.

**Fix (November 1, 2026):** the fix is in `ChatbotAPI` rather than the server's main loop, so every caller gets it.
`stop()` is final for an instance: it sets `stop_requested_`, which `start()` checks before listening (so a stop that came
before the server thread reached `start()` makes it return without listening), then waits while `start()` is running,
sends httplib's `Server::stop()` once httplib reports it is listening, and returns once `start()` has returned. The old
`stop()` cleared `running_` itself, so a second call couldn't help either. `Server::stop()` is sent only once (a
`listener_stop_sent_` flag): calling it again while `listen()` winds down trips httplib's `assert` on the already closed
socket, which the first version of this fix hit (exit 134). Tests: `ChatbotAPITest.StopBeforeStartIsNotLost` (failed on
the old code: `start()` listened for the full 5 s) and `StopRightAfterStartBeginsAlwaysEndsIt` (20 trials; the old code
hung), and `ChatbotApiServerStartupTest.SigtermDuringStartupExitsPromptly`, which runs the real binary, reads its output
through a pipe and sends SIGTERM right after `[4/4] Starting API server`: the old binary was still running 10 s later in
10 of 10 trials, the fixed one exits 0 in well under a second. The same narrow window remains in `registry_server`
(TD-494), `mns_server` (TD-464) and `metrics_api_server` (TD-528), which could use the same approach.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp` (server thread start, shutdown), `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (`start()`, `stop()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-248`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`
- `src/ChatbotAPI.{hpp,cpp}`

### TD-242: `SIGHUP` Reload Discards `chatbot_api_server`'s CLI Generation Overrides

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| November 1, 2026 | Inference / Serving / CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-240. `ConfigLoader::reload()` rebuilds the config from the file and env only,
and `ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`'s main loop then pushes `max_gen_length`, `temperature`, `top_p` and
`strategy` from it into `ChatbotAPI::set_generation_config()`. CLI flags are never re-applied, so a
server started with `--temperature 0.7` silently reverts to the file's temperature on the first
`SIGHUP`, contradicting the documented precedence (CLI > env > file). Found by reading the code.

Action Items:

- [x] Re-apply the original argv overrides after `reload()` (keep `argc`/`argv` or the parsed overrides), or record which keys came from the CLI and keep them fixed across reloads.
- [x] Log which settings changed on reload, and which were held by CLI overrides.
- [x] Test: CLI-set temperature survives a reload.

**Fix (November 1, 2026).** `ConfigLoader::reload()` takes two more optional arguments: a callback that re-applies the binary's
command-line flags to the reloaded config (after the file and environment, before validation, so a flag that makes the result
invalid is caught as at startup), and the set of keys those flags set. `apply_chatbot_api_server_args()` now records that set
(`ChatbotApiServerArgsResult::cli_keys`, e.g. `TEMPERATURE` for `--temperature`), and `chatbot_api_server`'s reload branch passes a
callback that runs the same parser over the original `argv` again. A file change to a held key is logged as
"TEMPERATURE changed in the file but is held by a command-line flag" instead of as applied or needing a restart (TD-285's logging
covers every other change), and the reload now logs the generation values it applies
("Generation configuration updated: max_length=… temperature=… top_p=… strategy=…"). Tests:
`ReloadReappliesCommandLineOverridesAndSaysWhichAreHeld`, `ReloadValidatesWithTheCommandLineOverridesApplied`,
`RecordsTheConfigKeysTheFlagsSet`, and `ChatbotApiServerStartupTest.ACommandLineSettingSurvivesAReload` (the real binary with
`--temperature 0.3`: after the file changes `TEMPERATURE` and `TOP_P` and a `SIGHUP`, temperature stays 0.3 and top_p becomes 0.5;
fails on the old binary).

Location in code: `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp` (main loop reload branch); tagged `TD-242`.

- `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`
- `src/ChatbotApiServerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}` (`reload()`)
- `tests/config_test.cpp`, `tests/chatbot_api_server_args_test.cpp`, `tests/chatbot_api_server_startup_test.cpp`

### TD-290: `ConfigLoader` Output Hygiene

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 31, 2026 | Config | Code fix (LOW, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-283:

- Load-time messages go to `std::cerr` (partly unavoidable before the logger starts), and the header's
  inline `gpu_strategy_from_string()` writes to `std::cerr` too.
- `print()` writes to `std::cout` and covers only server, architecture, generation and RAG settings
  (no metrics, registry, MNS, GPU, training or world-model sections).
- `HIPPOCAMPAL_COVERAGE_LOSS_WEIGHT` ships in `config.chatbot.conf`/`config.trainer.conf`, is
  deliberately unread, and produces an "Unknown configuration key" warning on every load.

Action Items:

- [x] Buffer pre-logger messages and replay them through `adai::Logger` once initialised.
- [x] Extend `print()` (or a `to_string()` used by every binary) to all sections, still redacting secrets.
- [x] Accept reserved keys silently (or remove the key from the shipped files).

**Fix (October 31, 2026).** Every load-time message in `Config.cpp` (file not found, loading from, invalid line/value, unknown key,
bad environment values, unknown `GPU_STRATEGY`) now goes through a new `Logger::deferred()`. Before the binary calls `Logger::init()`
it prints to the console as before and keeps the message (at most 256); the next `init()` with a log file writes them to that file
with their original times, so start-up warnings are in the log, not only on a terminal nobody watches. After `init()` it's an
ordinary log call. `gpu_strategy_from_string()` moved out of the header into `Config.cpp` and logs instead of writing to `std::cerr`;
`GPU_STRATEGY` is matched in any case like the TD-289 enums. A new `ConfigLoader::to_string()` lists every setting by its config key,
grouped into 16 sections (server, logging, architecture, training, checkpointing, generation, RAG, GPU, metrics client and daemon,
dataset registry, FTP, MNS, trainer admin, world model, hippocampal memory), with secret values (`SECRET`/`PASSWORD`/`TOKEN`/`HEADERS`/
`CREDENTIAL` keys and `METRICS_DB_URL`) shown as `<hidden>`; `print()` logs it through `Logger` (it wrote a four-section listing to
`std::cout`). `chatbot_api_server` is still the only caller; the daemons log their own resolved settings, which include CLI overrides.
`HIPPOCAMPAL_COVERAGE_LOSS_WEIGHT` is a reserved key, accepted without a warning, and stays in the shipped files. Tests:
`ConfigStartupLogTests` (its own binary, since it needs a logger nobody has set up: a load warning before `init()` reaches the log
file, before the logger's own lines, and the reserved key isn't mentioned; fails on the old code), `ToStringCoversEverySectionAndHidesSecrets`,
`PrintGoesThroughTheLoggerNotStdout`, `GpuStrategyIsMatchedInAnyCase`.

Location in code: `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}`; tagged `TD-290`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/Logger.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/config_test.cpp`, `tests/config_startup_log_test.cpp`

### TD-289: `ConfigLoader` Keeps Inline Comments and Silently Accepts Enum Typos

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 31, 2026 | Config | Code fix (LOW, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-283 and confirmed by running the real loader. `#` is a comment only at the start
of a line, so `MODEL_PATH=/models/chat # production model` stores the comment as part of the path.
`TOKENIZER_MODE` treats anything but `unicode` (e.g. the typo `utf8`) as ASCII without a warning;
`STRATEGY`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `METRICS_STORAGE_BACKEND` and `DATASET_KIND` aren't checked at load either.

Action Items:

- [x] Strip an unquoted ` #…` suffix (or document that inline comments aren't supported, and warn when a value contains ` #`).
- [x] Warn on unknown enum values for `TOKENIZER_MODE`, `STRATEGY`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `METRICS_STORAGE_BACKEND`, `DATASET_KIND`.

**Fix (October 31, 2026).** A file value now ends at an unquoted `#` that follows a space or tab, so
`MODEL_PATH=/models/chat # production model` is `/models/chat` and `PORT=8080 # note` is 8080 again (TD-287 had made it refused).
A `#` with no space before it stays (`FTP_DATA_SERVER_SECRET=abc#def`), and a value in matching quotes is taken as written, with only
a comment allowed after the closing quote. `TOKENIZER_MODE` (`unicode`/`ascii`), `STRATEGY`, `LOG_LEVEL` (also `WARNING`, as `Logger`
takes it, stored as `WARN`), `METRICS_STORAGE_BACKEND` (`sqlite+file`/`sqlite`/`postgres+file`/`postgres`/`file`) and `DATASET_KIND`
(empty or `encoder`/`decoder`/`world_model`/`chatbot`) are matched in any case and stored in their canonical spelling; anything else is
refused with a warning and the default stays, in the file and the environment. Whether this build has PostgreSQL is still TD-439's.
Tests: `AnInlineCommentEndsTheValue`, `AnUnknownEnumValueLeavesTheDefault`, `EnumValuesAreMatchedInAnyCase`,
`EnvironmentEnumValuesAreCheckedTheSameWay`, `ATokenizerModeTypoDoesntSwitchToAscii` (all fail on the old loader),
`AnEmptyDatasetKindIsTheLegacyPool`; `EmptyValues` now expects an empty `LOG_LEVEL` to keep the default.

Location in code: `src/Config.cpp` (`load_from_file()`); tagged `TD-289`.

### TD-288: `ConfigLoader::validate()` Misses Fields That Crash or Misbehave

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 31, 2026 | Config | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-283 and confirmed by running the real `validate()`: it accepts
`gradient_accumulation_steps = 0` (`ChatbotTrainer` divides by it and takes a modulo by it),
`learning_rate = -1` and `gpu_memory_fraction = 7.5`. It also never checks `batch_size`,
`num_epochs`, `weight_decay`, any adaptive-clipping field, `hippocampal_association_decay`/
`cross_reference_alpha`, any metrics/registry/FTP/MNS/trainer-admin port, interval or size,
`FTP_PASV_PORT_MIN ≤ MAX`, or auto-save values. And `validate()` itself only runs on reload (TD-241).

Action Items:

- [x] Add range checks for every numeric field used for division, allocation, ports or probabilities.
- [x] Run `validate()` at startup in every binary (TD-241 covers `chatbot_api_server`).
- [x] Tests for each new rule.

**Fix (October 31, 2026).** `validate()` now also checks: `learning_rate > 0`, `num_epochs`/`batch_size`/
`gradient_accumulation_steps >= 1`, `weight_decay`/`gradient_clip >= 0`, every adaptive-clipping field (min > 0, max >= min,
EMA decay in (0, 1], headroom and spike k > 0, warmup >= 0), `hippocampal_association_decay` in (0, 1],
`hippocampal_cross_reference_alpha >= 0`, `gpu_memory_fraction` in (0, 1], `gpu_device_id >= 0`, `speculative_num_candidates >= 1`,
`vocab_build_size >= 0`, every metrics/registry/FTP/MNS/trainer-admin port in 1–65535, `FTP_PASV_PORT_MIN <= MAX`, the trainer's
admin and child admin ports differing, and every metrics, registry, FTP, MNS and auto-save interval, size and count. Fields whose 0 means
"off" or "no limit" (retention days, file rotation size, claim lease, auto-save intervals, `MAX_SESSIONS_TO_KEEP`…) accept 0 and refuse
negatives; the rest need at least 1. A new `ConfigLoader::validate_or_exit()` logs every error and exits 1; `metrics_api_server`,
`mns_server`, `registry_server`, `trainer_service` and `incremental_trainer` call it right after loading their config file
(`chatbot_api_server`'s startup call remains TD-241's). CLI flags that override the file are checked by the per-binary items
(TD-240/TD-438/TD-456/TD-488). Tests: `TheDefaultsPassEveryRule`, `ValidateRejectsEachBadValue` (60 cases, including the TD's three),
`ValidateAcceptsTheDocumentedZeroes`, `EveryShippedConfigFilePassesValidation`, and `SighupTest.EveryBinaryRefusesAnInvalidConfigAtStartup`
(each of the five real binaries with `GRADIENT_ACCUMULATION_STEPS=0` exits 1; on the old code `metrics_api_server` started).

### TD-287: `ConfigLoader` Accepts Negative and Partial Numbers

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 31, 2026 | Config | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-283 and confirmed by running the real loader. File values are parsed with
unchecked `std::stoi`/`stof`/`stoull`/`stoul`: `PORT=8080x` gives 8080 (trailing garbage dropped),
and `size_t` fields wrap negatives, so `D_MODEL=-1` gives **18446744073709551615**. Nothing
range-checks at load time (TD-241), so these reach model construction and port binding directly.

Action Items:

- [x] Use full-consumption parsing that rejects negatives for `size_t` fields; warn and keep the default on any rejection.
- [x] Tests for trailing garbage and negative sizes.

**Fix (October 31, 2026).** Every number in `load_from_file()` (about 85 call sites) and the `get_env_int()`/`get_env_size_t()`/
`get_env_float()` helpers now goes through three strict parsers in `Config.cpp`: `parse_int()`, `parse_size()` and `parse_float()`.
Each must consume the whole value; `parse_size()` refuses any `-` (so `D_MODEL=-1` no longer becomes 18446744073709551615), and
`parse_float()` refuses `nan`/`inf`. A rejected file value logs "Invalid value for KEY" and keeps the previous value; a rejected env
value warns and is ignored, as before. Signed `int` keys still accept negatives (`GPU_DEVICE_ID=-1`); range checks are TD-288's.
Until TD-289 strips inline comments, `PORT=8080 # note` is now refused (and warned about) instead of reading as 8080; none of the
shipped config files has one. Tests: `ANumberWithTrailingCharactersLeavesTheDefault`, `ANegativeSizeLeavesTheDefault`,
`ANonFiniteFloatLeavesTheDefault`, `EnvironmentNumbersAreCheckedTheSameWay` (all four fail on the old parser) and
`WellFormedNumbersStillLoad`.

Location in code: `src/Config.cpp` (`load_from_file()`, `get_env_*()` helpers); tagged `TD-287`.

### TD-286: `ConfigLoader` Parses Booleans Two Different Ways

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 31, 2026 | Config | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-283 and confirmed by running the real loader. Eight file keys accept
`true/1/yes/on` case-insensitively; seven others (`GRADIENT_CLIP_ADAPTIVE`, `ENABLE_METRICS_SERVICE`,
`METRICS_ENABLE_PERSISTENCE`, `METRICS_ENABLE_PROMETHEUS`, `METRICS_API_ALLOW_CONTROL`,
`ENABLE_GENERATION_QUALITY_METRICS`, `FTPS_ENABLED`) accept only lowercase `true/1/yes`. Any other
spelling is silently **false**, with no warning: `ENABLE_METRICS_SERVICE=On` and
`METRICS_API_ALLOW_CONTROL=True` both turn the feature off. The env parser is stricter (warns on
unknown values), except `FTPS_ENABLED`, which bypasses it.

Action Items:

`parse_file_bool()`) and the environment (`get_env_bool()`, now also used for `FTPS_ENABLED`, which bypassed it). It accepts
`true/1/yes/on/enabled` and `false/0/no/off/disabled` in any case (`enabled`/`disabled` added so the likeliest wording isn't refused).
Anything else is refused: a file value logs "Invalid value for KEY" and the setting keeps its default, an env value warns as before.
This changes one behaviour: an unrecognised value used to mean false and now leaves the default, which is true for
`METRICS_API_ALLOW_CONTROL` (and is warned about). Tests: `EveryBooleanKeyAcceptsAnyCaseOfTheSameWords` (all 12 boolean keys with

`ABooleanThatIsntOneLeavesTheDefault`, `FtpsEnabledFromTheEnvironmentAcceptsAnyCase`.

### TD-285: `ConfigLoader::reload()` Reports Success Without Applying Untracked Changes

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 31, 2026 | Config | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-283 and confirmed by running the real loader. `reload()` returns `true`
**without applying the new config** whenever `detect_changes()` finds nothing, but `detect_changes()`
compares only about 25 of roughly 110 fields (paths, port, session timeout, logging, architecture, six
generation fields). Changing only other keys (`METRICS_SERVER_URL`, `AUTO_SAVE_*`, RAG, GPU, MNS,
hippocampal…) logs "No configuration changes detected" and keeps the old values. Verified with
`METRICS_SERVER_URL` and `AUTO_SAVE_EVERY_MINUTES`. Conversely, if any tracked field changes, the
whole new config (untracked fields included) is applied, but only tracked changes are logged.

Action Items:

- [x] Always apply the validated new config (or compare every field, ideally via a generated field list) and log every change.
- [x] Separately report which changed keys the calling binary can't apply live (pairs with TD-251).
- [x] Test: an untracked-only change is applied and logged.

**Fix (October 31, 2026).** `reload()` always applies a config that passes validation. Every config loaded from a file now records the
file's `KEY=VALUE` pairs (`ServiceConfig::file_values`), and `detect_changes()` compares those, reporting every added, changed or removed
key (values of keys containing `SECRET`, `PASSWORD`, `TOKEN`, `HEADERS` or `CREDENTIAL` shown as `<hidden>`); configs not read from a
file still get the old field comparison. `reload()` takes an optional set of the keys the calling binary applies live and warns
"`KEY` changed but takes effect only after a restart" for every other changed key; `chatbot_api_server` passes its six (`LOG_LEVEL`,
`MAX_LENGTH`/`MAX_GEN_LENGTH`, `TEMPERATURE`, `TOP_P`, `STRATEGY`), replacing its port-only warning (TD-251's logging item). Tests:
`ReloadAppliesAndLogsAChangeToAnyKey` (`METRICS_SERVER_URL` and `AUTO_SAVE_EVERY_MINUTES`; the old loader kept both old values),
`ReloadReportsAddedRemovedAndHidesSecrets`, `ReloadNamesChangesTheBinaryAppliesOnlyAfterARestart`. Checked on the real
`chatbot_api_server`: changing `TEMPERATURE` and `SESSION_TIMEOUT` and sending `SIGHUP` logged both changes and the restart warning for
`SESSION_TIMEOUT` only.

Location in code: `src/Config.cpp` (`reload()`, `detect_changes()`); tagged `TD-285`.

### TD-284: `registry_server` Ignores the FTP/FTPS Security Keys Its Config File Ships With

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 31, 2026 | Config | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-283. `registry_server` reads only `FTP_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES` and
`FTP_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_RUN` from its config file (`RegistryServerArgs.cpp`). The FTP listener settings
are **CLI-only** (`--ftp-port`, `--ftp-pasv-min/max`, `--ftp-secret`, `--ftps`, `--ftp-cert`,
`--ftp-key`), per `RegistryServer.cpp`'s own "CLI-only listener settings" comment. Yet
`config.registry.conf` ships `FTP_SERVER_PORT`, `FTP_DATA_SERVER_SECRET=change-me-in-production` and
`FTPS_ENABLED`, and `ConfigLoader` parses them without a word. An operator who sets
`FTPS_ENABLED=true` or a real HMAC secret in the file silently gets **plaintext FTP and random token
passwords**. Nothing in `src/` reads `ServiceConfig::ftp_data_server_secret`, and the PASV-range
fields are also unread.

Action Items:

- [x] Make `registry_server` honour the file keys (CLI still overriding), or remove them from `ServiceConfig` and `config.registry.conf`.
- [x] Warn at startup when file and CLI disagree, and when FTPS is off on a non-loopback advertise IP.
- [x] Until fixed, the shipped config file carries a note (annotated with this TD).

**Fix (October 31, 2026).** `registry_server` honours the file keys, CLI flags overriding: `FTP_SERVER_PORT`,
`FTP_PASV_PORT_MIN`/`MAX`, `FTP_DATA_SERVER_SECRET`, `FTPS_ENABLED`, `FTP_CERT_FILE`/`FTP_KEY_FILE`, plus two new keys,
`FTP_SERVER_ENABLED` (for `--ftp-enabled`) and `FTP_ADVERTISE_IP` (for `--ftp-ip`), so a config-only deployment can run the listener at
all. `RegistryServerArgs`' FTP fields became `std::optional`, and `resolve_registry_server_config()` resolves them (file < CLI) into
`RegistryServerEffectiveConfig` together with `warnings`, logged at startup: a CLI flag overriding a different file value; the old
placeholder secret `change-me-in-production`, now ignored (a publicly known HMAC key would let anyone compute token passwords; the
`ServiceConfig` default is empty, meaning a random password per token); and FTP enabled without FTPS on a non-loopback advertise
address. `config.registry.conf` now documents every key, sets `FTP_SERVER_ENABLED=false` and leaves the secret commented out. Tests:
`FtpSettingsComeFromTheConfigFile`, `FtpCliFlagsOverrideTheFileAndSaySo`, `ThePlaceholderSecretIsIgnored`,
`PlaintextFtpOnANetworkAddressWarns`, updated parse and config defaults tests. Verified with the real binary: `FTP_SERVER_ENABLED=true`
and `FTPS_ENABLED=true` in the file alone started a TLS listener (`AUTH TLS` → `234`, certificate pin logged) and logged the
placeholder warning; the old binary with the same file started no FTP listener at all.

Location in code: `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}` (FTP keys), `src/RegistryServer.cpp`, `src/RegistryServerArgs.cpp`, `config.registry.conf`; tagged `TD-284`.

- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `src/RegistryServerArgs.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}`
- `config.registry.conf`
- `tests/registry_server_args_test.cpp`

### TD-283: `SIGHUP` Terminates Every Binary Except `chatbot_api_server`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 31, 2026 | Config | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [Config.md](../reference/source/Config.md). CLAUDE.md says "Client binaries
(`chatbot_api_server`, `incremental_trainer`) additionally hot-reload their file via `SIGHUP`." Only
`chatbot_api_server` registers a `SIGHUP` handler. `incremental_trainer`, `trainer_service`,
`metrics_api_server`, `mns_server` and `registry_server` register only `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`, so
`SIGHUP` takes the default action and **terminates the process**. An operator following the docs
(`kill -HUP <trainer pid>`) kills a training pass mid-epoch; sending it to `trainer_service` kills the
supervisor and its admin API. Found by inspecting every `std::signal()` registration.

Action Items:

- [x] Install a `SIGHUP` handler in every long-running binary: either a real reload (where `ConfigLoader::reload()` makes sense) or `SIG_IGN` with a log line saying reload isn't supported.
- [x] Correct CLAUDE.md's "Configuration" paragraph (annotated with this TD for now) and the operations docs.
- [x] Test: `SIGHUP` doesn't terminate each daemon.

**Fix (October 31, 2026).** New `src/SignalSetup.hpp` (`adai::ignore_sighup(name)`) sets `SIGHUP` to `SIG_IGN` and logs that the
binary doesn't reload its configuration and needs a restart. `incremental_trainer`, `trainer_service`, `metrics_api_server`, `mns_server`
and `registry_server` call it next to their `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` registration. `SIG_IGN` runs no handler code (nothing
async-signal-unsafe, cf. TD-249), and an ignored disposition survives `exec()`, so `trainer_service`'s child passes ignore it too.
A real reload wasn't added: none of these binaries applies config at runtime outside its admin API. Side effect: closing the terminal
or SSH session of a foreground `incremental_trainer train` no longer kills the pass. CLAUDE.md's "Configuration" paragraph and
OPERATIONS_MANUAL.md's hot-reload section now say only `chatbot_api_server` reloads. Tests: `SighupTests` starts the four daemons
for real (temporary configs, ports and data directories), sends `SIGHUP` once `/health` answers, and checks each is still running and
answering, then still stops on `SIGTERM`; on the old binaries all four died with signal 1. A forked-child test covers
`ignore_sighup()` itself, as `incremental_trainer` calls it before a pass.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`, `src/TrainerServiceMain.cpp`, `src/TrainingMetricsAPIServer.cpp`, `src/ModelNameServiceServer.cpp`, `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (signal registration); CLAUDE.md; tagged `TD-283`.

Files to Modify:

- the five binaries above
- `CLAUDE.md`
- `docs/operations/...` (any reload instructions)

### TD-241: `chatbot_api_server` Never Validates Its Configuration at Startup

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 31, 2026 | Inference / Serving / CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-240. `ConfigLoader::validate()` (`src/Config.cpp`, port 1–65535,
`session_timeout >= 1`, log level and size limits, `d_model` range and more) is only called from
`ConfigLoader::reload()`, the `SIGHUP` path. At startup `ConfigLoader::load()` doesn't call it, and
`validate_chatbot_api_server_config()` checks only that `vocab_path` is set. So values from the
CLI, env or file that `validate()` would reject are accepted at startup, and then the same file is
**rejected on the next `SIGHUP`** ("keeping current configuration"). Verified with the real
parser: `--timeout -5` is accepted, after which every session counts as expired at the next
`/health`.

`validate()` also checks none of the generation settings: `strategy` (an unknown value such as
`--strategy bogus` is accepted and silently becomes nucleus sampling in `ChatbotAPI`),
`temperature`, `top_p`, `max_gen_length`.

Action Items:

- [x] Call `ConfigLoader::validate()` from `validate_chatbot_api_server_config()` (after CLI flags are applied) and fail startup on errors.
- [x] Extend `validate()` with generation settings: `strategy` in {greedy, beam, temperature, top_k, nucleus}, `temperature >= 0`, `0 < top_p <= 1`, `max_gen_length >= 1`.
- [x] Tests: invalid port/timeout/strategy fail validation; the default config passes.

**Fix (October 31, 2026).** `validate_chatbot_api_server_config()` now runs `ConfigLoader::validate()` after the CLI flags are
applied and returns every error in one message ("Error: the configuration is invalid:" plus one line each), which `main()` prints
before exiting 1. So the server refuses at startup exactly what a `SIGHUP` reload would refuse. The generation checks were already in
`validate()` (strategy, temperature 0–2, top_p 0–1, `max_gen_length` 1–4096; `top_p = 0` stays valid, TD-516 made it top-1), and since
TD-288 it covers every other numeric field; since TD-289 an unknown `STRATEGY`/`LOG_LEVEL` in the file or environment is already
refused at load, so `validate()` catches the CLI forms (`--strategy bogus`, `--log-level LOUD`). `chatbot_api_server` was the last
long-running binary without a startup check. Tests: `OutOfRangeFlagsFailStartupValidation` (`--timeout -5`, `--port 0`/`70000`,
`--strategy bogus`, `--temperature -1`, `--top-p 1.5`, `--max-gen-len 0`, `--d-model 100`, `--log-level LOUD`), `ListsEveryError`,
and `ChatbotApiServerStartupTest.AnInvalidConfigExitsOneAtStartup` (the real binary with `SESSION_TIMEOUT=-5` exits 1 and names
the setting; the old binary started); all three fail on the old code. The startup test's model went from `D_MODEL=32` to 64, the
validator's minimum.

### TD-240: `chatbot_api_server` Silently Accepts Non-Numeric and Partial Numbers

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 31, 2026 | Inference / Serving / CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [ChatbotApiServerArgs.md](../reference/source/ChatbotApiServerArgs.md), and confirmed by running the real
parser. `apply_chatbot_api_server_args()` parses every numeric flag with `std::atoi`/`std::atof`,
which return 0 for non-numbers and stop at the first non-digit, and nothing reports either case:

| Input | Applied |
|---|---|
| `--port abc` | `port = 0`, which the OS treats as "any free port", so the server starts somewhere unannounced |
| `--port 8080x` | `port = 8080` |
| `--temperature hot` | `temperature = 0`, i.e. greedy decoding |
| `--timeout abc` / `--max-gen-len abc` / `--batch-timeout-ms abc` | 0 |

The same applies to every architecture flag and `--speculative-candidates`.

Action Items:

- [x] Parse with full-consumption checks (`std::from_chars` or `std::stoi`/`std::stof` plus a check that the whole string was consumed) and return `error = true` with a message naming the flag and value.
- [x] Tests: non-numeric and trailing-garbage values for each numeric flag are errors.

**Fix (October 31, 2026).** TD-287's strict parsers are now public in `Config.hpp` (`parse_strict_int()`, `parse_strict_size()`,
`parse_strict_float()`, returning `nullopt` on failure) so command-line flags share them with config files and environment variables;
TD-438, TD-456 and TD-488 can reuse them. Every numeric flag of `chatbot_api_server` goes through one: the value must be the whole
number, the seven architecture/length flags (`--d-model`, `--num-heads`, `--d-ff`, `--enc-layers`, `--dec-layers`, `--max-seq-len`,
`--max-gen-len`) refuse negatives, and `--temperature`/`--top-p` refuse `nan`/`inf`. A bad value stops parsing with
`Invalid value for --port: '8080x' (expected a whole number)`; the real binary prints it with the usage text and exits 1. Range
checks (port 1–65535 and so on) are TD-241's. Tests: `EveryNumericFlagRefusesANonNumberAndTrailingCharacters` (all 13 numeric flags
with `abc`, `8x`, an empty string and `1 2`), `SizeFlagsRefuseNegatives`, `FloatFlagsRefuseNonFiniteValues`,
`AnInvalidNumberStopsBeforeLaterFlagsApply`; all four fail on the old parser.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotApiServerArgs.cpp` (`apply_chatbot_api_server_args()`); tagged `TD-240`.

### TD-475: `PipelineInferenceEngine` Throughput Claims, Greedy Uncached Decoding and Stats

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 28, 2026 | `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp` (removed) | Retirement of `PipelineInferenceEngine` |

Summary:
Retired per the owner's decision (October 28, 2026), as `IntegratedInferenceEngine` was (TD-420): the engine was no faster than plain `/chat` (1.017× best case, measured) and answered differently from it. Deleted `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp` (with `ThreadSafeQueue`, used by nothing else), `tests/pipelineinferenceengine_test.cpp` and its target, `benchmarks/PipelineBenchmark.cpp` (`pipeline_benchmark`), and `ChatbotAPI::enable_pipeline_inference()` with its tests. `chatbot_api_server --pipeline-inference` now exits 1 with a message saying it was removed. Real batching is planned in real_batching_v2_plan.md. Filed October 16, 2026.

Original description:
Found while tracing `PipelineInferenceEngine`:
- **Throughput (verified).** The header promises "2–3× throughput", but only the encoder stage overlaps decoding. On a real model (d_model 256,
  4+4 layers, debug build) one encoder pass took 144 ms and 50 greedy decode steps 8,480 ms: a best-case pipelining speedup of **1.017×**. The
  decode loop re-runs the full decoder over all tokens so far each step (no KV cache, O(n²)), and a batch's inputs are decoded one at a time. The
  documented 1.24× (PARALLEL_OPTIMIZATIONS_QUICK_REFERENCE.md) comes from `benchmarks/PipelineBenchmark.cpp`, whose stages are `sleep()`s.
- **By inspection.** Generation is greedy only, with `BOS`/`EOS` added to encoder input (TD-364) and no repetition handling, so answers differ from
  normal `/chat` (as TD-417). `avg_throughput_rps` divides by time since construction (decays while idle); `PipelineConfig::enable_profiling` is
  never read. `ThreadSafeQueue` uses one condition variable with `notify_one()` for producers and the consumer, so a push can wake another blocked
  producer instead of the consumer (up to 50 ms extra latency). Stage errors go to `std::cerr`; only `std::exception`s are caught.

Action Items:

- [ ] Correct the header and PARALLEL_OPTIMIZATIONS_QUICK_REFERENCE.md claims; benchmark against the real model.
- [ ] Use the KV-cached decode path (or retire the engine in favour of the real-batching v2 plan, with TD-420).
- [ ] Pass the request's generation settings through; fix the throughput stat; separate not-full/not-empty condition variables; `Logger` instead of `std::cerr`.

Location in code: `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp` (header comment, `decoder_worker()`, `ThreadSafeQueue`, stats); tagged `TODO: See TD-475`.

- `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp`
- `benchmarks/PipelineBenchmark.cpp`

### TD-474: `PipelineInferenceEngine` Strands Queued Requests on Shutdown and Skips `model_mutex_`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 28, 2026 | `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp` (removed) | Retirement of `PipelineInferenceEngine` |

Summary:
Closed without a fix: the code was deleted when `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp` and `--pipeline-inference` were retired (owner decision, October 28, 2026; see TD-475). Filed October 16, 2026.

Original description:
Found while tracing `PipelineInferenceEngine`:
- **Stranded requests (verified).** `shutdown()` sets `running_ = false`, shuts down both `ThreadSafeQueue`s and joins the workers, which exit on
  the next loop check and leave any queued `PipelineRequest`/`EncoderOutput` (each owning its `std::promise`) inside the queues until the engine
  is destroyed. With 3 requests submitted and `shutdown()` called while the first was in the encoder stage: request 0 → `Broken promise`, requests
  1–2 **still pending 3 s later** (a probe without a timeout hung for 1.5 h). `push()` after shutdown silently drops the item (the caller's future
  fails with `Broken promise`). In `chatbot_api_server` the engine is destroyed after the HTTP server stops, so its workers drain the queue first;
  the defect bites any direct caller of `shutdown()`.
- **No `model_mutex_` (by inspection).** `ChatbotAPI::generate_response()` routes through the pipeline without `model_mutex_`, while
  `/chat/batch` runs `model_->forward()` under it, so a batch request can run concurrently with the decoder thread on layers that cache forward
  state in members. Same as TD-419.

Action Items:

- [ ] On shutdown, drain both queues and fail (or finish) every pending request explicitly; make `push()` after shutdown report failure to the caller.
- [ ] Hold `model_mutex_` around the decoder stage (or give the pipeline exclusive use of the model), consistently with TD-419's fix.
- [ ] Test: shutdown with queued requests resolves every future promptly.

Location in code: `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp` (`shutdown()`, workers, `ThreadSafeQueue::push()`); `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (pipeline branch of `generate_response()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-474`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp`
- `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp`
- `tests/pipelineinferenceengine_test.cpp`

different answers than the normal `/chat` path, for reasons unrelated to performance.

### TD-418: `IntegratedInferenceEngine` Worker Exceptions Terminate the Server; Shutdown Drops Requests

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|

Summary:
Closed without a fix: the code was deleted when `src/IntegratedInferenceEngine.hpp` and `--integrated-inference` were retired (owner decision, October 27, 2026). Filed October 13, 2026.

Original description:
Found while tracing `IntegratedInferenceEngine`; the shutdown part verified. The encoder thread calls
`encode_with_mask()` and the decoder thread calls `forward_with_encoder()`/`lm_head_->forward()` with no
`try`. Any exception (for example a token id outside the model's vocab when the tokenizer and model
disagree) escapes the `std::thread` and calls `std::terminate()`, taking `chatbot_api_server` down, and
the rest of the batch's promises are never fulfilled. `shutdown()` stops the queues and joins the
threads without failing queued or in-flight requests: destroying an engine with three queued requests
left all three futures throwing `std::future_error` (broken promise). Same class as TD-212 for
`BatchedInferenceEngine`.

Action Items:

- [ ] Catch per request in the encoder and decoder stages and deliver the exception to that request's promise; on shutdown, drain the queues and fail pending promises with a clear "shutting down" error.

Found while tracing `IntegratedInferenceEngine`, by inspection. The engine holds raw pointers to the
model's encoder, decoder and LM head and runs them from its own encoder and decoder threads without
`EncoderDecoderModel::model_mutex_`. `/chat/batch` bypasses the engine dispatcher (TD-234) and calls

class of bug that `model_mutex_` exists to prevent).

### TD-487: `RAGInference` Misconfiguration and Observability Gaps

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 27, 2026 | RAG / RAGInference | Code fix (LOW, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `RAGInference.cpp` (by inspection):
- **`RAG_NUM_DOCS ≤ 0`** isn't validated; once any document is indexed, `DocumentStore::retrieve()` throws `"k must be positive"` on every request, so every
  chat request fails (an empty store returns before the check).
- **`RAG_THRESHOLD`** can remove every retrieved document silently: the prompt loses its `Context:` section and nothing is logged.
- **No retrieval logging:** nothing records which documents were used or their scores; the server calls `generate()`, discarding
  `generateWithRetrieval()`'s list.
- **`getConfig()`/`setConfig()`** are unsynchronized (no production caller of `setConfig()` today).

Action Items:

- [x] Validate `RAG_NUM_DOCS > 0` and `RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH > 0` at startup (with TD-241/TD-288).
- [x] Log retrieved document IDs and scores at debug level, and warn when the threshold empties the context.

**Fix (October 27, 2026).** `RAGInference::validateConfig()` runs in the constructor and `setConfig()` and throws
`std::invalid_argument` for `num_retrieved_docs` or `max_context_length` below 1 (a rejected `setConfig()` keeps the old config).
`chatbot_api_server` builds the engine inside its RAG setup's `try`, so a bad `RAG_NUM_DOCS`/`RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH` is logged at
startup and the server runs without RAG, instead of failing every request. `ConfigLoader::validate()` checks both when RAG is
enabled (it still runs only on reload, TD-241). `buildPrompt()` logs each retrieved document's id and similarity at debug level, and
warns when `RAG_THRESHOLD` removes every retrieved document. `getConfig()`/`setConfig()` remain unsynchronized; nothing calls
`setConfig()` while serving. Tests: `ConfigWithNoDocumentsOrNoContextIsRejected`, `RetrievalIsLoggedAndAnEmptyingThresholdWarns`
(both fail on the old code).

Location in code: `src/RAGInference.cpp` (`generateWithRetrieval()` steps 1–2), `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp` (`rag_config` setup); tagged `TD-487`.

### TD-486: RAG Path Bypasses Strategy, Reloaded Settings and GPU Generation

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 27, 2026 | RAG / RAGInference | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `RAGInference.cpp` (by inspection). When RAG is enabled, `ChatbotAPI::generate_response()` returns
`rag_engine_->generate(input)` before any other path, and:
- **Strategy:** `generateWithRetrieval()` always passes `strategy = ""` (the default combined sampling branch), so `STRATEGY=nucleus` (shipped) and
  `BEAM_WIDTH` have no effect. `gen_config.num_beams` stays 1, so TD-261 isn't reached from the server, but any caller setting it above 1 gets beam search.
- **Settings copied once:** `ChatbotAPIServer.cpp` copies `MAX_GEN_LENGTH`/`TEMPERATURE`/`TOP_P`/`TOP_K` into `RAGConfig::gen_config` at startup. A `SIGHUP`
  reload updates `ChatbotAPI`'s `default_config_`, which RAG bypasses, and per-request values never reach it either (TD-254).
- **CPU only:** `EncoderDecoderModel::generate_response_with_strategy()` is the CPU path, so on a GPU server enabling RAG moves every request off TD-033's GPU
  decode path.

Action Items:

- [x] Give `RAGInference` a way to build the augmented prompt only, and let `ChatbotAPI` generate from it through its normal path (strategy, config, GPU).
- [x] (Not needed: the first item covers it.) Or pass the request's `GenerationConfig` (strategy included) into `generate()`.
- [x] Test that RAG honours `strategy` and reloaded settings.

**Fix (October 27, 2026).** `RAGInference::buildPrompt(query, history)` does retrieval and the budgeted prompt only (steps 1–4).
`ChatbotAPI::generate_response()` asks the RAG engine for the prompt and then generates from it like any other request, so the
request's strategy and `GenerationConfig`, `SIGHUP`-reloaded settings, speculative decoding, the TD-038 engines and the GPU decode
all apply. `RAGInference::generate()`/`generateWithRetrieval()` remain for standalone use with `RAGConfig::gen_config` on the CPU;
`buildPrompt()` is the virtual test seam now (`generate()` no longer is), so `RAGInference.hpp` is version 2.0.0. Tests:
`RagHonoursTheRequestStrategyAndConfig` (greedy through RAG equals greedy from the same prompt without RAG, three times, and a
changed `max_length` reaches RAG requests) and, in GPU builds, `RagRequestsTakeTheGpuDecode` (run on the oneAPI CPU device with
`ADAI_SYCL_ALLOW_CPU_DEVICE=1`). The old RAG path couldn't be run against these tests (the seam they override is new); by
inspection it called `generate_response_with_strategy()` on the CPU with an empty strategy and startup settings.

Location in code: `src/RAGInference.cpp` (`generateWithRetrieval()` step 5), `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (`generate_response()`'s RAG branch), `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp` (`rag_config` setup); tagged `TD-486`.

### TD-485: RAG Session Retrieval Uses the Start of the Conversation

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 27, 2026 | RAG / RAGInference | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `RAGInference.cpp` (by inspection). For `/chat/session`, `ChatbotAPI` passes the whole formatted conversation
(`ConversationContext::format_for_model()`, `"User: …\nAssistant: …"`) to `generate_response()`, and the RAG branch hands that string to `RAGInference::generate()`
as the query. `DocumentStore::retrieve()` embeds it with `LLMEncoder::encode()`, which keeps only the **first** `max_seq_length` tokens, so once a
conversation is longer than that, retrieval is chosen by the system message and the oldest turns, and the latest question doesn't take part. The same
string then becomes the "Question:" after the context, compounding TD-484.

**Correction (October 27, 2026):** this was written before TD-365, which made the encoder keep the **last** `max_seq_length` tokens.
Since then the whole-conversation query does include the latest question, but mostly earlier turns, so retrieval still didn't follow
the question; the fix below doesn't depend on which end is kept.

Action Items:

- [x] Pass the latest user message to RAG as the retrieval query, separately from the conversation history.
- [x] Build the prompt as context + (budgeted) history + latest question.
- [x] Test retrieval in a multi-turn session longer than `max_seq_length`.

**Fix (October 27, 2026).** `handle_chat_session()` and the batch-session path capture the conversation before the new user
message (`format_for_model()`) and pass `ChatbotAPI::RagTurn{message, history}` to `generate_response()`; its RAG branch calls
`RAGInference::generate(question, history)`. Non-RAG paths still get the whole formatted conversation. Retrieval uses the question
alone. `buildBudgetedPrompt(query, context, history)` builds context + history + question within `max_seq_length`: the question
whole, the context within `max_context_length`, then as much of the history's end as fits (cut from the front at a UTF-8 boundary),
so the oldest turns go first. Tests: `RetrievalUsesTheLatestQuestionInALongSession` (a 60-turn session about one document whose
latest question is the other document's text; the fix retrieves that document with similarity 1, while the whole-conversation
query used before scores it strictly lower; which document an untrained encoder then ranks first varies, so that isn't asserted),
`HistoryKeepsItsLatestTurnsWithinTheBudget`, and `SessionTurnsGiveRagTheLatestMessageAndTheHistory` (the second turn's query is the
message alone, the history holds the first turn). These tests exposed TD-222 (the tokenizer cache leaked between tokenizers at a reused address, so token counts depended on
test order), fixed alongside; both new RAG tests also failed in the full binary on the old tokenizer.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (`handle_chat_session()` → `generate_response()`'s RAG branch), `src/RAGInference.cpp` (`generateWithRetrieval()`); tagged `TD-485`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp`
- `src/RAGInference.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/raginference_test.cpp`

### TD-484: RAG Prompt Budget Lets the Question Fall Past `max_seq_length`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 27, 2026 | RAG / RAGInference | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `RAGInference.cpp` (see [RAGInference.md](../reference/source/RAGInference.md)). `truncateContext()` converts
`max_context_length` to characters at 4 per token, and only the retrieved context is budgeted: `context_prefix`, `query_prefix` and the query are added
afterwards. The shipped values are `RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH=512` and `MAX_SEQ_LENGTH=512`, so even with an exact estimate the context alone fills every
position and the question lands after position 512, where the encoder adds no positional encoding (the input isn't truncated, TD-365).
- **Verified:** with a vocabulary built by this repo's `BPETokenizer` from the project's guides, a 2,048-character context of three of those documents was
  **1,150 tokens** (1.8 characters per token) and the full prompt **1,178 tokens**, 2.3× `max_seq_length`. (That vocabulary had 402 entries; a production
  one compresses better, but not to 4 characters per token for this kind of text.)
- **By inspection:** the character cut can split a UTF-8 sequence before the `...`.

Action Items:

- [x] Budget the whole prompt in real tokens (the model's tokenizer): `max_seq_length` minus the query and prefixes, the rest for context.
- [x] Truncate documents at token (or at least UTF-8 character) boundaries; prefer dropping whole lower-ranked documents first.
- [x] Clamp `RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH` to the model's `max_seq_length` and document the relationship in `config.chatbot.conf`.
- [x] Test: the augmented prompt never exceeds `max_seq_length` tokens.

**Fix (October 27, 2026).** `RAGInference::buildBudgetedPrompt()` replaces `truncateContext()`. It counts real tokens with the
model's tokenizer and keeps the question (with its prefix) whole. The context, documents in rank order, is cut from the end at a
UTF-8 boundary (`"..."` appended) by a binary search for the longest prefix with which the context fits `max_context_length` and the
whole prompt fits the model's `max_seq_length`. Cutting from the end drops lower-ranked documents first and trims the top-ranked one
only when it alone is too long. When no context fits, or the question alone reaches `max_seq_length`, the prompt is the question alone
(the encoder keeps its last tokens, TD-365). `chatbot_api_server` caps `RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH` to the model's `max_seq_length` with
a warning, and `config.chatbot.conf`/`OPERATIONS_MANUAL.md` describe the relationship. Tests (`RAGInferencePromptBudgetTest`, which
replaces the `truncateContext()` tests): a three-document context where the old rule overflowed `max_seq_length` now fits with the

### TD-350: `DocumentStore::retrieve()` Isn't Safe to Call Concurrently

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 27, 2026 | RAG / DocumentStore | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-349, by inspection. `retrieve()` is `const` but calls `encoder->encode()`, which
mutates the encoder's caches (`requires_grad` defaults to true) and prints `Encoding N tokens...` to
stdout on every query; `DocumentStore` has no lock. Today RAG generation runs under
`ChatbotAPI::config_mutex_` (TD-230), so requests are serialized and there's no race. Fixing TD-230
by releasing that lock, as its own action item suggests, would expose concurrent `retrieve()` calls
to data races inside the encoder.

Action Items:

- [x] Before (or with) TD-230: give `DocumentStore` a mutex around encode+score, or put the RAG encoder in inference mode (`set_requires_grad(false)`) and make `encode()` side-effect free; drop the stdout print.
- [x] Test: concurrent `retrieve()` under TSan.

**Fix (October 27, 2026).** `DocumentStore` has a mutex held by every method, so a query is encoded and scored under it and
documents can be added while others retrieve. `LLMEncoder::encode()` logs its token count at debug level instead of printing to
stdout on every call (the constructor and save/load prints stay with TD-367). Tests: `ConcurrentRetrieveMatchesSerialResults` (four
threads get the same hits and scores as serial queries) and `AddDocumentWhileRetrieving`. Under TSan (`OMP_NUM_THREADS=1`) the old
code reported 74 data races and 4 heap-use-after-frees in these two tests; the fixed code reports none. Pointers `retrieve()` returns
are still valid only until the next add/remove/clear, as documented.

Location in code: `src/DocumentStore.cpp` (`retrieve()`); tagged `TD-350`.

code reported 2 data races on `running_`, the fixed code none. Stopping before `listen()` has bound is still lost (TD-248).

### TD-232: ChatbotAPI Accepts Unlimited Client-Chosen Session IDs

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 27, 2026 | Inference / Serving / API | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [ChatbotAPI.md](../reference/source/ChatbotAPI.md). `get_or_create_session()` creates a session under any unknown non-empty `session_id` a client
sends, with no limit on ID length, format, or the number of sessions. One request per new ID adds a
session (with its `ConversationContext`), so any client can grow server memory without bound; with
TD-231, nothing reclaims it unless `/health` is polled. The ChatbotCLI relies on choosing its own
IDs, so the fix must keep that working. Found by reading the code.

Action Items:

- [x] Cap total sessions (evict least-recently-used) and validate client IDs (length and character set).
- [x] Decide whether client-chosen IDs stay allowed or move to server-issued IDs only (needs a ChatbotCLI change).
- [x] Tests: cap enforcement and ID validation.

**Decision (owner, October 27, 2026):** session ids become server-issued only; at the cap the least recently used session is
evicted.

**Fix (October 27, 2026).** `get_or_create_session()` creates a session only for an empty `session_id` and returns a fresh
server-generated id; an id it doesn't hold throws `SessionNotFound`, which every route answers with HTTP 404
`{"success":false,"error":"Session not found"}` (`/chat/session`, `/clear-session`, `/chat/session/export`, `/chat/session/import`,
`/chat/batch-session`, where every named id is checked before any session is created). So no ID validation is needed: a
client-supplied id is only ever looked up. `set_max_sessions()` caps live sessions (config key `MAX_SESSIONS`, default 10,000, at
least 1; `chatbot_api_server` applies it at startup): creating one more evicts the least recently used. Clients: `ChatbotCLI`
already adopted the returned id; on a 404 it now drops its id and sends the message again in a new session (`/load` imports into a
new session, `/clear` reports no session). The Android app creates conversations with `serverSessionId = ""`, stores the id the
first reply carries (`ConversationDao.updateServerSessionId()`), starts a new session once on a 404 (conversations created before
this hold a client UUID and take that path once), and skips `/clear-session` for a conversation with no session. No Room schema
change. Tests: `UnknownSessionIdIsNotFoundAndCreatesNothing`, `IssuedSessionIdContinuesTheConversation`,
`SessionCapEvictsTheLeastRecentlyUsed`, `GenerateBatchSessionResponses_UnknownIdIsNotFound`, the real-binary
`ChatRoutesParseJsonAndRejectMalformedBodies` (404 on all four session routes; 200 on the old server, which created a session under
the invented id), the CLI's `LostSessionStartsANewOneAndTheTurnSucceeds` (`Error: 404` with the old CLI), and three Android
`ChatRepositoryTest` cases.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (`get_or_create_session()`); tagged `TD-232`.

### TD-230: RAG Mode Serializes Every ChatbotAPI Request Behind `config_mutex_`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [ChatbotAPI.md](../reference/source/ChatbotAPI.md). In `generate_response()`, the RAG path is

`config_mutex_` is held for the **whole RAG generation**. Every handler takes that same mutex to copy
`default_config_`, and `set_generation_config()` (including on `SIGHUP` reload) needs it too. So with

generation is running. Found by reading the code.

concurrent calls, which race inside the RAG encoder; see [TD-350](#td-350-documentstoreretrieve-isnt-safe-to-call-concurrently), which must land first or together.

**Fix (October 27, 2026).** `generate_response()` copies the `rag_engine_` `shared_ptr` under `config_mutex_` and generates after
releasing it. The model guards itself (`model_mutex_`) and the store now does too (TD-350). `RAGInference::generate()` is virtual so a
test can stand in an engine that blocks: `SlowRagGenerationDoesNotBlockConfigChanges` holds a RAG generation open and calls
`set_generation_config()`, which waited the full 5 s timeout on the old code and returns at once now.

### TD-222: `apply_bpe()`'s Thread-Local Cache Is Never Invalidated

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 27, 2026 | NLP / Tokenizer | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-220 and confirmed by running the real code. `apply_bpe()` memoizes results in a
`thread_local` map keyed by `(tokenizer address, word)`. The cache was added for preprocessing
speed, and its comment assumes merges never change while it's in use. But it's never invalidated:

- **After `load_vocab()`** on an instance that has already encoded text, words encode with the
  **old** merges. Verified: after reloading to a tiny vocab, `"abab"` still encoded to the old
  single token instead of the correct four.
- **Address reuse:** a tokenizer constructed at the same address as a destroyed one, on the same
  thread, inherits its cached results. Verified with placement-new.
- **Never freed:** entries for destroyed tokenizers stay for the thread's lifetime.
  `measure_fertility()` creates a temporary tokenizer on every call, adding another entry each
  time.

Production mostly dodges this (each `trainer_service` pass is a fresh process; servers load once),
but `--pipeline-inference`'s reload of the encoder's tokenizer and any in-process
reload-and-retrain path are exposed. The cache comment also refers to a nonexistent
`train_bpe()` (the real mutators are `build_vocab()`/`build_bpe_merges()`/`load_vocab()`).

**Seen again October 26, 2026:** `EncoderDecoderModelTest.OneUpdateIsOneStepWithOrWithoutAnOptimizer` (TD-297) failed only after another test in the same process. A 100-token tokenizer's cached IDs encoded `"hello world"` to IDs at or above 60 for a 60-token model, so two otherwise identical models read past their embedding tables differently. The test now uses token IDs; the cache itself is still unfixed.

Action Items:

- [x] Give each tokenizer a unique, never-reused instance ID plus a generation counter bumped by
  every mutator, and key the cache on `(instance_id, generation)`, dropping stale entries on
  mismatch. Alternatively, move the cache into the instance behind a lock-free or sharded
  structure.
- [x] Bound the cache size, and free a destroyed tokenizer's entries.
- [x] Fix the comment (`train_bpe()` → the real mutators).
- [x] Tests: reload-then-encode matches a fresh tokenizer; same-address reconstruction doesn't
  inherit results.

**Fix (October 27, 2026).** Found blocking TD-485's tests: they passed alone and failed after other tests in the same binary. The
cache is keyed by `cache_key_`, a process-unique number that is never reused, set at construction and renewed by every change to the
merges or the mode (`build_bpe_merges()`, so `build_vocab()`, and `load_vocab()`). A reload or a tokenizer at a reused address
therefore starts with an empty cache. Each thread keeps the caches of its 4 most recently used keys (RAG alternates between the
model's and the encoder's tokenizers) and clears a cache at 65,536 words, so a destroyed tokenizer's or `measure_fertility()`'s
probe's entries are dropped as others are used. The comment names the real mutators. Tests: `BPETokenizerCacheTest`
(`ReloadThenEncodeMatchesAFreshTokenizer` and `ATokenizerAtAReusedAddressInheritsNothing`, placement-new at the same address, both
fail on the old code; `AlternatingTokenizersKeepTheirOwnResults`).

Location in code: `src/BPETokenizer.cpp` (`apply_bpe()`, `load_vocab()`, `measure_fertility()`);
tagged `TD-222`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/BPETokenizer.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/tokenizer_test.cpp`

### TD-516: `TextGenerator` Ignored `min_length`/`early_stopping`, Silent NaN Output and Config Semantics

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | NLP / TextGenerator | Code fix (LOW, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `TextGenerator.{hpp,cpp}`:
- **Verified:** `min_length` is never read (with `min_length = 4` and an EOS-preferring model, greedy and `generate()` stopped after one token: an empty
  response); all-NaN logits pick token 0 (PAD, a stop token), so a broken model (e.g. TD-423) silently returns an empty response
  (`std::discrete_distribution` over NaN is also undefined); `max_length` counts the starting BOS and prompt (`max_length = 6` → 5 new tokens).
- **By inspection:** `early_stopping` has no effect (both branches break only when no beams remain) and beam search never stops once the best finished
  beam is unbeatable; the repetition penalty runs after top-k/top-p, so penalized tokens stay in the nucleus; `top_p <= 0` disables filtering; beam search
  calls the model once per beam per step; seed 0 means random.

Action Items:

- [x] Implement `min_length` (mask EOS/PAD until reached) and real early stopping, or remove both fields. (Owner chose to implement both, October 26, 2026.)
- [x] Detect non-finite logits and report an error; define `max_length` as new tokens; apply the penalty before filtering; treat `top_p <= 0` as top-1. (Owner chose new tokens.)

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** Every strategy now takes its next-token logits from one helper, `next_logits()`.
- **Non-finite logits.** A NaN or +inf logit, or a row with no finite value, throws `std::runtime_error`. A broken model no longer
  silently returns an empty response.
- **`min_length`.** EOS and PAD are masked to −inf until `min_length` new tokens exist. This applies in greedy, sampling, top-k,
  nucleus, `generate()` and beam search.
- **`max_length` counts new tokens.** The BOS and prompt are no longer counted, so `max_length = 6` gives up to 6 new tokens, not 5.
  `ChatbotAPI`'s and `MAX_GEN_LENGTH`'s "maximum response tokens" now mean what they say. `EncoderDecoderModel`'s TD-347 cap
  (`capped_generation_length()`) becomes `max_seq_length − 1` new tokens, so the sequence with BOS still fits in `max_seq_length`.
- **Early stopping.** With `early_stopping` (the default), beam search stops once no running beam can still win. A running beam's
  raw score can only fall, since log-probabilities are clamped at 0. Its best possible final score is therefore its current score
  divided by the largest length penalty it can still get (the current or the final length, whichever penalty is larger). When the
  best finished beam is at least that for every running beam, the search ends. The result is identical to the full search.
- **Filter order.** The repetition penalty runs before temperature and the top-k/top-p filters, in every strategy. Temperature
  commutes with the penalty, since the penalty keeps each logit's sign.
- **`top_p <= 0`** keeps only the top token (top-1).

Not changed (by inspection, LOW):
- beam search still calls the model once per beam per step;
- seed 0 still means a random seed.

Tests (`TextGeneratorTD516Test`, all failing on the old code):
- `MinLengthKeepsStopTokensOutUntilReached`: five strategies, with an EOS-preferring model;
- `NonFiniteLogitsThrow`: NaN, +inf and all −inf;
- `MaxLengthCountsNewTokensAfterThePrompt`: six strategies;
- `EarlyStoppingKeepsTheResultAndSavesModelCalls`: 160 hashed-logit beam searches, with and without the length penalty and with
  α of 0.6 and −0.5, give identical output and fewer model calls;
- `RepetitionPenaltyRunsBeforeTopK`;
- `TopPZeroOrBelowIsTopOne`.

`MaxLengthEnforced` and `VeryShortMaxLength` were updated to the new-token count. `TextGenerator` is now `@adai-version 2.0.0`, since
the change in `max_length` breaks compatibility.

Location in code: `src/TextGenerator.cpp` (`next_logits()`, `start_tokens()`, every generation loop, `generate_beam_search()`,
`apply_top_p()`), `src/TextGenerator.hpp` (`GenerationConfig`), `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp` (`capped_generation_length()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/TextGenerator.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/textgenerator_test.cpp`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | NLP / TextGenerator | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `TextGenerator.cpp`; verified. `apply_temperature()` returns the logits unchanged for `temperature <= 0`, which is only correct where
the caller then takes the argmax (`generate()`, `generate_sampling()`). `generate_top_k()` and `generate_nucleus()` sample instead, at an effective
temperature of 1: with temperature 0, 50 runs gave 33 distinct nucleus outputs and 17 distinct top-k outputs (`generate()`: 1). `STRATEGY=nucleus` is the
shipped default, so `TEMPERATURE=0` (allowed by `validate()`) doesn't make chat deterministic. Negative temperatures behave the same.

Action Items:

- [x] Take the argmax at `temperature <= 0` in every sampling strategy (or reject negative temperatures).
- [x] Test determinism at temperature 0 for each strategy.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** A temperature of 0 or below is greedy in every strategy:
- `generate_top_k()` and `generate_nucleus()` take the argmax of the filtered, penalized logits;
- `generate_sampling()` and `generate()` treat a negative temperature like 0 (they used to test `== 0` and sample a negative temperature at 1).

`TEMPERATURE=0` now makes chat deterministic with the default nucleus strategy.

Tests:
- `TemperatureZeroOrBelowIsGreedyForEveryStrategy`: top-k, nucleus, sampling and `generate()` match greedy for 20 seeds, at T = 0 and
  T = −0.5. On the old code it fails 114 checks.
- `PositiveTemperatureStillSamples`: nucleus output still varies at T = 1.

Location in code: `src/TextGenerator.cpp` (`apply_temperature()`, `generate_sampling()`, `generate_top_k()`, `generate_nucleus()`, `generate()`).

### TD-514: `TextGenerator` Beam Width of Zero or Less Crashes the Process

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | NLP / TextGenerator | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `TextGenerator.cpp` (see [TextGenerator.md](../reference/source/TextGenerator.md)); verified under AddressSanitizer.
`generate_beam_search()` builds `std::vector<BeamHypothesis> beams(num_beams)` and writes `beams[0]` without checking: width 0 is a SEGV
(`vector::capacity()`), a negative width an uncaught `std::length_error` (`terminate`). `ChatbotAPI` passes `BEAM_WIDTH` straight in for `STRATEGY=beam`
(and in `/chat/batch`), and `ConfigLoader::validate()`, which rejects widths outside 1–16, runs only on `SIGHUP` reload (TD-241), so `BEAM_WIDTH=0` with the
beam strategy crashes `chatbot_api_server` on its first chat request.

- [x] Test widths 0 and −1. (−1 means "the configured width", so the test uses 0, −2 and a configured 0.)

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** `generate_beam_search()` throws `std::invalid_argument` ("beam width must be at least 1") when the width is
below 1, whether passed directly or read from `config.num_beams`. `BEAM_WIDTH=0` with `STRATEGY=beam` now fails each request with an
error instead of crashing `chatbot_api_server`. `ConfigLoader::validate()` at startup is still TD-241. Very large widths aren't capped
here; `validate()` limits them to 16.

Test: `TextGeneratorBeamSearchTest.BeamWidthBelowOneThrows`. On the old code it kills the test process at width 0.

### TD-508: Speculative Decoding Speedup Statistic and Hygiene

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Inference / SpeculativeDecoding | Code fix (LOW, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `SpeculativeDecoding.hpp`: `get_speedup()`/`calculate_theoretical_speedup()` return `K·α/(K+1)`, which is below 1 for every
acceptance rate (verified: 0.6 at 80% acceptance, 0.8 at 100%) and isn't a speedup (expected tokens per target pass is `(1 − α^(K+1))/(1 − α)`, before
costs); the tests assert this formula and the replaced doc promised "2–3×". By inspection: `acceptance_threshold` is never read; `print_stats()`/
`print_speedup_table()` use `std::cout`; `generate()` uses `goto`; the RNG is unseeded (TD-368's class).

Action Items:

- [x] Report tokens per target pass (and measured time if available) instead; update the tests.
- [x] Remove or implement `acceptance_threshold`; route output through `Logger`; seedable RNG.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-507).**

  (`get_target_passes()`, `get_draft_passes()`, `get_generated_tokens()`). `calculate_theoretical_speedup()` is replaced by
  `expected_tokens_per_target_pass(K, α)` = (1 − α^(K+1))/(1 − α), which is K + 1 at α = 1. Timing isn't measured, since it depends
  on the draft-to-target cost ratio.
- **Removed:** `acceptance_threshold`, `print_speedup_table()` and the `goto`.
- **Output.** `print_stats()` is now `log_stats()`, through `Logger`.
- **RNG.** The constructor takes a seed (default `std::random_device`).
- **Tests.** The speedup tests became `ExpectedTokensPerTargetPassTest`, and `SpeculativeDecodingTD508Test.SameSeedSameOutput` is new.
