### TD-507: Speculative Decoding Isn't Target-Distributed, Greedy or Faster

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Inference / SpeculativeDecoding | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `SpeculativeDecoding.hpp`; verified with toy fixed-distribution `TextGenerator`s:
- **Wrong residual:** on rejection it samples from `max(0, p_target − p_draft)` with `p_draft` non-zero only for the rejected token. With target
  (0.5, 0.3, 0.2) and draft (0.2, 0.3, 0.5), 40,000 first tokens were (0.40, 0.40, 0.20), not the target distribution the header promises.
- **Greedy isn't greedy:** acceptance stays random (`p_t/p_d`), so 41% of "greedy" first tokens were the draft's argmax rather than the target's.
- **Never faster:** each candidate gets its own target `get_next_token_probs()` call (no parallel verification, no bonus token): 41 tokens took 41 target
  passes plus draft passes; `generate_tokens(…, 40)` returned 41 tokens. `chatbot_api_server` builds the draft with the target's own architecture, so
  even a correct algorithm couldn't save time.
- **By inspection:** candidates are sampled from the temperature-scaled draft distribution but accepted with unscaled draft/target probabilities.

Action Items:

- [x] Verify all K candidates in one target forward (logits for every position), use the full draft distribution in the residual `max(0, p − q)`, sample a bonus token when all K are accepted, and cap output at `max_new_tokens`.
- [x] Greedy mode: accept iff the candidate equals the target argmax.
- [x] Apply temperature consistently to both distributions; allow a smaller draft architecture (`DRAFT_*` config) in `chatbot_api_server`. (The draft's architecture comes from its own checkpoint instead of `DRAFT_*` keys.)
- [x] Test the output distribution and greedy equivalence.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** `SpeculativeDecoder` (`SpeculativeDecoding.hpp` 2.0.0) is rewritten as standard speculative sampling.
Each round works as follows:
1. The draft samples up to K tokens from q = softmax(draft logits / T).
2. One target pass over the context plus the proposals gives K + 1 rows (`TextGenerator::get_logits()`).
3. Each proposal is accepted with probability min(1, p/q), where p = softmax(target logits / T), the same temperature for both models.
4. The first rejection is replaced by a sample from norm(max(0, p − q)), using the whole draft distribution.
5. When all K are accepted, a bonus token is sampled from the target's next row.

Greedy mode (`use_greedy`, or T ≤ 0 as in TD-515) accepts a proposal only when it is the target's argmax, so the output equals the
target's greedy output. A round never drafts more than the remaining budget, and the output is cut at `max_new_tokens`. A target that
returns only its last row still works: the decoder calls it once per prefix it needs and remembers the mode.

Model side:
- `EncoderDecoderModel::next_token_logits(…, last_rows)` returns the last K + 1 rows, and `ChatbotAPI`'s target callback asks for
  them.
- `chatbot_api_server` builds the draft from `EncoderDecoderModel::read_checkpoint_architecture(DRAFT_MODEL_PATH)`. The draft can now
  be smaller than the target, but its vocabulary must match the tokenizer's. `num_candidates < 1` throws.

Measured on the old code with the same mocks:
- first-token distribution (0.391, 0.411, 0.197) instead of (0.5, 0.3, 0.2);
- (0.396, 0.341, 0.264) at T = 0.5 instead of (0.658, 0.237, 0.105);
- greedy output equal to the target's greedy output in 0 of 10 runs;
- 20 target calls for 20 tokens.

New tests (`SpeculativeDecodingTD507Test`):
- `FirstTokenFollowsTheTargetDistribution` and `TemperatureAppliesToBothModels` (20,000 draws each, within 0.015);
- `GreedyOutputEqualsTheTargetsGreedyOutput` (10 draft/target pairs);
- `OneTargetPassPerRoundAndABonusToken`: 4 target passes for 20 tokens at K = 4;
- `OutputNeverExceedsMaxNewTokens`;
- `LastRowOnlyTargetGivesTheSameGreedyOutput`.

Supporting tests:
- `ChatbotAPIEchoTest.NextTokenLogitsLastRowsMatchTheAlignedForward`;
- `EncoderDecoderModelTest.ReadCheckpointArchitectureMatchesTheSavedModel`;
- `ChatbotAPIEchoTest.SpeculativeDecodingEchoesExactly`, which now uses the one-pass target.

Location in code: `src/SpeculativeDecoding.hpp`, `src/TextGenerator.{hpp,cpp}` (`get_logits()`), `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}`
(`next_token_logits()` `last_rows`, `read_checkpoint_architecture()`), `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp`, `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/SpeculativeDecoding.hpp`
- `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`
- `tests/speculativedecoding_test.cpp`

### TD-506: CPU Chat Generation Is Off by One Because `model_fn` Uses the Training Forward

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Inference / Serving / API | Code fix (HIGH, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `SpeculativeDecoding.hpp` (see [SpeculativeDecoding.md](../reference/source/SpeculativeDecoding.md)); verified.
`EncoderDecoderModel::forward(input, targets)` is the training forward: it feeds `[BOS] + targets[:-1]` to the decoder, so its last logits row predicts
`targets.back()`, the last token already in the context. `TextGenerator` (and `SpeculativeDecoder`) read the last row as the next-token prediction.
`ChatbotAPI` builds every CPU generation `model_fn` as `model_->forward(input_tokens, decoder_tokens)`: the plain path (the default on a server without a
GPU), speculative decoding, `--batched-inference` and `/chat/batch`.

Reproduced with a tiny `EncoderDecoderModel` trained on the CPU (`forward()`, loss ≈ 0) to echo 12 five-token sequences: greedy generation through
`ChatbotAPI`'s `model_fn` got **0/12** exactly right (`2 2 15 24 31 30 26 3` for `15 31 24 30 4`); with an aligned `model_fn` (decoder input =
the generated tokens) **12/12**; speculative decoding likewise 0/12 vs 12/12. So a correctly trained model answers wrongly on a CPU
`chatbot_api_server`. The GPU path, `generate_response()`'s cached path, and the RAG, pipeline and integrated engines are aligned and unaffected.

Action Items:

- [x] Add an inference forward that takes the decoder input directly (e.g. `forward_decoder(input_tokens, decoder_input)`) and use it in all four `ChatbotAPI` `model_fn`s.
- [x] Add a regression test: a model trained on an echo task must generate it exactly through `ChatbotAPI::generate_response()` on the CPU.
- [x] Have that forward project only the last decoder row (TD-424's `ChatbotAPI` part; `EncoderDecoderModel`'s beam callbacks already do, October 26, 2026).

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** `EncoderDecoderModel::next_token_logits(input_tokens, decoder_tokens)` is the inference forward. Its decoder
input is the generated sequence as given: `TextGenerator` starts it with BOS, and a BOS is put in front when it is missing (as from
`SpeculativeDecoder`'s empty context). It returns the logits of the last decoder row only. It shares `run_decoder()` with `forward()`:
the encoder (tail-truncated, TD-365), world-model and hippocampal reads are the same, and nothing is committed to the hippocampal memory.
All four `ChatbotAPI` CPU callbacks use it: plain, speculative (draft and target), batched and `/chat/batch`. `forward()` keeps the
training shift and the full projection.

Tests (`ChatbotAPIEchoTest`): the fixture trains a tiny model on the CPU to echo four phrases (mean loss below 0.01; a fresh model is
tried when an unseeded run doesn't converge, TD-368). Then every path must reproduce each phrase exactly:
- `PlainCpuGenerationEchoesExactly` (greedy) and `PlainCpuBeamSearchEchoesExactly`;
- `BatchEndpointEchoesExactly` (`generate_batch_responses()`);
- `SpeculativeDecodingEchoesExactly` (the model as its own draft);
- `BatchedInferenceEchoesExactly` (temperature 0, TD-214).

With the old callbacks, the four plain, beam and batch tests fail with every token doubled: "hheelloo w wororlldd" for "hello world".
`NextTokenLogitsIsTheLastRowOfTheAlignedForward` checks the logits against the training forward's last row (within 1e-4) and checks that
a missing BOS is added.

Not changed: these CPU paths still re-run the encoder every step with no KV cache, don't commit hippocampal steps, and don't cap
generation at `max_seq_length` the way `generate_response_with_strategy()` does (TD-347). That is part of TD-362's CPU/GPU differences.
(TD-362, October 26, 2026: the plain CPU path now uses `generate_response_with_strategy()`; the speculative, batched and `/chat/batch`
paths still use `next_token_logits()`.)

Location in code: `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (`generate_response()` plain, speculative and batched `model_fn`s; `generate_batch_responses()`),
`src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}` (`next_token_logits()`, `run_decoder()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp`
- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/chatbotapi_test.cpp`

Description:
Found while tracing `LanguageModelHead` and measured. The uncached generation callbacks run

### TD-423: A Truncated `.lm_head` File Loads as All-`NaN` Logits

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Models / LanguageModelHead | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `LanguageModelHead` and verified. `load()` checks the two dimension ints, then
pre-fills each weight and bias value with `NaN` and reads without checking the stream. A `.lm_head`
file cut in half **loaded without error**: 751 of 1,600 weights were `NaN`, and all 100 logits of a
forward pass were `NaN`. Every checkpoint written by `EncoderDecoderModel::save_model()` has this
sidecar and `load_model()` reads it, so a checkpoint damaged by a full disk or a crash during save
produces a server that generates garbage instead of refusing to load. `save()` doesn't check its writes.
Same defect as TD-298 (`CrossAttention::load()`).

Action Items:

- [x] Check the file size (or the stream after each read) and throw on short files, leaving the head unchanged; check `save()`'s stream.
- [x] Do this with the other legacy loaders (TD-298, TD-345, TD-357, TD-367, TD-369). (Owner chose every checkpoint loader, October 26, 2026.)

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** The new `adai::binio::Reader`/`Writer` (`src/BinaryIO.{hpp,cpp}`, in `adai_core`) handle checkpoint I/O:
- **Reads.** A short read throws `std::runtime_error` naming the file and field, and `expect_end()` rejects trailing bytes, so a file
  that doesn't match the model's shapes fails too.
- **Writes.** Matrices are written a row at a time, and `close()` throws when a write or the final flush failed (a full disk).

Every file `save_model()`/`load_model()` touches uses them:
- `.config` and the encoder and decoder headers (`LLMEncoder`, `LLMDecoder`);
- token embeddings, layer norms (including the encoder/decoder final norms) and the LM head;
- self- and cross-attention, feed-forward;
- encoder and decoder blocks, including the gated paths' flags and gates.

Each loader reads its whole file into temporaries and validates it before changing anything, so a failed load leaves that layer as it
was. `CrossAttention`/`DecoderBlock` no longer overwrite `learning_rate`/`dropout_rate` before the dimensions are checked.

Not covered:
- `load_model()` reads its files one after another, so a failure in a later file leaves earlier layers already replaced. Callers
  treat the throw as a failed load.
- The `.vocab` text file (TD-223), other formats (`.optimizer` training state, `LeJEPAEncoder`, `HippocampalMemory`) and the
  remaining items of each loader's own TD stay open.

Tests:
- `EncoderDecoderModelTest.EveryCheckpointFileIsCheckedOnLoad`: each of the 22 binary sidecars of a 2+2-layer checkpoint is cut one
  byte short, then grown one byte long, and `load_model()` must throw each time. On the old code 43 of the 44 cases loaded without
  error.
- `LanguageModelHeadPersistenceTest.TruncatedFileThrowsAndLeavesTheHeadUnchanged` and `FailedWriteThrows` (`/dev/full`), both
  failing on the old code.
- `CrossAttentionPersistenceTest`/`FeedForwardPersistenceTest`.TruncatedOrEmptyFileThrowsAndLeavesTheLayerUnchanged.
- `BinaryIOTest.*`.

Location in code: `src/BinaryIO.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/LanguageModelHead.cpp`, and the loaders listed above.

Files to Modify:

- `src/LanguageModelHead.cpp`
- `tests/languagemodelhead_test.cpp`

### TD-422: `KVCache` Copies the Whole Cache on Every Append

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Inference / KVCache | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `KVCache` and measured. `append()` allocates new `[current_length + new_rows ×
d]` matrices and copies the old contents on every call. Self-attention caches get one append per decode
step per layer, so a generation of *n* tokens does O(n²·d) copying per layer before any attention work.
Measured for one cache at d_model 512, one row per step: 128 steps 15.6 ms, 256 steps 53.8 ms, 512 steps
255 ms (quadratic), which is about 6 s of pure copying for a 24-layer decoder generating 512 tokens on the
CPU serving path. `GPUKVCache` already pre-allocates to `max_seq_length`; this one doesn't. (The old
`kvcache.md` claimed O(d²) per cached step.)

Action Items:

- [x] Pre-allocate `keys`/`values` to `max_seq_length` (or grow geometrically) and track the populated length; give `MultiHeadAttention`/`CrossAttention` a view of the populated rows instead of a full copy.
- [x] Do this with TD-388 and TD-398, which have the same per-step copy pattern. (TD-388 was fixed October 26, 2026; TD-398 stays open on its own. Originally not done here: TD-388 is the GPU cache and TD-398 the
  hippocampal memory. Both are left open.)

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** `append()` grows the cache in place. `Matrix` keeps one vector per row, so new rows are pushed and no
cached row is copied (amortized O(new rows × d)). Attention reads the populated matrix by reference as before. Measured for one cache
at d_model 512, one row per step (`-O2`):

| Steps | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 128 | 19.8 ms | 0.37 ms |
| 256 | 52.7 ms | 0.42 ms |
| 512 | 219 ms | 1.03 ms |

Test `AppendDoesNotCopyCachedRows` checks that the first row's buffer survives 300 appends; the old code reallocated it.
`AppendKeepsEveryRowInOrder` checks the contents. `MultiHeadAttention::forward_with_cache()` still copies the cache into
`cached_K`/`cached_V` for a backward pass that nothing runs after cached decoding, one more O(n·d) copy per step; that remains.

Location in code: `src/KVCache.hpp` (`append()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-422`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/KVCache.hpp`
- `src/MultiHeadAttention.cpp`
- `src/CrossAttention.cpp`

### TD-421: `KVCache::append()` Has No Shape Checks

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Inference / KVCache | Code fix (LOW, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `KVCache` and verified under AddressSanitizer. `KVCache::append()` never compares
`new_keys` with `new_values`, or the new columns with the cached ones:
- Appending wider rows (`Matrix(1,8)` onto a cache of width 4) writes 8 columns into 4-column rows:
  **heap-buffer-overflow WRITE**.
- Appending fewer value rows than key rows (`append(Matrix(3,4), Matrix(1,4))`) indexes `new_values` by
  `new_keys.rows`: **heap-buffer-overflow READ**.
- An inconsistent first append (`keys 3×4`, `values 1×8`) is accepted silently.

Today's callers always pass matching shapes, so this is latent, but the failure mode is memory
corruption. `DecoderKVCache::get_self_attention_cache()`/`get_cross_attention_cache()` don't
bounds-check the layer index, and `current_length()` reads only layer 0.

Action Items:

- [x] Validate shapes in `append()` (throw `invalid_argument`), bounds-check layer indices, and add a direct `KVCache` test file.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-422).** `append()` throws `invalid_argument` when keys and values differ in shape or the new rows
have a different width from the cache, and a rejected append changes nothing. `DecoderKVCache::get_*_attention_cache()` throw
`out_of_range` for a bad layer index. New `tests/kvcache_test.cpp` (`kvcacheTests`): `RejectsMismatchedShapes` (the three cases from
the description), `LayerIndicesAreChecked`, plus TD-422's tests. Clean under AddressSanitizer.

Location in code: `src/KVCache.hpp` (`append()`, `get_*_cache()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-421`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/KVCache.hpp`
- `tests/` (new KVCache test)

### TD-388: `GPUKVCache` Copies the Whole Cache Every Decode Step

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | GPU / GPUMatrix | Code fix (LOW, filed October 12, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MatrixGPU.hpp`, by inspection. `GPUKVCache::get_keys()`/`get_values()` allocate a
new `GPUMatrix` and copy the whole populated prefix on every call. Cached self-attention and
cross-attention call them once per layer per decode step, so a generation of `n` tokens copies
O(n²·d_model) floats per layer and performs two allocations per layer per step. That works against
TD-050's goal (no per-step device malloc/free churn) and will show up in TD-033/TD-050's still-open
GPU latency benchmark.

Action Items:

- [x] Return a non-owning view (pointer, rows, cols) of the populated prefix and have attention consume it directly (cuBLAS/oneMKL take a leading dimension, so no copy is needed).

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- **Cache view.** `GPUKVCache::get_keys()`/`get_values()` (and `materialize()`) are replaced by a view: `keys_data()`,
  `values_data()` and `leading_dimension()`.
- **Strided GEMM.** The new `matrix_gemm_strided_gpu()` is a row-major `C = alpha·op(A)·op(B)` with leading dimensions:
  `cublasSgemm` in CUDA and oneMKL `gemm` in SYCL, using `matrix_multiply_gpu()`'s column-major trick.
- **Cached attention.** `MultiHeadAttention::gpu_forward_with_cache()` and `CrossAttention::gpu_forward_with_cache()` compute each
  head as `scale·Q_h·K_hᵀ` straight from the cache, and write `scores·V_h` into that head's columns of the output.
- **Removed per step.** Each layer used to copy the whole cache prefix twice (two allocations), copy every head's Q/K/V columns out
  one row at a time (about `total_len × heads` device copies), transpose, scale into a new matrix and scatter the head output back.
  All of that is gone.

Measured on the oneAPI CPU device, with d_model 128, 8 heads and 2+2 layers: a 100-token GPU greedy decode took 6.6 s before and
1.4 s after (4.6× faster). On a real GPU the removed per-row copies were separate device calls, so the gain should be larger;
measuring it is part of TD-033/TD-050's benchmark. The CUDA backend is compile-checked only.

Tests:
- `MatrixGPUTD388Test.StridedGemmMatchesHostReference`: all four transpose combinations, offset views and wider leading
  dimensions, and the columns outside the view are untouched.
- `EncoderDecoderGPUTest.CachedGpuDecodeMatchesCpuOverALongGeneration`: 4 heads, 2+2 layers, 20 greedy tokens, equal to the CPU
  output.
- The existing GPU generation tests.

### TD-369: `FeedForward::load_weights()` Loads Truncated Files as a Silent Mix of Old and New Weights

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Transformer / FeedForward | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 12, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `FeedForward` and verified. `load_weights()` checks the two dimension ints but
never checks the stream afterwards. A file cut off after 10 floats loaded **without an exception**:
the start of `W1` came from the file, and the rest of `W1`, all of `W2` and both biases silently kept
their previous values. This is the per-block `<block>_feedforward.bin` file that
`EncoderDecoderModel::save_model()`/`load_model()` use through the block and encoder save paths, so a
damaged checkpoint becomes a silent mix of old (often random) and new weights. `save_weights()`
doesn't check its writes. Same class as TD-298, TD-345, TD-357 and TD-367.

Action Items:

- [x] Check the file size up front (`8 + 4·(2·d_model·d_ff + d_ff + d_model)` bytes), read into temporaries, check the stream, and assign only on success.
- [x] Check `save_weights()`'s stream before returning; write each matrix in one call rather than one float at a time. (One call per row.)
- [x] Test: truncated and empty files throw and leave the layer unchanged.

**Load/save checks (October 26, 2026, with TD-423).** `save_weights()`/`load_weights()` reads and writes through `adai::binio` (`src/BinaryIO.{hpp,cpp}`): a short or over-long file throws `std::runtime_error`, the file is read into temporaries before anything changes, and a failed write or flush throws. Covered by `EncoderDecoderModelTest.EveryCheckpointFileIsCheckedOnLoad` and `FeedForwardPersistenceTest.TruncatedOrEmptyFileThrowsAndLeavesTheLayerUnchanged`.

Location in code: `src/FeedForward.cpp` (`load_weights()`, `save_weights()`); no longer tagged (TD-370's console output remains).

Files to Modify:

- `src/FeedForward.cpp`
- `tests/feedforward_test.cpp`

### TD-366: Serving Encoders Cache Activations for Backward; Dead State and Duplicate API

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Transformer / LLMEncoder | Code fix (LOW, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `LLMEncoder`, by inspection. `requires_grad` defaults to `true` and nothing clears it
for the serving encoders (the chat encoder in `chatbot_api_server` and the RAG encoder). So every
inference `encode*()` call copies `(num_layers + 1) × seq × d_model` floats into
`cached_encoder_outputs`, which `backward()` never reads (it relies on each block's own caches).
`cached_embeddings` and `cached_pos_encoded` are declared and never used.
`get_sentence_embedding()` and `get_sentence_embedding_trainable()` are identical, and neither has a
production caller (`DocumentStore` pools for itself).

Action Items:

- [x] Remove `cached_encoder_outputs`, `cached_embeddings` and `cached_pos_encoded`, or at least stop filling the first.
- [x] Clear `requires_grad` for serving instances (`EncoderDecoderModel::set_training(false)` already forwards it; make the server and RAG setup call it).
- [x] Merge the two sentence-embedding functions.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- `cached_encoder_outputs`, `cached_embeddings` and `cached_pos_encoded` are removed, along with the per-call copies into the first.
  That was `(num_layers + 1) × seq × d_model` floats per encode, never read.
- The serving model is put in inference mode with `set_training(false)`: `chatbot_api_server`'s model and draft model, and
  `chatbot_gui`'s. The RAG encoder calls `set_requires_grad(false)`.
- `get_sentence_embedding_trainable()` now calls `get_sentence_embedding()`; the name is kept as the pair of
  `backward_sentence_embedding()`.

Test: `LLMEncoderTD366Test.SentenceEmbeddingFunctionsAgreeInEitherMode` (both functions, and `encode()` with `requires_grad` on and
off, give the same result). The removed state had no reader, so the change is otherwise behavior-neutral.

Location in code: `src/encoder.hpp` (members), `src/LLMEncoder.cpp`, `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`, `src/ChatbotGUI.cpp`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/encoder.hpp`
- `src/LLMEncoder.cpp`
- `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`

### TD-365: Encoder Input Is Never Truncated to `max_seq_length` When Serving

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Transformer / LLMEncoder | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `LLMEncoder` and verified. Only `encode(text)` truncates. `encode_with_mask()` and
`gpu_encode()` take any length, and neither `EncoderDecoderModel`'s generation entry points nor
`ChatbotAPI` truncate the input. A 60-token input on a `max_seq_length = 16` model completed generation
after `PositionalEncoding` warned *"Positions beyond max_len will not receive positional encodings"*, so
44 positions had no order information. Attention cost also grows as O(n²) with no bound, so a long chat
message costs more CPU or GPU time than the configured model size suggests. Related: TD-347 (decoder
side past `max_seq_length`) and TD-294 (the conversation token budget isn't tied to `max_seq_length`).

Action Items:

- [x] Decide on keep-the-tail truncation or rejection, and apply it once where `EncoderDecoderModel` tokenizes encoder input (CPU and GPU, training and generation).
- [x] Add a `max_seq_length` check (assert or throw) in `encode_with_mask()`/`gpu_encode()`.
- [x] Coordinate with TD-294 so the conversation context fits the encoder. (Done with TD-294 on November 4, 2026: a session's
  token budget is now the model's `max_seq_length` in real tokens, and the encoder keeps a conversation's last `max_seq_length` tokens.)

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- **Policy.** Keep the tail: the rule `ChatbotTrainer` already applies to training inputs (`truncate_tokens_tail()`), so serving now
  sees inputs shaped like training's.
- **One helper.** `LLMEncoder::keep_last_positions()` applies it, used by:
  - `EncoderDecoderModel`: all four generation paths, `forward()` (which `ChatbotAPI`'s CPU callbacks call with whole
    conversations) and `gpu_forward()`;
  - `encode()`;
  - `RLHFTrainer::encode_to_vector()`;
  - `IntegratedInferenceEngine`'s tokenization.
- **Checks.** `encode_with_mask()` and `gpu_encode()` throw `invalid_argument` past `max_seq_length` instead of running with
  unencoded positions.

Tests:
- `OverLongInputKeepsTheTail` and `EncodeWithMaskRejectsOverLongInput` (`llmencoder_test.cpp`).
- `OverLongEncoderInputKeepsTheTail` (`encoderdecoder_test.cpp`): `forward()` on 60 tokens at `max_seq_length = 16` equals `forward()`
  on the last 16, and plain and beam generation accept a 480-character input.

The RAG, pipeline and integrated engine suites still pass.

Location in code: `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp` (input tokenization in `generate_response()`, `generate_response_with_strategy()`, both GPU generation paths), `src/LLMEncoder.cpp` (`encode_with_mask()`, `gpu_encode()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-365`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`
- `src/LLMEncoder.cpp`
- `tests/llmencoder_test.cpp`

### TD-364: `LLMEncoder::encode()` Input Doesn't Match the Model's Encoder Input

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Transformer / LLMEncoder | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `LLMEncoder` and verified. `encode(text)` tokenizes with the encoder's own
tokenizer and `add_special_tokens = true`, so `"hello world"` becomes `[BOS, 80, 77, EOS]`.
`EncoderDecoderModel` always tokenizes encoder input with `encode(input_text, false)` (`[80, 77]`), in
training and in generation, so the trained encoder has never seen `BOS`/`EOS` at its input and every
real token sits one position later under `encode()`. The first output row differed (1.398 vs 0.980).
`PipelineInferenceEngine`'s encoder stage calls `encode()` on the trained chat encoder and hands the
result to the decoder, so pipeline-mode answers come from out-of-distribution encoder input. For RAG
(`DocumentStore`) it only needs to be consistent, which it is.

Also verified: when `encode()` truncates to `max_seq_length` it uses `resize()`, dropping the `EOS` it
just added (32 ids cut to 8, last id no longer `EOS`).

Action Items:

- [x] Give `encode()` an `add_special_tokens` parameter (default matching the model: `false`), or have `PipelineInferenceEngine` tokenize with the model's tokenizer and call `encode_with_mask()`.
- [x] When truncating with special tokens, keep the final `EOS`.
- [x] Add a test that pipeline and plain generation produce the same encoder output for the same text.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-365).** `encode(text, add_special_tokens = false)`: the default gives what `EncoderDecoderModel` feeds
the encoder, so `PipelineInferenceEngine`'s encoder stage is in distribution. With special tokens, BOS and EOS are kept at the ends
when the input is truncated (TD-365's tail rule). RAG (`DocumentStore`) re-embeds its documents and queries with `encode()` on every
start and saves nothing, so it stays consistent. Without special tokens it now embeds the last `max_seq_length` tokens of a long
document instead of the first (TD-349 still applies).

Tests (`llmencoder_test.cpp`):
- `EncodeMatchesTheModelsEncoderInput`: `encode(text)` equals `encode_with_mask(tokenize(text, false))`.
- `OverLongInputKeepsTheTail`: covers the special-token case (BOS + last 6 + EOS at `max_seq_length = 8`).

Location in code: `src/LLMEncoder.cpp` (`encode()`), `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp` (encoder stage); tagged `TODO: See TD-364`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/LLMEncoder.cpp`
- `src/encoder.hpp`
- `src/PipelineInferenceEngine.hpp`
- `tests/llmencoder_test.cpp`

### TD-363: `EncoderDecoderModel` Clone, Load and World-Model Input Gaps

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Models / EncoderDecoderModel | Code fix (LOW, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-358, by inspection:
- `clone()` round-trips `save_model()`/`load_model()`, so the copy lacks the world model, hippocampal
  memory, generation config, repetition params and LoRA adapters. `ChatbotTrainer`'s async BLEU/ROUGE
  snapshots therefore generate differently from the live model.
- `load_model()` doesn't check its config reads, and restores special-token IDs onto the model but not
  into the generator's config until `sync_special_tokens()` runs.
- `forward()` re-derives the world model's input by decoding token ids back to text, which is lossy
  under the tokenizer's normalization (TD-224).

Action Items:

- [x] Copy the extra state in `clone()` (or document the snapshot's scope); check reads and sync the generator in `load_model()`; pass the original text to the world model where available.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- **`clone()`.** The copy is built with the original's `world_model_inject_every_n_layers`, now kept on the model. It used to be built
  without the gated decoder paths, so for any world-model-enabled model `load_model()` threw on the gated-path flag and the per-epoch
  quality snapshot failed. The copy also gets:
  - an independent world model, through the new `LeJEPAEncoder::clone()` (temp save/load, tokenizer, SIGReg settings);
  - a snapshot of the hippocampal memory;
  - the repetition and cross-reference parameters, the hippocampal-updates flag, the generation config and the learning rate.
- **`load_model()`.** Reads were already checked (TD-423), and it now calls `sync_special_tokens()`, so the generator's BOS/EOS/PAD
  follow the loaded tokenizer immediately.
- **World-model input.** The world model encodes the caller's text where one exists: `train_step()`, and the new `input_text`
  argument of `next_token_logits()`, which `ChatbotAPI`'s speculative, batched and `/chat/batch` callbacks pass. The token-only
  `forward()` still decodes.

Not covered: LoRA adapters aren't saved (TD-302), so a clone has none. The copied memory keeps the original's swap file path;
`ChatbotTrainer`'s copy has hippocampal updates off, so it never writes.

Tests:
- `CloneCopiesGatedPathsAttachmentsAndSettings`: on the old code `clone()` throws.
- `LoadModelSyncsTheGeneratorsSpecialTokens`: on the old code the generator kept 57.
- `WorldModelSeesTheOriginalInputText`: with an open gate, "hello jazz" (whose letters the model's vocabulary lacks) changes the
  logits; without the text, the decoded tokens are used.

Location in code: `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}` (`clone()`, `load_model()`, `run_decoder()`, `forward_impl()`,
`train_step_impl()`, `next_token_logits()`), `src/LeJEPAEncoder.{hpp,cpp}` (`clone()`), `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}`

### TD-362: CPU and GPU Generation Paths Behave Differently

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Models / EncoderDecoderModel | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-358, by inspection. The four generation entry points diverge:
- Invalid-vocab masking (IDs ≥ the tokenizer's vocab) happens only in the CPU strategy path and the
  CPU beam paths; the CPU plain cached path and every GPU path don't mask.
- Only CPU paths write hippocampal memory or attach the world model (beam only).
- An unknown strategy goes to `generate()` on CPU but to nucleus sampling on GPU.
- `num_beams > 1` forces beam on CPU (TD-261) but is ignored by the GPU non-beam strategies.

The same request can therefore produce different output depending on whether the server runs on a
GPU build.

Action Items:

- [x] Factor one shared model_fn/strategy-dispatch for CPU and GPU (masking, defaults, beam handling, memory write), differing only in the forward call.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** By then TD-342/343 had already given the GPU paths the world model and the hippocampal writes, and TD-261
had fixed `num_beams` on the CPU. The remaining differences now go through shared members of `EncoderDecoderModel`:
- `normalize_strategy()` (public, static): `temperature`→`sampling`, `top_k`/`top-k`→`topk`, `top_p`/`top-p`→`nucleus`. The CPU
  strategy path used to accept only the hyphenated forms.
- One beam decision on both: "beam", or an unrecognized strategy with `num_beams > 1`.
- `sync_generation_config()`, which stores the beam width only when beam search runs. The GPU path used to store it for every
  strategy, so a later plain call could switch to beam search.
- `mask_unknown_ids()`, now used by every CPU and GPU model callback. The CPU plain cached path and all four GPU callbacks didn't
  mask IDs beyond the tokenizer's vocabulary.
- `run_single_hypothesis()`, which runs `TextGenerator::generate()` on the configured filters for an unrecognized strategy. The GPU
  path used nucleus sampling.

`ChatbotAPI`'s CPU fallback (no GPU) now calls `generate_response_with_strategy()`, as its GPU branch calls the GPU version. It used to
run its own `TextGenerator` loop over `next_token_logits()` (TD-506), re-running the encoder and the whole decoder every step, with no
hippocampal commits and no `max_seq_length` cap. Generation therefore tokenizes with the model's tokenizer on both paths. When no
checkpoint loads, `chatbot_api_server` gives that tokenizer `VOCAB_PATH`.

Tests:
- `NormalizeStrategyAcceptsEverySpelling`.
- `PlainCachedPathMasksIdsTheTokenizerLacks`: with the logits favouring an ID the tokenizer lacks, the plain call must equal greedy. On
  the old code it returned "" against "worlhellod worl amm".
- `EncoderDecoderGPUTest.GpuAndCpuGenerationAgree` (oneAPI CPU device): GPU greedy, plain, beam and "other" with 3 beams equal the CPU
  greedy/beam output, and an explicit greedy call doesn't store its `num_beams`. On the old code every GPU result was "".
- The `ChatbotAPIEchoTest` paths, with the fixture's model given the API's vocabulary.

Location in code: `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}` (`normalize_strategy()`, `sync_generation_config()`, `mask_unknown_ids()`,
`run_single_hypothesis()`, all four generation entry points), `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (`generate_response()`), `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`

### TD-360: `EncoderDecoderModel` No-Optimizer Path Never Updates the Encoder

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Models / EncoderDecoderModel | Code fix (LOW, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-358 and confirmed. `update_weights()` and `set_learning_rate()` skip the encoder
(the calls are commented out: "LLMEncoder doesn't have this method"), and the LM head's LR isn't set
either. **Corrected October 11, 2026** ([LLMEncoder.md](../reference/source/LLMEncoder.md)): that
comment is stale for `set_learning_rate()`, which `LLMEncoder` has had since the TD-093 fix; only
`LLMEncoder::update_weights()` is missing. Ten `train_step()` calls with no optimizer left the encoder's weights exactly unchanged while
the decoder's moved. Combined with TD-346 (final decoder norm), `train_step()` trains only the decoder
blocks, embeddings and head. `ChatbotTrainer` registers an optimizer and is unaffected.

Action Items:

- [x] Add `LLMEncoder::update_weights()`, call it and the existing `LLMEncoder::set_learning_rate()`; set the head's LR; fold into TD-297's single-step design for the optimizer case.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-297/TD-346).** `LLMEncoder::update_weights()` is new: it steps a registered optimizer once, or runs plain SGD in the token embedding, every block and the final norm. `EncoderDecoderModel::set_learning_rate()` reaches the encoder and the LM head. The no-optimizer `update_weights()` updates the encoder, the decoder (final norm included) and the head; with an optimizer it steps once. Test: `EncoderDecoderModelTest.OneUpdateIsOneStepWithOrWithoutAnOptimizer`: two copies of a 2+2-layer model, one with an SGD optimizer registered (twice) and one without, take one `train_step()`. The encoder's weights and the decoder's final norm must move, and the two models must give the same logits (within 1e-4). On the old code the encoder and the final norm didn't move, and the logits differed by up to 4.65.

Location in code: `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp` (`update_weights()`, `set_learning_rate()`), `src/LLMEncoder.cpp`/`src/encoder.hpp` (`update_weights()`).

- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`

### TD-359: `generate_response()` and `gpu_generate_response()` Ignore `max_length`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Models / EncoderDecoderModel | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-358 and confirmed. Neither method forwards its `max_length` argument to
`TextGenerator`, which uses its stored `max_length` (initially `max_seq_length`):
`generate_response("hello world", 5)` produced 9 tokens with the generator at 64. The GPU version
documents it ("kept for interface parity"). `ChatbotTrainer`'s generation-quality metrics
(`generation_quality_max_tokens = 50`) and label backfill call `generate_response()`, so their
generations can run to `max_seq_length`, slowing metric computation. The `_with_strategy` variants do
honour `max_length`.

Action Items:

- [x] Apply `max_length` for the call (temporarily set it on the generator config and restore it, or pass it through), on both CPU and GPU.
- [x] Test: `generate_response(…, 5)` returns at most 5 new tokens.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).** `generate_response()` and `gpu_generate_response()` apply their `max_length` for the call through a scoped
override (`ScopedMaxLength`, under the model lock), and the generator's stored value is put back afterwards. `max_length <= 0` keeps
the stored value. `ChatbotTrainer`'s generation-quality and backfill calls now stop at `generation_quality_max_tokens` (50) and
`generation_backfill_max_tokens` instead of running to the stored length. (The count still includes BOS, TD-516.)

Tests:
- `GenerateResponseHonoursMaxLength` (CPU): three inputs at `max_length = 5` stay within 5 tokens with the generator at 64, a limit of
  40 gives longer output, and the stored 64 is unchanged. The old code returned 10, 12 and 14 tokens.
- `EncoderDecoderGPUTest.GpuGenerateResponseHonoursMaxLength`: the same on the GPU path, run on the oneAPI CPU device
  (`ADAI_SYCL_ALLOW_CPU_DEVICE=1`, `build/sycl-cpudev`).

**Test update (October 26, 2026).** `GenerateResponseHonoursMaxLength` and its GPU twin failed about 1 run in 15: the untrained, unseeded model (TD-368) sometimes stopped before 6 tokens, and re-encoding the decoded answer doesn't count tokens exactly. Both now decode greedily with the special tokens ruled out, and check that the 5-token answer is a strict prefix of the 40-token one (40 of 40 runs pass).

Location in code: `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp` (`generate_response()`, `gpu_generate_response()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-359`.

- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`
- `tests/encoderdecoder_test.cpp`

### TD-347: Cached and Full Decoder Forwards Diverge Past `max_seq_length`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Transformer / Decoder | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-346 and confirmed by running the real class. Within `max_seq_length` the KV-cached
incremental forward matches the full forward (|Δ| = 0.000002). Past it they split:
`PositionalEncoding::forward()` leaves rows beyond `max_len` without positional encoding (stderr
warning), while `forward_with_cache()` and `gpu_decode_step()` compute positional encoding inline for
any position. With `max_seq_length = 4` the last token of a length-6 sequence differed by 13.6 (L1 over
`d_model = 16`). Over-length generation therefore produces different hidden states depending on the
strategy (KV-cached greedy/sampling vs full-recompute beam), and neither has positions the model was
trained on.

Action Items:

- [x] Cap decoder input + generated length at `max_seq_length` in generation (truncate the oldest context or stop), and make the cached paths refuse or clamp positions ≥ `max_seq_length` consistently with `PositionalEncoding`.
- [x] Test: generation never exceeds `max_seq_length`; cached and full forwards agree at the boundary.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- **Cached forward.** The CPU `forward_with_cache()` takes its positional rows from `PositionalEncoding`'s table and adds none at or past
  `max_seq_length`, like the full forward; the GPU cached path already did so (TD-547). This also removes one of TD-478's inline copies
  of the formula.
- **Generation cap.** Every generation entry point (`generate_response()`, `gpu_generate_response()`, and both
  `*_with_strategy()`) caps the length at `max_seq_length` through `capped_generation_length()`, so the decoder never sees
  positions the model has no encoding for. Generation stops there.

Tests:
- `CachedMatchesFullPastMaxSeqLength` (`inference_optimization_test.cpp`): 6 tokens at `max_seq_length = 4`, cached vs full within
  1e-3 at every step. The old code diverged by 4.0 and 7.7 L1 at positions 4 and 5.
- `GenerationNeverExceedsMaxSeqLength` (`encoderdecoder_test.cpp`): `max_length = 100` at `max_seq_length = 8` stays within 8
  tokens for plain, greedy, sampling and beam generation. The old code produced 92–99.

Location in code: `src/Decoder.cpp` (`forward_with_cache()`, `gpu_decode_step()` positional encoding); tagged `TODO: See TD-347`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/Decoder.cpp`
- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`
- `src/PositionalEncoding.cpp`

**GPU follow-up (October 19, 2026, TD-547).** `LLMDecoder::gpu_decode_step()` now takes positional rows from the shared table, adding none past
`max_seq_length`, like the full forward. So the GPU cached path no longer diverges this way; the CPU `forward_with_cache()` still does.

### TD-346: `LLMDecoder::update_weights()` Never Updates the Final Norm

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Transformer / Decoder | Code fix (LOW, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [Decoder.md](../reference/source/Decoder.md) and confirmed by running the real class.
`update_weights(float lr)` calls the token embedding's and every block's `update_weights()`, but the
final norm's update is commented out ("For now, we'll skip if the method doesn't exist"), although
`LayerNorm::update_weights()` exists; the `lr` argument is ignored. Twenty steps through this path
moved the token embeddings (L1 0.22) while the final norm's gamma and beta stayed exactly unchanged.
`EncoderDecoderModel::update_weights()`/`train_step()` use this path; the shipped `ChatbotTrainer`
calls `optimizer->step()` and is unaffected.

Action Items:

- [x] Test: `update_weights()` changes the final norm's parameters.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-297/TD-360).** Without an optimizer, `LLMDecoder::update_weights(lr)` applies `lr` to every sub-layer (`set_learning_rate()`) and updates the token embedding, every block and the final norm. With one, it steps it once (TD-297). Test: `EncoderDecoderModelTest.OneUpdateIsOneStepWithOrWithoutAnOptimizer`: two copies of a 2+2-layer model, one with an SGD optimizer registered (twice) and one without, take one `train_step()`. The encoder's weights and the decoder's final norm must move, and the two models must give the same logits (within 1e-4). On the old code the encoder and the final norm didn't move, and the logits differed by up to 4.65.

Location in code: `src/Decoder.cpp` (`update_weights()`); no longer tagged.

### TD-298: `CrossAttention::load()` Loads Truncated Files as NaN Weights

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Attention / CrossAttention | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 10, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-297 and confirmed by running the real class. `load()` pre-sets each value to
`NAN` and never checks the stream, so a file cut off after `W_k` loaded **without error** with all of
`W_v`/`W_o` NaN. `learning_rate` is read into the member before the dimension check, so a rejected
(mismatched) file still changes the layer's learning rate. `save()` doesn't check its writes. This
is the legacy per-block `<block>.cross_attn` format written by `DecoderBlock::save()`; the main
checkpoint path is SafeTensors (`ModelSerializer`).

Action Items:

- [x] Check the stream after every read (and the file size up front); throw on short reads.
- [x] Read the header into locals and assign `learning_rate` only after validation; check `save()`'s stream before returning.
- [x] Test: truncated and empty files throw and leave the layer unchanged.

**Load/save checks (October 26, 2026, with TD-423).** `save()`/`load()` reads and writes through `adai::binio` (`src/BinaryIO.{hpp,cpp}`): a short or over-long file throws `std::runtime_error`, the file is read into temporaries before anything changes, and a failed write or flush throws. Covered by `EncoderDecoderModelTest.EveryCheckpointFileIsCheckedOnLoad` and `CrossAttentionPersistenceTest.TruncatedOrEmptyFileThrowsAndLeavesTheLayerUnchanged`; `learning_rate` is assigned only after the whole file is read and validated.

Location in code: `src/CrossAttention.cpp` (`load()`, `save()`); no longer tagged.

### TD-297: Layer `update_weights()` Steps a Shared Optimizer Once per Layer

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Attention / CrossAttention | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 10, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [CrossAttention.md](../reference/source/CrossAttention.md) and confirmed by running the real
class. `CrossAttention::update_weights()` calls `optimizer->step()`, but `Optimizer::step()` steps
**every** parameter group ever registered with it, not just this layer's.
`DecoderBlock::register_parameters_with_optimizer()` registers every sub-layer with one shared
optimizer, and `DecoderBlock::update_weights()` then calls each sub-layer's `update_weights()` in
turn. With two `CrossAttention`s sharing an SGD optimizer, the second layer's weights moved a full
step on the first layer's call and again on its own: two steps. A full decoder block makes 6–10
`step()` calls per update (each also advancing Adam's step counter). `MultiHeadAttention`,
`FeedForward`, `LayerNorm`, `TokenEmbedding` and `LanguageModelHead` follow the same pattern.
Calling `set_optimizer()` twice with the same optimizer also registers the groups twice (verified:
8 groups instead of 4), doubling every update.

The shipped trainers (`ChatbotTrainer`, `RLHFTrainer`) call `optimizer->step()` once directly and
are unaffected, but the public `EncoderDecoderModel::train_step()`/`update_weights()` path
over-steps whenever an optimizer is registered. `LeJEPAEncoder` hit and fixed exactly this
(TD-178).

Action Items:

- [x] Apply TD-178's fix at the model level: when an optimizer is registered, `EncoderDecoderModel`/`LLMDecoder`/`DecoderBlock` `update_weights()` call `step()` once at the top and only zero grads below; or have layers skip `step()` when the optimizer is shared.
- [x] Make `set_optimizer()`/`register_parameters()` idempotent for the same optimizer (or dedupe in `Optimizer::add_parameter_group()`).
- [x] Test: two layers on one optimizer each move by exactly one step per `EncoderDecoderModel::update_weights()`.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-346/TD-360).** TD-178's fix is now applied at every composite level.
- **One step.** `EncoderDecoderModel`, `LLMEncoder`, `LLMDecoder`, `EncoderBlock` and `DecoderBlock` remember the optimizer they were registered with. `update_weights()` calls its `step()` once, then zeroes the gradients. Before, every sub-layer's `update_weights()` stepped the shared optimizer again. `register_lora_parameters()` also sets the model's optimizer, so `update_weights()` steps the adapters rather than running SGD on the frozen base.
- **Registration.** `Optimizer::add_parameter_group()` ignores a matrix that is already registered (and throws if it comes with different gradients), so registering twice no longer doubles updates.
- **Unchanged.** Leaf layers still call `step()` in their own `update_weights()`; that is correct for a layer with an optimizer of its own.

Test: `EncoderDecoderModelTest.OneUpdateIsOneStepWithOrWithoutAnOptimizer`: two copies of a 2+2-layer model, one with an SGD optimizer registered (twice) and one without, take one `train_step()`. The encoder's weights and the decoder's final norm must move, and the two models must give the same logits (within 1e-4). On the old code the encoder and the final norm didn't move, and the logits differed by up to 4.65.

Location in code: `src/CrossAttention.cpp` (`update_weights()`, `register_parameters()`), `src/DecoderBlock.cpp` (`update_weights()`); no longer tagged.

Files to Modify:

- `src/CrossAttention.cpp`
- `src/DecoderBlock.cpp`
- `src/Decoder.cpp`
- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`
- `src/Optimizer.cpp`
- `tests/encoderdecoder_test.cpp`

### TD-293: A Malformed Conversation Import Wipes the Live Session

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | NLP / ConversationContext | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-291 and confirmed by running the real class. `deserialize()` calls
`clear_all()` **before** parsing, and a bad line (e.g. a non-numeric token count, so `std::stoi`
throws) aborts mid-parse, leaving the context empty. `ChatbotAPI::handle_import_session()` reports
"Failed to import conversation", but the session's previous history is already gone.
`load_from_file()` has the same exposure.

Action Items:

- [x] Parse into a temporary `ConversationContext` and swap it in only on success (strong exception guarantee); skip or report bad lines instead of throwing mid-way.
- [x] Test: a malformed import leaves existing history unchanged.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-291).**
- **Strong guarantee.** `deserialize()` parses into a temporary context and swaps it in only at the end.
- **No mid-parse throws.** Token counts are no longer parsed (they're recomputed), so a bad count can't throw halfway.
- **Bad lines.** Lines without the `role|count|content` shape are skipped.
- **Non-conversations.** Data with no `---` line isn't a serialized conversation: it throws `std::invalid_argument` and leaves the
  history unchanged. `load_from_file()` gets all of this too, since it calls `deserialize()`.

Tests: `BadTokenCountNoLongerWipesTheHistory` and `NonConversationDataLeavesTheHistoryUnchanged`, both failing on the old code.

Location in code: `src/ConversationContext.cpp` (`deserialize()`); no longer tagged.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ConversationContext.cpp`
- `tests/conversationcontext_test.cpp`

### TD-292: One Long Message Wipes the Whole Conversation

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | NLP / ConversationContext | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-291 and confirmed by running the real class. `truncate_to_limits()` evicts
the oldest messages until under `max_tokens`, keeping a lone remaining message only if it's
within 1.2× the budget. The **newest** message isn't protected, so a message that alone exceeds
1.2 × `max_tokens` evicts **everything, including itself**. With `ChatbotAPI`'s 2048-token session
budget, a 12,000-character user message left 0 messages. `handle_chat_session()` then formats an
empty prompt, `generate_response("")` fails (`BPETokenizer::encode("")` throws), the client gets
HTTP 500, and the conversation history is gone.

Action Items:

- [x] Never evict the message just added: truncate it (e.g. keep its tail) to fit, or reject it with a clear error before touching history.
- [x] In `ChatbotAPI`, reject over-long messages with a 4xx before adding them.
- [x] Test: an oversized message leaves earlier history intact and produces a clear error or truncated content.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- **Eviction.** `truncate_to_limits()` evicts the oldest messages but never the newest. A lone newest message keeps the existing
  1.2× slack; beyond that it keeps its tail, cut on a UTF-8 boundary, within the space the system message leaves. It is evicted only
  when the system message alone already exceeds the budget, which keeps TD-125's tests' behaviour.
- **Serving.** `ChatbotAPI::handle_chat_session()` refuses a message larger than the session's whole budget with HTTP 400 before it
  touches the history.

Tests: `ConversationContextTest.OversizedNewestMessageKeepsItsTail` and
`ChatbotAPITest.OversizedChatMessageIsRejectedAndTheHistoryKept` (the earlier turn survives). Both fail on the old code.

Location in code: `src/ConversationContext.cpp` (`truncate_to_limits()`), `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (`handle_chat_session()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ConversationContext.cpp`
- `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp`
- `tests/conversationcontext_test.cpp`

### TD-291: Conversation Imports Can Lift Session Limits and Budgets

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | NLP / ConversationContext | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [ConversationContext.md](../reference/source/ConversationContext.md), and confirmed by running the real
class. `ConversationContext::deserialize()` **replaces** the instance's `max_messages`/`max_tokens`
with the imported `MAX_MESSAGES`/`MAX_TOKENS` lines, and trusts each message's stored `token_count`:

- `MAX_MESSAGES:0`/`MAX_TOKENS:0` make the session **unlimited**. 500 imported messages were all
  kept (a 2.5 MB prompt), and the session stayed unlimited for later messages.
- A token count of `1` on huge messages, or a **negative** count (`-100000` made `total_tokens`
  negative), defeats the token budget.

`chatbot_api_server` exposes this as `POST /chat/session/import` (TD-053), so any client can give its
session unbounded history, memory and prompt size, overriding `ChatbotAPI`'s `Session(10, 2048)`
limits, and combined with TD-232 it can do so across unlimited sessions.

Action Items:

- [x] In `deserialize()` (or an import-specific overload), keep the caller's limits instead of adopting imported ones; ignore or clamp imported metadata.
- [x] Recompute token counts on import (ignore stored counts), rejecting negative values; enforce a maximum import size in `ChatbotAPI`.
- [x] Tests: imported limits and token counts can't exceed the receiving session's limits.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-292/293).**
- **Limits.** `ConversationContext::deserialize()` keeps the receiving context's limits and ignores the imported `MAX_MESSAGES`,
  `MAX_TOKENS` and `KEEP_SYSTEM` lines.
- **Token counts.** Every message's token count is recomputed from its content; stored counts are ignored.
- **Size cap.** `ChatbotAPI::handle_import_session()` refuses data over 1 MiB with HTTP 400.

An import can no longer make a session unlimited or under-count it.

Tests: `ImportKeepsTheReceivingContextsLimits` (50 messages with `MAX_*:0` into a 5-message context) and
`ImportRecomputesTokenCounts` (counts of 1 and −100000), plus `ChatbotAPITest.OversizedImportIsRejected`. All fail on the old code.

Location in code: `src/ConversationContext.cpp` (`deserialize()`), `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (`handle_import_session()`); no longer tagged.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ConversationContext.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp`
- `tests/conversationcontext_test.cpp`
- `tests/chatbotapi_test.cpp`

### TD-246: `chatbot_api_server` Serves a Randomly Initialized Model When Loading Fails

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Inference / Serving / Server | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [ChatbotAPIServer.md](../reference/source/ChatbotAPIServer.md). In `main()`, if
`model->load_model(MODEL_PATH)` throws (missing file, architecture mismatch after an MNS outage
falls back to local config, a corrupt checkpoint, or one missing its `.vocab` per TD-221), the server
logs a warning, "Using random initialization", and **keeps serving the untrained model**. With no
`MODEL_PATH` at all it does the same, logging only "training required". In both cases
`GET /health` reports `{"status":"ok"}`, so clients get gibberish and monitoring sees a healthy
service. Found by reading the code.

Action Items:

- [x] Fail startup (exit 1) when the model can't be loaded, unless an explicit development opt-in (e.g. `ALLOW_UNTRAINED_MODEL=true`) is set.
- [x] Report model state in `/health` (`model_loaded`, model path/name), and return a non-`ok` status when serving untrained weights.
- [x] Test: a bad `MODEL_PATH` exits non-zero by default.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- **Startup.** `chatbot_api_server` exits 1 when `MODEL_PATH` is unset or can't be loaded (logged as an error), unless the new
  development opt-in `ALLOW_UNTRAINED_MODEL=true` (config key or environment) is set.
- **`/health`.** It reports `model_loaded` and `model_path`, and answers `"status":"untrained"` with HTTP 503 when serving untrained
  weights, so load balancers and monitoring see it. A loaded model gives `"ok"` with 200. `ChatbotAPI::set_model_status()` carries
  the state; library users that build their own `ChatbotAPI` default to "loaded".
- **Docs.** `config.chatbot.conf` and the operator docs describe both behaviours.

Test: `chatbotApiServerStartupTests` spawns the real binary with a minimal environment:
- `MissingModelFileExitsOne`;
- `NoModelPathExitsOne`;
- `OptInServesButHealthSaysUntrained` (503, `"untrained"`, `"model_loaded":false`).

On the old server, both missing-model cases were still running after 60 s, and `/health` answered 200 without `"untrained"`.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp` (model load), `src/ChatbotAPI.{hpp,cpp}` (`handle_health()`, `set_model_status()`), `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}` (`ALLOW_UNTRAINED_MODEL`).

### TD-229: ChatbotAPI Responses Can Be Invalid JSON (Unescaped Control Characters)

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Inference / Serving / API | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [ChatbotAPI.md](../reference/source/ChatbotAPI.md). `escape_json_string()` (the single escaping function since TD-063) escapes only `"`, `\`, `\n`,
`\r` and `\t`. Other characters in U+0000–U+001F pass through raw. Verified: `"a\x01b\bc"` is
emitted with bytes `01` and `08`, which strict JSON parsers reject. Model output, exception messages
and imported session data can all carry such bytes. nlohmann/json's `dump()` escapes them
correctly (`"a\u0001b\bc"`).

Action Items:

- [x] Escape every control character (`\b`, `\f`, and `\u00XX` for the rest), or build responses with nlohmann/json.
- [x] Test that every response parses with a strict JSON parser.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- **Control characters.** `escape_json_string()` escapes every one: `\b`, `\f`, and `\u00XX` for those without a short form.
- **Invalid UTF-8.** It is replaced with `\ufffd`, one per byte that can't start a well-formed sequence. That covers a stray byte, a
  truncated sequence, an overlong form or a surrogate. Byte-level model output can split a multi-byte character, and strict parsers
  reject invalid UTF-8 too.

Tests (`chatbotapiTests` now compiles against the vendored nlohmann/json):
- `EscapeJsonString_EveryControlCharacterAndInvalidUtf8ParseStrictly`: all 32 control characters, valid 2-, 3- and 4-byte
  characters, and the four invalid cases, parsed strictly and round-tripped.
- `ResponsesAreStrictJsonWhateverTheyCarry`: the success, error and batch responses.

Both fail on the old code.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp` (`escape_json_string()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChatbotAPI.cpp`
- `tests/chatbotapi_test.cpp`

Description:

|---|---|---|

| `{"message":"path C:\\","session_id":"abc"}` → `message` | `path C:\",` (runs past the closing quote) | `path C:\` |

It also can't distinguish a missing key from an empty string. Wrong session IDs and garbled
messages reach the model and the session map. nlohmann/json handles all of these correctly.

### TD-227: ChatbotAPI Session Pointers Are Used Outside the Session Lock

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Inference / Serving / API | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [ChatbotAPI.md](../reference/source/ChatbotAPI.md). `get_or_create_session()` returns a raw `Session*` after releasing `sessions_mutex_`.
`handle_chat_session()`, `handle_import_session()` and `generate_batch_session_responses()` then
read and mutate `session->context` (a `ConversationContext`, which has no internal locking) with no
lock held, across a generation that can take seconds. Consequences:

- two concurrent requests on the same `session_id` race on the same `ConversationContext`
  (undefined behaviour, corrupted history);
- `POST /clear-session` can clear the history mid-request;
- `cleanup_expired_sessions()` (run by `GET /health`) can **erase** the session mid-request, a
  use-after-free. That's unlikely with the default 30-minute timeout, since `last_access` is
  refreshed when a request starts, but nothing prevents it.

Found by reading the code paths.

Action Items:

- [x] Hold sessions as `std::shared_ptr<Session>` so an in-flight request keeps its session alive after erasure.
- [x] Add a per-session mutex held for the read-modify-generate-append sequence (serializing turns within one conversation, which is also the correct conversational semantics).
- [x] Tests: concurrent same-session requests under TSan; cleanup during an in-flight request.

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- **Ownership.** `sessions_` holds `std::shared_ptr<Session>`. `get_or_create_session()` returns a `shared_ptr` and sets an empty
  `session_id` to the new id, which removes the three reverse pointer lookups. A new `find_session()` looks one up without creating it.
- **Locking.** `Session` has a mutex, held for a whole turn: user message, generation and reply in `handle_chat_session()`, and in
  `handle_import_session()`, `handle_clear_session()` and `handle_export_session()`. `last_access` is atomic, since cleanup reads it
  under `sessions_mutex_`.
- **Batches.** `generate_batch_session_responses()` keeps every session alive and locked from the user messages to the replies. It
  locks each distinct session once, in address order, so a batch naming a session twice, or two overlapping batches, can't deadlock.
- **Lock order.** `sessions_mutex_` is never held while waiting for a session's mutex.

Tests:
- `ChatbotAPITest.ConcurrentTurnsOnOneSessionAreSerialized`: four threads on one session; all succeed and the history holds all 8
  messages.
- `CleanupDuringAnInFlightRequestKeepsTheSessionAlive`: with a 0-minute timeout, `/health` cleanup erases the session during
  generation.

Under the TSan build, with `OMP_NUM_THREADS=1` (TSan reports OpenMP's parallel regions in the model math falsely, since libgomp isn't
instrumented), the old code reports data races in `ConversationContext::add_message`, then a heap-use-after-free and a SEGV. The new
code is clean.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotAPI.{hpp,cpp}` (`Session`, `get_or_create_session()`, `find_session()`, the session handlers, `generate_batch_session_responses()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/ChatbotAPI.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/chatbotapi_test.cpp`

### TD-216: Softmax and GELU Math Is Duplicated Across CPU and GPU Code

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Core Math / Activation | Code fix (LOW, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-215. `Activation` is meant to be the reference implementation, but the same
math is re-typed in many places, so a change in one place (a different masking convention,
temperature, exact-`erf` GELU) silently leaves the others behind. For GELU specifically, that
means CPU and GPU training would quietly diverge, and checkpoints trained on one path would behave
differently on the other.

Independent copies today:

- **Softmax forward (CPU), max-subtracted, inline:**
  `MultiHeadAttention::forward_parallel()` (`src/MultiHeadAttention.cpp`, the main self-attention
  path), `TextGenerator::softmax()` (`src/TextGenerator.cpp`), two loss/gradient loops in
  `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`, and two in `src/RLHFTrainer.cpp`.
- **Softmax backward (CPU), inline copies of `softmax_derivative`'s formula:**
  `MultiHeadAttention::backward()` and `CrossAttention::backward()`.
- **GELU constants (`0.044715`, `√(2/π) = 0.7978845608`), hardcoded literals:** the forward
  activation and `gelu_backward` kernels in both `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.cu` (CUDA) and
  `src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.cpp` (SYCL), besides `Activation`'s own private constants.

The CPU copies exist for a reason: every `Activation` call allocates a new `Matrix`, and the hot
paths avoid that by working in place or on `std::vector<float>`. So the fix is a shared,
allocation-free primitive, not routing everything through the current API.

Action Items:

- [x] Add an allocation-free row primitive (e.g. `Activation::softmax_row_inplace(float*, int)` and
  a matching backward helper) and switch the CPU copies above to it. Verify with the existing
  attention gradient checks and `chatbotapiTests`/`textgeneratorTests`.
- [x] Move the GELU constants into a small header usable from host C++, CUDA, and SYCL device code
  (plain `constexpr float`s) and include it in all three places.
- [x] Add a CPU-vs-GPU GELU agreement test to the existing GPU test targets (runs only where a GPU
  backend is built).

**Fix (October 26, 2026).**
- **Row primitives.** `Activation` gains allocation-free `softmax_row()`/`softmax_row_inplace()`, `softmax_row_backward()` (the
  vector-Jacobian product) and `log_sum_exp_row()`.
- **CPU sites.** `Activation::softmax()`/`softmax_derivative()` and every inline CPU copy use them:
  - `MultiHeadAttention::forward_parallel()` and `backward()`, `CrossAttention::backward()`;
  - `TextGenerator::softmax()`, both loss loops in `EncoderDecoderModel`;
  - `RLHFTrainer`'s policy gradient, and its log-probabilities through `log_sum_exp_row()`.

  They run the same operations in the same order, so results are bitwise unchanged. The exception is RLHF's log-probability, which
  is mathematically the same with a different rounding order.
- **GELU constants.** They live in the new `src/ActivationConstants.hpp` (`adai::activation::kGeluCoef`/`kSqrt2OverPi`, namespace
  `constexpr float`s). `Activation` and the CUDA and SYCL forward and backward kernels all include it.

Tests:
- `ActivationTD216Test.RowPrimitivesMatchTheMatrixFunctionsBitForBit` and `GeluUsesTheSharedConstants`.
- `MatrixGPUTD216Test.GeluForwardAndBackwardMatchTheCpu`: 64 points in [−4, 4] within 1e-5, on the oneAPI CPU device; the CUDA
  version is compile-checked only.
- The attention gradient checks and `chatbotapiTests`/`textgeneratorTests` still pass.

Location in code: `src/Activation.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/ActivationConstants.hpp`, the CPU sites above, `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.cu`,
`src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.cpp`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/Activation.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/MultiHeadAttention.cpp`, `src/CrossAttention.cpp`
- `src/TextGenerator.cpp`, `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`, `src/RLHFTrainer.cpp`
- `src/gpu/MatrixGPU.cu`, `src/gpu/sycl/MatrixGPU_SYCL.cpp`
- new shared constants header under `src/` or `src/gpu/`

### TD-215: Activation Has Misleading Header Comments and Unchecked Inputs

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 26, 2026 | Core Math / Activation | Code fix (LOW, filed October 8, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [Activation.md](../reference/source/Activation.md).
`src/Activation.{hpp,cpp}` is tagged `stable`, but:

- **Wrong comment, `softmax_derivative`.** The header says the formula is "For cross-entropy
  loss". It's actually the general softmax vector–Jacobian product, correct for any upstream
  gradient. For softmax + cross-entropy the right gradient is `y − one_hot(target)` directly, and
  chaining `softmax_derivative` after it differentiates through softmax twice. The old API doc's
  examples made exactly that mistake (corrected in the October 7 merge), so the comment has
  already misled once.
- **Wrong comment, `leaky_relu_derivative`.** The header says "alpha if x < 0, else 1", which gives
  1 at `x == 0`. The code uses `x > 0 ? 1 : alpha`, so it returns `alpha` at 0, and the tests
  encode the code's behaviour.
- **Undefined behaviour, `softmax` on an empty row.** The row-max step reads `input(i, 0)`
  unconditionally, which is out of bounds when `cols == 0`. No production caller passes empty rows
  today.
- **No shape check, `softmax_derivative`.** `output` and `grad_output` are assumed to have the same
  shape; a smaller `grad_output` reads out of bounds.

Deliberately **not** filed: the derivatives' mixed input conventions (some take the
pre-activation input, `sigmoid_derivative`/`tanh_derivative` take the output). That's by design,
each being the cheapest form, and it's documented per function in Activation.md.

Action Items:

- [x] Fix both header comments to match the code.
- [x] Guard `softmax` against `cols == 0` (return the empty result) and validate shapes in
  `softmax_derivative` (throw `std::invalid_argument`, matching `FeedForward`'s style).
- [x] Add tests for the two new guards.

**Fix (October 26, 2026, with TD-216).**
- **Comments.** `softmax_derivative()`'s comment describes the general softmax vector-Jacobian product and warns against chaining
  it after a softmax + cross-entropy gradient. `leaky_relu_derivative()`'s says 1 if x > 0, else alpha.
- **Guards.** `softmax()` of a matrix with no columns returns the empty result, and `softmax_derivative()` throws
  `std::invalid_argument` on mismatched shapes.

Tests: `ActivationTD215Test.SoftmaxOfAMatrixWithNoColumnsIsEmpty`, `SoftmaxDerivativeRejectsMismatchedShapes`.

Location in code: `src/Activation.hpp` (`softmax_derivative`, `leaky_relu_derivative` doc
comments), `src/Activation.cpp` (`softmax`, `softmax_derivative`); no longer tagged.

Files to Modify:

- `src/Activation.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/activation_test.cpp`
- `docs/development/reference/source/Activation.md` (§11)

### TD-555: Abnormal-Sample Pushes 404 and Flood the Log With Session Re-Registration

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Metrics / Push client and API | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 24, 2026) |

Description:
Filed after the owner reported an excessive number of "session gone, re-registering" warnings in training logs. Verified against the
real `metrics_api_server`.

`MetricsPushClient::report_abnormal_sample()` enqueues `POST /api/sessions/<key>/metrics/abnormal` (`MetricsPushClient.cpp`, ~line 323).
`TrainingMetricsAPI` registers that path only as a `GET` (~line 338), and httplib answers a POST to a GET-only path with 404.
`push_loop()` treats every 404 on a non-lifecycle endpoint as a lost session (~line 490). So for every flagged sample it:
1. logs `MetricsPushClient: session gone on /metrics/abnormal, re-registering`;
2. posts `/start` again, which gets 409 because the session is still live, so the client treats the re-registration as successful;
3. retries the abnormal post, which gets 404 again and is silently dropped.

Reproduced with curl against the real server: `/start` 200, `/metrics/sample` 200, `POST …/metrics/abnormal` 404, the client's
re-`/start` 409, and `GET …/metrics/abnormal` returns `{"abnormal_samples":[],"count":0}`.

Consequences:
- **Log noise:** a warning per flagged sample (up to `max_abnormal_samples` per epoch), which looks like the session keeps being lost when
  it isn't.
- **Lost data:** abnormal samples pushed by remote trainers never reach the metrics server or its DB, so the dashboard's abnormal-sample
  view and `review_abnormal_samples.py`'s server source stay empty.
- **Wasted calls:** three HTTP calls per flagged sample on the push thread.

A genuine metrics-server restart mid-pass does lose every session. Re-registering is correct there, but every queued event also warns
until the session exists again.

Related but distinct: TD-444 (the client ignores every non-404 status), TD-445 (the full registry answers 503, which the trainer turns into
"no metrics for this run"), TD-442 (slow end-of-pass drain when events fail), TD-399 (untruncated abnormal-sample texts).

Action Items:

- [x] Server: add a session-scoped `POST /api/sessions/<key>/metrics/abnormal` handler that records the sample in the session (and the
  metrics DB, like the in-process path), with the TD-526/TD-550 write guard and sensible text-length limits (see TD-399).
- [x] Client: re-register only when the server says the session key is unknown, i.e. a 404 whose body is `Unknown session key`, not on
  any 404. Treat a 404 for a missing route as a client/server version mismatch, logged once per endpoint. Log a real re-registration once
  per outage, not per event.
- [x] Tests:
  - a route test that a pushed abnormal sample is stored and readable via GET;
  - a `MetricsPushClient` test against a real server that one flagged sample logs no re-registration;
  - a restart test where re-registration still recovers after a genuine server restart.
- [x] Check the other push endpoints against the server's POST routes in one test, so a future mismatch fails a test instead of the log.

Location in code: `src/MetricsPushClient.cpp` (`report_abnormal_sample()`, `push_loop()`), `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp` (session
routes, `handle_post_*`).

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Server:** `TrainingMetricsAPI` has `POST /api/sessions/<key>/metrics/abnormal` (`handle_post_abnormal_sample()`), which parses the
  body with nlohmann/json and calls `TrainingMetricsService::flag_abnormal_sample()`. That keeps the sample in memory, writes it to the
  metrics DB and persists it to the JSON file. It truncates `input_text`/`target_text` to 4 KiB on a UTF-8 boundary (marked "…") and
  `reason` to 128 characters (TD-399). A non-object body gets 400 and an unknown session 404 `Unknown session key`. The TD-526/TD-550
  write guard applies.
- **Client:** `MetricsPushClient::attempt_post()` can return the response body. `push_loop()` re-registers only on a 404 whose body
  says `Unknown session key`:
  - it logs that once per outage, reset when an event is accepted again;
  - a 404 without it (a route the server doesn't have) is logged once per endpoint, and those events are dropped without
    re-registering.

Tests:
- `MissingRouteIsNotTreatedAsALostSession` (`metrics_push_client_test.cpp`): two flagged samples against a server without the route give
  one `/start` and two posts. The old client gave three `/start`s and four posts.
- `ReconnectAfter404DoesNotReplayResetBest` now answers with the real server's `Unknown session key` body.
- Route tests (`training_metrics_api_routes_test.cpp`):
  - `PushedAbnormalSampleIsStoredAndReadable`: stored, readable via GET, the 10 KB text truncated, a non-object body 400, an unknown
    session 404. The old server answered the POST with 404.
  - `PushClientAbnormalSampleReachesTheServer`: the real push client against the real API, end to end.

- `EveryPushClientEndpointHasAPostRoute`: drives every `IMetricsReporter` method of a `MetricsPushClient` against a recording server,
  then replays each recorded request against the real API and requires a POST route for it. Against the old server it reports "no POST
  route for /metrics/abnormal", so a future client/server mismatch fails a test instead of flooding the training log.
