### TD-529: Metrics Service Re-Inserts DB Rows When the JSONL File Can't Be Written

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Metrics / Service | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainingMetricsService.cpp` (see [TrainingMetricsService.md](../reference/source/TrainingMetricsService.md)); verified with
the real SQLite backend. `persist_metrics()` inserts the records after `persisted_up_to_` into the database, then opens the JSONL file; if the open fails
it logs a warning and returns **before** advancing `persisted_up_to_`, so the next persist inserts the same rows again plus the new ones. With the JSONL
path in a read-only directory, 30 samples at `persist_every_samples = 10` (3 history records) left 9 rows in `metrics_history` (1 + 2 + 3 + 3): duplicates
grow quadratically while the file is unwritable, and `db-history`, compare and export all return them. (The converse, a DB exception mid-loop advancing
the marker past rows that never reached the DB, is TD-479's drop.)

Action Items:

- [x] Track DB and file progress separately (two markers), advancing each only after its own write succeeds.
- [x] Test persistence with an unwritable JSONL path and with a failing DB.

**Fix (October 25, 2026).** `persist_metrics()` keeps a DB marker (`db_persisted_up_to_`) next to the file marker, and each advances only
past rows its own write accepted: the DB marker one row at a time, so a DB exception leaves the failed row for the next persist, and the
file marker only after the JSONL write and close succeed. `clear_history()` and `trim_history()` adjust both markers. Tests
(`MetricsDatabaseTest.cpp`):
- `UnwritableMetricsFileDoesNotDuplicateDbRows`: with the JSONL path unopenable, 10 samples give 10 DB rows. The old code left 75.
- `FailingDbRowsAreInsertedOnceWhenItRecovers`: rows whose inserts threw are inserted once, by the first persist after the DB recovers.
  The old code dropped them.

Location in code: `src/TrainingMetricsService.cpp` (`persist_metrics()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-529`.

- `src/TrainingMetricsService.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/MetricsDatabaseTest.cpp`

### TD-528: `metrics_api_server` Stop/Start Race, Stale Help Text and Default-Session Slot

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Metrics / Server CLI | Code fix (LOW, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainingMetricsAPIServer.cpp` (see [TrainingMetricsAPIServer.md](../reference/source/TrainingMetricsAPIServer.md)); by inspection
(40 SIGTERMs sent 0–90 ms after start all exited, so the race below wasn't reproduced):
- **Stop/start race:** `TrainingMetricsAPI::stop()` returns early unless `running_` is set, which `start()` does on the server thread; a SIGTERM after the
  handlers are installed but before `start()` runs makes `stop()` a no-op and the shutdown `join()` waits for a server that then runs forever (the
  `mns_server` TD-464 race).
- **Help/banner drift:** `--help` lists `--max-disk-records` (unenforced, TD-440); both endpoint lists (help and startup banner) show the legacy flat
  routes and omit most session-scoped, compare, export, db-history, LeJEPA and admin routes.
- **Default-session slot:** the `0-default` session created at startup counts toward `max_live_sessions`, so trainers get one fewer slot than configured
  (relevant to TD-445).

Action Items:

- [x] Make `stop()` effective before `listen()` (e.g. set `running_` before spawning the thread, or have `start()` check a stop flag first).
- [x] Generate or trim the endpoint lists (point to TRAINING_METRICS_API.md). (`--max-disk-records` is enforced since TD-440's fix, October 25, 2026.)
- [x] Exempt `0-default` from the live-session cap (or stop creating it when no legacy client uses it).

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Stop/start.** `TrainingMetricsAPI::start()` binds, then calls `listen_after_bind()`. It marks itself starting before it checks a
  stop-requested flag. `stop()` sets that flag first, then waits up to 5 s for a start in progress to be listening, the point where
  httplib's `stop()` works. So whichever comes second sees the other, and a stop can no longer be lost. `metrics_api_server` doesn't
  report "failed to start" when the start gave way to a shutdown.
- **Endpoint lists.** `--help` and the startup banner share one short list of the main routes and point to TRAINING_METRICS_API.md.
- **`0-default`.** It doesn't count toward `max_live_sessions` (`counted_sessions_locked()`) and isn't an eviction candidate.

Tests:
- `TrainingMetricsAPIStartStop.StopBeforeStartIsNotLost`;
- `StopRacingStartAlwaysEndsIt`: 50 starts, each stopped at once;
- `MetricsSessionRegistry.DefaultSessionDoesNotTakeALiveSlot`.

All three fail against the old code: start() kept serving, the stop was lost on the first iteration, and `0-default` took a slot.
`NeverStartedPlaceholderIsNotEvicted` and `SessionStartReturns503WhenRegistryIsFull` had pinned `0-default` taking a slot; each now
uses a cap of 1 with one trainer session.

End to end: 30 real `metrics_api_server` starts got a SIGTERM 0–90 ms in. None hung: 15 exited 0 through the handler, and 15 were
ended by SIGTERM's default action before the handler was installed (143).

Location in code: `src/TrainingMetricsAPIServer.cpp` (`print_usage()`, startup banner, shutdown sequence, `0-default` creation); tagged `TODO: See TD-528`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainingMetricsAPIServer.cpp`
- `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp`
- `src/MetricsSessionRegistry.hpp`

### TD-511: `SQLiteMetricsDatabase` Busy Timeout, Transactions and Setup Gaps

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Metrics / SQLite Database | Code fix (LOW, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp`:
- **No busy timeout (verified):** with another connection holding a write transaction, an insert threw `database is locked` after 0.3 ms; callers log
  and drop the row (as TD-304 for `DaemonConfigStore`).
- **Missing directory (verified):** the default `training_sessions/metrics.db` fails to open (`unable to open database file`) if the directory doesn't
  exist.
- **By inspection:** every write is its own autocommit transaction (many tiny transactions for per-step rows); `PRAGMA` and `ALTER TABLE` migration
  errors are ignored; `schema_version` is written but never read.

Action Items:

- [x] `sqlite3_busy_timeout()` (a few seconds); create the parent directory; check PRAGMA/migration results.
- [x] Batch per-step inserts in transactions; use or drop `schema_version`.

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Opening the database.** The constructor creates the parent directory and sets a 5 s busy timeout. A failed `PRAGMA` is logged.
  WAL is a performance setting, so a missing WAL isn't fatal.
- **Migrations.** These are now table-driven, through one `has_column()` probe instead of four copy-pasted blocks. A failed
  `ALTER TABLE` throws and names the statement, where it used to be ignored and left a store missing columns.
- **`schema_version`.** It was dropped, since it was written but never read and the column probes are what decide. Existing
  databases keep the table.
- **Batching.** One autocommit per row measured 316 µs against 4.7 µs batched (WAL, `synchronous=NORMAL`). `IMetricsDatabase` gained
  `insert_metrics_records()` and `insert_gradient_variance_samples()`, one transaction each, all or nothing, and both throw when not
  stored. Both backends implement them. `TrainingMetricsService` writes each persist's history rows as one batch (TD-529's marker
  moves only on success). It buffers the per-step gradient-variance rows and writes them at each persist or every 256 rows. Past
  100,000 pending rows while the DB is down, the oldest are dropped.
- **Flushing.** Buffered rows are flushed before a session is archived and before `set_database()` switches keys, so they never land
  under a key without a session row.

Tests:
- SQLite (`MetricsDatabaseTest.cpp`): `CreatesMissingParentDirectory`, `WriteWaitsForAnotherConnectionsTransaction` (another
  connection holds a write for 300 ms), `BatchInsertsAreAllOrNothing` (a trigger rejects one row and the whole batch rolls back),
  `ServiceBatchesGradientVarianceRows`, `NewDatabaseHasNoUnusedSchemaVersionTable`, `FailedMigrationFailsTheOpen`.
- Postgres, live: `BatchInsertsAreAllOrNothing`.

Five of the SQLite tests failed against the old behavior: unable to open, `database is locked`, a partly stored batch, a
`schema_version` table, and an open that succeeded silently with a column missing. `SchemaBootstrap` no longer expects
`schema_version`. The failing-DB test (TD-529) now fails the batch method.

Location in code: `src/SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp` (constructor, `bootstrap_schema()`, insert methods); tagged `TODO: See TD-511`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp`

Found while tracing `SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp`; verified. SQLite stores a bound NaN as NULL, and `sqlite3_column_double()` reads NULL as 0.0. A

pre-migration rows also read as 0. Infinity round-trips correctly.

Action Items:

**Fix (October 25, 2026).** Every nullable float column read (20 of them, in `query_history()`, `list_sessions()` and `get_session()`)

### TD-509: `SQLiteMetricsDatabase::get_session()` Blocks WAL Checkpoints

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Metrics / SQLite Database | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp` (see [SQLiteMetricsDatabase.md](../reference/source/SQLiteMetricsDatabase.md)); verified.
`get_session()` steps its prepared statement and returns on `SQLITE_ROW` without `sqlite3_reset()`, so the statement keeps a read snapshot open until
the next `get_session()` call. In WAL mode that stops checkpoints: 20,000 `insert_metrics_record()` calls after one found `get_session()` left a
**254 MB WAL and a 4 KB main database** (all data only in the WAL), against a 4 MB WAL and 2.1 MB database without it. In production,
`TrainingMetricsService::restore_from_summary()` calls it at service construction; for an existing key (`0-default` after a restart, or a trainer
re-registering after a `metrics_api_server` restart mid-pass) the snapshot stays open until a service with a new key is constructed, while every write
(including one gradient-variance row per optimizer step) grows the WAL.

Action Items:

- [x] `sqlite3_reset()` the statement after copying the row (and on every return path), e.g. with a scope guard.
- [x] Test that the WAL stays bounded after a found `get_session()`.

Location in code: `src/SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp` (`get_session()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-509`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp`
- `tests/MetricsDatabaseTest.cpp`

**Fix (October 25, 2026).** `get_session()` resets its prepared statement on every return path with a scope guard, so a found row no
longer holds a read snapshot. Test `FoundGetSessionDoesNotBlockWalCheckpoints` (`MetricsDatabaseTest.cpp`): a found `get_session()`,
then 4,000 inserts of a few KB each. The WAL stays under 16 MB and the rows reach the main database. With the old code the WAL grew to
86 MB.

### TD-494: `registry_server` Startup, Lease, Thread-Pool and Parsing Gaps

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Data / Registry Server | Code fix (LOW, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryServer.cpp`:
- **Bind failure exits 0 (verified):** with the port in use, `listen()` returns false and the server logs "registry_server stopped" and exits 0, so
  restart-on-failure never fires.
- **Compact-only JSON (verified):** `{"run_id": "r2"}` (space after the colon) gave `400 run_id required`; incoming strings aren't unescaped and
  `json_int_array()` turns bad values into 0.
- **By inspection:** SIGTERM before `listen()` is lost (as TD-464); claims have no lease, so a crashed trainer's files stay claimed until released by
  hand; fetch downloads run in the request thread and can occupy httplib's pool (8 threads on small hosts), stalling `acquire`/`trained`; upload bodies
  are unbounded and held in memory; `session/next` keys on `model_name|run_id` with `model_name` unvalidated; `/health` is ok even without
  `session_counters.db`.

Action Items:

- [x] Log and exit non-zero when `listen()` fails; handle a stop requested before `listen()`. *(October 24, 2026, with TD-551: exits 1 with the port in the log; a stop requested before `listen()` skips it, though one arriving in the last instant before `listen()` is still lost.)*
- [x] Parse request bodies with the vendored `nlohmann/json` (with TD-453).
- [x] Consider claim leases (expiry + renewal) or an explicit stale-claim report; run fetches off the request pool; cap upload size. *(October 25, 2026, owner choices: leases with renewal, a concurrent-fetch cap, a configurable 2 GiB upload cap.)*

Location in code: `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`main()`, JSON helpers, `handle_session_next()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-494`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`

**Partial fix (October 24, 2026).**
- **Request bodies:** parsed with the vendored nlohmann/json behind the same helper signatures, so none of the ~60 call sites changed.
  Each request thread caches its parse. As a result:
  - whitespace is accepted (`{"run_id": "r2"}` works);
  - escapes are decoded (`\u00e9` becomes `é`, `\"` becomes `"`);
  - only top-level keys match, where a key name inside a value used to match;
  - non-integers, fractions and out-of-range numbers give the default;
  - an integer array with a bad element is treated as not sent instead of carrying a silent 0, since those arrays are aligned with
    `files`;
  - a body that isn't a JSON object gives the defaults.
- **`session/next`:** rejects a `model_name` outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]*` or a `run_id` containing `|` (400), since either could make two
  (model, run) pairs share one counter.
- **`/health`:** reports `{"status":"degraded","session_counters":false}` when `session_counters.db` couldn't be opened. It stays 200,
  since everything but session numbering works and clients treat a failed `/health` as down. The bind-failure item was fixed earlier the
  same day with TD-551.

Live tests: `BodiesWithWhitespaceAreParsed`, `EscapesInBodiesAreDecoded`, `SessionKeysCantCollideThroughAPipe` and
`ReportsTheSessionCounterStore` all fail against the old server; the whole live suite passes (101 tests).

**Still open:**
- claim leases or a stale-claim report;
- running fetch downloads off httplib's request pool;
- capping upload size (the body is still held in memory unbounded);
- the narrow stop-before-`listen()` window.

**Rest of the fix (October 25, 2026).** These follow the owner's choices.
- **Claim leases.**
  - **Server:** each claim records `claimed_unix` (a new 11th column of the pending file, `PendingEntry::claimed_unix`; older files
    and older binaries ignore it). `handle_acquire()` lets another run take an entry whose claim is older than the lease (logged).
    `POST …/renew {"run_id"}` restarts a run's leases and answers `{"renewed":N}`. Acquire responses (both shapes) carry
    `claim_lease_seconds`, release clears the claim time, and the queue shows it.
  - **Setting:** `REGISTRY_CLAIM_LEASE_MINUTES` / `--claim-lease-minutes`, default 30; 0 turns leases off.
  - **Upgrade safety:** a claim with no recorded time has its lease counted from server start, so upgrading releases nothing at once.
  - **Client:** `RemoteTransport` reads the lease and implements `renew_claims()`. `DatasetRegistry::acquire_pending()` starts a
    background renewer that calls it every third of the lease (at least every 5 s), and `mark_trained()`, `release_pending()` and the
    destructor stop it. Every trainer acquire site (`train`, `retrain`, `resume` and so every `trainer_service` pass, LeJEPA) is covered
    without changes. If the claims are gone (renewed 0), it logs an error once.
  - **Result:** a crashed trainer's files return to the pool after the lease, which also helps TD-415's LeJEPA run IDs. A late report
    from the old run is rejected by TD-493's claim check.
- **Fetch concurrency:** at most `REGISTRY_MAX_CONCURRENT_FETCHES` / `--max-concurrent-fetches` (default 2) Gutenberg/HuggingFace
  fetches run at once (`with_fetch_slot()`). Others get 429 with `Retry-After: 30`, leaving the request threads for
  `acquire`/`trained`.
- **Upload size:** `REGISTRY_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` / `--max-upload-mb` (default 2048) sets httplib's payload limit; larger bodies get 413.

Tests:
- `registry_server_args_test.cpp`: defaults, file, CLI precedence and clamping.
- `DatasetRegistryTests.cpp`: the renewer renews during a pass and stops after `mark_trained()`, and stays off without a lease.
- Live:
  - `AcquireReportsTheClaimLease`
  - `ExpiredClaimIsTakenByAnotherRun`: a backdated claim is taken; the old run renews 0 and records nothing.
  - `RenewKeepsAClaim`
  - `ClaimWithoutATimeIsNotReleasedAtOnce`
  - `RemoteTransportReadsTheLeaseAndRenews`
  - The first three fail against the old server.
- TD-491's concurrent-fetch test now retries 429s, as clients should; the server log shows the cap refusing extra fetches.
- The whole live suite passes (106 tests). A server with `--max-upload-mb 1` answered a 2 MiB upload 413 (not stored) and a 1 KB one
  200.

**Still open:** the narrow window where a stop arriving just before `listen()` is lost.

### TD-479: Postgres Backend Drops Each Session's First History Batch on Foreign-Key Violations

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Metrics / Database | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `PostgresMetricsDatabase` and verified on a real PostgreSQL 16 cluster through the real `TrainingMetricsService`. The Postgres schema
has `session_key REFERENCES sessions(key)` on `metrics_history`, `gradient_variance_history`, `generation_quality` and `abnormal_samples` (SQLite doesn't
enforce foreign keys, so its backend is unaffected). `TrainingMetricsService` writes the session row only in `persist_summary()`, which runs **after**
`persist_metrics()` at each periodic persist and at `end_session()`; gradient-variance rows are inserted on every optimizer step from the start. Until the
first persist, every child insert fails with `violates foreign key constraint … Key (session_key)=(…) is not present in table "sessions"`, is retried 3
times by `execute_with_retry()` (~0.5 s of sleeps, blocking the ingest handler) and is dropped. With a fresh key and `persist_every_samples = 5`, the run
ended with the session row present but **0 history rows and 0 gradient-variance rows**. At the defaults every session loses its first persist batch and every
gradient-variance row before the first persist (100 steps or 30 s), and the trainer's per-step `/metrics/advanced` pushes stall 0.5 s each meanwhile; short
sessions can lose everything. The backend's own tests always upsert the session first.

Action Items:

- [x] Upsert the session row in `TrainingMetricsService::start_session()` (and/or run `persist_summary()` before `persist_metrics()`).
- [x] Don't retry constraint violations (check the SQLSTATE class) in `execute_with_retry()`.
- [x] Add a live test that writes child rows through `TrainingMetricsService` without a prior upsert.

**Fix (October 25, 2026).** `start_session()` upserts the session row as soon as a database is attached, so every child row that follows
has its parent. `execute_with_retry()` retries only when the connection is gone: a statement the server rejects on a healthy connection
(a constraint violation, a bad value) fails at once and is logged, instead of sleeping ~0.5 s in retries. Test
`FreshServiceSessionKeepsFirstRowsWithoutRetryStalls` (`postgres_metrics_database_test.cpp`, real PostgreSQL 16): a service with a fresh
key and no upsert first writes 5 samples and 5 gradient-variance rows. All of them are stored, in about 1 s. With the old code it stored
0 history rows and 0 gradient-variance rows and took 5.5 s.

Location in code: `src/TrainingMetricsService.cpp` (`start_session()`, `persist_metrics()`/`persist_summary()` order); `src/PostgresMetricsDatabase.cpp` (child inserts, `execute_with_retry()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-479`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainingMetricsService.cpp`
- `src/PostgresMetricsDatabase.cpp`
- `tests/postgres_metrics_database_test.cpp`

### TD-446: `MetricsSessionRegistry` Sweep-Interval Changes, Miss Logging and Lock-Held I/O

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Metrics / Session Registry | Code fix (LOW, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MetricsSessionRegistry`:
- **Runtime sweep interval (verified).** `set_sweep_interval_seconds()` (reachable via `PUT /admin/config`, no range
  check, TD-306) to ≤ 0 while the thread runs makes `sweep_loop()`'s `wait_for(0)` return immediately, so it spins:
  0.51 CPU-seconds in 2 s with an empty registry, taking the exclusive registry lock each iteration. Going from 0
  (thread never started by the constructor) to a positive value does nothing; a finished session with a 1 s TTL
  was still present after 3 s while `GET /admin/config` reported the new interval.
- **Miss logging (by inspection).** `get_session()` logs a warning plus one line per live key for every unknown key.
  `handle_prometheus_aggregate()` calls it for each session in `list_sessions()`, which includes DB-only completed
  sessions, so each aggregate request logs `(DB sessions) × (1 + live)` lines; any 404 for a completed key does too.
- **I/O under the lock (by inspection).** Eviction archiving (a DB transaction and file renames) runs under the
  exclusive registry lock on every start and sweep; `list_sessions()` queries the DB under the shared lock.
- **Late writes (by inspection).** An evicted service still referenced by an in-flight request can persist after its
  files were renamed, recreating them under the original key, which a new session with that key then shares.

Action Items:

- [x] Reject or clamp intervals ≤ 0 in the setter (or treat as "disabled" without spinning); start the thread when moving from 0 to positive.
- [x] Log misses at debug (or once), without listing every key.
- [x] Do archiving I/O and DB listing outside the registry lock; mark evicted services so late persists are dropped.

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Sweep thread.** It always runs, and an interval ≤ 0 means disabled: the thread waits with no timeout until the interval changes or
  it's stopped. Every `set_sweep_interval_seconds()` bumps a generation counter that wakes the thread to start a fresh wait. A change
  to a shorter interval used to wait out the old one, because `wait_for()`'s predicate only checked for a stop. The destructor sets the
  stop flag under the sweep mutex, so the stop can't be missed.
- **Misses.** `get_session()` logs one debug line.
- **Archiving outside the lock.** Under the exclusive lock, a leaving session is only detached from the map and its key is marked as
  archiving. `archive_detached()` then runs after the lock is released. It calls the new `TrainingMetricsService::retire()` (a final
  flush, then no more file or DB writes), renames the DB rows and files, and releases the key. A start or create for a key being
  archived waits (`archive_cv_`) until that finishes, so a new session never shares the old one's rows. `list_sessions()` queries the
  DB after releasing its shared lock.
- **Late writes.** These are dropped: a retired service has no DB and persistence off.

Tests (`metrics_session_registry_test.cpp`):
- `DisabledSweepIntervalDoesNotSpin`;
- `EnablingSweepLaterStartsSweeping`;
- `ShorterSweepIntervalAppliesImmediately`;
- `EvictedServiceStopsWriting`;
- `ConcurrentKeyReuseWithArchivingOutsideTheLock`: 4 threads × 15 reuses of one key; every run's row lands under exactly one key.

The first four fail against the old registry: 0.28 CPU-seconds in 1 s, no sweeping after enabling, the hour-long wait kept, and a
late persist recreating the old key's file. The registry suite is also clean under ThreadSanitizer (34 tests). TSan needs
`setarch $(uname -m) -R` on this kernel.

**Follow-up (October 25, 2026, found by the stress test above under parallel ctest load).** `start_session_or_conflict()` handed a
never-started placeholder to every caller. Two concurrent starts for one key could share a service; if one finished and a third start
archived it, the other's writes were dropped. Over HTTP, two concurrent `/start` requests could share a session. Fixes:
- A start now claims the session under the registry lock (`SessionEntry::claimed`), and another start before it has run gets the
  conflict (409).
- `POST …/start` parses its body before claiming, so a malformed body can't leave a claim behind.

Tests: `SecondStartBeforeTheFirstHasRunIsRefused`, `MalformedStartBodyDoesNotBlockTheKey`. The stress test passed 30 repeats.

Location in code: `src/MetricsSessionRegistry.hpp` (`sweep_loop()`, `set_sweep_interval_seconds()`, constructor, `get_session()`, `archive_and_remove_locked()`, `list_sessions()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-446`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/MetricsSessionRegistry.hpp`
- `tests/metrics_session_registry_test.cpp`

### TD-445: Finished Metrics Sessions Hold `max_live_sessions` Slots for an Hour

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Metrics / Session Registry | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MetricsSessionRegistry` and verified with the real registry. `start_session_or_conflict()`
(and `create_or_get_session()`) refuse a new key when `sessions_.size() >= max_live_sessions_`, and the map holds
**every** session, including ones that completed normally or went stale. A finished session leaves only when
idle for `completed_ttl_seconds` (3,600 in `config.metrics.conf`) or when its own key is reused; nothing evicts
one to make room. With a cap of 2, two started-and-ended sessions left the registry full and a third key got no
service (the API answers `503 metrics_server_full`).

Every chatbot pass registers a new key (`<session_id>-<host>`; the session number increments per pass), and
`trainer_service` launches the next pass immediately after one that did work; crashed passes' stale sessions count
too. So with the shipped cap of 16, more than 16 passes within an hour fills the server, and later passes log
"training will proceed WITHOUT metrics reporting" until the oldest finished session ages out.

Action Items:

- [x] Before refusing, evict (archive) the least recently updated finished or stale session; count only live sessions against the cap.
- [x] Add a test: cap N, N finished sessions, a new key still starts.
- [x] Update TRAINING_METRICS_API.md's capacity note.

Location in code: `src/MetricsSessionRegistry.hpp` (`start_session_or_conflict()`, `create_or_get_session()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-445`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/MetricsSessionRegistry.hpp`
- `tests/metrics_session_registry_test.cpp`
- `docs/development/TRAINING_METRICS_API.md`

**Fix (October 25, 2026).** `create_or_get_session()` and `start_session_or_conflict()` call a new `make_room_locked()` instead of
refusing at the cap. While the registry is full, it archives (`archive_and_remove_locked()`, so the history stays in the metrics DB as on
key reuse) the least recently updated session that is finished or stale. Live sessions and never-started placeholders, such as the
startup `0-default` alias, are never evicted, so in effect only live sessions count against `max_live_sessions`, and 503 means every
slot is training.

Tests (`metrics_session_registry_test.cpp`):
- `FinishedSessionsDontBlockANewKey`: with a cap of 2 and two finished sessions, a third key starts, the oldest is archived, and
  `create_or_get_session()` does the same.
- `LiveSessionsStillFillTheRegistry`
- `NeverStartedPlaceholderIsNotEvicted`

The first and third fail against the old registry. The existing 503 capacity route test still passes.

Against a real `metrics_api_server --max-live-sessions 3`, with the startup `0-default` and two started-and-ended passes, a third and a
fourth pass both started (200). Two finished sessions were archived "to make room"; before, the third got 503.

### TD-444: `MetricsPushClient` Transport Gaps: No HTTPS, a Connection per Event, Silent Failures

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Metrics / Push Client | Code fix (LOW, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MetricsPushClient`, by inspection:
- **No HTTPS.** `ParsedUrl` recognizes `https://` and switches to port 443, but `attempt_post()` always uses a
  plain `httplib::Client` (no `CPPHTTPLIB_OPENSSL_SUPPORT`), so it sends plain HTTP to a TLS port and
  `start_session()` returns 0; the run trains without metrics. There's no way to add headers (Cloudflare Access
  tokens), so metrics can't go through the tunnel. Today's `config.trainer.conf` uses a LAN `http://` URL.
- **A connection per event.** A new `httplib::Client` (TCP connection) per attempt, including per optimizer step
  for `/metrics/sample` and `/metrics/advanced`.
- **Silent failures.** `push_loop()` ignores every status except 404 (e.g. a 400 for a malformed body, a 503
  "server full"); failures are logged at debug level only.
- **Race and naming.** `reconnect_body_` is written by `start_session()` while the push thread runs (read only after
  a 404); the heartbeat can fire before `start_session()`. `detect_hostname_fragment()` cuts hostnames to 8
  characters, so `ai-machine`/`ai-machine2` share keys (409 retry handles it, with confusing keys).

Action Items:

- [x] Support `https://` (`httplib::SSLClient` with OpenSSL) and configurable extra headers, or reject `https://` with a clear error.
- [x] Reuse one keep-alive client in the push thread.
- [x] Log non-2xx results at warn (rate-limited); guard `reconnect_body_`; consider a longer host fragment or a hash suffix.

**Owner decision (October 25, 2026).** HTTPS through libcurl, which the trainer already uses for FTP. The other options were
rejecting `https://`, or httplib with OpenSSL, which would have to be enabled for every file that includes httplib.

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Transport.** When libcurl is found, CMake links it into `adai_core` and defines `ADAI_METRICS_PUSH_CURL`. `MetricsPushClient` then
  posts through one reused libcurl handle, behind a transport mutex, since `start_session()` posts from the caller's thread. That gives
  real HTTPS with certificate checks and one kept-alive connection. Without libcurl, a reused keep-alive httplib client handles
  `http://`, and `start_session()` refuses an `https://` URL with an error saying why.
- **New keys.** `METRICS_SERVER_HEADERS` holds extra headers ("Name: value" pairs separated by `;`, e.g. a Cloudflare Access service
  token). `METRICS_SERVER_CA_FILE` holds a private CA. Both go in `config.trainer.conf`/env, are mapped through `IncrementalConfig`,
  and are used by both the chatbot and LeJEPA passes. CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_RELAY.md §6c covers pushing through the tunnel.
- **Failures.** A rejected or failed request (4xx other than the handled 404s, 5xx after retries, no connection) is a warning at most
  once a minute, with a count.
- **Smaller fixes.** `reconnect_body_` is mutex-guarded. The heartbeat starts only after `start_session()` succeeds. The host
  fragment in session keys and labels is now up to 32 characters, so `ai-machine` is no longer `ai-machi` and no longer collides
  with `ai-machine2`.

Tests (`metrics_push_client_test.cpp`):
- `ParsesSemicolonSeparatedHeaders`;
- `SendsExtraHeadersOnEveryRequest`;
- `ReusesOneConnection`: 22 requests, one client port;
- `NoHeartbeatBeforeTheSessionStarts`;
- `HttpsWithCaFileAndHeaders`: a real local TLS server (Python, throwaway certificate). It returns 200 with the CA file and header,
  403 without the header, and 0 when the certificate isn't trusted.

Against the old client, `ReusesOneConnection` saw 22 connections for 22 requests, and `NoHeartbeatBeforeTheSessionStarts` saw 7
heartbeats before any session. The other three tests need the new constructor. The API route tests (the real push client against
the real `metrics_api_server`, now over libcurl) still pass.

Location in code: `src/MetricsPushClient.cpp` (`ParsedUrl`, `attempt_post()`, `push_loop()`); `src/MetricsPushClient.hpp` (`detect_hostname_fragment()`, `reconnect_body_`); tagged `TODO: See TD-444`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/MetricsPushClient.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/CMakeLists.txt`

### TD-443: Metrics Push Payloads Send `nan`/`inf`, Round Small Values to 0 and Omit Adaptive Clipping

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Metrics / Push Client | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MetricsPushClient` and verified against a real `metrics_api_server`:
- **Non-finite values.** Payloads are built with `operator<<`, so NaN/infinity are sent as `nan`/`inf` (not
  JSON). The server's hand-written parser (`std::stof`) accepts them and its output re-emits them: after pushing
  an epoch with a NaN loss and an infinite validation loss, `GET /api/sessions/{key}/epochs` returned
  `"epoch_losses":[nan,2.5],"epoch_validation_losses":[inf,2.6]`, which Python's `json` rejects. The epoch view
  breaks exactly when a run diverges. `end_epoch()`'s derived perplexity `exp(loss)` is `inf` above loss ≈ 88.
- **Rounding.** `end_epoch()` uses `std::fixed` (6 decimals): a learning rate of 1e-7 was stored as **0**
  (`"epoch_learning_rates":[0,0]`), as are epoch `gradient_variance`/`weight_update_ratio` below 5e-7 (typical
  update ratios are 1e-4–1e-6). `update_generation_quality_metrics()` also uses `std::fixed` (harmless there).
- **Adaptive clipping never sent.** `update_adaptive_clip_metrics()`/`update_adaptive_clip_epoch()` store into
  `buf_adaptive_clip_*`, which `end_epoch()` never writes, and no server endpoint accepts them; the probe
  session's `epoch_adaptive_clip_thresholds` was `[]`, as it is for every pushed session.

Action Items:

- [x] Serialize floats with a helper that writes non-finite values as `null` (or a documented sentinel) and uses enough significant digits (`std::defaultfloat` with `max_digits10`, or `%.9g`).
- [x] Make the server reject or normalize non-finite input and never emit `nan`/`inf`.
- [x] Add the adaptive-clip fields to the `end_epoch` payload and its server handler.
- [x] Tests for NaN/inf/tiny values and adaptive-clip fields, end to end.

Location in code: `src/MetricsPushClient.cpp` (`end_epoch()`, `update_adaptive_clip_*()`); `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp` (`/epoch/end` parsing); tagged `TODO: See TD-443`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/MetricsPushClient.cpp`
- `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp`
- `tests/metrics_push_client_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Client:** `MetricsPushClient` writes every float through `jnum()`: NaN/infinity as `null`, finite values as the shortest decimal that reads back as the same value (at most 9 digits for a float). That replaces
  `operator<<` and `end_epoch()`'s and `update_generation_quality_metrics()`'s `std::fixed`, so a 1e-7 learning rate stays 1e-7.
  `end_epoch()` also sends `adaptive_clip_threshold`/`adaptive_clip_spikes` (from `update_adaptive_clip_epoch()`).
- **Server input:** `TrainingMetricsAPI`'s 31 `std::stof` field reads go through `parse_json_float()`, which reads `null` as NaN;
  `std::stof` threw on it and failed the whole event. The float-array parser keeps `null` elements in place as NaN, so a layer's norm
  never shifts. `/epoch/end` applies the adaptive-clip fields through `update_adaptive_clip_epoch()`.
- **Server output:** `sanitize_non_finite_json()` runs on every JSON response in the post-routing handler. It rewrites a bare
  `nan`/`-nan`/`inf`/`-inf`/`infinity` value outside strings to `null` and resets `Content-Length` (httplib has set it by then, and an
  unchanged length truncated the reply). It skips compressed bodies. So no endpoint, including future ones and in-process NaNs, emits
  invalid JSON.

Tests (`training_metrics_api_routes_test.cpp`):
- `NonFiniteValuesBecomeNull`: the sanitizer, with strings and escapes left alone.
- `NonFiniteAndTinyEpochValuesRoundTripAsValidJson`: the real push client sends a NaN-loss/infinite-validation-loss epoch, a 1e-7
  learning rate and adaptive clipping. `/epochs` and `/metrics/current` parse as strict JSON (nlohmann), with `null` losses, a 1e-7
  learning rate and `epoch_adaptive_clip_thresholds:[0.5]`.

Against a real `metrics_api_server`, `/epochs`, `/metrics/current`, `/metrics/summary` and `/status` were all valid JSON after a diverged
epoch. The `Content-Length` problem showed up first in the end-to-end test, and the real-server check confirmed it as a 360-byte truncated `/epochs` reply.

### TD-442: `MetricsPushClient::end_session()` Drain Can Delay a Pass's Final Save by an Hour

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Metrics / Push Client | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MetricsPushClient` and verified. `end_session()` enqueues `/end`, sets the stop flag and
joins the push thread, which first sends **every** queued event. Each failing event costs up to 3 attempts plus
1.2 s of back-off (plus `timeout_ms` per attempt when the connection times out rather than being refused). With
the server down (connection refused), 10 queued epoch events plus `/end` took **13.2 s**. If the server goes
away mid-pass the queue fills to 1,024 step events, so the drain takes about 20 minutes (refused) or about 70
minutes (timeouts, default 1 s). The destructor drains the same way.

`IncrementalTrainer` calls `push_client_->end_session()` **before** saving the final checkpoint and calling
`mark_trained()`, so a metrics outage near the end of a chatbot pass delays its results by that long, and a stop
in that window (`systemctl stop`, `trainer_service`'s 10 s SIGKILL escalation, a GPU-driver crash) loses the
final save and leaves the files claimed. (`run_lejepa_training_pass()` saves first and is only delayed.)

Action Items:

- [x] Bound the drain: a deadline for `end_session()`, and once stopping, drop `Sample` events and skip retries/back-off.
- [x] In `IncrementalTrainer`, save the final checkpoint and `mark_trained()` before `end_session()`.
- [x] Add a test: `end_session()` with the server down returns within the deadline.

Location in code: `src/MetricsPushClient.cpp` (`end_session()`, `push_loop()`); `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`end_session()` before the final save); tagged `TODO: See TD-442`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/MetricsPushClient.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
- `tests/metrics_push_client_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Bounded drain:** `MetricsPushClient` has a drain deadline (`set_drain_timeout_ms()`, default 10 s), set when `end_session()` or the
  destructor stops the push thread. While draining:
  - queued `Sample` (per-step) events are dropped;
  - every remaining event, re-registration included, gets one attempt with no back-off;
  - heartbeats stop;
  - at the deadline everything still queued is dropped except one attempt at `/end` (logged).

  Epoch and session events queued before the stop are still sent while there's time.
- **Order in `IncrementalTrainer::run_training()`:** `end_session()` is now its last step, after the final checkpoint save, the session
  finalize and the MNS candidate report. Before, it came first. `mark_trained()` runs in the callers after `run_training()` returns, so
  it waits at most the drain deadline instead of up to an hour. The trainer's reporter pointer is also cleared there instead of being left
  pointing at the destroyed client.

Tests (`metrics_push_client_test.cpp`):
- `EndSessionWithTheServerDownReturnsWithinTheDeadline`: 41 queued events with nothing listening, a 1 s deadline, and `end_session()`
  returned in about 1.2 s. The old client took 50.45 s for the same queue.
- `EndSessionDrainsAllQueuedEventsBeforeJoin` now requires every epoch and session event and allows the step samples queued at the stop
  to be dropped.

### TD-441: `IMetricsDatabase` Contract Gaps: Step Counter, `limit` Order, Unbounded Reads

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Metrics / Database | Code fix (LOW, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MetricsDatabase`, by inspection:
- **Step counter restarts.** `insert_gradient_variance_sample()`'s `step` is `TrainingMetricsService`'s
  `gradient_variance_step_counter_`, which starts at 0 whenever a session's service is recreated (server
  restart, restored session), giving duplicate `(session_key, step)` pairs; the interface comment calls it
  "monotonic".
- **`limit` keeps the oldest rows.** Both backends' `query_history()` sort `recorded_at ASC` then apply
  `LIMIT`, so `GET .../metrics/db-history?limit=500` returns a run's first 500 records, not the latest.
- **Unbounded reads.** `TrainingMetricsAPI`'s compare and export call `query_history()` with no limit,
  materializing whole histories per request; the interface has no paging.
- **Undocumented contract.** Throwing on error, thread safety, ascending order, `limit = 0` = all, and the
  `FLT_MAX` "no best loss" sentinel are only discoverable from the implementations;
  `MetricsDatabaseFactory::create()` is declared here but defined in `SQLiteMetricsDatabase.cpp`.

Action Items:

- [x] Seed the step counter from the DB (`MAX(step)`) on restore, or drop the "monotonic" claim.
- [x] Add an order/"latest N" option to `query_history()` and use it for `db-history`; document `limit`.
- [x] Cap or page compare/export reads; document the interface contract; move the factory to its own file.

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Step counter.** The new `IMetricsDatabase::max_gradient_variance_step()` returns `COALESCE(MAX(step), 0)`.
  `TrainingMetricsService::set_database()` seeds the counter from it, so a service attaching to a session with stored rows
  continues its numbering.
- **`limit`.** It now keeps the newest rows in both backends (`ORDER BY recorded_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT n`, reversed to oldest
  first). Nothing used the old meaning; `db-history?limit=N` now returns the latest N.
- **Read bounds.** Export reads the newest 200,000 rows, and its JSON says `"truncated"` when older ones were left out. Compare takes
  at most 16 sessions, each from its newest 200,000 rows. TD-440's per-session cap normally keeps a session well under that.
- **Contract and factory.** The interface contract (thread safety, errors per backend, ordering, `limit`, sentinels, retention) is
  documented at the top of `IMetricsDatabase`. The factory and `plan_row_cap()` moved to the new `src/MetricsDatabase.cpp`.

Tests:
- `LimitClause` now expects samples 15–19 of 20;
- `GradientVarianceStepsContinueAcrossServiceInstances`;
- `CompareRefusesTooManySessions`;
- `ExportReportsTruncationAndDbHistoryLimitKeepsNewest`;
- Postgres, live: `LimitKeepsNewestAndMaxStep`.

With the old ordering and no seeding, the first, second and fourth fail: samples 0–4, duplicate steps 1–5, and the first three
rows.

### TD-440: Metrics Storage Has No Retention and `max_records_on_disk` Is Never Applied

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Metrics / Database | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `MetricsDatabase` and verified by search:
- **No retention.** `IMetricsDatabase` has no delete/prune operation, and neither `SQLiteMetricsDatabase`
  nor `PostgresMetricsDatabase` deletes rows except while renaming them in `archive_session()`. The JSONL
  file (`TrainingMetricsService::persist_metrics()`, `std::ios::app`) is never rotated or trimmed.
- **A dead setting.** `MetricsServiceConfig::max_records_on_disk` (default 100,000; `--max-disk-records`,
  `config.metrics.conf`, admin-mutable via `PUT /admin/config`, reported by `GET /admin/config`) is read by
  no persistence code; only `max_records_in_memory` is enforced (on the in-memory ring buffer).
  `compress_old_records` is likewise never read. TRAINING_METRICS_API.md documents "Max records on disk" as
  a real limit.
- **Write-only tables.** `gradient_variance_history` (one row per optimizer step per session, unthrottled)
  and `generation_quality` have insert methods but no query method; no C++ code or repository tool reads
  them (`tools/abnormal_review/` reads only `abnormal_samples`). The dashboards use the in-memory snapshot.

So the metrics host's DB and JSONL grow for as long as `metrics_api_server` runs, fastest in the table
nothing reads.

Action Items:

- [x] Owner decision: retention policy (per-session row cap, age, or both) and whether `gradient_variance_history`/`generation_quality` get readers (an API endpoint) or are dropped/throttled.
- [x] Add a prune operation to `IMetricsDatabase` (both backends) and apply `max_records_on_disk` (per session) on persist or in the registry sweep; trim or rotate the JSONL to match.
- [x] Remove `compress_old_records` or implement it; correct TRAINING_METRICS_API.md.

**Owner decision (October 25, 2026).** Both a per-session row cap and an age limit; read endpoints for the two write-only tables; the
JSONL rotated by size.

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Row cap.** `max_records_on_disk` (default 100,000) is enforced per session on `metrics_history` and `gradient_variance_history`.
  After each DB persist, `TrainingMetricsService` calls the new `IMetricsDatabase::cap_session_rows()`. Once a table exceeds the
  cap, it is trimmed to 3/4 of the cap by deleting every second row among the oldest (`plan_row_cap()`). Repeated trims make older
  history progressively sparser while the start and the recent end of the run stay. Only when more than half the rows must go are the
  oldest deleted.
- **Age limit.** New `METRICS_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 90, 0 = forever; `--retention-days`). Once an hour the registry sweep
  (`MetricsSessionRegistry::apply_retention()`) deletes every session not updated for that long, with all its rows, through the new
  `delete_sessions_updated_before()` (children first, one transaction). It also deletes archived session files older than the
  cutoff.
- **Readers.** `query_gradient_variance()`/`query_generation_quality()`, served as `GET …/metrics/db-gradient-variance[?limit=N]` and
  `…/metrics/db-generation-quality`.
- **JSONL rotation.** New `METRICS_FILE_MAX_MB` (100) and `METRICS_FILE_BACKUPS` (3), with matching flags. A session's file moves to
  `<file>.1` at the limit, and archiving renames the backups with the session.
- **Admin and docs.** All four settings are admin-mutable through `PUT /admin/config`. `compress_old_records` was removed.
  TRAINING_METRICS_API.md documents the routes and the retention behavior.

Tests (all new):
- SQLite: `CapSessionRowsThinsOldestAndKeepsNewest`, `DeleteSessionsUpdatedBeforeRemovesAllTheirRows`,
  `GradientVarianceAndGenerationQualityReadBack`, `ServiceKeepsSessionRowsUnderMaxRecordsOnDisk`,
  `MetricsFileRotatesAtSizeAndKeepsBackups`, `MetricsRowCapPlan.ThinsOldestOrDeletesOldest`.
- Registry: `RetentionDeletesOldSessionsAndArchivedFiles`, `EvictionArchivesRotatedMetricsBackups`.
- Postgres, live: `RetentionAndReadersWork`.
- API: `GradientVarianceAndGenerationQualityAreReadable`, `RetentionSettingsAreAdminMutable`.
- Args: `RetentionFlagsAreApplied`, plus the seed and override tests extended.

End to end: two real `metrics_api_server`s each received 3,000 samples and gradient-variance pushes with `--max-disk-records 50`. The
new binary kept 49 rows in each table, including samples 1 and 3,000. The old binary kept 3,000 in each. A 6,000-sample run with
`--metrics-file-max-mb 1` rotated the JSONL to `.1` at 1 MB.

Location in code: `src/MetricsDatabase.hpp` (`IMetricsDatabase`); `src/TrainingMetricsService.hpp` (`max_records_on_disk`, `compress_old_records`); `src/TrainingMetricsService.cpp` (JSONL append); tagged `TODO: See TD-440`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/MetricsDatabase.hpp`
- `src/SQLiteMetricsDatabase.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/PostgresMetricsDatabase.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/TrainingMetricsService.{hpp,cpp}`
- `docs/development/TRAINING_METRICS_API.md`
