### TD-378: BLEU Smoothing Inflates Unrelated Answers and Zeroes Correct Short Ones

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Metrics / GenerationQuality | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 12, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `GenerationQualityMetrics` and verified against a textbook (Papineni et al.)
BLEU. `compute_corpus_bleu()` uses `(matches + 1) / (hypothesis n-grams + 1)` for **every** order,
including unigrams, and a fixed `log = -20` when the hypothesis has no n-grams of some order. The
header labels this "add-1 smoothing (Lin & Och 2004, method 1)", but Lin & Och's add-one smoothing
applies only to n ≥ 2. Single-pair results:

| Case | This code BLEU-4 | Textbook BLEU-4 |
|---|---|---|
| Unrelated 5-word answer (no words in common) | 0.230 (BLEU-1 0.167) | 0 |
| Same 5 words, scrambled | 0.359 | 0 |
| Exactly correct 3-word answer | 0.0067 | 0 (no 4-grams) |

So an unrelated answer's BLEU-4 exceeds its BLEU-1, and a correct short reply scores far below an
unrelated long one. The per-epoch metric (10 pairs by default) is less distorted (0.015 for fully
unrelated output) but still biased against short targets, which dominate conversational data such as
daily_dialog. The per-sample backfill (TD-273) gets the full sentence-level distortion. The tests
(`CompletelyDifferentHypothesisScoresNearZero`, `BLEU1AtLeastBLEU2AtLeastBLEU4`) pass only on their
particular examples.

Action Items:

- [x] Use unsmoothed corpus BLEU for the per-epoch metric, or a documented standard smoothing (Chen & Cherry 2014 method 1 — epsilon for zero-match orders — or add-1 for n ≥ 2 only); keep sentence-level BLEU only behind an explicitly smoothed function.
- [x] Handle hypotheses shorter than `n` the standard way, and fix the header's citation.
- [x] Add tests against known reference values (for example, sacreBLEU/NLTK outputs recorded as constants): unrelated → 0, scrambled → low, short exact match.

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Per-epoch score.** `evaluate()` reports unsmoothed corpus BLEU (Papineni et al.). Matches and n-gram counts are summed over every
  pair, and an order with no matches makes the score 0. For a single pair, the textbook value of a 3-word answer's BLEU-4 is 0. With
  the default 10 pairs that only happens when the model gets no 4-gram right anywhere.
- **Per-sample score.** The new `sentence_bleu()` is the explicitly smoothed single-pair score, used by the per-sample backfill
  (TD-273). It follows sacreBLEU's sentence settings: Chen & Cherry (2014) method 1 (an order with no matches counts 0.1 matches,
  `smooth_method="floor"`) and effective order (orders the hypothesis is too short for are left out). An exactly correct 3-word answer
  scores 1, and 5 unrelated words score 0.025.
- The header's citation is corrected.

Tests (`generation_quality_test.cpp`). sacreBLEU and NLTK aren't installed here, so the reference values come from an independent
Python implementation of the published formulas, recorded as constants. The partial-match value, 0.537285, matches a hand
calculation.
- Corpus: an unrelated answer → 0, scrambled words → BLEU-4 0 (BLEU-1 1), partial match, brevity penalty, a corpus summed across
  pairs, and a short exact match (BLEU-2 1, BLEU-4 0).
- Sentence: reference values, and a correct short answer outranking an unrelated long one.

The old code fails 5 of the 6 new corpus tests: unrelated BLEU-4 0.188, scrambled 0.359, short exact match 0.0067.
`IdenticalReferenceShouldScoreOne` now expects exactly 1.

Per-epoch BLEU-4 values from before this fix aren't comparable with later ones. The old numbers were inflated for poor outputs and
deflated for short correct ones.

**Superseded (October 25, 2026, TD-380).** The scores now follow sacreBLEU's defaults (13a tokens, `exp` smoothing) on 0–100. Corpus
BLEU is no longer unsmoothed, and `sentence_bleu()` uses `exp` instead of floor smoothing. The fix against the add-1 distortion
stands.

Location in code: `src/GenerationQualityMetrics.cpp` (`compute_corpus_bleu()`), `src/GenerationQualityMetrics.hpp` (class comment); tagged `TODO: See TD-378`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/GenerationQualityMetrics.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/generation_quality_test.cpp`

### TD-261: `generate_response_with_strategy()` Forces Beam Search Whenever `num_beams > 1`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 25, 2026 | Core Model / Generation | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-260. In `EncoderDecoderModel::generate_response_with_strategy()`, the beam
branch is taken when `normalized_strategy == "beam" || num_beams > 1`, and it returns before the
`greedy`/`sampling`/`topk`/`nucleus` branches. The comment just above says those explicit
strategies "are unaffected", but the code order contradicts it. So any caller passing
`num_beams > 1` gets beam search **whatever strategy it asked for**:

- `chatbot_gui` always passes its Beam Width spin box (default **5**), so choosing Nucleus, Top-k,
  Greedy or Sampling still runs beam search unless the user sets Beam Width to 1.
- `RLHFTrainer` (≈ line 177) omits `num_beams`, so it gets the header default of **4**: its
  configured `generation_strategy` (e.g. sampling, which policy-gradient training relies on for
  diverse rollouts) is silently replaced by beam search.
- RAG passes `num_beams` from its config (default 1), so it's unaffected.

The `num_beams > 1` guard exists for a real reason: an unrecognized strategy falls through to
`TextGenerator::generate()`, which itself routes to beam search when `num_beams > 1`, and must not
be handed the KV-cached `model_fn`.

Action Items:

- [x] Take the beam branch only for `strategy == "beam"`, or for an *unrecognized* strategy with `num_beams > 1` (preserving the cache-safety guard); explicit greedy/sampling/topk/nucleus must ignore `num_beams`.
- [x] Change the header default `num_beams = 4` to 1 (in both overloads) so omitted arguments don't imply beam search.
- [x] `chatbot_gui`: pass `beam_width` only when the strategy is beam (otherwise 1). `RLHFTrainer`: pass `num_beams` explicitly.
- [x] Fix the misleading comment; add tests that each explicit strategy with `num_beams = 5` does not run beam search.

**Fix (October 25, 2026).**
- **Dispatch.** `generate_response_with_strategy()` decides `use_beam` up front: true for `"beam"`, or for an unrecognized strategy
  with `num_beams > 1`, which keeps the guard against handing the KV-cached `model_fn` to beam search. Explicit
  greedy/sampling/topk/nucleus ignore `num_beams`.
- **Stored width.** The generator's stored config gets `num_beams` only when beam search runs, otherwise 1. A nucleus call with
  `num_beams = 5` used to leave 5 behind, and a later plain `generate_response()` then switched to beam search.
- **Defaults and callers.** Both overloads, CPU and GPU, default `num_beams` to 1; the GPU dispatch already ignored `num_beams` for
  explicit strategies. `chatbot_gui` passes its Beam Width only for `"beam"`. `RLHFTrainer` passes `num_beams = 1` explicitly
  (TD-500's deterministic-rollout part).

Test `ExplicitStrategiesIgnoreNumBeams` (`encoderdecoder_test.cpp`):
- six sampling/topk/nucleus calls with `num_beams = 5` give more than one distinct answer, and leave no beam width stored;
- greedy with 5 equals greedy with 1;
- `"beam"` and an unrecognized strategy still store their width.

Against the old code all three sampling strategies ran deterministic beam search (one answer each) and left 5 behind.
`GenerateWithStrategySyncsGeneratorConfig` now expects 1 after a `"topk"` call. The RLHF tests pass 3/3 with random rollouts.

Location in code: `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}` (`generate_response_with_strategy()`), `src/ChatbotGUI.cpp` (`generateResponse()`), `src/RLHFTrainer.cpp`; tagged `TODO: See TD-261`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/ChatbotGUI.cpp`
- `src/RLHFTrainer.cpp`
- `tests/encoderdecoder_test.cpp`

### TD-551: A Second Daemon Instance Silently Shares the Port

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 24, 2026 | Services / HTTP | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 24, 2026) |

Description:
Filed while fixing TD-491, verified with `registry_server`. cpp-httplib's `default_socket_options` sets `SO_REUSEPORT` as well as
`SO_REUSEADDR` (`external/cpp-httplib/httplib.h`, around line 1867). A second instance started on a port that's already in use
therefore binds without error and logs a normal startup. The kernel then spreads new connections across both processes.

A stale test `registry_server` left on port 18491 took part of eight concurrent fetches. Each process had its own cursor locks and its
own in-memory group mutexes over the same data directory, so two requests both served row 0, and both reported `added:true` into
pending lists that overwrote each other.

The same applies to every httplib daemon (`registry_server`, `mns_server`, `metrics_api_server`, `chatbot_api_server`,
`trainer_service`), for example a manual start next to the systemd unit, or an overlapping restart. TD-494's "bind failure exits 0" is
the other half: the start doesn't fail at all.

Action Items:

- [x] Give every server socket options without `SO_REUSEPORT` (`set_socket_options()` with `SO_REUSEADDR` only, in one shared helper),
  so a second instance fails to bind.
- [x] Make a failed bind exit non-zero with a clear message (TD-494 for `registry_server`; check the other daemons).
- [x] Test: a second instance on the same port must fail.

Location in code: every `httplib::Server` (`RegistryServer.cpp`, `ModelNameService.cpp`, `TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp`, `ChatbotAPI.cpp`,
`TrainerServiceProxy.cpp`, `TrainerAdminAPI.cpp`).

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** `src/HttpListenSocket.hpp` adds `use_exclusive_listen_port()`, a header template over the httplib server
type. It replaces httplib's POSIX socket options (`SO_REUSEPORT` only) with `SO_REUSEADDR` alone, which still allows an immediate
restart over TIME_WAIT connections but makes a second listener's bind fail. Windows is unchanged; httplib already sets
`SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` there.

It's installed next to the TD-550 write guard in every server: `registry_server`, `ModelNameService`, `TrainingMetricsAPI`, `ChatbotAPI`,
`TrainerServiceProxy` and the child's `TrainerAdminAPI`.

`registry_server` was the only daemon that ignored a failed `listen()` (TD-494). It now logs the port and exits 1. It also skips
`listen()` when a stop was already requested; one arriving in the narrow window just before `listen()` is still lost. The other daemons
already treated a failed start as an error.

Verified against the real binaries by starting a second instance on the port of a running one:
- **Second instance:** `registry_server`, `mns_server`, `metrics_api_server` and `chatbot_api_server` exit 1. `trainer_service` logs
  "admin proxy failed to bind" and keeps supervising without an admin port, its documented behavior for an admin bind failure.
  Before, it would have shared the admin port, so a pause reached either supervisor at random. Two supervisors still both launch
  passes; the registry's claims keep them on different files.
- **First instance:** answers `/health` in every case.

Tests: `http_listen_socket_test.cpp` (4):
- with httplib's defaults a second server binds the same port (the problem);
- with the helper a second server is refused, even one with default options;
- the port can be bound again right after the server stops.

### TD-550: Registry, MNS and Other Daemons Accept Cross-Origin Writes

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 24, 2026 | Services / HTTP | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 24, 2026) |

Description:
Filed while fixing TD-526, verified against the real `registry_server`. Its routes parse request bodies whatever their `Content-Type`,
and there's no authentication. A web page open in a browser on the LAN can therefore send a CORS "simple" request (`text/plain`, no
preflight) that the server executes:
- `POST /registry/g1/pending/add` with `Origin: http://evil.example` and `Content-Type: text/plain` returned `{"added":true}`;
- the page can't read the reply (no CORS headers), but the write happens. Delete, assign, requeue and fetch routes are reachable the
  same way.

By inspection, the same applies to `mns_server` (state, role and registration writes), `chatbot_api_server` and `trainer_service`'s
admin API (pause/resume/checkpoint, when enabled). This matters most behind the Cloudflare tunnels (`*.kerfbit.dev`), where an
operator's authenticated browser session carries the Access cookie.

Action Items:

- [x] Move TD-526's write guard into one shared helper (refuse writes whose `Origin` isn't listed with 403, and preflight-free
  `Content-Type`s with 415) and install it in `registry_server`, `mns_server`, `chatbot_api_server` and `TrainerServiceProxy`.
- [x] Check the Android ops dashboard and `dataset_manager`/`mns_cli` still work (they send no `Origin`). `upload` takes a raw body
  sent as `application/octet-stream` by both `RegistryTransport` and the Android app, so the 415 rule doesn't affect it.

Location in code: `src/RegistryServer.cpp`, `src/ModelNameServiceServer.cpp`, `src/ChatbotAPIServer.cpp`/`src/ChatbotAPI.cpp`,
`src/TrainerServiceProxy.cpp`; the guard to share is in `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp` (pre-routing handler).

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** The rule now lives in one component, `src/BrowserWriteGuard.{hpp,cpp}` (`adai_core`):
- **Refused writes** (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE): an `Origin` that isn't listed gets 403. A preflight-free `Content-Type` (`text/plain`,
  form-encoded, multipart) gets 415.
- **Installer:** `install_browser_write_guard()`, a header template over the httplib server type, so the header needn't include httplib.
  It sets the server's pre-routing handler, logs each refusal and answers `{"error":…}`.
- **Where it's installed:** `registry_server`, `mns_server` (`ModelNameService`), `chatbot_api_server` (`ChatbotAPI`), `trainer_service`
  (`TrainerServiceProxy`) and the child's loopback `TrainerAdminAPI`, which a browser on the same host can reach. None of these get an
  allow-list, since nothing browser-based writes to them.
- **Metrics API:** `TrainingMetricsAPI` now uses the same component with its TD-526 allow-list, replacing its own copy.

Clients without an `Origin` keep working:
- `RemoteTransport`/`dataset_manager`, `mns_cli`, the trainer's clients, and the Android app (Retrofit JSON; `application/octet-stream`
  uploads) are unaffected.
- Every documented `curl` write already sets `application/json`. A bare `curl -d` (form-encoded) now gets 415.

Verified against the real binaries with a cross-origin `text/plain` write from `Origin: http://evil.example`. Each one returned 403,
logged the refusal and changed nothing:
- **`registry_server`:** `pending/add` returned `{"added":true}` before the fix. A form-encoded body without `Origin` got 415, and JSON
  still got 200.
- **`mns_server`:** `POST /models` was refused and the model wasn't registered; JSON still registers (201).
- **`trainer_service`:** `POST /admin/pause` was refused and `supervisor_paused` stayed false; without `Origin` it got 202 and paused.
- **`chatbot_api_server`:** `POST /clear-session` was refused; JSON got 200, and a GET with `Origin` got 200.

Tests: `browser_write_guard_test.cpp` (7: the decision table, JSON escaping, and a real `httplib::Server` where refused writes never reach
the route), plus TD-526's route tests through the shared code.

### TD-549: FTPS Data Channel Doesn't Require TLS Session Reuse

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 24, 2026 | Data / FtpDataServer | Code fix (LOW, filed October 21, 2026) |

Description:
Filed while fixing TD-372. The data connection is now accepted only from the control connection's client IP, but under `PROT P`
any TLS client from that address still passes the data-channel handshake. A process on the same host as the trainer (or behind the
same NAT) could still race for the file. vsftpd's `require_ssl_reuse` closes this by requiring the data channel to resume the
control channel's TLS session. It was left out of TD-372 because session reuse interacts badly with some TLS 1.3 clients (session
tickets), and libcurl, the trainer's client, would need verifying on both sides first.

Action Items:

- [x] Enable the server session cache with a session-id context. After the data-channel `SSL_accept()`, require
  `SSL_session_reused()` and the control channel's session; refuse with 425/522 otherwise.
- [x] Verify libcurl (`CURLOPT_SSL_SESSIONID_CACHE`, on by default) still downloads under TLS 1.2 and 1.3.

Location in code: `src/FtpDataServer.hpp` (`cmd_retr()`).

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** A `PROT P` data connection must resume its own control connection's TLS session, or `RETR` answers 522
and sends nothing.
- **Why a token:** checking `SSL_session_reused()` alone isn't enough, because another client on the same host could resume a session
  from its own control connection.
- **The token:** each control connection gets a random 16-byte token, set as the SSL object's app data before its handshake.
- **Where it's carried:** `SSL_CTX_set_session_ticket_cb()` writes the token into every session ticket the server issues
  (`SSL_SESSION_set1_ticket_appdata()`), for both TLS 1.3 and TLS 1.2 tickets. It's also set on the control session itself, for TLS 1.2
  session-ID resumption from the server cache (`SSL_CTX_set_session_id_context()` + `SSL_SESS_CACHE_SERVER`).
- **The check:** after the data channel's `SSL_accept()`, `data_session_matches()` requires a resumed session whose ticket appdata equals
  the control connection's token (constant-time compare). The data connection issues no tickets of its own.
- **Compatibility:** OpenSSL ≥ 1.1.1 (the ticket appdata API).

Tests (`FtpDataServerTests.cpp`, an OpenSSL client against a real server, under both TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3):
- `ResumingTheControlSessionDownloads`
- `FreshTlsSessionOnTheDataConnectionIsRefused`
- `AnotherControlConnectionsSessionIsRefused`: the TD-549 threat.

On the old server the two refusal tests fail under both versions; the file was delivered.

libcurl, the trainer's client, still works. `DataTransportFtpsTests` (TLS 1.3) pass. `curl --tlsv1.2 --tls-max 1.2` and `--tlsv1.3`
against a real FTPS `registry_server` (token from `acquire`) both downloaded the file byte for byte, with no refusal logged.

### TD-526: Metrics API Accepts Cross-Origin Writes and Reads From Any Web Page

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 24, 2026 | Metrics / API | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp` (see [TrainingMetricsAPI.md](../reference/source/TrainingMetricsAPI.md)); verified against the real
`metrics_api_server`. A post-routing handler adds `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` to every response, there is no authentication, and push/control
routes parse any body regardless of `Content-Type`. A `POST` with `Content-Type: text/plain` is a CORS simple request that browsers send without a
preflight. With `Origin: http://evil.example`: `POST /api/sessions/{key}/control/clear` → 200 "Metrics history cleared"; `POST …/metrics/sample`
`{"sample":5,"loss":99.0}` → 200, recorded. Any web page opened in a browser on the LAN (or by a Cloudflare-Access-authenticated operator for
`metrics.kerfbit.dev`) can therefore clear histories, inject fake metrics or end sessions (`PUT /admin/config` needs a preflight and is blocked), and, because the wildcard
origin permits reading responses, read every endpoint, including `metrics/abnormal`'s raw `input_text`/`target_text`. TRAINING_METRICS_API.md's
"add a reverse proxy" advice doesn't help against a browser already inside it.

Action Items:

- [x] Replace the wildcard with a configured allow-list of dashboard origins (or no CORS for write routes).
- [x] Reject write/control requests whose `Content-Type` isn't `application/json` (forcing a preflight); consider a shared token for writes.
- [x] Update TRAINING_METRICS_API.md's security notes; check `mns_server`/`registry_server` for the same exposure.

Location in code: `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp` (post-routing CORS handler, `OPTIONS` route, push/control routes); tagged `TODO: See TD-526`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainingMetricsAPI.cpp`
- `docs/development/TRAINING_METRICS_API.md`
- `tests/training_metrics_api_routes_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** `TrainingMetricsAPI` takes an allow-list of browser origins: `METRICS_API_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` in
`config.metrics.conf` or the environment, or `--cors-allowed-origins`. **Owner decision: empty by default.** Browsers always send
`Origin` on cross-origin requests and on POSTs; the trainer, the Android app and `curl` don't, and are unaffected.
- **Writes** (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE): refused with 403 if they carry an `Origin` that isn't explicitly listed, and with 415 if their
  `Content-Type` is one a browser may send without a preflight (`text/plain`, form-encoded, multipart). This runs in a pre-routing
  handler, so no write route runs.
- **Responses:** carry `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` only for a listed origin. A `*` entry lets any origin read, never write.
  `Vary: Origin` is set whenever an `Origin` came in.
- **Preflights:** answered (204, methods GET/POST/PUT) only for a listed origin; otherwise 403 with no CORS headers.
- **Tizen app:** it reads with `fetch(…, {mode: 'cors'})`. If its runtime enforces CORS, its origin must be listed. Its exact `Origin`
  header can't be checked without the device.

Tests (`training_metrics_api_routes_test.cpp`, against the real HTTP server):
- `CrossOriginTextPlainWriteIsRefusedAndNotApplied`: the verified attack; the injected sample isn't recorded.
- `SimpleContentTypeWriteIsRefusedWithoutOrigin`
- `NonBrowserJsonWriteStillWorks`: the trainer's path.
- `DefaultGrantsNoCrossOriginReadsOrPreflights`
- `ListedOriginReadsAndWrites`
- `WildcardGrantsReadsButNotWrites`

**Same exposure elsewhere:** the other daemons send no CORS headers, so responses can't be read, but `registry_server` executed a
cross-origin `text/plain` `pending/add` (verified). Filed as TD-550.

### TD-493: Registry `trained` Ignores Claim Ownership and Records Each Path Once

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 24, 2026 | Data / Registry Server | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryServer.cpp`; verified. `handle_trained()` adds a registry record for every listed file not already in the registry,
regardless of `run_id`; only the pending removal checks the claim. With `d.jsonl` claimed by `r1`, `trained` from run `other` returned `trained: 1` and
recorded it, while the entry stayed pending and claimed by `r1`; `r1`'s own `trained` then returned `trained: 0` (path already recorded) but removed the
pending entry, so `r1`'s sample count and `model_id` were never recorded. Because the registry is deduplicated by bare path, a file re-queued and trained
again is never recorded again either (TD-333 covers segments).

Action Items:

- [x] Record a file only when it is pending and claimed by the calling `run_id` (or an explicit force), and report rejected files.
- [x] Key registry records by (path, segment, run) or append history instead of skipping already-recorded paths.

Location in code: `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`handle_trained()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-493`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `src/RegistryTransport.cpp` (`LocalTransport` equivalent)
- `tests/dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** A report with a `run_id` records a unit only when that run holds the unit's claim: a pending entry for the
path, or exactly that segment in exact mode, with the same `run_id`.
- **Server (`handle_trained()`):** a unit reported by a run that doesn't hold its claim isn't recorded, and the reply lists it in a new
  `"rejected"` array (`{"trained":N,"rejected":[…]}`). The pending removal was already claim-checked and is unchanged.
- **Retraining:** a claimed unit is recorded even when an earlier pass recorded it, so a unit re-queued (or re-uploaded with
  `overwrite=true`, TD-492) and trained again keeps each pass's record and sample count. That's the "append history" option; duplicates
  within one request still collapse.
- **Forced reports:** an empty `run_id` is still an explicit force, as for `release`: it records a unit not already recorded.
- **Standalone mode:** `LocalTransport::commit_trained()` applies the same claim check under its pending lock.
- **Client:** `DatasetRegistry::build_new_versions()` no longer drops already-recorded units from run-scoped commits
  (`record_again`), so a re-trained unit is sent with its real count instead of 0. The run-less test overload keeps the old skip.
  `RemoteTransport::commit_trained()` logs a warning when the registry rejects units.
- **Requeue:** `requeue_trained()` with several records for one path re-queues it once, reports the others as `already_pending`, and
  removes all of them.

Tests:
- `RegistryTransportTests.cpp`: `CommitTrainedRecordsOnlyUnitsTheRunClaimed`, `CommitTrainedRecordsAUnitTrainedAgain`.
- Live: `TrainedFromAnotherRunIsRejected` (`trained:0`, path rejected, and then the owner's report records it with its count) and
  `ReTrainedUnitIsRecordedAgain` (two records, 5 and 7 samples). Both fail against the old server.
- `TrainedDeduplicatesInRegistry` asserted the old skip for a re-trained unit. It now checks that a forced report still skips one.

The whole live suite passes against the fixed server (97 tests).

### TD-492: Registry Upload Silently Replaces Pending or Claimed Files

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 24, 2026 | Data / Registry Server | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryServer.cpp`; verified. `handle_upload()` truncates and rewrites `<group_dir>/uploads/<filename>` whatever its queue state.
Uploading `d.jsonl`, claiming it as run `r1`, then uploading different content under the same name returned `added: true`, replaced the bytes under the
claim, and queued nothing new (`add_pending_path_locked()` returned false; its result is ignored). A trainer then trains, or downloads over FTP, data
that is not what was queued, and a trained file's recorded checksum no longer matches.

Action Items:

- [x] Refuse (409) an upload whose target is pending, claimed or trained, unless an explicit `overwrite` is given and the entry is unclaimed.
- [x] Write to a temporary name and rename; report `added:false` when the path was already queued.

Location in code: `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`handle_upload()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-492`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `tests/dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** `handle_upload()` writes the body to `<path>.upload-<n>.tmp` and decides under the group lock whether it may
replace the target:

| Target | Result |
|---|---|
| claimed by a run | 409 `"reason":"claimed"` (even with `overwrite=true`) |
| trained (in the registry) | 409 `"trained"`; with `overwrite=true`, replaced and queued again as a new version |
| queued, unclaimed, whole file | 409 `"already_queued"`; with `overwrite=true`, replaced, and its pending entry's size, checksum, entry count and `added_utc` refreshed (`{"added":false,"replaced":true}`) |
| queued as TD-205 segments | 409 `"segmented"`, since a new version would break the row ranges |
| not queued or trained | renamed into place and queued (`{"added":true}`), as before |

A refused upload leaves the existing file untouched and deletes the temporary file. `RemoteTransport::upload_file()` now logs the
server's reason with the status, so `dataset_manager add` of an already-queued file says why it failed. It used to overwrite silently;
neither it nor the Android app offers `overwrite` yet, so a deliberate replacement is a `curl` with `?overwrite=true` (adding the option to both is TD-552).

Tests (live, `dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`):
- `UploadOverAClaimedFileIsRefused`: the file's bytes are unchanged, checked with `REGISTRY_SERVER_DATA_DIR`.
- `UploadOverwriteReplacesAnUnclaimedQueuedFile`: still one queue entry, with the new size and entry count.
- `UploadOverATrainedFileNeedsOverwrite`
- `UploadDeduplicatesSamePath`: now expects 409 `already_queued`; it had asserted the old overwrite.

All four fail against the old server, and the whole live suite passes against the new one (95 tests).

### TD-491: Concurrent Registry Fetches Serve and Overwrite the Same Slice

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 24, 2026 | Data / Registry Server | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryServer.cpp`; verified. `handle_fetch_huggingface()`/`handle_fetch_gutenberg()` read the per-(source, model) cursor, write
`…_row<offset>_training.jsonl` and write the cursor back **without holding any lock** (the group mutex is taken only to queue the result). Eight
concurrent `fetch/huggingface` requests for 1,000 pairs each, against a pre-cached 20,000-row dataset, all returned `served_from_row: 0` and
`added: true`; one file was queued and the cursor advanced to 1,000. Callers were told 8,000 pairs were added; 1,000 were, written by eight writers into the
same file at once. After a wrap-around a fetch also rewrites an earlier `_row<offset>` file that may still be pending or claimed.

Action Items:

- [x] Serialize cursor read → write → advance per cursor (a per-cursor mutex, or the group mutex around the slice step).
- [x] Make output names unique (e.g. include a sequence number) and report `added:false` when nothing new was queued.
- [x] Test concurrent fetches.

Location in code: `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`handle_fetch_gutenberg()`, `handle_fetch_huggingface()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-491`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `tests/dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** `handle_fetch_huggingface()` and `handle_fetch_gutenberg()` now hold a mutex per cursor file
(`fetch_cursor_mutex()`) from reading the cursor to queuing the slice and advancing it:
- **Concurrent fetches:** for one (source, model) they run one after another, each serving the next slice. Different cursors don't wait
  for each other, and the download/cache step stays outside the lock.
- **Slice names:** `unique_slice_path()` appends `_<n>` when `…_row<offset>_training.jsonl` already exists. After a wrap-around, a fetch
  no longer rewrites an earlier slice that may be pending, claimed or trained.
- **Queuing:** `queue_fetched_slice()` uses `add_pending_path_locked()`'s result. If nothing new was queued, it removes the file, answers
  409 `{"added":false,"reason":"already_queued"}`, and doesn't advance the cursor.

Tests: the live registry suite gains `REGISTRY_SERVER_DATA_DIR`, so a test can seed a cached dataset in the server's data directory (no
network).
- `ConcurrentFetchesServeDistinctSlices`: eight concurrent fetches of 10 pairs serve rows 0–70 once each and queue eight files.
- `WrappedFetchesNeverReuseASliceFile`: six fetches over a 20-row dataset give six files and six queue entries.

On the old server, the first served only rows 0 and 10 (two files queued, eight `added:true`), and the second gave three files for six
fetches. The whole live suite passes against the fixed server (92 tests).

While testing, a stale server left on the same port took part of the traffic; that's TD-551.

### TD-471: `ParquetReader` Trusts Declared Sizes for Allocations

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 24, 2026 | Data / ParquetReader | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `ParquetReader`. Sizes read from the file drive allocations before being checked against the bytes actually present:
`read_page_body()`'s `compressed.resize(compressed_page_size)` (a negative `int32` becomes a huge `size_t`), Snappy's declared
uncompressed length (`out.reserve()`), a page's `dp_num_values` (`int32` → `size_t`, then `def_levels.assign()`/`reserve()`), and
`decode_column_chunk()`'s `reserve(num_rows)`.
- **Verified:** 25,000 fuzz mutations produced **62 escaped `std::length_error`s** (`vector::reserve`, `string::resize`). Nothing in
  `ParquetReader` or `DataFetcher` catches them; `httplib` converts them to HTTP 500, so `registry_server` survives, but partially
  downloaded parts aren't cleaned up (compounding TD-313).
- **By inspection:** a plausible lie is worse than an absurd one: a page claiming 2³¹ values in a `REQUIRED` column allocates and fills 8 GB
  of definition levels from a few bytes (one RLE run can expand to `num_values` entries), pushing the host toward the OOM killer.

Action Items:

- [x] Validate every declared size before allocating: non-negative, bounded by the file size / remaining bytes, page `num_values` ≤ the column chunk's remaining values, Snappy length ≤ the page's `uncompressed_page_size` (and a sane cap).
- [x] Catch exceptions in `convert_to_jsonl()` (return −1) and clean up in `DataFetcher` on failure.

Location in code: `src/ParquetReader.cpp` (`read_page_body()`, `snappy_raw_uncompress()`, `decode_column_chunk()`); `src/DataFetcher.cpp` (the `convert_to_jsonl()` call); tagged `TODO: See TD-471`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ParquetReader.cpp`
- `src/DataFetcher.cpp`
- `tests/parquet_reader_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** Each declared size is checked against what can actually be present before it sizes an allocation:
- **Page bodies:** the compressed size must be non-negative and fit in the bytes left in the file, and the uncompressed size must be
  non-negative.
- **Snappy:** the declared length must be at most the page's `uncompressed_page_size` and at most 32 bytes per compressed byte (no Snappy
  element of n ≥ 2 bytes produces more than 64).
- **Pages:** a page's value count must be non-negative and at most the values left in its column chunk.
- **Columns:** a column chunk's value count must equal its row group's row count, since a flat schema has one value or null per row. This
  is checked for every chunk before any output.
- **Row groups:** at most 2²⁴ rows (`kMaxRowsPerRowGroup`, 16× pyarrow's default row group). The reader buffers a whole row group
  (TD-472), and a constant column RLE-encodes any number of rows in a few bytes, so the file size alone can't bound this.
- **Dictionaries and PLAIN values:** the count must be non-negative and at most 8 per byte; the smallest PLAIN value is one bit.
- **Bit-packed runs:** the group count is compared before multiplying, so it can't wrap past the bounds check.

`convert_to_jsonl()` catches exceptions (−1) and now keeps the header's promise that a failure leaves the output as it was:
- **Before:** a failure in a later row group kept the earlier row groups' rows, and a replacing write had already truncated the file.
- **Now:** an append is cut back to its original size, and a replacing write goes to `<out>.tmp`, which is renamed over the target only
  on success.

`DataFetcher` deletes a part it couldn't convert.

Tests (`parquet_reader_test.cpp`, using a small Thrift writer that builds a one-column file):
- `SyntheticColumnFileConverts`: the control.
- `RowGroupDeclaringBillionsOfRowsIsRejected`
- `PageClaimingMoreValuesThanItsColumnIsRejected`: the 8 GB definition-level fill.
- `NegativeOrOversizedPageSizeIsRejected`
- `MutatedFixturesNeverThrowAndFailuresLeaveOutputUnchanged`: 9,000 deterministic byte mutations of the six fixtures, each converted
  in append and replace mode.

On the old reader under a 4 GB address-space limit, the three crafted files throw `std::bad_alloc`/`std::length_error`, and the
mutation test fails on its 13th mutated file, where a failed replacing write had wiped the output. Without the limit, the page test would fill 8 GB.

### TD-470: Malformed Parquet Footers Hang or Crash `registry_server`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 24, 2026 | Data / ParquetReader | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `ParquetReader` and verified with hand-crafted files. `skip_value()` (the Thrift compact-protocol skipper for footer and
page-header fields the reader doesn't parse) has two unbounded paths:
- **Infinite loop.** A list's size comes from a varint, and skipping a `BOOL` element (types 1/2) consumes **no bytes**: that's the
  struct-field form, but in the compact protocol each list element is one byte. A **26-byte** file whose footer holds one unknown field with
  a bool list of size ~2⁶² made `convert_to_jsonl()` spin at 100% CPU until killed (20 s timeout).
- **Unbounded recursion.** Nested structs recurse once per byte; a footer with 400,000 nested struct fields crashed with **SIGSEGV** (stack
  overflow).

`ParquetReader` runs inside `registry_server` on every HuggingFace part fetched through `POST /registry/<group>/fetch/huggingface` (and the
dashboard's fetch dialog), so a malicious or corrupt dataset part ties up a request thread forever or **kills the registry daemon** (a
segfault can't be caught). Same class as TD-309. (25,000 random mutations under ASan/UBSan found no memory errors; these needed crafted input.)

Action Items:

- [x] Consume one byte per bool element when skipping a list; reject list sizes larger than the remaining bytes.
- [x] Add a recursion depth limit (e.g. 64) to `skip_value()` and the struct parsers.
- [x] Regression tests with the two crafted footers.

Location in code: `src/ParquetReader.cpp` (`skip_value()`, `read_list_header()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-470`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/ParquetReader.cpp`
- `tests/parquet_reader_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).**
- **List sizes:** `read_list_header()` rejects a size larger than the bytes left, since every compact-protocol list element takes at
  least one byte. That bounds every list loop in the reader, not just the skipper.
- **Bool elements:** a new `skip_list_element()` consumes the one byte a bool element takes inside a list. All five list loops that
  skip elements use it.
- **Nesting:** `skip_value()` takes a depth and refuses beyond 64 levels.
- **Struct parsers:** these follow the fixed schema (one function per known struct), so data can't make them recurse; only
  `skip_value()` did.

Tests (`parquet_reader_test.cpp`):
- `HugeBoolListInFooterFailsInsteadOfLooping`: a 24-byte file with a 2⁶²-element bool list in an unknown footer field.
- `DeeplyNestedFooterFailsInsteadOfCrashing`: 400,000 nested structs.

Both now return −1, and the real fixtures still parse (12/12). On the old reader, the first was still spinning when killed after 20 s,
and the second segfaulted.

### TD-339: FTPS Downloads Don't Verify the Registry's Certificate

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 24, 2026 | Data / DataTransport | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-337, by inspection. With FTPS enabled, `fetch()` sets `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER`
and `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST` to 0 to accept the registry's self-signed certificate. The control
channel is encrypted, but anyone able to intercept the connection can impersonate `registry_server`,
serve arbitrary training data, and collect the one-time credentials. There's no option to pin the
server certificate or trust a private CA. This pairs with TD-284 (`registry_server` ignores the
config file's FTPS keys).

Action Items:

- [x] Add a trainer config option for a CA bundle or pinned certificate (`CURLOPT_CAINFO` / `CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY`), enable verification when set, and warn loudly when FTPS runs unverified.

Location in code: `src/DataTransport.hpp` (`fetch()` FTPS options); tagged `TODO: See TD-339`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DataTransport.hpp`
- `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).** `DataTransport` takes an `FtpsVerification` (`ca_file`, `pinned_public_key`). The trainer fills it from
two new `config.trainer.conf` keys, also read from the environment and carried through `DatasetConfig` to `resolve_pass_files()`:
- **`FTPS_PINNED_PUBLIC_KEY`:** curl's `CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY` (`sha256//<base64>` or a public-key file), checked on its own, so it
  authenticates the default self-signed certificate. `registry_server` now logs its pin at startup (`[FTP/TLS] Certificate public-key
  pin …`, `FtpDataServer::public_key_pin()`). A generated certificate's key changes on every restart, so a pinned deployment should give
  `registry_server` `--ftp-cert`/`--ftp-key`.
- **`FTPS_CA_FILE`:** a PEM CA bundle (or the registry's own certificate). It turns on peer and hostname verification
  (`VERIFYPEER`/`VERIFYHOST 2`), so the certificate must name the host `registry_server` advertises.

With either key set:
- a registry that offers plain FTP is refused before any credentials are sent;
- a missing CA file fails before connecting.

With neither set, FTPS works as before and logs one loud warning per process.

**Found while testing:** `FtpDataServer` survived a client that dropped a TLS session only because `httplib::Server`'s constructor
ignores SIGPIPE process-wide; OpenSSL writes with plain `write()`. In the test process the wrong-pin case killed the server with SIGPIPE
(exit 141). `FtpDataServer::start()` now ignores SIGPIPE itself. The shipped `registry_server` was not affected (30 wrong-pin `curl`
connections against the real binary, which survived).

Tests:
- `DataTransportFtpsTests` (new; a real `FtpDataServer` with FTPS serving a real libcurl `DataTransport` on loopback):
  - the server publishes a well-formed pin;
  - the matching pin downloads;
  - a different pin is refused (the impersonation case, which the old code accepted);
  - a CA file must sign the server's certificate (generated with SAN `IP:127.0.0.1`; a different self-signed certificate is refused);
  - a missing CA file fails before connecting;
  - configured verification refuses plain FTP;
  - unverified FTPS still downloads;
  - the keys reach `DatasetConfig`.
- `config_test`: `FtpsVerificationKeysLoad`.
- The new tests can't build against the old code, which had no verification API. Its `fetch()` set both checks to 0 and no pin, which
  is the path `UnverifiedFtpsStillDownloads` covers.

### TD-310: HuggingFace `split` Can Write Outside the Registry Data Directory

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 24, 2026 | Data / DataFetcher | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-309 and confirmed by running the real code. `registry_server`'s
`fetch/huggingface` allow-lists `dataset_id` and `split` to `[A-Za-z0-9._-/]+`, which permits `..`
and `/`. `DataFetcher` flattens `/` in `dataset_id` but concatenates `split` into the cache path
as-is (`<dir>/<safe_id>_<split>/`), and the registry builds the training-file path from `split` the
same way. `split = "x/../../../../ESCAPED"` made `ensure_huggingface_cached()` create `ESCAPED/`
outside the group's data directory. With a real download, `parquet_info.json`, `parquet/` and
`full_dataset.jsonl` would be written there, and the produced training file and pending entry would
point there too. Any client that can reach the registry's fetch endpoint can do this.

Action Items:

- [x] Reject `..` path components (or any `/`) in `split` in the registry allow-list, and flatten `split` in `DataFetcher` like `dataset_id`.
- [x] Test: the endpoint rejects a `split` containing `..`, and `DataFetcher` never creates paths outside its output dir.

Location in code: `src/DataFetcher.cpp` (`ensure_huggingface_cached()`, `fetch_huggingface()`), `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`kSafeHfIdentifier`); tagged `TODO: See TD-310`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DataFetcher.cpp`
- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `tests/dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).**
- **Registry allow-list:** `fetch/huggingface` replaces its `[A-Za-z0-9._-/]+` allow-list with `is_safe_hf_component()` (one
  `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` name, never `.` or `..`) for `split`, and `is_safe_hf_dataset_id()` (`name` or `org/name`, every component
  safe, no leading, trailing or doubled `/`) for `dataset_id`. Anything else gets 400 before any fetch.
- **Registry training-file name:** built with `flatten_for_path(split)`.
- **`DataFetcher`:** `fetch_huggingface()` and `ensure_huggingface_cached()` build the per-dataset directory with
  `hf_dataset_dir_name()`, which flattens `/` and `\` in both `dataset_id` and `split`. That also protects `dataset_manager`'s
  local `huggingface` command, which doesn't go through the registry check.

Tests:
- `DataFetcherTests.cpp`'s `SplitIsFlattenedIntoTheOutputDirectory`: split `x/../../ESCAPED` resolves inside the output directory,
  and nothing named `ESCAPED` is created outside it (offline, with a pre-created cache).
- `dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`'s `TraversalInDatasetIdOrSplitIsRejected`: nine traversal cases get 400. 90/90 live tests pass
  against a fresh server.

### TD-309: Gutenberg Sentence Splitting Can Crash `registry_server`

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 24, 2026 | Data / DataFetcher | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [DataFetcher.md](../reference/source/DataFetcher.md) and confirmed by running the real
code. `DataFetcher::extract_sentences()` matches `std::regex("[^.!?]+[.!?]+")` over the whole cleaned
book. libstdc++'s regex engine recurses per character, so a long run with no `.`, `!` or `?` overflows
the stack: 20,000 characters was fine, but **100,000 and 400,000 characters died with SIGSEGV**.
Realistic triggers include a book in a script without ASCII sentence punctuation (e.g. Chinese, which
uses `。`), a long poem, or a large index or table.

`registry_server`'s `POST /registry/<group>/fetch/gutenberg` runs `ensure_gutenberg_cached()` →
`extract_sentences()` in its request thread, so **one fetch request kills the registry daemon**. No
sentence cache is written on the way, so every retry of the same book crashes it again.
`dataset_manager`'s local `gutenberg` command crashes the same way.

Action Items:

- [x] Replace the regex with a linear hand-written scanner (also the natural place for TD-311's abbreviation handling).
- [x] Cap the length of a candidate sentence span, and treat a book with no usable sentences as a clean failure.
- [x] Test: a 1 MB unpunctuated input returns without crashing.

Location in code: `src/DataFetcher.cpp` (`extract_sentences()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-309`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DataFetcher.cpp`
- `tests/DataFetcherTests.cpp`

**Fix (October 24, 2026).**
- **Sentence splitting:** `extract_sentences()` is one linear pass with the regex's rules: a run of non-terminators plus its
  terminators; text after the last terminator dropped; a `.` between digits isn't a boundary; whitespace collapsed; 21–499 characters
  kept. A candidate stops being built once it reaches 500 characters.
- **Other whole-text regexes:** three more could overflow the same way, and are now linear loops too:
  - `clean_gutenberg_text()`'s `[ \t]+` and `\n{3,}` collapses (a long run of spaces or newlines);
  - `strip_illustration_markers()`' `\[(Illustration|…)[^\]]*\]` (an unclosed `[Illustration` before a long text).

### TD-548: Standalone World-Model Pool and Checkpoint Share One Directory

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 21, 2026 | Training / World model | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 20, 2026) |

Description:
Found while verifying TD-342 end to end, and reproduced with the real binaries on the oneAPI CPU device.
- **The collision:** in standalone mode (no `REGISTRY_SERVER_URL`), `LocalTransport` keeps each kind's queue in
  `<SESSION_DIR>/<kind>/` (TD-202). `<SESSION_DIR>/world_model/` is also the default world-model checkpoint directory.
- **LeJEPA pass:** `dataset_manager --kind world_model add` creates that directory. `incremental_trainer --objective=lejepa`
  then finds it, tries to load a checkpoint from it (`Failed to open file for reading: …/world_model/config.bin`), and the
  pass exits 1.
- **Chatbot pass:** `IncrementalTrainer::maybe_attach_world_model()` sees the same directory, fails to load, and continues
  without the world model.
- **Who is affected:** `--objective=lejepa` always uses `<SESSION_DIR>/world_model` (it ignores `WORLD_MODEL_ARTIFACT_PATH`),
  so standalone world-model training can't be configured around this. Against `registry_server` the queue lives server-side,
  so ai-machine isn't affected.

Workaround: queue the LeJEPA data under another kind and pass `--dataset-kind` (e.g. `--dataset-kind chatbot`).

Action Items:

- [x] Put the world-model checkpoint in its own directory (e.g. `<SESSION_DIR>/world_model_checkpoint`), with a fallback that
  reads an old-layout checkpoint, or move the standalone pools under `<SESSION_DIR>/pools/<kind>/` with a migration.
- [x] Have `--objective=lejepa` honor `WORLD_MODEL_ARTIFACT_PATH`, like the chatbot attach.
- [x] Test a standalone LeJEPA pass, then a chatbot pass that attaches its world model.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (the `lejepa` world-model directory), `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
(`maybe_attach_world_model()`), `src/DatasetRegistry.cpp` (`local_pool_dir()`).

**Fix (October 21, 2026).**
- **Shared rule:** three new static helpers on `LeJEPAEncoder`, used by the LeJEPA pass, `IncrementalTrainer::maybe_attach_world_model()`
  and `chatbot_api_server`:
  - `default_checkpoint_dir()` is `<SESSION_DIR>/world_model_checkpoint`.
  - `has_checkpoint()` requires the checkpoint's `config.bin`, so a dataset pool in the same directory no longer counts.
  - `resolve_checkpoint_dir()` picks `WORLD_MODEL_ARTIFACT_PATH` (or MNS's artifact path) when set, else the new default, else a
    pre-fix `<SESSION_DIR>/world_model` checkpoint.
- **The LeJEPA pass:** saves to `WORLD_MODEL_ARTIFACT_PATH` when set (it used to ignore it) or the new default. A checkpoint resumed
  from the old directory moves to the new one on the next save.
- **Metrics label:** kept as `world_model`.

Verified:
- **Test:** `lejepaencoder_test.cpp`'s `CheckpointDirectoryResolution`.
- **Real binaries** (SYCL build, oneAPI CPU device):
  - the original sequence (`dataset_manager --kind world_model add`, a LeJEPA pass, then a chatbot pass) now trains and attaches the
    world model without the `--dataset-kind` workaround;
  - a session with only an old-layout checkpoint resumes it and saves to `world_model_checkpoint`.

### TD-490: `registry_server` Group Names Escape `data_dir`, Letting Delete Unlink Outside It

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 21, 2026 | Data / Registry Server | Code fix (HIGH, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `RegistryServer.cpp` (see [RegistryServer.md](../reference/source/RegistryServer.md)); verified with the real binary. The route
regex captures `<group>` as `[^/]+` and every handler uses it unvalidated in `data_dir + "/" + group` (`group_dir()`, `get_group()`, `handle_delete()`'s
`group_root`). httplib accepts both `/registry/../…` and `/registry/%2e%2e/…`:
- `upload?filename=t1.jsonl` through group `..` wrote `<data_dir>/../uploads/t1.jsonl` (and a `pending_files.txt` in `data_dir`'s parent).
- **File deletion:** with `<parent>/models/checkpoint.bin` present, `pending/add` + `delete {"delete_files":true}` through group `g` refused to unlink it,
  but through group `..` the containment root became the parent and the file was **deleted** (`file_deleted:true`).
With the default relative `REGISTRY_DATA_DIR=registry_sessions`, the parent is the working directory (checkpoints, configs, binaries). The server has no
authentication (trusted-LAN design), so any LAN host, or anyone past Cloudflare Access, can delete files there with two requests. By inspection, group `.`
maps to `data_dir` itself, reaching `daemon_config.db`, `session_counters.db` and other groups' files.

Action Items:

- [x] Validate `<group>` against a strict pattern (e.g. `[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]*`, never `.`/`..`) in every route, returning 400.
- [x] Check `group_dir()` results resolve under `data_dir` (canonicalized) before use.
- [x] Add live tests for `..`, `%2e%2e` and `.` groups.

Location in code: `src/RegistryServer.cpp` (`group_dir()`, `get_group()`, `handle_delete()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-490`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `tests/dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 21, 2026).**
- **Route check:** every `/registry/<group>/…` route (all 16) checks the group with `group_ok()` before calling its handler, and
  answers 400 `invalid group name` otherwise. A valid name is one plain path component, `[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]*` of at most
  128 characters, so `.` and `..` can't pass. httplib decodes the URL before routing, so `%2e%2e` is checked as `..`.
- **Defense in depth:** `group_dir()` throws for an invalid name, and `handle_delete()`'s containment root is built from it.
- **Not changed:** existing group names (`chatbot-v1`, `my-training-group`) are unaffected. MNS doesn't validate `run_group`, so an
  invalid one stored there now gets a clear 400 from the registry.

Verified against the real binary:
- **The attack:** a `checkpoint.bin` was placed in `data_dir`'s parent, then `pending/add` and `delete {"delete_files":true}` sent
  through group `..` (`curl --path-as-is`) and `%2e%2e`. All three got 400, the file survived, and no `pending_files.txt` appeared
  in the parent.
- **Live tests:** `dataset_registry_live_test.cpp`'s new `LiveRegistryGroupNames` tests:
  - `%2e%2e`, `%2E%2E`, `.`, `%2e`, `.hidden` and a kind-scoped `%2e%2e/chatbot` get 400, or no 200 for `delete`/`pending/add`;
  - ordinary names still work.
- **Suite:** 89/89 live tests pass against the fixed server.

### TD-396: Hippocampal Memory Eviction Starves New Memories

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 21, 2026 | Memory / HippocampalMemory | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `HippocampalMemory` and verified by simulation with the real class. TD-193's
least-used eviction removes the slot with the lowest `coverage_`, but a newly written slot starts at
coverage 0, while every older slot carries accumulated, decayed coverage. Under `DecoderBlock`'s
bookkeeping (each forward step: `decay_coverage(0.95)`, then add each slot's mean attention weight),
a new slot needs about `1/(1 − γ)` = 20 steps to approach the others. With near-uniform attention it
never catches up before the next write, so it is the slot evicted next. Simulation (capacity 8, one
write per "response" followed by 50 forward steps, 40 responses): with uniform attention the
survivors were writes **0–6** plus the newest, so the first `capacity − 1` memories are permanent and
nothing new persists. With peaked random attention turnover was normal (20, 22, 26, 33, 35, 37, 38,
39). Near-uniform attention is the likely case in shipped models: the hippocampal cross-attention gets
no gradient while its gate is stuck at 0 (TD-341), and keys are mean-pooled world-model embeddings of
whole responses. The failure is masked today only because TD-341 zeroes the path's output.

Action Items:

- [x] Give new slots a protection window (not evictable for N steps/writes), or start them at the current mean coverage, or evict by `coverage / age` (or LRU on last significant attention).
- [x] Add a test that simulates the decay-and-accumulate bookkeeping under uniform attention and asserts recent writes survive.
- [x] Do this together with TD-341.

Location in code: `src/HippocampalMemory.cpp` (`evict_least_used()`, `insert_slot()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-396`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/HippocampalMemory.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/hippocampalmemory_test.cpp`

**Note (October 20, 2026, TD-341).** The hippocampal gate now trains on the CPU path, so this eviction behavior is now
reachable in training, not only in theory.

**Fix (October 21, 2026).** Of the options above, a new slot (from `write()` or `recall_from_swap()`) now starts at the
**mean coverage of the slots it joins**, 0 when it's the first. Eviction ties go to the oldest.
- **Uniform attention:** every slot stays level, so eviction becomes FIFO.
- **Peaked attention:** usage decides as before.
- **Why not a protection window:** it doesn't fix exactly uniform attention. A slot leaving the window is still the youngest,
  so it's still the least covered.
- **Repetition penalty:** at the mean coverage, it adds the same bias to every slot under uniform attention, which doesn't
  change the softmax.
- **Format:** the saved file format is unchanged.

Tests (`hippocampalmemory_test.cpp`):
- `RecentWritesSurviveUnderUniformAttention`: the TD's own simulation (capacity 8, 40 writes, 50 committed steps each). The
  survivors are writes 32–39; the old code left {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 39}, as described above.
- `BufferTurnsOverUnderPeakedAttention`.
- `NewSlotsStartAtTheMeanCoverageOfTheOthers` replaces the test that asserted the old zero start.
- Two coverage expectations in the eviction and recall tests were updated to the mean.

TD-341 (the gates) and TD-343 (one update per decode step) landed first, so the simulation uses the real per-step bookkeeping.

### TD-373: `--ftps` Doesn't Require Encryption

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 21, 2026 | Data / FtpDataServer | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 12, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `FtpDataServer` and verified. With `--ftps` enabled, nothing requires
`AUTH TLS` before `USER`/`PASS` or `PROT P` before `RETR`: a plaintext client logged in and downloaded
the full file from the FTPS server. Credentials and data can therefore cross the network unencrypted
on a server operators believe is "FTPS". `DataTransport` requests TLS (`CURLUSESSL_ALL`), so today's
trainer is protected unless the connection is downgraded or a client is misconfigured.

Action Items:

- [x] When FTPS is enabled, refuse `USER`/`PASS` with `530`/`534` until `AUTH TLS` has completed, and refuse `RETR` unless `PROT P` is set.
- [x] Do this together with TD-339 (client certificate verification) and TD-284 (FTPS keys from config). (Both done: TD-339 October 24, TD-284 October 31, 2026.)

Location in code: `src/FtpDataServer.hpp` (`cmd_pass()`, `cmd_retr()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-373`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/FtpDataServer.hpp`
- `tests/FtpDataServerTests.cpp`

**Fix (October 21, 2026).** With FTPS enabled:
- **Login:** `USER` and `PASS` get `530 TLS required` until `AUTH TLS` has completed, and are logged (`[AUDIT] Plaintext login refused`).
- **Download:** `RETR` gets `521` (RFC 4217) unless `PROT P` is set.

TD-339 (client certificate checks) and TD-284 (FTPS keys from config) remain open.

Tests:
- `FtpDataServerTests.cpp`'s `PlaintextLoginIsRefusedWhenFtpsIsEnabled`. The old code accepted plaintext `USER`/`PASS` (331/230).
- End to end against `registry_server --ftps`:
