  - `curl --ftp-ssl-control` (TLS login, clear data) gets 521;
  - `curl --ssl-reqd` downloads normally.

### TD-372: FTP Data Connections Are Accepted From Any Host, So Files Can Be Stolen

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 21, 2026 | Data / FtpDataServer | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 12, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `FtpDataServer` and verified against a live server. `cmd_retr()` calls
`accept()` on the PASV socket and takes the **first connection from any address**; it never checks
that the peer matches the control connection's client IP. A third socket that connected to the
advertised data port before the real client received the entire file (300,000 of 300,000 bytes), and
the server logged `226 Transfer complete` and marked the token consumed. **The same worked under FTPS
with `PROT P`**: the data-channel `SSL_accept()` accepts any TLS client (no session-reuse or peer
binding), so a TLS-capable thief also received all 300,000 bytes. PASV ports come lowest-first from a
small fixed range (default 50000–50099), so an attacker on the network only has to keep connecting
to them. Consequences: dataset confidentiality is lost, and the real trainer's download fails while
its token is consumed, so every download can be denied as well. The per-file token and TLS design is
bypassed entirely at the data channel.

Action Items:

- [x] Record the control connection's peer address; after `accept()` on the PASV socket, compare the data peer's address and reject (close, keep listening until the timeout) any mismatch.
- [x] Under `PROT P`, additionally require TLS session resumption (The peer-IP check is done; session reuse is TD-549, fixed October 24, 2026.) from the control channel (as vsftpd's `require_ssl_reuse` does) or at least the peer-IP check above.
- [x] Don't consume the token unless the transfer went to the authenticated peer.
- [x] Add a live-session test: a foreign connection to the PASV port gets nothing and the real client still succeeds.

Location in code: `src/FtpDataServer.hpp` (`cmd_retr()`, `ConnState`); tagged `TODO: See TD-372`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/FtpDataServer.hpp`
- `tests/FtpDataServerTests.cpp`

**Fix (October 21, 2026).**
- **Peer check:** `cmd_retr()` accepts through `accept_from_client()`, which takes only a connection from the control connection's
  client IP. Any other peer is logged (`[AUDIT] Data connection refused`) and closed while it keeps waiting, within the same 30 s.
- **Backlog:** the PASV listen backlog is now 4 (was 1), so a squatter can't block the real client.
- **Token:** consumed only after a transfer to that peer.
- **Not done:** requiring TLS session reuse on the data channel, the stronger binding, is TD-549.

Tests:
- `FtpDataServerTests.cpp`'s `ForeignDataConnectionGetsNothingAndTheClientStillDownloads`: a socket bound to 127.0.0.2 connects to
  the PASV port before `RETR`. It receives nothing, and the client gets all 300,000 bytes. On the old code the foreign socket took
  the data connection and the client couldn't connect.
- End to end, with the real `registry_server --ftps` and `curl --ssl-reqd --ftp-method nocwd` (the trainer's libcurl options), the
  download still completes (226, contents match).

### TD-343: Hippocampal Memory Is Updated on Every Forward Pass

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 21, 2026 | Transformer / DecoderBlock | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-341, by inspection. When `memory` is passed, `forward()` decays and accumulates
coverage and Hebbian associations on **every** call: training forwards, validation forwards, and one
call per hypothesis in beam search (the only generation branch that passes memory). The design
("called once per decode step") assumes one update per generated token, so coverage and associations
build up several times faster than intended, strengthening the repetition penalty and cross-reference
pull, and training passes pollute the persistent memory state that's saved on shutdown.

**Update (October 11, 2026, from [Decoder.md](../reference/source/Decoder.md)):** `LLMDecoder` passes the
same `memory` to every block with the gated path, and each block updates it, so one forward applies
one decay-and-accumulate round **per injected layer** (6 with `WORLD_MODEL_INJECT_EVERY_N_LAYERS = 1`
and 6 layers). The fix should update memory once per forward, at the decoder or model level.

**Update (October 11, 2026, from [EncoderDecoderModel.md](../reference/source/EncoderDecoderModel.md)):**
`generate_response()` writes the response into hippocampal memory after every CPU generation, including
`ChatbotTrainer`'s label-backfill and generation-quality calls on the live model, so training-time
evaluation also writes episodic memories. Only serving generations should write.

Action Items:

- [x] Separate scoring from state update: let the caller commit coverage/association updates once per decode step (and never during training/validation unless intended).
- [x] Test: beam search with width k updates coverage once per step.

Location in code: `src/DecoderBlock.cpp` (`forward()` hippocampal coverage/association update); tagged `TODO: See TD-343`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DecoderBlock.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`
- `src/HippocampalMemory.{hpp,cpp}`

**Note (October 20, 2026, TD-342).** The GPU forward and KV-cached generation now update the memory too, through the same
shared `update_hippocampal_memory()`, so this per-forward update also happens there.

**Fix (October 21, 2026).**
- **Forwards only read the memory:** `DecoderBlock`'s forwards (CPU, KV-cached and GPU) read the memory for scoring and never
  update it.
  - `last_hippocampal_attention()` returns the last forward's mean attention weights. On the GPU they are downloaded only when
    asked, so GPU training no longer downloads them every forward.
  - `LLMDecoder::last_hippocampal_step_weights()` averages the newest token's row over the blocks whose path ran: one update per
    step, not one per injected layer.
- **One commit per step:** the update moved to `HippocampalMemory::commit_attention()`. Every generation path (CPU and GPU, beam and
  cached) commits it through a `HippocampalStepCommitter`, once per decode step.
  - A step is a token length, and beam hypotheses at the same step are averaged.
  - The pending step is flushed when generation ends.
  - All hypotheses in a step now see the same coverage, from the end of the previous step.
- **Training and validation:** teacher-forced forwards never commit.
- **Training-time generation:** `EncoderDecoderModel::set_hippocampal_updates_enabled(false)` stops step commits and response writes.
  `ChatbotTrainer::train()` sets it for its whole run (restored on exit), so quality and backfill generations no longer pollute the
  serving memory.
- **Diagnostics:** `HippocampalMemory::committed_steps()` counts committed steps.

Tests:
- `encoderdecoder_test.cpp`:
  - `BeamSearchCommitsOncePerDecodeStep`: beam width 3, two injected layers, at most 10 tokens → at most 10 commits. Before,
    about width × layers per step.
  - `CachedDecodingCommitsOncePerToken`.
  - `TrainingForwardsAndDisabledUpdatesLeaveTheMemoryAlone`.
- `decoderblock_test.cpp`: `CommittedStepStrengthensAssociationBetweenAttendedSlots` (a forward alone leaves coverage and
  associations at 0). The coverage and association bound tests commit after each forward.
- `gpu_optimizer_test.cpp`: the GPU block test commits from both paths and compares coverage.

### TD-503: SIGReg Loss Has a Sequence-Length-Dependent Floor

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 20, 2026 | World Model / SIGReg | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `SIGReg.cpp`; verified. The squared characteristic-function gap is a biased estimator with an expected floor ∝ 1/n, and
`LeJEPAEncoder::train_step()` applies SIGReg to one text's token embeddings (n = token count). A true N(0, I) set scores 0.0785 at n = 8, 0.0331 at 20,
0.0225 at 32, 0.0057 at 128 and 0.0003 at 2,048; fully collapsed is 0.343. Short texts are pushed away from a target they already meet (the small-n
minimizer isn't Gaussian), and the logged `sigreg_loss` mostly reflects text length, so it can't be compared across datasets or over training. (The paper
applies SIGReg across a batch of samples; per-sequence application is a deliberate deviation that makes the bias matter.)

Action Items:

- [x] Use the unbiased estimator of |φ̂(t) − φ(t)|² (remove the (1 − |φ̂|²)/n-style self-term), or scale and document the n-dependence.
- [x] Consider applying SIGReg across a batch of sequences' pooled embeddings, as the paper does.

Location in code: `src/SIGReg.cpp` (`compute_loss()`, `backward()`), `src/LeJEPAEncoder.cpp` (`train_step()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-503`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/SIGReg.cpp`
- `src/LeJEPAEncoder.cpp`
- `tests/sigreg_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 20, 2026).**
- **Unbiased estimator:** `compute_loss()` adds the bias correction `(|φ̂|² − 1)/(n − 1)` to each squared gap, which replaces
  `|φ̂|²` with its unbiased U-statistic `(n|φ̂|² − 1)/(n − 1)`, and `backward()` is its exact gradient. Its expectation is 0 for an
  N(0, I) sample of any size, so a single value can be slightly negative. Fewer than two rows return 0, with a zero gradient.
- **Measured on the real class:** mean over 300 N(0, I) samples with fresh directions:

  | n | Old | New |
  |---|---|---|
  | 8 | 0.0865 | 0.0019 |
  | 32 | 0.0211 | 0.0002 |
  | 128 | 0.0054 | 0.0001 |

  A collapsed batch still scores above 0.2 at n = 8.
- **Metrics ingest:** `metrics_api_server` recorded LeJEPA epoch metrics only when `sigreg_loss >= 0`, which would have dropped
  real epochs. It now gates on `predictor_loss` alone; the two always arrive together.

Tests:
- `sigreg_test.cpp`: `UnbiasedLossDoesNotDependOnSequenceLength` and `FewerThanTwoRowsScoreZeroWithZeroGradient`.
  `LossNearZeroForIsotropicGaussianBatch` now allows small negative values. The existing finite-difference gradient check passes
  against the new gradient.
- `training_metrics_api_routes_test.cpp`: `NegativeSigregLossIsStillRecorded`.

**Batch application (October 20–21, 2026, the second action item, requested by the owner).**
- **`LeJEPAEncoder::train_batch(texts)`:**
  - Phase 1 encodes every text's target view and mean-pools it to one row per text, then takes SIGReg's loss and gradient over
    that `[batch, d_model]` matrix.
  - Phase 2 trains each text as `train_step()` does. Its pooled row's SIGReg gradient, scaled by `sigreg_lambda` and the batch
    size, is spread evenly over its tokens.
  - The batch-size factor keeps the paper's balance: in the batch objective each sample gets `(1/B)·∂predictor_b + λ·∂SIGReg/∂pooled_b`
    in one step, but here each text takes its own step with its full predictor gradient. Unscaled, the SIGReg term was B times
    weaker: at λ = 3 it barely held the embeddings.
  - Texts that fail to tokenize or give fewer than 2 tokens are skipped rather than failing the batch, and a batch with fewer
    than 2 usable texts contributes no SIGReg.
- **`train_step(text)`:** unchanged, the per-sequence form. Both share a private `train_tokens()`.
- **The pass:** `incremental_trainer --objective=lejepa` trains in batches of the new `WORLD_MODEL_SIGREG_BATCH_SIZE` (default 32,
  2–4096; `config.trainer.conf`). It still pushes per-sample predictor-loss metrics and checks auto-save per sample, and the
  batch SIGReg loss and diagnostics count once per trained text in the epoch averages.

Tests (`lejepaencoder_test.cpp`):
- `TrainBatchSkipsUnusableTextsAndReportsTheTrainedOnes` and `TrainBatchOfOneHasNoSigregLoss`.
- `TrainBatchSigregPullsPooledEmbeddingsTowardGaussian`: two encoders from the same weights, 30 batches of 16 texts, λ = 1 vs
  λ = 0. The pooled embeddings' gap from N(0, I) ended at 0.25–0.36 with SIGReg against 0.56–0.59 without, from a 0.27–0.31 start.
- The config key's parsing, env override and validation are tested in `config_test.cpp`.

### TD-502: SIGReg's Fixed Sketch Directions Leave Most Dimensions Unregularized

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 20, 2026 | World Model / SIGReg | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `SIGReg.cpp` (see [SIGReg.md](../reference/source/SIGReg.md)); verified. The `num_sketches` projection directions are drawn
once in the constructor (`std::random_device` seed) and reused for every call, so the loss only constrains their K-dimensional span: 64 of 768 dimensions
at the shipped `WORLD_MODEL_SIGREG_NUM_SKETCHES=64`. A 256-row Gaussian batch and the same batch projected onto that span (collapsed in 704 of 768
dimensions) gave identical loss (0.00265) and variance mean (1.004); through a fresh set of directions the collapsed batch showed variance 0.086 and loss
0.245. Within a pass, LeJEPA's encoder can collapse outside the sketched subspace with no penalty and nothing in the logged metrics. New directions each
process partly mask this across `trainer_service` passes but make runs irreproducible.

Action Items:

- [x] Resample the directions on every `compute_loss()`/`backward()` pair (share one draw between the two within a step), from a seedable RNG.
- [x] Add a test that a subspace-collapsed batch is penalized.

Location in code: `src/SIGReg.cpp` (constructor), `src/SIGReg.hpp` (`directions_`); tagged `TODO: See TD-502`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/SIGReg.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/LeJEPAEncoder.cpp`
- `tests/sigreg_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 20, 2026).**
- **Per-step directions:** `SIGReg::resample_directions()` draws new unit directions, and `LeJEPAEncoder::train_step()` calls it
  once per step. That step's `compute_loss()`, `compute_variance_stats()` and `backward()` then share the draw.
- **Seeding:** the RNG is a member `std::mt19937`, seeded from `std::random_device` at construction. `set_seed()` reseeds it and
  redraws, for reproducible runs and tests. `get_directions()` exposes the current draw.

Tests (`sigreg_test.cpp`):
- `RedrawnDirectionsPenalizeCollapseOutsideOneDrawsSpan`: a 512-row Gaussian batch projected onto one draw's 8-direction span
  (collapsed in 56 of 64 dimensions) scores the same as the full batch under that draw. Over 20 redraws it averages above 0.05,
  more than 10× the Gaussian batch.
- `SetSeedMakesTheDirectionsReproducible`.

### TD-434: `Matrix::operator*` Runs Short Products Single-Threaded and Portable Builds Have No SIMD

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 20, 2026 | Core / Matrix | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `Matrix` and verified by timing (8-core dev machine, AVX2 build):
- **Threading gate on `rows` only.** The AVX2 and NEON paths use `#pragma omp parallel for
  schedule(dynamic, 16) if (rows > 64)` (and the OpenMP fallback `rows > 64 && other.cols > 64`). Training
  samples and decode steps usually have ≤ 64 rows, so their weight-matrix products run on one thread however
  large the inner and output dimensions are. A work-based gate (`rows·cols·other.cols > 2¹⁸`, static
  schedule) measured 64×512×512: ~3 → ~0.8 ms; 64×512×2048: ~16 → ~7.5 ms; 8×512×8000 (LM head, decode):
  ~12.5 → ~2.2 ms; already-parallel 300×512×2048 unchanged or slightly faster. Callers already inside an
  OpenMP region (`MultiHeadAttention`'s per-head loop) get a serialized inner region under the default
  `OMP_MAX_ACTIVE_LEVELS`, so this doesn't oversubscribe.
- **No SIMD in `portable` builds.** `ADAI_SIMD_AVX2` comes from the compiler's `__AVX2__`
  (`MatrixSIMD.hpp`), which the `portable` preset (`-march=x86-64`) deliberately doesn't set, so
  `operator*` falls to the strided OpenMP ijk loop: 7–10× slower (64×512×2048: 162 ms vs 16 ms;
  8×512×8000: 93 ms vs 12.7 ms). CLAUDE.md recommends `portable` for binaries deployed to other machines;
  that's harmless for the daemons but costly for a CPU `chatbot_api_server` or trainer.

Action Items:

- [x] Replace the `rows > 64` gates in `operator*` with a work-based threshold (and a static schedule); benchmark before/after on a CPU training pass.
- [x] Add runtime ISA dispatch for the multiply (an AVX2/FMA kernel compiled with `__attribute__((target("avx2,fma")))`, selected once via the existing `adai::simd` CPUID helpers), so `portable` binaries use it on capable CPUs; extend the same to the element-wise ops if worthwhile.
- [x] Add a test that runs the multiply with OpenMP threads on a ≤ 64-row shape and compares against the scalar reference.

Location in code: `src/Matrix.cpp` (`operator*`'s OpenMP pragmas); `src/MatrixSIMD.hpp` (compile-time detection); tagged `TODO: See TD-434`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/Matrix.cpp`
- `src/MatrixSIMD.hpp`
- `tests/matrix_simd_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 20, 2026).**
- **Tiling and threading:** `operator*`'s CPU path computes tiles of one row × 256 output columns, with
  `#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)` over the tiles when the product has more than 2¹⁸ multiply-adds. A
  product with few rows (a training sample, a decode step, even one row) therefore splits across threads by
  column block. Every output element still sums over k in order, so the result doesn't depend on the tiling or
  the thread count.
- **Runtime ISA dispatch:** the tile kernel is an AVX2/FMA kernel compiled with
  `__attribute__((target("avx2,fma")))` into every x86 GCC/Clang build, chosen once per process with the new
  `adai::simd::cpu_supports_avx2_fma()`. That check also confirms OS support (OSXSAVE and XGETBV), the gap
  TD-437 notes in `has_avx2()`. `portable` binaries now use the kernel on capable CPUs. ARM keeps NEON.
- **Fallback:** the generic kernel is a contiguous ikj loop the compiler vectorizes, replacing the strided ijk
  loop.
- **Override and query:** `ADAI_MATMUL_KERNEL=generic` forces the generic kernel (for tests, or a CPU the
  detection gets wrong), and `Matrix::cpu_matmul_kernel()` reports the kernel in use.
- **Element-wise ops:** left compile-time only (still no SIMD in `portable` builds); the multiply dominates.

Measured (8-core dev machine, idle, best of 7; native → after, portable → after):

| Shape | Native before | Native after | Portable before | Portable after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64×512×512 | 2.31 ms | 0.48 ms | 23.6 ms | 0.53 ms |
| 64×512×2048 | 15.4 ms | 2.7 ms | 161 ms | 2.6 ms |
| 8×512×8000 | 10.4 ms | 1.9 ms | 88.9 ms | 1.9 ms |
| 1×512×8000 | 1.19 ms | 0.96 ms | 8.7 ms | 0.96 ms |
| 300×512×2048 | 15.7 ms | 16.9 ms | 108 ms | 16.6 ms |

The one-row case is memory-bound (it streams 16 MB of weights once). The 300-row case was already threaded.

Tests (`matrix_simd_test.cpp`):
- `MatrixTiledMulTest` compares short products above the threading gate (1×512×2000, 8×512×700, 64×512×513, …)
  with the scalar reference.
- `ResultDoesNotDependOnThreadCount` requires a bit-identical result with 1 thread and with all of them.
- `KernelMatchesTheCpuAndTheOverride` checks the kernel choice.
- A second ctest entry, `MatrixSIMDTestsGenericKernel`, runs the suite with the generic kernel forced.

All pass in the debug, `portable` (Release, `-march=x86-64`) and icpx SYCL trees, in both kernel modes. The CUDA
build compiles. A before/after real CPU training pass is not yet timed.

### TD-427: LeJEPA `Predictor` Is Never Saved, So Each Pass Restarts It

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 20, 2026 | World Model / LeJEPAEncoder | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 14, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `LeJEPAEncoder` and verified. `save()` writes `config.bin`, the token embedding,
the encoder blocks and the final norm, but not the `Predictor` (which has no save/load of its own).
`incremental_trainer --objective=lejepa` resumes the encoder from `<SESSION_DIR>/world_model` every pass
(TD-184) but constructs a fresh, randomly initialized predictor. After 60 epochs, the trained instance's
predictor loss was 0.0017; the same weights reloaded through `save()`/`load()` gave 2.053. Each pass
re-learns the predictor from scratch, and until it does, the random predictor's gradients flow into the
resumed encoder through the context view, disturbing the learned representation. The dashboard's
predictor-loss curve (stable `lejepa-<model>` session) restarts from about 2.0 each pass for this reason.

Action Items:

- [x] Add `Predictor::save()/load()` (it's a `FeedForward`) and include it in `LeJEPAEncoder::save()/load()`, tolerating its absence in older checkpoints with a warning.
- [x] Test: predictor loss is unchanged across save/load.

Location in code: `src/LeJEPAEncoder.cpp` (`save()`, `load()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-427`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/LeJEPAEncoder.cpp`
- `src/Predictor.{hpp,cpp}`
- `tests/lejepaencoder_test.cpp`

**Fix (October 20, 2026).**
- **Predictor persistence:** `Predictor::save()`/`load()` write and read the wrapped `FeedForward`'s weights.
  - `load()` returns false when the file is missing.
  - It throws when the file has a different shape, or is the wrong size, checked before any weights are read: a truncated
    file can't load partway (TD-369).
- **Encoder checkpoint:** `LeJEPAEncoder::save()` writes `predictor.bin` beside the encoder files, and `load()` restores it.
  A checkpoint from before this fix (no `predictor.bin`), or an unreadable predictor file, logs a warning and keeps a fresh
  predictor rather than failing the load. `get_predictor()` exposes it.

Tests:
- `predictor_test.cpp`:
  - a save/load round trip gives identical outputs;
  - a missing file returns false;
  - truncated and wrong-shape files throw and leave the weights unchanged.
- `lejepaencoder_test.cpp`:
  - `SaveAndLoadRestoreThePredictor`: identical predictor output after load. The old `save()`/`load()` fail it: no
    `predictor.bin`, and an output difference of 0.29.
  - `LoadOfACheckpointWithoutAPredictorStillLoads`.

Real passes: three consecutive `--objective=lejepa` passes from the same pre-fix checkpoint (SYCL build, oneAPI CPU device):
- the old binary's average predictor loss didn't improve (0.994, 0.667, 1.124);
- the new one's first pass warned and started fresh (1.072), then resumed (0.328, 0.217).

### TD-342: KV-Cached Generation and the GPU Path Skip the Gated Paths

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 20, 2026 | Transformer / DecoderBlock | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-341, by inspection (documented in the class header). `forward_with_cache()` has no
world-model or memory parameters, and its no-cache fallback calls `forward()` without them, so every
KV-cached generation strategy (greedy, sampling, …) ignores an attached world model and hippocampal
memory; only the non-cached beam branch passes them (TD-186). `gpu_forward()`,
`gpu_forward_with_cache()` and `gpu_backward()` implement only the core sub-layers, and the GPU
upload/download/zero helpers skip the gated sub-layers, so GPU training never trains them either.
Once TD-341 is fixed, inference behaviour will differ by generation strategy and device.

Action Items:

- [x] Thread `world_model_output`/`memory` (and the hippocampal knobs) through `forward_with_cache()` and `LLMDecoder::forward_with_cache()`, caching the world-model K/V like the encoder's.
- [x] Add the gated paths to the GPU forward/backward and the upload/download/zero helpers, or refuse to enable them on GPU with a clear error.

Location in code: `src/DecoderBlock.cpp` (`forward_with_cache()`, GPU functions); tagged `TODO: See TD-342`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DecoderBlock.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/Decoder.cpp`
- `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp`

**Fix (October 20, 2026).** The owner chose the full GPU scope.
- **CPU cached generation:**
  - `DecoderBlock::forward_with_cache()` and `LLMDecoder::forward_with_cache()` take the world-model output, memory and
    hippocampal settings. Both forwards share one helper, `apply_gated_paths()`.
  - The KV-cached `model_fn` in `generate_response()`/`generate_response_with_strategy()` passes them, so greedy and sampling
    decoding use the world model and memory like beam search.
  - The world-model K/V are recomputed each step rather than cached; the sequence is short.
- **Gate kernels:** `gated_residual_add_gpu()`/`gated_residual_backward_gpu()`, in CUDA and SYCL. They read `tanh(gate)` from
  a 1×1 device parameter and accumulate the gate gradient on the device.
- **Decoder block on the GPU:**
  - `gpu_forward()`/`gpu_forward_with_cache()` run both gated paths after the cross-attention residual, and `gpu_backward()`
    backpropagates them in reverse order.
  - The upload, download, collect and zero helpers include the gated sub-layers and both gates. `GPUOptimizer` therefore steps
    them on the device: a gated model has no host groups.
  - `current_gate()`/`current_gate_h()` read the live device values. `ChatbotTrainer`'s per-epoch gate log (TD-341) uses them,
    since the host copies are refreshed only at checkpoints.
- **Hippocampal path on the GPU:**
  - `CrossAttention::gpu_forward()` takes an optional score bias (added after scaling, before the mask, as
    `forward_with_scores()`), and `gpu_last_mean_attention_weights()` downloads the mean attention weights.
  - The coverage and association state stays in `HippocampalMemory` on the host. Each call uploads the keys and score bias
    and downloads the weights; both are small.
  - The bias and the update are shared with the CPU path (`hippocampal_score_bias()`, `update_hippocampal_memory()`).
- **World model on the GPU:** `LeJEPAEncoder::gpu_encode()` runs the frozen world model on the device. Its weights are
  uploaded on first use and again after `load()`. `EncoderDecoderModel` uses it for GPU training (on the decoded input, as
  `forward()`), for GPU generation, and for memory writes when the GPU is active.
- **Memory writes:** GPU generation now writes the response to the memory, as the CPU paths do (TD-185); it never did.

Tests:
- **CPU:** `decoderblock_test.cpp`'s `CachedForwardAppliesTheGatedPaths` (cached equals full forward with both gates open).
- **GPU** (`gpu_optimizer_test.cpp`, on the oneAPI CPU device):
  - the gate kernels against the host formula;
  - the GPU score bias against `forward_with_scores()`;
  - a block's GPU gated forward and backward against the CPU (output, input gradient, both gate gradients, memory coverage);
  - `gpu_encode()` against `encode()`;
  - a gated model training on the device with 0 host groups and opening both gates of every block.
- **Real binaries** (SYCL, CPU device): a LeJEPA pass, then a chatbot pass with the world model and memory attached. All 84
  groups were stepped on the device and the world-model gates opened across two resumed passes.

The memory gates stayed at 0 in that run, because training never writes the memory (only generation does). With nothing to
attend to, the hippocampal path is inactive. That run also found TD-548.

CUDA is compile-checked only.

### TD-545: `incremental_trainer reset` Works on the Legacy Pool, Not the Trainer's Own

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 19, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 19, 2026) |

Description:
Found while rechecking `IncrementalTrainer` after TD-413 (the same root cause). `reset_all()` removed `SESSION_DIR/pending_files.txt` and
`SESSION_DIR/data_registry.txt`, the legacy root pool's files. But `incremental_trainer` always sets `DATASET_KIND` (TD-204), so its local pool is
`SESSION_DIR/<kind>/` (TD-202). So, with a local registry:
- `reset` without `--keep-data` deleted the legacy pool's queue, which isn't the trainer's, and left the trainer's own trained records in place, so
  those files stayed marked trained after a reset;
- `--keep-data` also removed the pending queue before re-queuing the trained entries. Once pointed at the right pool, that would have thrown away
  every queued but untrained file.

Action Items:

- [x] Use the same pool directory `LocalTransport` uses (`DatasetRegistry::local_pool_dir()`), only for a local registry.
- [x] Keep the queue with `--keep-data`; clear it only on a full reset.
- [x] Test both modes against a kind pool next to a legacy pool.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).**
- **Shared pool directory:** the new `DatasetRegistry::local_pool_dir(cfg)` is used by both the transport factory and `reset_all()`. Against
  `registry_server` nothing local is touched.
- **Queue kept with `--keep-data`:** the queue is removed only without `--keep-data`.
- **Fresh weights forget the old state:** `reset_model_for_config()` also clears the loaded checkpoint's training-state path (TD-269), since fresh
  weights shouldn't inherit old optimizer moments.
- **Test:** `ResetWorksOnTheTrainersOwnPoolAndKeepDataKeepsTheQueue` failed three ways on the old code: the legacy queue was deleted, the full reset
  left the kind pool's queue, and the legacy file was gone again.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`reset_all()`, `reset_model_for_config()`), `src/DatasetRegistry.{hpp,cpp}` (`local_pool_dir()`).

### TD-544: `EncoderDecoderModel::clone()` Leaves Its Temp Checkpoint Files Behind

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 19, 2026 | Model / EncoderDecoderModel | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 19, 2026) |

Description:
Found while rechecking `EncoderDecoderModel` after TD-358/361/538. `clone()` saves the model to a temp checkpoint in the system temp directory and
loads it back. It then removed only the five top-level files (`.config`, `.vocab`, `.encoder`, `.decoder`, `.lm_head`), but `save_model()` also
writes a component file per embedding, block and norm. So every clone left a copy of the model's weights behind. `ChatbotTrainer` clones once per
epoch for the async BLEU/ROUGE metrics, so a long run with quality metrics on fills the temp directory with full-size weight copies. This machine's
`/tmp` held 115 clones' worth (4.6 MB) from test runs alone.

Action Items:

- [x] Remove every file of the temp checkpoint (`<tmp>.…` and `<tmp>_…`), as `IncrementalTrainer::checkpoint_files()` does.
- [x] Test: a clone leaves no files in the temp directory.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).** `clone()`'s cleanup removes every file in the temp directory whose name starts with the temp checkpoint's name followed
by `.` or `_`. Another clone's files can't match, since their names differ before that character. `CloneLeavesNoTempFiles` points `TMPDIR` at a
fresh folder and clones a one-layer model. The old code left 11 files and the new one none. Existing leftovers (`/tmp/adai_clone_*`) can be deleted by
hand.

Location in code: `src/EncoderDecoderModel.cpp` (`clone()`).

### TD-542: `dataset_manager segment` Keeps a Queued Whole-File Entry, So Its Pairs Train Twice

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 19, 2026 | Data / dataset_manager CLI | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 19, 2026) |

Description:
Found while checking TD-326's fix with the real binary: `dataset_manager add f.jsonl` then `dataset_manager segment f.jsonl --count 3` left four
pending entries, the whole file plus three segments. Training that pool trains every pair twice. `segment` neither removes the whole-file entry nor
warns about it. Segmenting a file that isn't queued yet (the documented flow) is fine. The Android dashboard's "Create segments" dialog mirrors the
command's sequencing (`RegistryRepository.createSegments()`), so it likely has the same gap.

Action Items:

- [x] Owner decision (October 19, 2026): the segments replace an unclaimed whole-file entry.
- [x] Apply the same rule in the Android `createSegments()`; refuse when the whole-file entry is claimed by a run.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).** `dataset_manager segment` and the Android `RegistryRepository.createSegments()` now follow the same steps:
- They look for a whole-file pending entry of the path first. If a run has claimed it, or the path already has trained records (the whole-path
  delete would erase them), they refuse before queuing anything.
- After adding the segments, they delete the unclaimed whole entry (`force=false`, so a claim taken in between makes the delete fail) and give
  the segments its model assignment.
- If that delete doesn't remove exactly one entry, the new segments are deleted again, so the file is never left queued both ways.

`createSegments()` now returns a `SegmentsResult` (`created`, `replacedWhole`, `error`), and the confirm dialog shows the extra delete call.

Verified with the real binaries, locally and against a `registry_server`. A whole entry assigned to `m1` became two or three segments assigned to
`m1`, with no whole entry left. An entry claimed by `run-01` was refused, and nothing was queued. Five Android repository tests cover the plain
path, the replacement, both refusals and the rollback. All 126 opsdashboard unit tests pass. The command still has no unit tests of its own
(TD-331).

Location in code: `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp` (`segment`), `android/opsdashboard/…/RegistryRepository.kt` (`createSegments()`).

Files to Modify:

- `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp`
- `android/opsdashboard/src/main/java/com/adai/ops/data/registry/RegistryRepository.kt`

### TD-541: A Pass Without Validation Data Has Its Checkpoint Discarded

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 19, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 19, 2026) |

Description:
Found while testing TD-269 (a one-pair pass's checkpoint wasn't resumed from). `ChatbotTrainer` reports a validation loss of 0 when there is no
validation data, which happens with `VALIDATION_SPLIT=0` or when a pass has fewer pairs than the split ratio (fewer than 10 at the default).
`IncrementalTrainer::is_sane_checkpoint_candidate()` rejects any `final_validation_loss <= 0` as "never measured". So that session is never
resumed from (TD-405's rule skips it), and `cleanup_dead_sessions()` removes it from the history and deletes its checkpoint at the next start. Its
training is lost, while its files are already marked trained.

Action Items:

- [x] Record "no validation" explicitly (for example NaN or a flag in the session record) instead of 0, and treat such a session as resumable
  under the most-recent rule; keep excluding it only from lowest-loss selection.
- [x] Test: a pass with no validation split is resumed by the next pass and survives cleanup.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).** A completed pass whose `ChatbotTrainer` recorded no validation loss now stores `TrainingSession::kNoValidationLoss`
(-1) instead of 0. The value round-trips through `session_history.txt` unchanged. 0 still means an in-progress session, and NaN still means a
diverged one.
- `is_sane_checkpoint_candidate()` accepts -1, so the session is resumed under the most-recent rule and survives `cleanup_dead_sessions()`.
- `has_validation_loss()` keeps it out of every lowest-loss choice: `RESUME_FROM_BEST_CHECKPOINT`, the best checkpoint picked at startup and
  after cleanup, and `update_best_checkpoint()`. That last one now takes an unmeasured pass as "best" only when no best exists yet, and never
  records -1 as the loss to beat.
- Other changes:
  - the MNS candidate summary leaves out `final_val_loss` for such a pass;
  - `history` and the trainer summary show "n/a" instead of a loss.

Verified: the new `PassWithoutValidationIsResumedAndSurvivesCleanup` test, a 2-pair pass, failed against the old code. Its validation loss was
0, and the next trainer's history was empty. With the fix it passes, and with `RESUME_FROM_BEST_CHECKPOINT=true` the session is still not
picked.

Not changed: the per-epoch callback still records 0 for the validation loss of an epoch without validation data, in the per-epoch arrays and
the MNS progress `best_loss`. These are reporting values only; they don't affect checkpoint selection.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`is_sane_checkpoint_candidate()`, `finalize_session()`), `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp` (validation
loss with no validation data).

Files to Modify:

- `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
- `tests/incrementaltrainer_test.cpp`

### TD-523: `trainer_service` Can't Tell a Failing Pass From an Idle One

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 19, 2026 | Training / Service Supervisor | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainerServiceMain.cpp` (see [TrainerServiceMain.md](../reference/source/TrainerServiceMain.md)); verified with the real binary and a
stub `incremental_trainer` that printed an error and exited 1. The supervisor treats exit 0 as "did work" and every other code as "nothing to do",
counting only codes other than 0/1 as crashes. `incremental_trainer resume` returns 1 when `resume_last_session()` returns false, which covers an empty
queue **and** a missing checkpoint, a failed `load_model()` and a failed `train_on_files()`. With the stub, `/admin/status` showed `"phase":"idle"`,
`"total_passes_crashed":0`, `"last_exit_code":1` (identical to a healthy idle service) and nothing reached `trainer_service`'s log. A corrupt checkpoint
or unreadable dataset therefore becomes a silent retry every 45 s: each attempt claims the pending files, fails and releases them (TD-333 leaves segments
stuck), indefinitely, while the dashboard shows an idle trainer.

Action Items:

- [x] Give `resume` distinct exit codes (e.g. 0 did work, 3 nothing pending, 1 failed) and have the supervisor count failures separately, log them, expose a `total_passes_failed`/`last_failure` field in `/admin/status`, and back off on consecutive failures.
- [x] Test the supervisor's handling of each exit code with a stub child.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).**
- **Distinct results:** `IncrementalTrainer::resume_last_session()` now returns `ResumeResult::Trained`, `NothingPending` or `Failed`.
  `resume` exits 0, 3 or 1 to match (`kResumeExit*` in `IncrementalTrainerArgs.hpp`).
- **Unreachable registry:** an unreachable registry (or a local lock failure) now sets a new `AcquireResponse::failed` flag. So a registry
  outage is a failure, not "nothing pending".
- **Supervisor:** `trainer_service` classifies each exit with `classify_pass_exit()`:
  - 0 trained; 3 idle; 128 and up crashed (a signal death);
  - anything else failed, including 127 for an exec failure.
- **On a failure or crash** it:
  - logs an error with the exit code;
  - counts it;
  - waits `failure_backoff_seconds()`: the 45 s poll interval, doubled for each consecutive failure up to 15 minutes. `POST /admin/resume`
    still wakes it at once.
- **`/admin/status`** gains `total_passes_failed`, `consecutive_failures` and `last_failure_unix`. `total_passes_crashed` now counts only
  signal deaths.

Verified:
- **Unit tests:** `ResumeReportsNothingPendingSeparatelyFromFailure` (empty local queue, then an unreachable registry), the exit-code
  classification and backoff tests.
- **Real `trainer_service` with a stub `incremental_trainer`:**
  - **exit 1:** `total_passes_failed: 1`, `consecutive_failures: 1`, `last_failure_unix` set, and a "training pass failed with exit code 1"
    error in its log;
  - **exit 3:** idle, with no failure recorded.

Location in code: `src/TrainerServiceMain.cpp` (exit-code handling), `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (`resume`'s `return 1`); tagged `TODO: See TD-523`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/TrainerServiceMain.cpp`
- `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`
- `src/TrainerServiceControlState.hpp`
- `src/TrainerServiceProxy.cpp`

### TD-519: Trainer Admin PUT Reads a Spaced `true` as False and Disables Auto-Save

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 19, 2026 | Training / Admin API | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `TrainerAdminAPI.cpp` (see [TrainerAdminAPI.md](../reference/source/TrainerAdminAPI.md)); verified against the real server.
`json_bool()` compares the four characters immediately after `"auto_save_enabled":` with `true`, so a space after the colon reads as false.
`PUT /admin/config {"auto_save_enabled": true}` (Python `json.dumps`' default formatting, and common in hand-typed `curl` bodies) answered
`"auto_save_enabled":false` and persisted that to `daemon_config.db`, so every later pass runs without auto-save; the compact form works.
`TrainerServiceProxy::handle_put_config_idle()` copies the same helper, so the request has the same effect when no child is running. (The integer keys
work: `stoi` skips leading whitespace. The Android dashboard sends compact JSON.)

Action Items:

- [x] Parse request bodies with the vendored `nlohmann/json` (with TD-453), rejecting non-boolean values with 400.
- [x] Test whitespace and pretty-printed bodies, in both handlers.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).** Both handlers now call one shared parser, `parse_trainer_admin_config()` (`src/TrainerAdminConfig.{hpp,cpp}`, in
`adai_core`), which reads the body with the vendored `nlohmann/json`.
- Any valid JSON spacing works. `auto_save_enabled` must be a JSON boolean, and the three counts must be integers in range.
- These are rejected with 400: malformed JSON, a body that isn't an object, the immutable keys, and a body with no mutable key.
- The whole body is validated before anything is applied or persisted, which also fixes TD-305's validate-first half for this endpoint.
- The old substring helpers (`json_int()`, `json_bool()`, `json_has_key()`) are removed from both files.

Verified:
- **Against the old handlers:** the new HTTP tests failed in both suites.
  - The live API with `"auto_save_enabled": true` left auto-save off.
  - A body rejected on its third key had already applied the first two.
  - The idle proxy wrote `false` for a spaced `true`.
- **With the fix:** they pass, along with `TrainerAdminConfigTests` (3 cases), `TrainerAdminAPITests` (16) and `TrainerServiceProxyTests` (18).

queue training data." Queuing without `--kind` passes the check, but the child's acquire looks in the

the same kind sub-pool the pass acquires from (`SESSION_DIR/<kind>/` locally). The new `DatasetRegistry::count_acquirable()` counts only
pending entries this model may claim: unassigned ones, plus ones assigned to `MODEL_NAME`, the same rule as `acquire()`. The remote check
used to count every pending entry, including other models'. The "no pending data" message now names the pool.

### TD-338: `DataTransport` Reuses Same-Size Stale Files Without Checking the Checksum

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 19, 2026 | Data / DataTransport | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-337 and confirmed end-to-end. "Condition B" returns an existing local file
whenever its size equals `token.size_bytes`, without downloading. A planted same-name, same-size file
of different content (all `Z` bytes) was returned and would have been trained, although the token
carried `checksum = "15769547_<mtime>"`, which would have caught it. The trainer's startup sweep
keeps non-empty files, so a stale copy survives across passes. Triggers include a dataset re-uploaded
under the same name with a size-preserving edit, and TD-337's basename collisions.

Action Items:

- [x] Store the token checksum alongside each download (e.g. a sidecar file) and skip only when it matches; otherwise re-download.
- [x] Test: same-size different-checksum file is re-downloaded.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).**
- **Sidecar:** `fetch()` writes the token checksum to `<download>.checksum` before the transfer starts.
- **Reuse check:** when the token has a checksum, an existing file (complete or partial) is reused or resumed only if its sidecar holds
  that same checksum. A missing or different sidecar deletes the file and downloads it again. A token without a checksum keeps the old
  size-only check.
- **Removal:** failed and mismatched downloads remove the sidecar too. `startup_sweep()` removes a sidecar with its download, or on its own
  once the download is gone.

Verified against the real `registry_server`:
- **New code:** a rerun reused the download (`[CLEANUP-B]`, no connection). After a same-size edit to the server's file, the next fetch
  logged "doesn't match the registry's checksum" and downloaded the new content.
- **Old code:** with a locally edited same-size copy, it skipped the download for all three tokens and kept the edited bytes.
- **Tests:** `SameSizeFileWithDifferentChecksumIsDownloadedAgain`, and the sweep's sidecar cases in
  `TrainedFileWithSameBasenameDoesNotDeleteAPendingDownload`.

Location in code: `src/DataTransport.hpp` (`fetch()` Condition B); tagged `TODO: See TD-338`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DataTransport.hpp`
- `tests/DataTransportFtpTests.cpp`

### TD-337: `DataTransport` Names Downloads by Basename, So Segments and Same-Named Files Collide

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 19, 2026 | Data / DataTransport | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [DataTransport.md](../reference/source/DataTransport.md) and confirmed end-to-end on loopback
(local `registry_server` with FTP enabled, a 15.8 MB file split into three TD-205 segments).
`fetch()` saves to `download_dir / filename(token.ftp_path)`:

- **Segments download the whole file N times, concurrently, to one path.** All three segment tokens
  had the same `ftp_path` and full-file `size_bytes`; `fetch_all()` sent all three to `dl/big.jsonl`
  in parallel, transferring the full 15.8 MB three times. The file was intact in 20 runs (identical
  bytes), but each thread opens with `trunc` and **deletes the file on a size mismatch**, so one
  thread's final check can delete another's in-progress download and fail the pass.
- **Different files with the same basename collide**, e.g. `<group>/uploads/x.jsonl` vs
  `<group>/datasets/x.jsonl`, or two kinds' sub-pools sharing one `download_dir`.

The `UsesBasenameOfFtpPath` test pins the basename behaviour.

Action Items:

- [x] Name local files from the full `ftp_path` (or a hash of it).
- [x] Deduplicate tokens by `ftp_path` in `fetch_all()` (download once, return the path for each segment token).
- [x] Tests: three segment tokens of one file trigger one download; same-basename files in different directories don't collide.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).**
- **Naming:** a download is named `download_file_name(registry_path)` (`RegistryTransport.hpp`): a 16-hex-digit FNV-1a hash of the full
  registry path, then `_` and the basename. The registry path is used rather than `ftp_path` because it is all `startup_sweep()` knows, so
  the sweep matches downloads by the same name, which also fixes TD-513's basename matching.
- **One download per file:** `fetch_all()` downloads each distinct local file once and returns that path for every token of it.
- **Cleanup:** the trainer's `cleanup_downloads()` tolerates the repeated path and removes TD-338's sidecar.
- **Upgrade:** downloads made under the old basename names look orphaned to the first sweep after an upgrade, and are deleted and fetched
  once more.

Verified against a real `registry_server --ftp-enabled`, with a 13 MB file queued as three segments:
- the old `DataTransport` made 3 `RETR`s into one `big.jsonl`;
- the new one made 1 `RETR`, and all three tokens got `909f16ee7ce07427_big.jsonl`.

Unit tests:
- `SegmentTokensOfOneFileDownloadOnce` (with no server listening, only a single shared request can succeed);
- `SameBasenameInDifferentDirectoriesDoesNotCollide`;
- the updated Condition B and `fetch_all()` tests (the pinned `UsesBasenameOfFtpPath` test is replaced).

Location in code: `src/DataTransport.hpp` (`fetch()` local path, `fetch_all()`); tagged `TODO: See TD-337`.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DataTransport.hpp`
- `tests/DataTransportFtpTests.cpp`

### TD-334: Trained Sample Counts Are Always Zero

|-----------------|-----------|-------------|

Description:
Found alongside TD-333, by inspection of every production call site. Each `mark_trained()` call
passes `std::vector<int> counts(n, 0)` (trainer, retrain, LeJEPA, `resume_last_session()`), so every
`DataVersion::num_samples` is 0 and `total_samples_trained()` (`dataset_manager status`'s
"Samples: N total trained") always reports 0. The trainer has the real per-file pair counts (it loads
them in `train_on_files()`); they're just not passed back.

Action Items:

- [x] Return per-file (per-segment) pair counts from `train_on_files()`/`retrain_on_files()` and pass them to `mark_trained()`.

**Fix (October 19, 2026).** `IncrementalTrainer::load_training_pairs()` records how many pairs each file contributed (a segment counts only its

- `train` and `resume_last_session()` pass them directly;
- `retrain` passes the trailing pending files' counts, since the trained files come first in its file list;
- the LeJEPA pass counts the pairs it loads per file.

Pairs that preprocessing later skips are still counted. The counts reach `registry_server` through the existing `trained` request.

Verified:

### TD-333: Segment Claims Aren't Released on Failure and Trained Records Ignore Segments

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 19, 2026 | Data / DatasetRegistry | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [DatasetRegistry.md](../reference/source/DatasetRegistry.md) and confirmed by running the real class
against a scratch `LocalTransport` pool (one 30-pair file split into three TD-205 segments).
`acquire_pending()` hands out segments correctly, but every production caller
(`IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`'s train/resume/retrain/LeJEPA paths and
`IncrementalTrainer::resume_last_session()`) then calls `mark_trained()`/`release_pending()` with
**bare paths** (`resp.registry_paths()`):

- **Failure doesn't release segments.** Since TD-205, a bare path releases only whole-file entries.
  `release_pending("run-A", {path})` left the segment **claimed by `run-A`**, and a pass with a
  different `run_id` couldn't acquire it. The same `run_id` can reclaim its own claims, so an MNS
  `resume` recovers. But after a `retrain` (new MNS run), or in standalone mode (run ID from
  hostname + PID, new every pass), the segment stays stuck until released by hand.
- **Success is recorded per path.** Training two segments of one file produced **one** trained
  file with 10 samples (`build_new_versions()` skips a path already in `trained_set_`), and the whole
  path now counts as trained, so re-queuing any segment of it is **rejected**. Segments trained in
  separate passes can't all be recorded.

`registry_server`'s release/trained handlers follow the same path-keyed rules.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 19, 2026:**
- **Record format:** `DataVersion` has `segment_start`/`segment_count` (-1 = whole file). `trained_matches()` is its identity check. The local
  registry file gains two trailing columns, and older lines without them still load as whole-file records. `GET …/registry` adds two JSON fields,
  and an absent field means whole file.
- **Registry API:** `DatasetRegistry` has `mark_trained(run_id, units, counts)` and `release_pending(run_id, units)` overloads taking the
  acquired `PendingFileRange`s. Every production caller (train, retrain, LeJEPA, failure releases, `resume_last_session()`) now passes
  `resp.file_ranges()`.
  - `build_new_versions()` records one entry per unit, so segments trained in separate passes each keep their sample count.
  - `is_trained(path, seg…)` is segment-aware. A whole-file query is still true if any part was trained.
- **Releasing:** `LocalTransport::release()` and `registry_server`'s release apply whole-file paths and segments together. They used to do one or
  the other.
- **Committing:** `commit_trained()` takes an optional segment list (exact mode). `RemoteTransport` sends aligned `segment_starts`/`segment_counts`,
  and `registry_server` records per unit and removes exactly those pending entries. Requests without the arrays keep the old path-wide behaviour,
  for older clients.
- **Delete and re-queue:** a whole-file target removes every record of the path, and a segment target removes just its record. `requeue_trained()`
  restores each trained segment as that segment (TD-540's last limitation).
- **Startup sweep:** it keeps the download of a file that is trained in part but still has pending segments.
- **Empty checksums:** the registry file writes `-` for an empty checksum, so the later columns can't shift.

Tests:
- `ReleasingAnAcquiredBatchFreesItsSegments`;
- `SegmentsTrainedSeparatelyAreEachRecorded` (two records, 10 + 7 samples, per-segment `is_trained`, segment-preserving re-queue);
- `LocalTransportSegmentRecordTest` (format round trip and legacy lines);
- `LiveRegistryTest.RemoteTransportCommitsAndReleasesExactSegments`, run against a real `registry_server` (all 87 live tests pass).

These tests need the new overloads, so they couldn't be run on the old code; the old behaviour was measured when this entry was filed.

- [x] Pass `FileToken` segment ranges through as `SegmentTarget`s to `release_pending()`/`mark_trained()` from every caller.
- [x] Key trained records by `(path, segment_start, segment_count)` (local registry format, `DataVersion`, `registry_server`), and make `is_trained()` segment-aware.
- [x] Tests: acquire → fail → release frees the segment for another run; training two segments records both, with their sample counts.

Location in code: `src/RegistryTransport.{hpp,cpp}`, `src/RegistryServer.cpp`, `src/DatasetRegistry.{hpp,cpp}`, callers in `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` and `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`, `src/StartupSweep.hpp`; the `TODO: See TD-333` tags are now fix comments.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DatasetRegistry.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/RegistryTransport.{hpp,cpp}`
- `src/RegistryServer.cpp`
- `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp`
- `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
- `tests/DatasetRegistryTests.cpp`

### TD-326: `dataset_manager migrate` Duplicates Segmented Data Across Pools

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 19, 2026 | Data / dataset_manager CLI | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 11, 2026) |

Description:
Found while writing the code-traced reference [DatasetManagerTool.md](../reference/source/DatasetManagerTool.md) and confirmed by running the real
binary against a scratch local pool. `migrate` copies each legacy entry with
`dest.add_pending_path_unchecked(entry.path)`, which **drops `segment_start`/`segment_count`**
(TD-205), then calls `source.delete_entries({entry.path}, …)` and `dest.assign_model(…)` **without
checking either result**.

Migrating a 30-pair file split into 3 segments:
- the `chatbot` pool got the **whole file** (all 30 pairs);
- the other two segments failed ("already pending");
- the source delete matched nothing (segment-aware identity), so **all 3 segments stayed in the
  legacy pool**;
- it printed "Migrated 1/3".

Training both pools trains every pair twice. Any failed source delete (e.g. a remote error) also
leaves an entry in both pools, and a failed `assign_model()` silently loses the model assignment.
`migrate` is TD-202's one-time upgrade path, so operators run it over their whole legacy pool.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 19, 2026:** `migrate` now moves each entry exactly.
- A file target takes every entry of that file.
- Each entry is added with its segment range, its model assignment is restored by segment, and the source entry is deleted by
  `(path, segment_start, segment_count)`.
- If the assignment or the source delete fails, the destination copy is rolled back and the entry isn't counted, so nothing is left in both pools.
  The result line counts entries.

Checked with the real binary on a scratch local pool holding a 30-pair file's whole-file entry and its 3 segments: all 4 moved with their ranges
(`Migrated 4/4 entries`), and the legacy pool ended empty.

There are still no command-level unit tests (TD-331). The run also showed TD-542: `segment` keeps an already-queued whole-file entry.

- [x] Carry `segment_start`/`segment_count` into `add_pending_path_unchecked()` and match/delete source entries by `(path, segment_start, segment_count)` (TD-205's `SegmentTarget`).
- [x] Check `delete_entries()`/`assign_model()` results; on failure, roll back the destination add (or report clearly) and don't count the entry as migrated.
- [x] Test: migrating a segmented file moves exactly its segments and leaves the source empty. (Checked end to end with the real binary; no unit test, TD-331.)

Location in code: `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp` (`migrate`); the `TODO: See TD-326` tags are now fix comments.

Files to Modify:

- `src/DatasetManagerTool.cpp`
- `src/DatasetRegistry.{hpp,cpp}`
- tests (new CLI-level test)

**Android follow-up (October 19, 2026).** The dashboard's `RegistryRepository.migrateToKind()` already carried the segment range but still ignored
its assign and delete results and returned success. It now checks both like the CLI and removes the destination copy on failure. New unit tests:
`migrateToKind removes the destination copy and fails when the legacy delete fails` and `… keeps the source when the assign fails`.

### TD-270: Adaptive Gradient Clipping Resets Every Epoch

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 19, 2026 | Training / ChatbotTrainer | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 9, 2026) |

Description:
Found alongside TD-267. The TD-017 adaptive-clipping state (`agc_ema`, `agc_step_count`,
`agc_spike_count`) is declared locally in `train_epoch()`, so each epoch restarts it: a new
`gradient_clip_warmup_steps` (default 100) warmup clipped at `gradient_clip_max` (5.0), with the EMA
re-seeded from `gradient_clip_norm`. With ≤ 100 optimizer steps per epoch (common for small passes
or large accumulation windows) **adaptive clipping never leaves warmup**, so enabling it just clips at
the 5.0 ceiling.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 19, 2026 (with TD-269):** `agc_ema_` and `agc_step_count_` are `ChatbotTrainer` members. They are initialized once, not
per epoch, and saved and restored with the training state, so they also carry across passes of a run. The per-epoch metrics (spike count,
average clip) stay per epoch. New test `AdaptiveClippingStateCarriesAcrossEpochs`: after 3 epochs of 2 steps, the clip warmup counter is 6.

- [x] Move the adaptive-clip state to `ChatbotTrainer` members (initialized once per `train()` call, or once per run alongside TD-269).
- [x] Test: the EMA and warmup counter carry across epochs.

Location in code: `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp` (`train_epoch()`); the `TODO: See TD-270` tag is now a fix comment.

### TD-539: `IncrementalTrainer` Constructors Never Load a Checkpoint

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 18, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 18, 2026) |

Description:
Found while fixing TD-405; verified. All three `IncrementalTrainer` constructors chose a checkpoint from session history and then loaded it only
`if (fs::exists(best_checkpoint_path))`. That tests the bare checkpoint path, which `EncoderDecoderModel::save_model()` never writes (only
`<path>.config`, `.vocab`, `.encoder`, `.decoder`, `.lm_head`; see TD-408). So with real checkpoints the constructors never loaded anything.

`resume_last_session()` checks `<path>.config` and does load, so `trainer_service` passes resumed (from the best-ever checkpoint, TD-405). But
`incremental_trainer train`/`retrain` call `train_on_files()`, which doesn't load either, so every such pass trained from freshly initialized
weights. The existing tests didn't notice because their stand-in checkpoints also create the bare file.

Verified with the real class and real `save_model()` checkpoints: a trainer constructed over two sessions matched neither checkpoint's weights.

**Fix landed October 18, 2026 (with TD-405):** the constructors share `init_from_session_history()`, which loads `select_resume_checkpoint()`.
That only returns sessions whose sidecars all exist (`is_sane_checkpoint_candidate()`). The new test
`IncrementalTrainerTest.ResumesFromMostRecentSessionNotLowestValidationLoss` uses real checkpoints, which have no bare file.

Action Items:

- [x] Test with real `save_model()` checkpoints.

### TD-512: Startup Sweep Deletes Every Download Because the Pending List Is Never Loaded

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 18, 2026 | Training / StartupSweep | Code fix (HIGH, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `StartupSweep.hpp` (see [StartupSweep.md](../reference/source/StartupSweep.md)); verified with the real classes.
`startup_sweep()` classifies `DOWNLOAD_DIR` files against `reg.pending_files()`, which returns `DatasetRegistry`'s in-memory `pending_` filled only by
`load_pending_list()`. All three call sites in `IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (`train`, `retrain`, `--objective=lejepa`) construct a fresh
`DatasetRegistry`, call **only `load_registry()`**, then sweep. Reproducing that sequence with two queued files (one partially, one fully downloaded) and
an operator's `notes.txt` in `downloads/`: the sweep saw 0 pending files and deleted all three as "orphaned" (condition G); with `load_pending_list()`
both downloads were kept. So conditions A/B/C never run: every pass deletes every completed and partial download (re-downloaded in full; resume never
happens) and anything else in `DOWNLOAD_DIR`. By inspection, a registry that can't be reached gives the same empty state and the same wipe. The tests
populate the pending list on the instance they sweep, so they pass.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** `startup_sweep()` now loads the pending list and the trained registry itself.
- **Pending list can't be loaded** (unreachable registry, or no pending list yet): it skips the sweep entirely, because without that list every
  file would look orphaned.
- **Trained registry can't be loaded:** it continues with an empty trained set, so nothing is deleted as already trained on missing information.

The `resume` command (every `trainer_service` pass, which downloads since TD-411) now runs the sweep too. New tests:
- `FreshRegistryKeepsQueuedDownloads`: production's call sequence, with a partial and a complete queued download kept;
- `UnreadablePendingListDeletesNothing`.

Both fail with the old sweep. The condition D/G tests now create an empty pending list, so "nothing pending" is actually known.

- [x] Call `reg.load_pending_list()` before `startup_sweep()` at all three call sites (or have `startup_sweep()` load it).
- [x] Skip all deletion when either load fails. (Skipped entirely when the pending list fails; a failed trained-registry load only disables condition D.)
- [x] Add a test that sweeps a freshly constructed registry, as production does.

Location in code: `src/StartupSweep.hpp`, `src/IncrementalTrainingTool.cpp` (call sites, plus the new one in `resume`); the `TODO: See TD-512` tags are now fix comments.

### TD-412: A Training Pass That Loads Zero Samples Marks Its Files Trained

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 18, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainingTool | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainingTool` and verified with `IncrementalTrainer` in a scratch
program. `ChatbotTrainer::train()` has no empty-data check, and neither do `train_on_files()` or
`retrain_on_files()`. Given a nonexistent file, the pass logged `Cannot open file`, `Total samples
loaded: 0`, `Training for 2 epochs...` and `Incremental training session completed successfully`, and
`train_on_files()` **returned `true`**. Every caller then calls `mark_trained()`, so a missing,
unreadable or empty file (or every file in a TD-411 remote-FTP `resume` pass) is recorded as trained
without any training, and a zero-sample session is added to the history.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** both `train_on_files()` and `retrain_on_files()` now load through `load_training_pairs()`, which warns about each
file that yields no pairs. If nothing loaded, they return false through `fail_empty_pass()`, which logs the failure and, under the admin API, sets
the phase back to idle; the callers then release the files. `ChatbotTrainer::train()` also returns false when nothing survives tokenization.

Two related changes:
- `initialize_session()` now runs after loading and the first-run vocab bootstrap. A failed pass leaves no zero-sample session, and
  `bootstrap_vocab()`'s `load_session_history()` no longer discards the pass's own entry.
- `retrain_on_files()` no longer divides by zero when `VALIDATION_SPLIT=0`.

New test `PassThatLoadsNothingFails` covers a missing file, an empty file and a retrain over both; it fails on the old code, which returned true
three times and recorded a zero-sample session.

- [x] Treat zero loaded (or zero tokenized) samples as failure in `train_on_files()`/`retrain_on_files()` (and guard in `ChatbotTrainer::train()`), so callers release the files; log which files failed to load.
- [x] Test: a nonexistent file → `false` → released, not marked trained.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`load_training_pairs()`, `fail_empty_pass()`, `train_on_files()`, `retrain_on_files()`), `src/ChatbotTrainer.cpp` (`train()`); the `TODO: See TD-412` tags are now fix comments.

### TD-408: `latest`/`best` Checkpoint Symlinks Always Dangle

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 18, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainer`, by inspection. `create_or_update_symlink()` links
`latest_checkpoint.bin`/`best_checkpoint.bin` (in the working directory) to the **bare** checkpoint path,
which `save_model()` never creates, so the links always dangle. Loading through a link looks for
`best_checkpoint.bin.config`, which isn't a link, so neither can be used as `MODEL_PATH`. On Windows
the fallback `copy_file()` copies the same nonexistent bare file and always fails.

Action Items:

like the checkpoint (usable as `MODEL_PATH`). On Windows the files are copied.

`remove_symlink_if_exists()` now removes every `<link>…` symlink before re-linking. On POSIX it never removes a regular file that only shares the
prefix. The same bare-path mistake is fixed in two more places:
- `cleanup_old_sessions()` re-pointed the latest link only if the bare checkpoint path existed, so it never did; it now checks the checkpoint's
  files.
- `reset_all()`'s model backup renamed the bare `MODEL_PATH`, which never exists; it now moves every file to the base `<MODEL_PATH>.bak`, which
  loads as a checkpoint.

Test: `CheckpointLinksLoadAndRepointCleanly` (loads through the link and matches the weights; re-pointing leaves no stale link).

### TD-407: Checkpoint Deletion Leaks the Per-Layer Weight Files

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 18, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainer` and measured. `EncoderDecoderModel::save_model()` writes
the top-level sidecars (`.config`, `.vocab`, `.encoder`, `.decoder`, `.lm_head`) plus per-layer files
(`_token_emb.bin`, `_encoder_block_<i>.bin` + `_attention.bin`/`_feedforward.bin`,
`_decoder_block_<i>.bin` + `.self_attn`/`.cross_attn`/`.ff`, `_final_norm.bin`), and the per-layer files
hold almost all the weights. `remove_model_files()` deletes only the five top-level sidecars plus
`.metrics.csv`: on a d_model 256, 4 + 4 layer checkpoint it removed **0.1 of 29.6 MB (0.2%)**. Every
retention rotation (`MAX_SESSIONS_TO_KEEP`), superseded best snapshot, broken-session cleanup and
`reset` therefore leaves almost a whole checkpoint behind. `cleanup_dead_sessions()` and
`reset_all()` scan for `*.bin` base files that `save_model()` never writes, so they only match
per-layer files by accident (partially deleting snapshots) and never the attention/FF files. Disk use
in `SESSION_DIR` grows by roughly one checkpoint per pass (plus snapshots and auto-saves) with no
bound.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** every file `save_model(base)` writes is named `base` + `.`… or `base` + `_`…, including TD-538's new encoder
files and `.metrics.csv`. The new `IncrementalTrainer::checkpoint_files(base)` lists a directory by that prefix, so it stays complete whatever
components a checkpoint has. It is used in three places:
- `remove_model_files()` deletes exactly those files.
- `cleanup_dead_sessions()` and `reset_all()` group a session directory's files by checkpoint base (`session_checkpoint_base_of()`) instead of
  scanning for bare `*.bin` files.
- `cleanup_dead_sessions()` also deletes checkpoint remnants whose `.config` is gone, which is what the old partial deletion left behind. So the
  first start after the fix reclaims existing leaked space without a separate command.

New tests, all three failing on the old code:
- `RemoveModelFilesDeletesTheWholeCheckpointOnly` (real checkpoint; `session_10` survives removing `session_1`);
- `CleanupDeadSessionsReclaimsCheckpointRemnants`;
- `CheckpointLinksLoadAndRepointCleanly` (TD-408).

`CleanupDeadSessionsRemovesOrphansAndBrokenHistory`'s stand-in auto-saves now have a `.config`, as real ones do.

- [x] Have `EncoderDecoderModel` expose (or return from `save_model()`) the list of files a checkpoint consists of, and delete exactly those in `remove_model_files()`, `cleanup_dead_sessions()` and `reset_all()`; or save each checkpoint into its own directory and remove the directory. (Done by file-name prefix, which every file `save_model()` writes follows.)
- [x] Add a test that save → remove leaves no files behind; offer a one-off cleanup command for existing session directories (ask the user to check ai-machine's `SESSION_DIR` size). (The cleanup happens automatically on the next start.)

### TD-406: A Paused or Crashed Pass's Checkpoint Is Deleted on the Next Start

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 18, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainer` and verified with the real class. `perform_auto_save()` (sample
cadence, forced `/admin/checkpoint`, and the `/admin/pause` drain path) writes `auto_save_session_N.bin`
and persists session N to `session_history.txt` with `final_validation_loss = 0`. On the next
construction:
1. `current_session_id` becomes N+1, so the in-progress check looks for `session_<N+1>_best.bin`
   and misses session N's best snapshot.
2. `cleanup_dead_sessions()` deletes session N's auto-save as an "orphaned snapshot from a
   crashed/superseded session".
3. It drops session N from the history ("Removing broken session") because its val loss is 0.

Verified: history with session 0 complete and session 1 paused (auto-save plus `session_1_best` on
disk) → the restart loaded session 0, removed session 1 and its auto-save, and left `session_1_best`
on disk unused forever. So TD-173's "pause drains the pass and checkpoints it" produces a checkpoint
the next pass deletes; the released files are retrained from older weights, and crash recovery from
auto-saves never happens.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** `take_interrupted_session()` runs at construction, from `init_from_session_history()`. It recognizes an
interrupted session by its history entry still pointing at `auto_save_session_N.bin` rather than a finalized `session_N_checkpoint.bin`. Then it:
1. picks the newer (by `.config` mtime) of that auto-save and `session_N_best.bin` among those with all five files;
2. sets `current_session_id` back to N, so `cleanup_dead_sessions()` keeps both snapshots;
3. removes the interim entry, which the resumed pass recreates.

The trainer loads that snapshot, and `resume_last_session()` (every `trainer_service` pass) uses it ahead of the TD-405 rule. Pause therefore
produces a checkpoint the next pass actually continues from, and crash recovery from auto-saves works. A session with no loadable snapshot is left
to the old cleanup.

New test `IncrementalTrainerTest.InterruptedSessionResumesFromItsNewestSnapshot` uses real `save_model()` snapshots and covers both newest-snapshot
orders. Against the old code it loaded the wrong weights, moved to session 2 and deleted the auto-save.

- [x] On startup, detect an interrupted session (val loss 0 with an existing auto-save or best snapshot) and resume from its newest snapshot instead of deleting it; keep `current_session_id` aligned or look up the snapshot by the interrupted session's id.
- [x] Only treat snapshots as orphaned when no history entry references their session. (Achieved by keeping `current_session_id` at the interrupted session's id.)
- [x] Test: pause → restart resumes from the paused pass's snapshot. (Restart from a paused pass's persisted state; the pause drain itself is covered by the existing control tests.)

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`take_interrupted_session()`, `init_from_session_history()`, `resume_last_session()`, `perform_auto_save()`); the `TODO: See TD-406` tags are now fix comments.

Files to Modify:

- `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
- `tests/incremental_trainer_control_test.cpp`

### TD-405: Each Training Pass Restarts From the Best-Ever Checkpoint, Not the Latest

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 18, 2026 | Training / IncrementalTrainer | Code fix (**HIGH**, filed October 13, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `IncrementalTrainer` and verified with the real class. All three constructors,
and `resume_last_session()`, load the session with the **lowest `final_validation_loss` across the
whole history**. But each pass's validation loss comes from a validation split of that pass's own
files, so losses from different passes aren't comparable. When a later pass trains on new data whose
validation loss is higher, the next pass starts from the older checkpoint again and the later
learning is discarded, while the registry has already marked those files trained. Verified: with
session 0 (val 1.20) and a newer session 1 (val 2.00), construction logged `Best checkpoint:
…/session_0_checkpoint.bin` and loaded it. In incremental training over a stream of datasets, the
model can stay pinned to one old checkpoint indefinitely; this could explain apparent lack of
progress across ai-machine passes.

Action Items:

**Fix landed October 18, 2026:** `select_resume_checkpoint()` returns the most recent completed session whose checkpoint passes
`is_sane_checkpoint_candidate()`. The new `RESUME_FROM_BEST_CHECKPOINT` key (`config.trainer.conf`, env, `IncrementalConfig`; default false)
selects the lowest-validation-loss session instead.

The constructors (through `init_from_session_history()`) and `resume_last_session()` both use it, and log the chosen checkpoint and the reason.
`best_checkpoint_path` is still tracked for the best symlink. Two more bugs turned up while testing, both fixed in the same change:
- [TD-539](#td-539-incrementaltrainer-constructors-never-load-a-checkpoint): the constructors never actually loaded any checkpoint.
- [TD-538](../guides/TECHNICAL_DEBT.md#td-538-encoder-token-embedding-and-final-norm-are-overwritten-in-every-checkpoint): checkpoints lost the encoder's embedding and final norm.

New test `ResumesFromMostRecentSessionNotLowestValidationLoss` uses real `save_model()` checkpoints. Session 1 is newer with validation loss 2.0,
session 0 older with 1.2; a new trainer matches session 1's weights by default and session 0's with the option set. On the old code it matched
neither.

- [x] Resume from the most recent completed session by default; keep "best" selection as an explicit option (or compare losses only on a fixed, shared validation set).
- [x] Apply the same rule in `resume_last_session()`, and log which checkpoint was chosen and why.
- [x] Test: two sessions where the newer has higher validation loss → the newer is resumed.

Location in code: `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp` (`select_resume_checkpoint()`, `init_from_session_history()`, `resume_last_session()`), `src/Config.{hpp,cpp}` (`RESUME_FROM_BEST_CHECKPOINT`); the `TODO: See TD-405` tags are now fix comments.

Files to Modify:

- `src/IncrementalTrainer.cpp`
- `tests/incrementaltrainer_test.cpp`

### TD-534: `vocab_builder` Defaults to Plain Text, Turning JSONL Syntax Into Vocabulary

| Resolution Date | Component | Resolved By |
|-----------------|-----------|-------------|
| October 17, 2026 | Tooling / vocab_builder | Code fix (MEDIUM, filed October 17, 2026) |

Description:
Found while tracing `VocabBuilder.cpp` (see [VocabBuilder.md](../reference/source/VocabBuilder.md)); verified. Training data is JSONL, but `--format`
defaults to `plain`, which takes each line as raw text; the help describes `pairs` (the loader that actually parses JSONL, by a leading `{`) only as
"INPUT/RESPONSE format". On a small JSONL corpus, `--format plain` produced JSON-syntax tokens (`{`, `{"`, `input`, `response`: 6 of 99 entries) that
never appear in the text the trainer tokenizes (it parses the JSONL first); `--format pairs` produced none. On real data the wasted merges grow with
escapes and key names.

**Fix landed October 17, 2026:** `--format` defaults to `auto`. `detect_input_format()` in `VocabBuilderHelpers.hpp` picks `pairs` for a file whose
first non-blank line starts with `{` or `INPUT:`/`RESPONSE:` (a UTF-8 BOM is skipped), `json` for `[`, and `plain` otherwise. The help describes
`pairs` as JSONL or `INPUT:`/`RESPONSE:` training data, and an explicit `--format plain` on such a file prints a warning.

On 300 TinyStories JSONL lines at `--vocab-size 400`:
- `auto` learned no `{`, `input` or `response` tokens (the 5 quote tokens left come from dialogue in the stories);
- `plain` learned 18 JSON-ish tokens.

5 new `DetectInputFormatTest` cases. OPERATIONS_MANUAL.md §4 is rewritten from `--help`.

Action Items:

- [x] Default to (or auto-detect) JSONL; describe `pairs` as "JSONL or INPUT:/RESPONSE: training files" in the help.
- [x] Warn when `plain` input looks like JSONL.

Location in code: `src/VocabBuilder.cpp` (`main()` format default, `print_usage()`), `src/VocabBuilderHelpers.hpp` (`detect_input_format()`); the `TODO: See TD-534` tag is now a fix comment.
